News.title: Man ‘jumps into tiger enclosure’ at Yorkshire Wildlife Park as zoo evacuated & witnesses reveal horror scenes
News.content:
TIGER HORROR Man ‘jumps into tiger enclosure’ at Yorkshire Wildlife Park as zoo evacuated & witnesses reveal horror scenes







Next

A MAN has reportedly jumped into a tiger enclosure in a “serious incident” at a UK wildlife park.

Witnesses revealed their horror after a visitor appeared to leap into the Land of the Tigers area at Yorkshire Wildlife Park.



Cops and an air ambulance swooped on the scene amid reports the park had been evacuated with visitors told to leave.

He is alleged to have been pounced on by at least one big cat and the tiger involved is believed to be called Altai.



Yorkshire Wildlife Park confirmed a “serious incident” had occurred with the zoo now closed today and tomorrow.

Some eyewitnesses at the zoo have even claimed to have heard shots fired at the tiger enclosure, reports The Star.



These sounds were believed to be gas canister and tranquilliser darts being fired with at least “five shots” reportedly heard.

Tia Hanson told The Star she was at the park for a day out with a pal when at around 2pm the walkway between the tiger enclosure and the exit was closed.



Speaking to the outlet, she claimed: “It looks as if someone has jumped into the enclosure.

“People are saying they heard a gunshot and they say someone either jumped in, or fell in.

“When you’re leaving you have to walk past the tiger enclosure and they’ve put up all sort of black tarpaulin so you couldn’t really see.”



A huge police and paramedic presence was spotted at the site as cops stood guard following the incident.

Eyewitnesses have also claimed they saw a black canvas up around the tiger enclosure.

An air ambulance was also pictured landing nearby alongside two ambulances.

Yorkshire Wildlife Park has posted a statement on their website: “We can confirm that a serious incident has occurred today at the tiger enclosure.



“Our emergency response procedures were immediately activated, and emergency services are currently attending the scene.

“We are working closely with the authorities to ascertain exactly what happened.

“The safety and wellbeing of our visitors, staff and animals remain our highest priority.

“The park is now closed and will remain closed tomorrow.”



A spokesperson for the Yorkshire Ambulance Service said: “I can confirm we were called at 13.33 on Saturday 10 October 2026 to an incident at Yorkshire Wildlife Park in Doncaster.

“We sent a number of resources, including two land ambulances, the Yorkshire Air Ambulance and a doctor.”

South Yorkshire Police has been contacted for comment.

News.title: Two friends, both 19, killed in horror BMW crash as families pay heartbreaking tribute to beloved duo
News.content:
TRAGIC PALS Two friends, both 19, killed in horror BMW crash as families pay heartbreaking tribute to beloved duo







Next

TWO teenagers who died in a horror crash have been pictured as their families pay tribute.

Jacob Patching and Jacob Skidmore, both 19, died when a white BMW left the road and reportedly collided with a lamppost. 4

Emergency services rushed to East Bawtry Road, Rotherham, but the pair were both pronounced dead at the scene on September 26 at around 6.45pm.

Their families are being supported by family liaison officers and they requested their tributes be shared.



The family of Jacob Patching said: “Jacob was a loyal, hardworking, caring and kind young man with a contagious sense of humour who had a love for the outdoors.



“Our whole lives have changed beyond measure in an instant and the pain left behind is immeasurable. Nothing will ever be the same without him.

“We would like to express our gratitude to the emergency services and the wider community affected by this tragedy.”

The family of Jacob Skidmore said: “We would like to thank all that are supporting us through this time.

“Jacob was loved by all who knew him, especially his work family at The Paint Factory, his girlfriend and his friends.

“He had a great love for mending anything with an engine as his mates know this well enough.



“He has left a big hole in our family that will never close. Forever in our hearts. Love Mum, Dad, Brothers and Sister.”

A spokesperson for the force said: “Our thoughts remain with the families, friends, and wider community affected by the loss of Jacob and Jacob.

“We are continuing to investigate the circumstances surrounding the collision and urge anyone with information or footage to contact us.”

News.title: Teen boy, 15, survives bear attack after ‘mobile phone exploded’ in his back pocket as rampaging brown bear mauled him
News.content:
Next

A TEENAGER has survived a horror bear attack after his phone reportedly exploded in his back pocket during the mauling.

The boy, 15, was being thrashed by the beast in Russia when his mobile burst in the animal’s face as it chomped on his backside.



Russian authorities said the youngster climbed up a tree to escape the animal before it pulled him down onto the ground.

The bear went on to claw and scratch the child during the terrifying assault.



Moments later, the boy’s phone reportedly exploded and caught fire, scaring the bear off in the process.

A witness, 24, who was with the boy at the time, said: “I heard him scream, turned my head, and saw the bear already dragging him down from the tree, so I unleashed the dogs.”

He added that the youngster’s phone battery apparently exploded when the bear “sank its teeth into the teenager’s buttocks”.

The unnamed teenager suffered serious wounds from the predator as well as burns from the blazing smartphone.



He underwent a three-hour operation as doctors said he suffered serious injuries to his chest, brain and abdomen.

Authorities said: “The young man climbed a tree, but the animal knocked him down, causing multiple bites and injuries to his body and head.

“During the attack, the bear damaged the victim’s phone, which caught fire, causing a thermal burn to the minor and scaring the animal away.”

Sergei Kovyazin, chief physician of Biysk Central City Hospital, said: “The patient arrived with multiple injuries to his head, scalp, facial bones and neck.

“These injuries presented the greatest challenge.”



The man with the boy was unharmed, officials said.

It is understood the pair had gone into the forest to check on his family’s bees.

The attack unfolded around 12 miles from the remote village of Solton.

A paramedic crew transported the victim to a medical facility.

Three rapid-response teams were dispatched to the area of the attack “to locate and eliminate a bear that attacked” the boy.



At least a dozen hunters were deployed to find and destroy the beast.

Bad weather hampered the search but the hunt is set to continue over the weekend.

Russia is suffering its worst year in living memory for deaths and injuries caused by bears.

Dozens have been killed and hundreds injured in attacks by the predators.

News.title: I was bitten & beaten in ‘circus’ relationship with ex – now he’ll walk free from jail…. this is my message to Burnham
News.content:
Next

A WOMAN who suffered vile abuse at the hands of her ex is now living in fear again after being told he will win back his freedom under the government’s early release scheme.

Grace Bennett, 22, used photos on her phone to convict Taylor Roddy, 27, after he subjected her to a horrific campaign of abuse – that saw her bitten and beaten – between January and September 2024.



The brute was jailed for three years at Truro Crown Court on May 26 this year.

But Grace said she was horrified to hear he would be coming out early – with his sentence slashed by six months under the government’s early release plans.



Prisoners held for all but the most serious offences can now leave prison after serving just a third of their sentence, rather than half after plans brought in by Sir Keir Starmer.

“How protected am I really going to be once he’s out?” she told The Sun.





“It just feels like the two year fight that took such a big chunk of me wasn’t worth it.”

Grace said she only found out Roddy was now being released in May next year after she spoke to her victim liaison officer.

And she called on the government to rethink their prison plans.

Grace said: “I think if I were going to have a message for the government [and Andy Burnham], I find myself thinking there should be or should have been a real conversation about the kinds of people you’re willing to early release into the public.

“I was really surprised to find that domestic abusers were part of the crowd that were being released because, to me, that seems like common knowledge that they aren’t the kind of people you’d release.”



She added: “Not only is it dangerous, but it’s so damaging to everyone who fought so hard to get these people into prison.

“What kind of faith are we supposed to have in the justice system if we spend more of our lives suffering and fighting for justice than they have to spend facing consequences?”

“He was a monster. This was not just a bad relationship, it was abuse,” she said, adding that it had permanently changed the way she lives her life – from meeting new people to moving around.

Speaking about the devastating impact of his abuse, Grace revealed she was “gaslit” into the relationship.

But she was found herself trapped and a network of abuse, being choked, slapped, shoved and bitten.



Grace was also psychologically controlled through jealousy, accusations of cheating, and online bullying orchestrated by Roddy.

And she then began sinking into debt amid the abuse.



The judge blasted Roddy saying he had no remorse and warned that any young woman he had a relationship with could be at risk of domestic abuse.

Yet – Grace now faces her abuser being back on the streets due to the early release scheme.

Grace described the atmosphere in that flat – stripped of furniture because they kept having to sell belongings to cover rent – as dehumanising, leaving her feeling like a “monkey in a circus”.

In March, while out in St Ives, the jury heard how Roddy rugby-tackled her to the ground, leaving her leg bruised and swollen and her arm shredded.



The court was also told of two occasions when he bit her, and of another incident in which he grabbed her arm, pulled her to the floor and left her so distressed she fled to her workplace in her dressing gown after he snatched her phone.

She also recounted being held in a chokehold so tight she could not breathe, striking Roddy with a nearby Wi-Fi router to get him to release her.

As well as physical violence, prosecutors said Roddy subjected the victim to sustained emotional manipulation and verbal abuse.

Grace met Roddy when she was just 19 back in 2023, while the pair were both working front of house in St Ives, Cornwall, where he appeared to be calm and charming.

She recounted how the relationship had moved quickly and within about a week she had moved in with him.



“Everyone thought he was amazing and so nice and how lucky I was,” she said.

“But I want everyone to know what type of person he was and to help prevent this happening ever in the future because I couldn’t live with myself knowing it could happen again.”

As part of the trial, jurors heard a voice recording made on 29 March 2024 capturing him shouting in rage.

The court was told that Roddy also frequently accused her of cheating, posted allegations about her online, and spread claims to family members in an effort to humiliate her.

He also controlled who she could speak to, repeatedly demanded to know her whereabouts and insisted she share her location so he could monitor her movements.



“I just felt completely alone. Because I went from speaking with my friends and my mum to not speaking to them at all,” she said.

On one occasion, he pushed her outside naked and locked her out.

She said the final straw came on her 20th birthday in Plymouth when Roddy slapped her across the face in public.

“When he slapped me across the face, I was just like, that’s it, I’m done,” she said.

In sentencing, the judge described the “appalling” psychological coercion, physical violence and emotional manipulation in what a judge described as a “deeply disturbing pattern of abuse”.



For Grace, the sentence brought some relief, but not closure.

She said: “I have nightmares that he is in my house controlling me in front of my friends and my family and people are just laughing at me.”

Prosecutors argued the case fell into the highest category of seriousness for coercive and controlling behaviour, pointing to repeated violence, damage to property, conduct intended to maximise fear and distress and behaviour designed to humiliate her publicly.

Sentencing, His Honour Judge James Adkin said Roddy’s behaviour towards his former partner during the relationship was appalling.

“You have no insight into the way that you behaved in that relationship and that you have deeply ingrained behavioural traits whereby I fear for any young woman that you’re in a relationship with in the future that they may well again be subjected to domestic abuse,” he said.



The judge also imposed a ten-year restraining order banning Roddy from contacting the victim directly or indirectly, going to the street where she lives and making any reference to her on social media.

A Ministry of Justice spokesperson said: “Domestic abuse devastates lives. We’re investing £1 billion in victim support, putting specialists in 999 call centres and strengthening protections for survivors.

TWO teenagers are in critical condition after being stabbed just minutes apart.

Police scrambled to the scene after reports of a stabbing in Dagenham, London, just after 6pm yesterday.



Upon arrival, emergency services found a 19-year-old man in life threatening condition.

Two minutes later, a 17-year-old was found less than a mile away also suffering from stab wounds.

They also have been arrested on suspicion of affray and possession of an offensive weapon.

News.title: Two men crushed to death and 16 injured after festival floats overturn during ‘high speed stunt’ in Japan
News.content:
Next

TWO men have been crushed to death and a further 16 injured after several packed floats flipped over during “high speed stunts” in Japan.

The performers, aged 48 and 51, were killed just hours apart on the streets of Osaka during an annual autumn festival.



Horrifying footage shows the double-decker cart swerving round a corner at high speed before tipping to one side and crashing to the ground.

At one point the truck leans towards a crowd of onlookers before swinging back and collapsing in front of a local’s home in Miyamachi.



Firefighters raced to reports of an overturned float at around 1.20pm.

A 48-year-old man was crushed beneath the structure and killed.



Nine other men – aged from their teens to their 60s – were rushed to hospital with non-life threatening injuries.

The terrifying tragedy unfolded while performers allegedly attempted a high-speed right-hand yarimawashi turn, police said.

Just hours earlier another massive float had flipped over and flattened a street performer.

The fatal accident unfolded at around 11.00am at Nagataki intersection.



Performers had been heaving a heavy, multi-ton float at high speed when the vehicle toppled to one side and fell on top of performers.

Several people were left trapped beneath the wooden float.

Rescuers scrambled to save survivors – and rushed one 51-year-old man to hospital.



Tragically, the company executive later succumbed to his injuries.

Teenagers were among seven other men hospitalised after the terrifying tragedy.

Two are believed to have suffered serious injuries.

Police have launched probes into both fatalities and have noted that both had been attempting high-speed 90 degree turns.

Traditional danjiri festivals are famed for their boozy exploits and high-risk street manoeuvres.



Just days earlier on October 3 several people were injured after a float overturned in Sakai City.

A WOMAN’S body has been found along the cliffs of a popular coastal beauty spot.

A search and rescue team found the body while assisting police in searching for a missing person in North Devon.

Exmoor Search and Rescue Team confirmed they spotted the body on the cliffs while searching through the area.

News.title: Head of Met's volunteer force fired after AI tool found deleted intimate images on work phone
News.content:
The Metropolitan Police has fired the head of its Special Constabulary after Palantir's AI monitoring uncovered that he had used his work phone to copy intimate images of a woman.

Special chief officer James Deller, who led the force's volunteer officers, was dismissed following a misconduct hearing on Friday.

The Met said investigators used lawful business monitoring and Palantir's Foundry system, which uses artificial intelligence (AI), to find the misconduct by Deller.

Cdr Pete Stevens said: "SCO Deller failed to meet that bar. His actions were an abuse of the trust put in him and it is right that he is no longer able to serve in policing."

Investigators found that in July and August 2025, Deller used his police-issued phone to take photos of two intimate images that had been sent to his personal phone.

The pictures had been sent using WhatsApp's "view once" feature, which makes them disappear after they are opened.

He then sent the copied images back to his personal device before deleting them from his work phone.

The misconduct was discovered during a week-long operation called Project Galatasaray, which used the AI technology in a bid to identify corruption and professional misconduct within the Met.

Deller will be added to the College of Policing's barred list, meaning he will not be able to serve in policing again.

Stevens added: "The vast majority of Met officers and staff serve London with dedication and integrity, and they rightly expect robust action against the small minority who abuse their position and undermine public trust.

"That is particularly true of those who serve in the Special Constabulary. They are volunteers who selflessly give up their time to keep London safe.

"They deserve to be led by people who demonstrate the highest standards in all parts of their lives."

News.title: Sara Sharif's grandfather granted guardianship of her siblings in Pakistan
News.content:
Sara Sharif's paternal grandfather has been granted guardianship of her siblings by a court in Pakistan.

The decision comes after years of legal limbo following the murder of 10-year-old Sara by her father and stepmother in 2023.

All five children, who are now aged between 16 and four, have been living in Pakistan since 2023. They were asked to speak to the judge in court, where the eldest said they were comfortable and the siblings were settled.

Sara's grandfather, Muhammed Sharif, told the BBC he was relieved to be granted guardianship after three years of legal battles, saying his hope is that the children "stay healthy" and receive "a good education".

"It is my responsibility to ensure they get the best possible education and care," he said.

When told by the judge that the grandfather would become their guardian, the eldest child responded saying "that's all good".

The five children have been in Pakistan since August 2023, when they were brought to the country by Sara's father, stepmother and uncle after Sara was killed.

The family was in hiding for weeks before the children were discovered by police at the grandfather's house. They were initially put into state childcare.

The adults flew back to the UK and were arrested at the airport. Sara's father Urfan Sharif and stepmother Beinash Batool were found guilty of Sara's murder. Sharif was sentenced to a minimum of 40 years in prison and Batool received a minimum of 33 years.

Her uncle, Faisal Malik, was found guilty of causing or allowing her death and given a 16-year sentence.

Sara had been hooded, burned and beaten during a "campaign of torture" that lasted two years before her body was found at the family home in Woking, Surrey.

News.title: Ashe was too scared to cancel her wedding, then her story became a hit song
News.content:
No songwriter is ever off duty. And for the US pop singer Ashe, that included her wedding day.

Last October, she was getting ready to tie the knot at a gorgeous hilltop ceremony in Nashville when inspiration struck.

As she watched her family gather, the musician flashed back to her first wedding, almost a decade earlier. The contrast was stark.

She's called that first marriage "horrifying". Her ex, who she met in college, was, she says, emotionally manipulative and psychologically abusive.

He had insisted on a beachfront wedding, which sounds romantic until you learn that Ashe has a fear of the ocean.

In the run-up, she had been tempted to call it off, but felt powerless to stand up for herself.

On her second wedding day, she realised the opposite was true.

"I'm in a happy, healthy relationship and I have total autonomy over my own life," says the singer, now in her early 30s.

"I thought, if this didn't feel right, I could totally put a halt to the whole thing. I definitely didn't have that first time around."

As she adjusted her veil and prepared to walk down the aisle, she filed that feeling away.

Two months later, and back at work, the idea resurfaced and a song spilled out.

Its name? Stop the Wedding.

It unfolds like a movie scene. Ashe pleads with her younger self to trust her instincts.

"You know how you really feel / You don't have to waste your life," she sings, as the wedding band stutters to an uncertain halt.

"Do I wish I'd had that advice at the time? 1,000 per cent," Ashe says.

"If someone had given me the insight that I was not stuck, and that I could run, I could have changed things sooner. Maybe not at the altar. Maybe weeks before â but it was something I really could have used."

What about the line where she pledges to "burn the wedding dress and run away"?

"I didn't burn my dress," she laughs, "but I did get into a bathtub with it for a photoshoot right after I left my ex-husband, which really ruined it!"

News.title: France's school protests are about more than broken classrooms
News.content:
As dustbins burn and students chant "everyone hates the police" in the French city of Lille, one teenager explains why he and his friends have taken to the streets.

"There aren't even enough chairs. We have to go and find some at the start of every lesson," the 16-year-old, who did not want to give his name, says of his school.

"We've got 50 minutes to eat at lunchtime but there are 2,000 of us that need to get through the canteen."

He is one of hundreds of thousands of students who have protested across France since the end of last month over staff shortages and dilapidated facilities in the country's lycÃ©es, secondary schools attended by 15 to 18-year-olds.

Despite the government's apparent attempts to make concessions, the students show no sign of backing down.

"They have armies, they have the police, they have the powers," says Massicella, 18, as she marches through Lille. "But we have the mass population."

The protests, which have turned violent, have become a focal point in France's polarised politics, with all sides accusing the other of escalating tensions. As a presidential election approaches, politicians on both the hard right and hard left have sought to capitalise on the unrest and on what many see as the government's inability to resolve the crisis.

News.title: I couldn't access my family's medical history - not knowing was terrifying
News.content:
When Aaliyah found a lump in her breast, she was anxious to find out if she had inherited an increased risk of cancer.

But because she had been removed from her biological parents at the age of seven months and later adopted, she had no way of accessing her family medical history.

"Not knowing anything about yourself genetically is terrifying," says the 26-year-old, "you can't even begin to imagine it."

The lump turned out to be non-cancerous, but it was one of many occasions when she found herself unable to answer questions about her biological family's health.

Aaliyah, now a trainee solicitor, spent years trying to source information from local authorities and eventually made an official data access request to Bradford Council, which removed her from her biological family as a baby.

She says the whole process took its toll.

"I would say bureaucratic hellscape is an understatement," she admits.

News.title: Public executions in the US stopped nearly a century ago, why are they resuming now?
News.content:
They came in their thousands from near and far. Men, women and children lined up on a Kentucky riverfront for the public hanging of a black man convicted of raping and killing an elderly white widow.

It was 14 August 1936 in Owensboro, Kentucky, a sweltering Friday in the middle of a legendary heatwave. Some slept overnight near the gallows to preserve their spots. Others held "necktie" parties the previous evening, arriving hungover as teenagers sold popcorn and soda to the spectators.

By the execution time of 5am, the crowd had swelled to an estimated 20,000.

That's when Rainey Bethea, an orphan in his 20s, stepped up to the gallows - sentenced to death after allegedly confessing to robbing, raping and killing Lischia Edwards, 70.

The previous afternoon, he'd eaten a last meal of fried chicken, pork chops, mashed potatoes, pickled cucumbers, cornbread, lemon pie and ice cream.

Many of those gathered - including press from as far away as Chicago and New York - came to see the rumoured "Lady Executioner;" the local sheriff had died four months earlier, and his widow became the unlikely female replacement. She declined to pull the trip lever herself, however, and it was hired hangmen who instead sent Bethea to his death.

That moment marked the last high-profile public hanging in America. The circus surrounding Bethea's death embarrassed many in Kentucky, and the governor outlawed public executions 18 months later.

By then, most states had abolished capital punishment in view of the masses as societal attitudes sought more humane and private methods. Another hanging was attended by a few hundred in Missouri in 1937, but that was lesser known and marked America's final public execution - until now.

News.title: Drumcree parade ban was in interests of peace, says Bryant
News.content:
The Northern Ireland secretary of state has said his decision to ban the Orange Order's Drumcree march was in the best interests of peace.

The decision came after an agreement couldn't be reached between the Portadown District Lodge and the Garvaghy Road residents over whether the march would be allowed down the predominantly nationalist road.

The stalemate has reopened what was once the most bitter parading dispute in Northern Ireland, with stand-offs in the mid-to-late 1990s accompanied by riots, roadblocks and killings.

Sir Chris Bryant said he received advice from the PSNI chief constable that allowing the procession to go ahead could lead to serious injury, disorder and wider unrest.

The Parades Commission was established in 1998 to regulate contentious processions.

Its decisions restricting the Drumcree march have been challenged by the Orange Order for decades.

Earlier this year, a court overturned the commission's original decision to stop the parade, ruling it could go ahead, with restrictions on 27 September.

But Garvaghy Road residents blocked the road that morning, preventing the Orangemen from marching, and a stand-off has continued for almost two weeks.

The Court of Appeal has reserved judgment on a legal challenge brought by Garvaghy Road residents against the decision to allow the march.

Sir Chris said he had spent almost two weeks trying to broker a deal and believed the two sides had come close to an agreement.

He said two outcomes were discussed. One would have allowed the Orangemen to complete one final march along the Garvaghy Road, on the condition it would not apply to march the route again.

The other would have seen the group accept that it had won the right to march, but agree not to exercise that right, but neither proposal secured agreement from both sides.

News.title: Green Party MP wants to make sure it is 'not vulnerable to extremists'
News.content:
A Green Party MP has said her party needs to make sure it is not "vulnerable to capture by extremists and racists" after members voted for a motion that claimed Zionism was racism.

The motion put forward by activists, which became formal policy after it was approved at the Green's conference earlier this month, has divided senior party figures and been criticised by Jewish groups.

Westminster leader Ellie Chowns told the BBC it was a "significant and damaging policy" and she would work to reform the Green Party.

It comes after ex-leader Caroline Lucas said it was not being protected from entryism - where people sign up to a party to try to change it.

Speaking to BBC Radio 4's Today Programme on Saturday, Chowns said: "I don't know if there are extremists and racists in my party. But I want to make sure that my party isn't vulnerable to capture by extremists and racists."

The MP described Zionism as a "contested concept" and said the motion did not represent the views of the large majority of Green Party members, "nor of people in the country".

Chowns said the motion would be a "distraction from the very important work" the party has been doing campaigning for Palestinian rights.

She added: "I think it is clear that if we have policy, such significant and damaging policy, made by a vote of just 0.4% of our members, that something isn't working in our structures and our policy-making process."

Members of the Green Party of England and Wales endorsed the policy motion by 1,022 votes to 813.

There are 230,000 members of the Green party overall and not everyone attended the conference.

The policy also backs a "single democratic Palestinian state in all of historic Palestine", which includes modern-day Israel.

It defines Zionism as an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state".

The Board of Deputies of British Jews and the Jewish Leadership Council, which criticised the motion, said: "Zionism is anti-racism, creating a refuge for Jews in their ancient homeland after millennia of persecution outside it."

News.title: Eight men arrested by Greater Manchester Police days after early release from jail
News.content:
Eight men have been arrested by Greater Manchester Police days after leaving prison under the government's early release scheme.

About 700 prisoners from across the country were released early on 1 October in a bid to tackle overcrowding, with about 50 of them being from Greater Manchester.

GMP confirmed that five men had been arrested for breaches of criminal orders, including a domestic abuse prevention order, and others were held on suspicion of robbery, drug offences and domestic violence.

In response, the Ministry of justice (MOJ) said: "We inherited a prison system on the brink of collapse. If we had failed to act, the police would have been forced to halt arrests."

News.title: Rail disruption after overhead line fault
News.content:
Rail passengers are being urged to check before they travel due to overhead line problems on the West Coast Main Line in Staffordshire.

Work was ongoing to fix a fault with the 25,000-volt wires which power trains near Penkridge, causing disruption between Stafford and Wolverhampton.

At 12:00 BST, National Rail confirmed that lines have reopened between Stafford and Birmingham New Street, but residual disruption can still be expected until 16:00 BST on Saturday.

Adam Checkley from Network Rail, said: "Our teams have now cleared the issue allowing the route to reopen, but with trains and their crew out of position, delays and cancellations will continue throughout the day."

Rail replacement buses are in place at Birmingham, Stafford and Wolverhampton.

Checkley added: "We're sorry to passengers impacted by the overhead line problems at Four Ashes near Penkridge.

"With disruption to train services likely throughout the day, I'd urge people to check National Rail Enquiries before they set off on their journey."

Ticket acceptance is in place on alternative routes including the East Coast Main Line, and Midland Main Line via Sheffield.

News.title: Queen reflects on reading 'forbidden' Lady Chatterley's Lover under the pillow
News.content:
Queen Camilla has recalled secretly reading Lady Chatterley's Lover, the passionate and controversial novel by DH Lawrence, as a teenager in the 1960s.

"As teenagers you read a lot of romances. It was the moment of Lady Chatterley, under our pillows, reading that by torchlight. You know the minute something is forbidden, you want to get hold of it," she said about the novel that had been at the centre of an obscenity trial.

The Queen spoke about memorable moments in her own reading for BBC documentary The Book That Changed My Life, and about the life-changing power of literacy and books.

She gave a glimpse of how regular reading is part of her royal marriage: "It's like the best tonic in the world. My husband and I actually read before dinner, just sitting quietly and reading.

"He loves biographies, and PG Wodehouse. I occasionally, when I'm deep in a book, hear him roaring with laughter about something," said the Queen about the King's affection for the author of the Jeeves and Wooster comic novels.

"It's very off-putting, I can't get back into my book, or I'll suddenly start weeping. But it's a lovely, quiet time. I think it would be a complete and utter tragedy if books went forever," she said.

The Queen also revealed more of her own youthful reading, saying she was "mesmerised" by Charles Dickens's Tale of Two Cities and its depiction of those watching the guillotine during the French Revolution.

"Those ghastly women sitting there knitting while everybody had their heads chopped off," she said.

The Queen, who is 79 years old, said she was part of a generation of women who missed out on higher education, which made reading and books even more important.

"I left school quite young. In my day, women didn't go to university, so I think reading has been most of my education," she said.

News.title: Four murder arrests after teenagers attacked
News.content:
Four people have been arrested on suspicion of murder after a man died and another suffered life-threatening injuries in Stoke-on-Trent.

A cordon remains in place on Brookhouse Road, in Meir, after police were called to reports of violence at 23:45 BST on Friday.

A man in his late teens was confirmed dead at the scene, Staffordshire Police said, and another man, also in his late teens, was taken to hospital, where he remains in a critical but stable condition.

Two 18-year-old men, a 20-year-old man and a 17-year-old boy, all from Stoke-on-Trent, were arrested on suspicion of murder, while the boy was also arrested on suspicion of attempted murder. All remain in police custody.

News.title: Man arrested after boy, 11, injured in 'dog attack'
News.content:
A man has been arrested after an 11-year-old boy was injured in an alleged dog attack.

Three dogs were reported to be "out of control" in the Scotland Hall Road area of Newton Heath in north Manchester at about 16:00 BST on Thursday, Greater Manchester Police said.

The force said one dog was seized and the other two were placed in kennels. The boy suffered minor injuries.

A 31-year-old man has been held on suspicion of possessing an aggressive animal.

The force has not confirmed the breed of dog.

News.title: 'Speculation over daughter's death is devastating'
News.content:
When Leah Croucher's body was found three years after she went missing, her family thought their torture would end. Instead it continued with conspiracy theories, fear and heartbreak haunting their lives.

The 19-year-old was walking to work on 15 February 2019 when she disappeared. Her parents say they went through more than three years of "absolute torture" before her dismembered body was discovered in a house in Milton Keynes, less than half a mile (0.8km) from her home in 2022.

She had been killed by a repeat sex offender Neil Maxwell, a man who her parents have branded "an animal". He was on the run from police at the time.

Despite overwhelming evidence of Maxwell's guilt, her parents Claire and John say they have been subjected to "devastating" speculation online, with some pointing the finger at her brother.

Leah's parents are now calling for 'Leah's Law', a mandatory minimum sentence for anyone convicted of a third sexual offence.

Haydon Croucher took his own life nine months after his sister went missing. Leah's parents say he struggled to cope with not knowing what had happened to her.

The Crouchers believe Leah's Law would have saved Leah and by extension Haydon.

News.title: Trump takes Nobel Prize snub to Truth Social in late-night rant: ‘Indelible stain’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

President Donald Trump continued his sour-grapes rant against Nobel Peace Prize winner Navi Pillay on Truth Social late Friday, claiming he deserved the award for settling eight wars and calling the decision to overlook him an “indelible stain” on Norway.

In a lengthy Truth Social post hours after the Nobel Committee announced Pillay as this year’s recipient, Trump questioned the South African human rights lawyer’s qualifications, accused her of hating Israel and listed what he described as his diplomatic achievements.

“This is the woman who received the Nobel Peace Prize over the Great United States of America, whose Representative, ME, settled eight Wars, and many other things,” Trump wrote alongside a photo of the 85-year-old Pillay.

“I know nothing about this woman, and neither does anyone else! In fact, to the best of my knowledge, no one ever heard of her other than the fact that she, very obviously, hates Israel. I don’t know what the woman has done.”

Pillay is a prominent jurist who has spent decades working on human rights and international justice. She previously defended imprisoned anti-apartheid leader Nelson Mandela and held senior positions within the United Nations.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump lashed out at Nobel Peace Prize winner Navi Pillay on Truth Social late Friday, claiming he deserved the award and calling the decision an ‘indelible stain’ on Norway ( Reuters )

At the Nuremberg court where Pillay was attending an academic and legal conference, she addressed attendees and made a joke at Trump’s expense, in footage shared by Amnesty International’s secretary general, Agnes Callamard.

Walking into a room of applause, she said: “If you clap a little bit more, I may share this prize with Trump.”

That may have helped set Trump off, but likely anyione who won would have been the target of his vitriol.

Trump went on to detail his claims of international diplomatic successes, writing: “I settled 8 WARS, am close to ending or settling 2 more, got all of the Israeli hostages back, including the final 28, both living and dead, had hundreds of hostages, from countries all over the World, released and sent back home, won a war in Venezuela, and captured the violent dictator who so viciously ran that country, and stopped the number one state sponsor of terror, the Islamic Republic of Iran, from obtaining a Nuclear Weapon — AND MUCH MORE! Yet, with all of that I, or the United States of America, did not get the Noble (sic) Peace Prize. WOW!”

Trump has repeatedly argued that his efforts to resolve international conflicts make him deserving of the prestigious award.

The president also criticized the Nobel Committee’s decision during a rally in Syracuse, New York, on Friday night, taking aim at Norway over the outcome.

“And this is a stain on the country of Norway,” Trump told the crowd. “We will not forget, Norway. It’s another sign of how they’re ripping off our country.”

open image in gallery Pillay is a veteran human rights lawyer and jurist who previously defended imprisoned anti-apartheid leader Nelson Mandela and held senior roles at the UN ( AFP/Getty )

He reiterated the criticism on Truth Social, writing: “The United States of America, represented by me, as your President, should have received the Nobel Peace Prize, but didn’t. This is an indelible stain on Norway, one that will never be forgotten.”

“The Nobel ‘Peace’ Prize has been forever discredited by a handful of Radical Ideologues who are Anti-Democracy, and Enemies of Civilization!” he added.

Last year, Pillay led a UN commission of inquiry that concluded Israel had committed genocide in Gaza, citing evidence that it intended to destroy Palestinians in the territory. Israel has strongly rejected allegations of genocide.

Her work on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict has also drawn criticism from Israeli officials, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who condemned the Nobel Committee’s decision.

Trump’s latest complaints follow a separate controversy over last year’s Nobel Peace Prize. Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado, who won the 2025 award, presented Trump with her medal in January after repeatedly praising his efforts.

Trump has cited Machado’s support as evidence that he deserves the honor, but the Norwegian Nobel Committee determines the laureate, and the prize itself is not transferred when a recipient gives away their medal

News.title: Cristiano Ronaldo suspended by Portugal after walking out on national team
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Cristiano Ronaldo has been provisionally suspended by Portugal after walking out on the national team.

Ronaldo left the Portugal squad after he was an unused substitute for a 2-1 win away to Norway in the Nations League on 27 September.

The 41-year-old, who has scored a record-breaking 146 goals in 234 appearances for his country, subsequently issued a near 2,000-word statement saying he withdrew from the squad after a “breach of trust” between him and head coach Jorge Jesus.

The Portuguese Football Federation have now acted, saying in a statement reported by Lisbon-based newspaper A Bola: “Disciplinary proceedings were initiated against Cristiano Ronaldo, by decision of the non-professional section, on October 9, 2026, with the objective of ascertaining the potential disciplinary relevance of the facts reported on October 7, 2026.

“Without prejudice to the automatic preventive suspension to which he was subject until the date of initiation, a non-automatic preventive suspension of the player was determined, and the proceedings were given urgent status.

“The proceedings were sent, on October 10, 2026, to the disciplinary instruction committee of the FPF (Portuguese Football Federation), with publicity excluded until the end of the investigation.”

Ronaldo missed Portugal’s following two fixtures, wins over Denmark and Norway, which left them top of Group A4 with four straight wins, fuelling speculation his international career could be over.

Jesus left the door open to the veteran forward in a press conference after Sunday’s win against Norway, saying: “If he wants to, he’ll return to the national team.”

Ronaldo argued Jesus had reneged on an agreement about how many minutes he would play but apologised for his actions and accepted he deserved to be sanctioned.

He put his difficulties to one side with a goal for club side Al Nassr on Friday in their 3-0 Saudi Pro League victory against Diriyah.

PA

News.title: Crazy Rich Asians is returning for a long-awaited sequel – but there’s a twist
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Fans of the 2018 romcom Crazy Rich Asians have been waiting for news of a potential sequel for years – and now an update has finally arrived.

The movie, which starred Constance Wu and Henry Golding and was based on the novel by Kevin Kwan, was a huge box office success story, grossing more than $239 million worldwide.

It was a critical hit, too, and rumours of a second movie, inspired by later books in Kwan’s series, began to circulate.

It has now been confirmed, however, that the sequel will come in the form of a TV series, rather than a film.

The series will include eight episodes and will feature returning cast members Wu, Golding and Ronny Chieng.

Oscar winner Michelle Yeoh will also reprise her role as Wu’s formidable on-screen mother-in-law.

open image in gallery Constance Wu is one of the original stars set to reprise their role ( Sanja Bucko/Warner Bros )

The series will air on HBO, and Crazy Rich Asians co-writer Adele Lim will serve as showrunner and executive producer.

“It’s a Crazy Rich family reunion!” Lim said in a statement. “This series is the sequel we've been waiting for, but instead of just one movie, we get eight episodes to delve into the characters and worlds of Kevin Kwan's brilliant books.”

“Our writers room is humming and we can't wait to share what we've come up with,” she added.

open image in gallery Michelle Yeoh, Constance Wu and Henry Golding in 'Crazy Rich Asians' ( Warner Bros. )

Author Kwan said that he was “thrilled that the Crazy Rich Asians family is getting back together” and thanked “our incredible fans around the world” for “patiently waiting” for the next installment, promising “it will be worth the wait!”

“Getting to see my stories and characters come to life with the breathing room of an HBO series is a dream come true,” he added.

Crazy Rich Asians tells the story of Rachel (Wu), an Asian-American woman who flies out to Singapore to meet her boyfriend Nick (Golding)’s super-rich family for the very first time – only to realise that his upbringing has been very different from her own.

News.title: Opposition leaders, activists and journalists detained as Delhi police block ‘cockroach’ protests
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Opposition leaders, student activists and journalists were detained as police launched a sweeping crackdown to thwart protests against India’s election chief in the capital Delhi on Saturday.

Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee and Pinarayi Vijayan, former chief ministers of Delhi, West Bengal and Kerala states, respectively, were held alongside Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, leaders of the youth-dominated Cockroach Janta Party (CJP). Student leader Neha Bora, communist figure Brinda Karat, and economist and activist Jean Drèze were also among the demonstrators taken into custody.

The CJP, which led the protests that forced the resignation of India’s education minister earlier this year, and the All India Students Association had called for demonstrations on Saturday to demand the removal of Gyanesh Kumar, the chief election commissioner, who they accused of controversially revising voter rolls to benefit prime minister Narendra Modi’s BJP party.

But the police refused permission for the demonstrations citing security concerns, insufficient notice, and alleged violations of conditions imposed during earlier protests.

On Friday, home secretary Govind Mohan directed all states and federal territories to coordinate with the Delhi police and take preventative measures to stop protesters travelling to Delhi, according to The Hindu. He also called for real-time intelligence sharing between state agencies, transport authorities, and the Delhi police.

open image in gallery Security personnel detain a protester in Delhi on Saturday ( AP )

Police sources told the Indian Express that they had detained nearly 1,200 people overnight to deter the protests. They detained many more over the course of the day.

Some 27,000 police and paramilitary personnel were deployed to prevent protesters from gathering in central Delhi. They were reportedly ordered to stop demonstrators from getting to the primary protest site at Jantar Mantar observatory and detain anyone who refused to turn back.

In central Delhi, metal barricades blocked roads and police stopped and checked vehicles.

India: SFI Protesters Detained by Police at Delhi’s Connaught Place Over CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Vote Chori Allegations.

As many as 45 metro stations were closed and more than 245 trains cancelled, severely disrupting public transport in and around the capital. Mobile internet services were suspended within a 4km radius of the main protest site from Friday night until Saturday night.

The three CJP leaders were detained at the Delhi airport before they could disembark their flight from Mumbai.

“We are here to be arrested, come and arrest us,” Mr Dipke was heard in a video telling police officers who had boarded the aircraft to detain him and his fellow leaders.

The party condemned the detention of its leaders and supporters as an attempt to cripple the protests and demanded their immediate release.

The party later announced that senior member Ajinkya Shinde would head the protests while the three leaders remained in custody.

Mr Kejriwal was detained while he was on his way to Jantar Mantar, while Ms Banerjee and several members of her Trinamool Congress party were taken away from outside her residence in the city, according to MP Saket Gokhale.

Ms Bora, activist Yogendra Yadav and lawyer Prashant Bhushan were detained as they were marching towards the protest site.

YouTuber Dhruv Rathee was detained at his home in Gurugram, while journalists from several media outlets, including Scroll, Newslaundry, Navbharat Times, and Reporter TV, were snatched from where they were covering the protests.

The Committee to Protect Journalists called on the police to release the detained journalists, return their equipment, and investigate reports of physical abuse against them.

The protests were triggered by allegations that changes made to electoral rolls had excluded millions of eligible voters and potentially affected election results. The revision had flagged more than 130 million names.

open image in gallery Security personnel detain a protester in Delhi on Saturday ( AP )

Opposition parties and critics say the latest revision, nearly two decades after the last, constitutes mass disenfranchisement to favour the BJP. They want the exercise scrapped ​and the old rolls reinstated.

The election commission says the ​numbers represent voter entries flagged during a draft revision in an exercise that is not complete, while those wrongly removed can enrol again.

open image in gallery Detained protesters shout slogans during a demonstration demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in Delhi ( AP )

BJP president Nitin Nabin accused the leader of the opposition, Rahul Gandhi, and the CJP of trying to destabilise the country “at the behest of foreign forces” through the protests.

Mr Gandhi and other opposition leaders were detained during protests against Mr Kumar earlier in the week.

On Friday, opposition leaders, including Mr Gandhi, met president Droupadi Murmu to convey their concerns about the election commission and the revision of voter rolls, and to demand Mr Kumar’s removal.

News.title: Adult acne is real, but there are ways to treat it. Here's what to know
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

As a teenager, Gillian Maegan Montalbo's pimples weren't too bad — just a few bumps on her forehead and nose.

But as an adult in the workforce, the breakouts returned and intensified. The acne on her cheeks and chin made her hesitant to look her bosses in the eye.

“It really took a toll on my self-esteem and my self-confidence,” said Montalbo, a marketer and content creator who lives in the Philippines.

Pimples and acne are an uncomfortable hallmark of teenage years, but adults can have breakouts too. Acne can also happen on other parts of the body like the chest and shoulders. And then there's bacne, the internet's term for back breakouts.

The best treatments vary from person to person depending on what's causing the acne and how it looks. And breakouts can leave behind dark marks and scars that take even longer to heal.

Pimples come and go, but if breakouts stick around and cause discoloration or changes in skin texture, it's a good idea to see a dermatologist.

“We know how to treat acne. We know the cause of it. So don't suffer alone,” said Dr. Crystal Aguh, a dermatologist and director of the Ethnic Skin Program at Johns Hopkins School of Medicine.

The causes of acne can vary

Teenage acne tends to affect the forehead, nose and cheeks. Older adults and women in particular can experience hormonal acne that pops up along the jawline and chin, Aguh said. Taking steroids can also trigger acne for some people.

Pimples happen when tiny pores in the skin get clogged by oil, bacteria and dead skin cells. They can fade over the course of weeks to months, but if patches persist and spread, it could be a sign of acne, which dermatologists consider a medical condition.

“Essentially, you’re not getting a break from a breakout,” Aguh said.

Acne is caused by many factors including genetics, hormones, environment and even diet — like eating excessive amounts of dairy. The causes of facial and body acne are similar, although skin bacteria sometimes plays a larger role in body acne.

Breakouts can look like milder, painless white bumps or dark specks known as whiteheads and blackheads, or more painful red bumps and deeper cysts — a mark of cystic acne.

There are OTC and prescription treatments for acne

Don't pick or pop your pimples, no matter how strong the urge or how satisfying it might be.

“Everyone wants to pick and squeeze. That will almost always make things worse,” said Dr. Lauren Fine, founder of Fine Dermatology in Chicago.

Picking can drive inflammation deeper into the skin and cause acne to spread. It also increases the risk of marks and scarring. For darker-skinned people, those marks take longer to go away because their skin produces extra pigment when stressed, Aguh said.

Treatments for acne range from over-the-counter creams and lotions to prescription-strength medications. Dermatologists say it’s somewhat easier to treat acne on the face compared to the rest of the body because the face has more sweat glands and doesn't dry out as easily. It's also harder to apply some treatments like creams to hard-to-reach areas like the back, so doctors often prescribe oral medications.

For milder forms of face acne, dermatologists may recommend face washes or creams containing benzoyl peroxide, salicylic acid or retinoids like adapalene.

For more frequent breakouts, they might prescribe higher-strength regimens like antibiotics or medicines with tretinoin. Isotretinoin may be an option if those medicines don't work, or for cases of severe cystic acne.

Treatments for adult hormonal acne, particularly in women, can differ from what's done for teens. Some dermatologists recommend birth control, which can help stabilize hormones, or treatments like spironolactone.

Shots of cortisone can help treat active acne spots in a pinch, but they aren't a long-term fix, Fine said.

Pimple patches containing a gel called hydrocolloid can absorb fluids from oozing pimples and stop you from picking at them. Aguh said they are suited only for mild forms of acne; Fine said the patches have given some of her patients discoloration and she doesn't recommend them.

Treat discoloration with exfoliants and face washes

Experts say exfoliants and face washes containing glycolic acid can help discoloration fade. Over-the-counter products containing adapalene and retinol creams can also help.

For more serious scarring, dermatologists can recommend more aggressive treatments like lasers that probe deeper into the skin.

It can take time to develop the right treatment plan, and longer still to see results. When starting a new treatment, some people can also experience skin purging: breakouts that happen when a product quickly brings clogged pores to the surface of the skin.

Montalbo’s acne cleared up within a year after seeing a dermatologist, but she was still dealing with acne scars. After that, she had to rebuild her self-confidence.

She said a strong support system was essential to getting through some of the hardest moments. Her dad, who also struggled with acne, was the one who encouraged her to see a doctor and find the right products. She also had a close friend who traveled with her overseas for a vacation during the worst of the breakouts, and mentioned in passing that she'd never even noticed Montalbo's acne.

“When you are with the right people, they won’t mind how you look,” Montalbo said. “Because to them, what’s important is how you treat them.”

News.title: Verstappen back to his best as Singapore GP pole follows sprint win
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the sprint race for the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix from the Marina Bay Circuit. Given the way the championship standings are, it looks like Kimi Antonelli has one hand on the drivers’ title. That means that the most significant thing is the battle for individual race victories. That includes grands prix, but also sprint races, like we have today.

Formula One is very keen on sprint races, increasing their number significantly next year, but we have never had one in Singapore before. We will find out today whether there was good reason for it. I suppose the logic is that even a processional sprint race is better than a free practice session and that having two qualifying sessions on a street circuit such as this is exciting, too.

Still, although he might be strolling towards the championship, he and Mercedes are not the dominant force they were at the start of the season when he won five in a row having finished second in the opening race. In fact, in the last 10 grands prix, Antonelli has won three and Russell two. With Max Verstappen’s win in Malaysia last weekend it meant each of Red Bull, McLaren, Ferrari and Mercedes have won races this season.

It is Verstappen who is in strong form in an upgraded Red Bull, as he snuck pole position from George Russell by just over a tenth of a second. He was followed by Charles Leclerc in the Ferrari and then Oscar Piastri in the McLaren. Antonelli, in the upgraded Mercedes, found things more difficult, finishing down in seventh nearly 0.7sec off the pace.

Anyway, the sprint gets under way in about 30 minutes and we will be here for all the updates from that, as well as qualifying later today.

News.title: Majestic All Blacks copy Springbok playbook to dismantle Australia
News.content:
Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Bledisloe Cup Test as New Zealand host Australia at Eden Park in Auckland.

The All Blacks are enduring one of the toughest periods in their history, having suffered three successive Test defeats against South Africa in August and September, which saw the Springboks claim the inaugural Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series tour. Dave Rennie’s men are under immense pressure to avoid a fourth consecutive Test defeat for the first time since 1998.

You could argue there’s never been a better opportunity for Australia to beat New Zealand at Eden Park. The Wallabies are enjoying a six-Test unbeaten run – their longest such streak since 2017, with five games in this rejuvenated period coming under new head coach Les Kiss. In their most recent outing, Australia secured an extraordinary 42-38 victory over a much-changed South Africa side in Perth, despite being reduced to 11 players at one point.

Australia will feel further encouraged due to several key absences for New Zealand, as Ardie Savea, Ruben Love, Richie Mo’unga, Caleb Clarke, Fehi Fineanganofo, Billy Proctor and Anton Lienert-Brown are all out injured. In a reshuffle for the All Blacks, Damian McKenzie will begin at fly-half for the first time in 2026. Other notable inclusions for the home side see all three Barrett brothers, Codie Taylor, Tupou Vaa’i, Cam Roigard and Will Jordan starting.

Meanwhile, the visitors are without the suspended Hunter Paisami, with Isaac Henry taking his place at centre. The likes of Ryan Lonergan, Len Ikitau, Harry Wilson, Ben Donaldson and Max Jorgensen, who were all key to the triumph against the Springboks, retain their starting spots.

All the statistics overwhelmingly favour New Zealand. The All Blacks have not lost any edition of the Bledisloe Cup since 2002, winning 51 series to Australia’s 12, and are unbeaten at Eden Park since 1994, when they lost to France. Australia are winless at Eden Park since 1986, tasting defeat there 30 times in 34 games, and have lost their last 11 Tests against New Zealand.

However, given the landscape heading into this historic rivalry between these two heavyweights, it genuinely feels like anything could happen.

Kick-off is at 7:10am.

News.title: Black British Business Awards 2026 winners revealed
News.content:
The chief executive of Dr. Martens has been named the Black British Business Person of the Year at the 2026 Black British Business Awards (BBBAwards).

Ije Nwokorie, who became chief of Dr. Martens in January last year and is the only black chief executive in the FTSE 250, was awarded in recognition of his role shaping Dr. Martens’ growth strategy.

He is recognised inside Dr. Martens for his strong communication with staff, according to the judges.

Before joining Dr. Martens, Mr Nwokorie spent more than 11 years at Wolff Olins, the marketing giant, before working as a senior director at Apple.

Born in the US but brought up from age six against the backdrop of post-civil-war Nigeria, Mr Nwokorie has described how he and his family went from the lifestyle trappings of 1960s America to a small Nigerian village and a home with no running water.

On winning the award, Mr Nwokorie said: “This recognition means a lot to me. While this award bears my name, it reflects the talent, dedication and generosity of the incredible teammates, mentors and leaders who have shaped me as a person and a professional.

“It is a powerful reminder that there is nothing more important in our leadership journeys than the time we invest to help others thrive.”

Alongside his executive career, he has served as a trustee at Charity: water for nearly a decade and held board roles at cultural and humanitarian organisations including the Institute of International Visual Arts and Malaria No More UK.

He also served as chairman of trustees for the Chineke! Orchestra, a British orchestra championing change and the first in Europe to feature a majority of black and ethnically diverse musicians.

The Black British Business Awards started in 2014 to celebrate the achievements of black people in British business. The Telegraph is the national media partner for the awards.

Mr Nwokorie was presented with the award at an exclusive ceremony sponsored by JPMorgan Chase at London’s Hilton Park Lane hotel.

Speaking at the ceremony, Sophie Chandauka, the executive founder of the awards, said: “You lend the BBBAwards credibility not simply to celebrate excellence, but to ensure the best and brightest from all communities get a fair shot. That commitment has made the BBBAwards the UK’s premium awards programme for black business achievement.”

A spokesman for JPMorgan Chase said: “We couldn’t be prouder to support and celebrate such an outstanding breadth of black British talent.

“Their accomplishments continue to inspire future generations and demonstrate the exceptional value they bring to businesses, communities and the wider UK economy.”
