News.title: Lionesses take step closer to World Cup but do not look like they can win it
News.content:
England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

The best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

“I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman said. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

“We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

News.title: What is the XFG Covid strain? Symptoms and what to know as the variant hits the UK
News.content:
Cases of Covid-19 have risen sharply across the UK this month, driven largely by a variant of the virus known as ‘XFG’.

Sometimes referred to as ‘Stratus’ and the ‘American strain’, owing to the fact that it is now the most common strain in North America, it was first identified in January 2025 and has since spread worldwide.

Between August and September, Covid cases in Britain jumped 230 per cent, from 1,374 to 4,589 new infections, half of which were caused by the XFG strain.

Hospitalisation rates have also increased by 15 per cent in the same period, according to the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA).

The true number of cases is likely to be much higher, as most people who contract Covid-19 experience a milder illness and will not visit hospital or receive an official diagnosis via their GP.

What are the symptoms, and how is it different from other variants?

Symptoms of XFG are similar to other variants of Covid-19 like Delta and Omicron, and typically begin with a sore throat, before developing into a cough and fever.

However, experts have noted that patients diagnosed with XFG tend to present with a characteristic hoarse, croaky voice, which is distinctive from older strains.

More than 30 other symptoms have been known to be associated with XFG and other Covid strains, including diarrhoea, vomiting, loss of taste and smell, shortness of breath, headache, and muscle aches.

Why are cases rising?

Current data does not suggest that XFG leads to more severe illness than any other variant in circulation, according to the UKHSA.

As the UK moves into winter, colder and wetter weather naturally influences the rise in respiratory illnesses like Covid-19 and the flu, given people spend more time indoors and in closer proximity to each other, where viruses can more easily transmit between them.

It has also been roughly a year since the last significant wave of Covid-19 cases, meaning that the population-wide immunity has somewhat waned, making people more susceptible to the disease, the UKHSA said.

Can you be vaccinated against XFG?

The current Covid-19 vaccine is designed to protect against XFG and related strains specifically, after modelling suggested it would become the dominant variant this season.

Those eligible for a Covid-19 autumn booster include adults over the age of 75, residents in care homes, and anyone over six months old with a weakened immune system, due to a health condition or treatment.

Covid vaccines are also available to buy privately for those who are not eligible for a free jab, and typically cost around £98 per dose.

What should you do if you suspect you have XFG?

The NHS no longer advises that people with symptoms of Covid-19 take a test, unless they want to do so.

If you feel unwell or have a high temperature, health authorities advise you to try and stay home and avoid contact with people until you feel better.

They also recommend avoiding contact with vulnerable people, like those undergoing chemotherapy or the elderly, for at least 10 days.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: Harry’s Invictus Games challenge in Kenya is helping veterans battle physical and mental scars
News.content:
Wounded veterans from 10 countries have gathered in Kenya’s Great Rift Valley for a week of endurance challenges, organised by the charity behind Prince Harry’s Invictus Games.

Twenty-five serving and former personnel, among them a Ukrainian who survived a direct bomb hit in Donetsk and a Danish combat engineer who cleared roadside bombs in Afghanistan, will run, hike or cycle up to 120km across the area on Saturday October 10, World Mental Health Day.

The Invictus Games Foundation, the charity the Duke of Sussex founded in 2014 for wounded, injured and sick service personnel, has organised the event.

For Vasyl, a Ukrainian soldier, it will be his first time in Africa and his first long-distance challenge.

After three weeks of military training in the UK, the 34-year-old joined a brigade in Donetsk as a reconnaissance squad commander, spending more than 19 months on the front line. He was wounded when a drone dropped a grenade three metres from him, and the shrapnel still causes frequent pain in his leg which can sometimes make walking difficult.

But he said the physical injury was easier to bear than the loss of the friends he made in the trenches.

“There is a level of kindness between comrades in a trench that you will never find in civilian life,” he said. “If someone made a mistake or said something wrong, we immediately forgave them and thought nothing more of it.

“For me, the pain of loss is the hardest thing the war has left behind.”

News.title: From Yale to the Congo: The mathematician who became one of Africa’s most intrepid reporters
News.content:
Sundaram has a lot of experience with the Rwandan methods of control. After spending 17 months in DRC, he moved to Kigali and he is eloquent about the convoluted effects of dictatorship. “Living in Rwanda taught me so much about how dictatorships function internally and how counter-intuitive they can be. A friend of mine who was working in public health told me ‘When we ask people in India to wash their hands we get a 30 per cent success rate from a campaign, but when we need people in Rwanda to wash their hands, we just need to slip a line in one of Kagame’s speeches and we get a 90 per cent success rate. That’s fantastic isn’t it?’

“And I said, ‘well is it? It’s great for short term health outcomes but what does that say about society? Isn’t democracy about people choosing freely? What if the government tells them to do something bad – like what happened in the genocide when people were told to kill all the Tutsis?’

“Kagame and his army stopped the genocide, and he has restored peace, but he governs using the same system that was used to perpetrate the genocide.”

In Bad News: Last Journalists in a Dictatorship, the book Sundaram went on to write about his time in Rwanda teaching journalists, he describes a more extreme version of this phenomenon, recalling how Kagame once commented that thatched roofs on huts were primitive. “And the local authorities took that as a sign that he didn’t like thatched roofs, and that they should get rid of them. And without replacements being built, people climbed up and dismantled their own thatched roofs. And I saw these villages with houses which just had mud walls without roofs, and the families were sitting outside with their children and their goats, the thatch strewn on the ground. In the rain, quite often. The children would get sick, and it was like a war zone.

“At the end of my time in Congo, I was at a UN base and they were digging latrines, when they found some human bones. They stopped digging and alerted the press, and I happened to be in Goma nearby.” He subsequently found out that it was one of a series of mass graves containing the bodies of Congolese killed by forces controlled by Kagame. “And so when I arrived I had a sense of what Rwanda had done in Congo, but I didn’t fully appreciate the extent to which it was totalitarian. I’d heard that the country was a shining example of progress – aid programs were successful, and poverty reduction programs. The streets were clean, public services functioned. I was living in a nice house with a big garden provided by the journalism programme I was working in.”

Many European governments, including Britain, are enamoured with Rwanda, because, says Sundaram, “dictatorships can be very efficient”. But it is a “mirage of a country”, he says.

The teaching programme he was running was briefed not to challenge the government on any level, and an embassy official told him that if any of the journalists mentioned repression they would be expelled.

“Layer by layer, as I began to talk to the journalists I was training, the true story unravelled. The first instance was when one of them left the programme, and I heard him on the radio one day praising the president, but with a degree of flattery that was completely exaggerated, and I didn’t understand why. The rest of the class were reluctant to talk about it but eventually I learned that another student had been beaten to a coma on the day he criticised the president.

“I started to realise that my class contained some of the most courageous journalists in the country.” As a foreigner, if he transgressed, Sundaram could have his visa cancelled or get kicked out, or even locked up for a couple of days, but for the Rwandan journalists, everything was at stake. They could be killed or their families threatened.

“But still they persisted, and they took me around the country and showed me all the things the government didn’t want anyone to see – things they couldn’t report on because it was too dangerous, so they wanted to show me because they wanted somebody to speak up. It’s really a book about them – they’ve been my greatest teachers in journalism.”

News.title: I tried Amazon’s new iPad rival – and there’s one standout feature
News.content:
Amazon says that this tablet has three times the computing power and nine times the graphics power of any previous Amazon tablet, so this is a significant boost in performance to previous models.

That will make light tasks, such as crunching through emails, browser-based activity like online shopping and document work. With a keyboard factored in, it could work as a laptop alternative for some. The same could be said of the iPad Air, although with recent price increases from Apple and the matte screen, for my money, this is a better proposition.

The premium makeover that comes with the Alexa Tablet Pro includes a slim aluminium design, with flattened edges, so it looks like an iPad or Samsung tablet, only 6.5mm thick. The Pro version only comes in the Graphite colour seen here. All models in the new line-up feel more grown-up and less like kid’s tablets than the Fire range. Plus the switch to proper Android over Fire OS is welcome and will result in better app compatibility (although I noticed that these tablets were running Android 16, which is now an old version).

It has a battery that’s good for 16 hours of video playback and supports 27W charging. There are cameras front and rear although like any tablet, these won’t be as good as your phone, while there’s support for Dolby Atmos from the speakers, so your movies will sound decent.

The AI capabilities are a step up

As the name suggests, Amazon is keen to promote the AI element here. It has customised the interface slightly with access to Alexa+ meaning you can utilise Amazon’s AI at any time to ask about what’s on the screen, to control smart home devices or search for content. If you are a keen Alexa user, then that will be a plus, but for me it’s not the headline news.

Sports.title: Our 20mph road has become a RAT RUN for Premier League stars – we’ve had two wrecks in weeks & players block our parking
Sports.content:
STRIPES BACK Our 20mph road has become a RAT RUN for Premier League stars – we’ve had two wrecks in weeks & players block our parking







Next

FURIOUS residents have called foul on Premier League footballers for using their quaint village road as a “rat run”.

After two crashes in a matter of weeks, residents who have Hull City‘s training ground at the bottom of their 20mph road in Cottingham, East Riding of Yorkshire, have had enough.



Wreckage is still visible from the back-to-back prangs on Millhouse Woods Lane – the first involving Hull midfielder Sorba Thomas on September 11.

His £60k Land Rover overturned onto its roof in the crash after clipping a black Renegade Jeep and writing off a £13,000 Mini Countryman.



And the second crash saw French summer arrival Lucas Gourna-Douath have a near identical accident in the exact same spot three weeks later.

He rolled his black Mercedes car onto its side, completely blocking the road and damaging a parked car.



When The Sun visited this week following the crashes, we found fed up residents who complained their narrow road was being used as a “rat run” by stars of the newly promoted side.

Resident of 15 years and Hull supporter Liz Green, 50, said: “It is not great. I have lived on this street for a long time and it has always been an issue.

“It is a big problem when they train every day.

“I think they are just a bit reckless and the new signings don’t realise this is probably the narrowest street in Cottingham.

One neighbour, who asked not to be named, said: “I was first on the scene with both crashes. I was just having a coffee with the first one.



“I heard a huge crash. I came out on the pavement and the car was on its roof.

“The second one happened when I came off night shift. I was having a coffee when I heard a huge bang. I came out and saw Lucas peering through the window.

“They are trying to organise a residents meeting with police and national highways to stop it happening again.



“I hope Hull FC would come. It is hard to know what happened. No one has any camera footage.”

Kay Stevenson, who has lived in a cul-de-sac for 20 years opposite the training ground, said: “The first one was bad enough but then to get a second one.

“The club should have a word with them. They do have bigger cars when they are in the Premier League.

“People living in my cul-de-sac sometimes cannot get out of the road because of players parking opposite.

“Women have been hammering on the door of the club to get them to come out and move them.”



Bob Folckton, 70, said that locals are looking for answers as “no one has come clean” about what happened.

“One assumes after twice in a matter of weeks they have encouraged them to drive more slowly,” he said.

Mike Russell, 79, believes the club should be “safeguarding its players”.



The 79-year-old said: “The road has been here a long time. It has not happened very often.

“The drivers who have been coming down are relatively new to the area and Hull FC.

“Perhaps there should be some guidance from Hull City to keep their foot off the accelerator.”

“The younger players get a hell of a lot of money, and have some very nice cars. Perhaps they need to know how to drive them a bit better.”

Linda Russell, 71, added : “Everyone has said around here it has never happened before. I don’t know how you can possibly go fast down this road. It is so narrow.”



A woman whose Mini Countryman was written off in the first crash spoke of her fury.

The woman, who did not wish to be named, said: “My car was parked outside my house. I was at work.

“I had a call from a neighbour to say my car had been damaged. I spent a whole morning on the phone trying to sort it out with my insurers.”

Meanwhile, local councillor Phil Redshaw is calling for an urgent review of road safety.

“Both incidents occurred at the same location on this narrow lane,” he said in a letter to East Riding Council.



“I therefore request that the traffic management team undertake an urgent safety review of this section of Millhouse Woods Lane, seek to identify the likely cause and ask what immediate measures can be implemented to reduce the risk of a further incident.

“On both occasions, the incidents occurred at times when the lane is used by pedestrians.

“On this morning’s occasion, parents and children were using the footpath just five minutes earlier on their way to school.”

A spokesperson for East Riding Council said: “We are aware of the recent road traffic incidents on Millhouse Woods Lane, Cottingham, and understand the concerns these have generated locally.

“Millhouse Woods Lane is a relatively narrow rural road, but it is of sufficient width to accommodate traffic safely when vehicles are driven in a manner appropriate to the road conditions and environment.



“As with all roads, motorists are expected to travel at a speed suitable for the conditions and position their vehicles appropriately.

“We are not currently aware of any highway maintenance defects or road condition issues at this location that would prevent road users from travelling along the route safely when exercising due care and attention.

“The council will continue to monitor the location and will consider any information provided by the police or other relevant parties as part of its ongoing review of the highway network.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Sun approached Hull City for comment.

In a previous statement issued after the second crash, the club said: “Hull City is aware of images circulating on social media following a road traffic accident near the club’s training ground and can confirm that no one was harmed in the incident.”

Sports.title: LaLiga clash ABANDONED after hundreds of fans hurl paper aeroplanes in protest at their own owner
Sports.content:
Next

A LALIGA clash between Rayo Vallecano and Athletic Bilbao was abandoned after fans threw paper aeroplanes on the pitch in protest at their owner.

Rayo were hosting domestic rivals Bilbao on Saturday in their first match since the international break.



But the game was halted in the 13th minute – with the score at 0-0 – after crazy scenes saw fans hurling objects onto the pitch.

The referee had to suspend the match as paper planes became littered around the grass.



The game was paused for a total of ten minutes as official attempted to clear the projectiles from the playing surface.

An in-game announcement warned supporters that the game would be called off if the interruptions continued.

Rayo stars Oscar Valentín and Isi Palazon even spoke to the club’s ultras in a bid to get them to stop.

Play eventually resumed before more planes were thrown onto the turf and the match was stopped again at 25 minutes.

Players looked bewildered as they walked off the pitch and the referee then decided to abandon the game after speaking to police and both teams.

The stadium quickly emptied as Rayo posted on X to confirm the game had been called off.



The club wrote: “The match is definitely suspended by the referee’s decision at the police’s recommendation.”

Athletic Bilbao added in their own post: “The match has been abandoned following further incidents of objects being thrown onto the pitch.”

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Fans had been protesting against owner and president Raul Martin Presa and his running of the club.

It comes amid an uncertain start to the season for Rayo, who were forced to play their first three home games in Leganes due to safety concerns at their Vallecas Stadium.



La Liga released a statement condemning the ugly scenes and said a rescheduled date would be confirmed later on.

It said: “La Liga strongly condemns this behaviour, which endangers safety and obstructs the normal running of the competition.

“The new date for the match will be announced soon.”

Rayo are 13th in LaLiga on eight points after five games, while Bilbao are on the same points tally in tenth place.

Sports.title: Arsenal player ratings: Bruno stakes case to Arteta with vital impact off bench but Havertz off pace after shock start
Sports.content:
Next

ARSENAL pulled off a second-half comeback to see off Leeds United and pile the pressure on Manchester City at the top of the table.

The Gunners were desperate for a response after losing 3-0 to Brighton last time out and had to work hard to earn it.



James Justin‘s 55th-minute goal caused panic at the Emirates, but Mikel Arteta‘s side showed fight to turn things around.

Riccardo Calafiori turned in an equaliser when he got on the end of a Ben White header.



And Bruno Guimaraes came off the bench to net the winner with a delightful strike from outside the box.

Here’s how SunSport Arsenal Reporter Joshua Hall rated each individual Arsenal performance…



DAVID RAYA – 8

David Seaman was in the crowd at the Emirates and would have been proud of some of the saves Raya made.

He did incredibly well not to run over the line with the ball in his hand when he plucked Ethan Ampadu‘s header out of the air.

And pulled off a stunning stop from point blank range to deny Gabriel Gudmundsson just before half time.

His impact can sometimes go under the radar but this was another top showing.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

BEN WHITE – 7

Put in a solid performance on his return from injury, but still feels like he is just a level below Jurrien Timber.

That said, his header to find Noni Madueke for the equaliser was quick thinking and an important moment in the game.

EZRI KONSA – 7

A surprise inclusion, given he pulled out of England’s camp with an injury earlier this week.

Konsa looked impressive when he was tidying up attempted balls in behind from Leeds and has been filling in for William Saliba brilliantly.



GABRIEL MAGALHAES – 6

Knew he was in for a battle with Leeds’ physical side, but dealt with it well.

It wasn’t a standout performance from the Brazilian, but it was assured enough to keep Arsenal secure in the late stages.

RICCARDO CALAFIORI – 7

His overlapping runs were slightly less effective given Noni Madueke’s lack of threat when cutting in on his weaker foot.



But he was still popping up in dangerous areas when he could, which paid off when he found himself inside the box to knock home the equaliser.

Calafiori has been one of the most exciting players in the league this season.

DECLAN RICE – 7

Back in action after missing England’s international fixtures due to load management.

At times he took it upon himself to try and drive forward with the ball at his feet.

It was his clever flick that teed up Bruno Guimaraes for Arsenal’s second.



MYLES LEWIS-SKELLY – 7

Just a few months ago Lewis-Skelly was an out-of-favour left-back, now he is starting in midfield for England and Arsenal.

This was another assured performance that saw him draw countless fouls from the Leeds players and help Arsenal transition from defence to attack effectively.

MARTIN ODEGAARD – 7

The Arsenal captain has been in electric form since the start of the season and continued it with Norway during the break.

This performance didn’t quite follow the same pattern, but he still kept Arsenal ticking on the ball.



BUKAYO SAKA – 6

Struggled to beat his man down the right side for large parts of the game.

Saka still seems to be lacking that electric burst of pace he had a few seasons ago, which is hurting his threat when he has the ball at his feet.

NONI MADUEKE – 7

Starting on the left wing in place of the injured Christos Tzolis.

Arteta opted for Madeueke over Ebere Eze, who has failed to impress when played out wide since joining Arsenal last summer.



A surprisingly positive first half saw him find Havertz with two dangerous crosses.

But he was caught sleeping and allowed James Justin to drift off him to score Leeds’ opening goal.

The England an made up for it by playing a cross into the box a few moments later to tee up Arsenal’s equaliser.

An up and down performance that ultimately showed he can contribute in Tzolis’ absence.



KAI HAVERTZ – 6

Arteta’s thoughts on Viktor Gyokeres were made very clear when he chose to start a half-fit Havertz over the Swede.

Had to do better than his tame header into the chest of James Trafford in the first half.

A disappointing showing from the German.

SUBSTITUTES

Drove forward well and was looking to cause problems.



A positive cameo after being left out from the start despite his form for Sweden in the international break.

As soon as he came on, Bruno was looking to be involved in the game and make a difference.

Sports.title: Authorities reveal huge Rui Pinto update after Man City whistleblower went into hiding over threats to his life
Sports.content:
Next

PORTUGAL’S Ministry of Justice has confirmed that it has REVERSED its decision to move Man City whistleblower Rui Pinto out of witness protection.

Pinto, 37, rocked the football world by founding Football Leaks in 2018.



After showing confidential documents from major football clubs to German magazine Der Spiegel, he gained international attention and was extradited from Hungary in 2019.

He was then introduced to Portugal’s witness protection programme in 2020 and agreed to co-operate with authorities by providing information he had come across through computer hacking.



As part of that, he has provided essential, confidential documents – including emails and financial records – relating to Manchester City.

Just days after the Premier League released the independent commission’s guilty verdict for City, Pinto publicly explained that he was planning to leave Portugal after being told his participation in the country’s witness protection programme had been terminated.



This is despite the fact he received “multiple death threats” and faced “the serious risk of an assassination attempt” against him.

On X, he wrote: “I have no alternative but to relocate, within the next few days, to an undisclosed location for an indefinite period of time.”

However, given that the case is going through an appeal and it is not closed, the Ministry has changed its mind.

A statement from the Ministry read: “The protection program remains in effect until a new decision is adopted by the Special Security Programs Commission.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“The Minister of Justice met yesterday, October 8th, with the Special Security Programs Commission (CPES), within the scope of monitoring the situation regarding the special security program of Rui Pedro Gonçalves Pinto.

“The CPES verified that the beneficiary was not duly notified of the grounds for the decision to close the program, nor was he assured of the information and the possibility of exercising the right to a hearing, as provided for in the Witness Protection Law (Law No. 93/99, of July 14).

“For this reason, the Commission declared the decision of September 22, 2026, null and void, as well as the subsequent procedure and the notification made on September 30, 2026.

“Consequently, the special security program remains in effect until a new decision is made by the Special Security Programs Commission.

“The Commission also decided to proceed with a new notification to the beneficiary, providing them with the risk reassessment report and the relevant elements of the minutes of its meetings, granting them a period of ten working days to comment on the meaning and grounds of the projected decision.



“Only after this procedure has been completed and the beneficiary’s statement, if submitted, has been assessed will the CPES make a new decision on maintaining or terminating the special security program.”

Sports.title: Arsenal 2 Leeds 1: Super-sub Guimaraes screamer snatches comeback win as Gunners survive scare to go level with Man City
Sports.content:
Next

BRUNO GUIMARAES became the new darling of Arsenal’s North Bank and saved his team as time ran out.

The Brazilian scored his first home goal and was mobbed by the fans who felt the relief as much as any player as the Premier League champions turned things around on a day their famous team spirit went missing.



Guimaraes, boss Mikel Arteta’s marquee summer signing at £75 million, came off the bench and grabbed the winner with just 20 minutes left.

It capped a second half turnaround for Arteta’s team who were way below par in the first 45 minutes and found themselves a goal down and staring at an embarrassing defeat.



Not ideal just a few days after the boss signs a brand new four year contract and wants to see a response from his team after nailing his colours to the mast.

From weak and wobbly in the first half, on a day when who was playing and who was not played a big part in proceedings, Arteta was forced to admit defeat with his tactics and change things around as a key game was drifting away from his side.

After failing to raise a sweat, Arsenal at last found their character and went on to draw level then win to go level with table toppers Manchester City, who play tomorrow.

Arsenal’s legendary keeper David Seaman turned up on the pitch before kick off wearing a half and half scarf.

And that kind of summed up the first 45 minutes. A bit of this and a bit of that. Wishy washy.

To be fair, Seaman grew up as a Leeds fan and started his illustrious career there, so is perhaps the only exception to the rule that trying to support everybody in football should be banned.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Even Leeds in their blue and yellow away kit bore a resemblance to their traditional old change strip, blurring the lines even more between the two sides.

The distinction came in the approach to the game though.

Leeds, resolute at the back, strong and organised and trying to pickpocket Arsenal with the odd charge forwards.

The Gunners, mainly in control but running out of steam at the very pinch point of the team up front.



Havertz barely tested James Trafford in the visitors’ goal with a couple of first half headers.

The German, who never really fitted as an out and out striker during his Chelsea days, only just passed fit after getting injured on duty with Germany and it showed.

It took until the 51st minute for Arsenal to register their first proper shot with captain Martin Odegaard driving low from a Noni Madueke centre.

Trafford simply dropped to the deck and gathered the ball.



In reply, Arsenal keeper David Raya threw his body at a ferocious Gabriel Gudmundsson shot from point blank range a minute before the break.

He was almost caught out when he advanced far off his line to punch clear a cross and then had to scamper back.

But the shot-stopper was able to claim a looping header from Ethan Ampadu off his line.

Naturally, for the most one-eyed fan base outside of Cyclops United, it was everybody’s fault bar boss Mikel Arteta and the Arsenal players that things weren’t going to plan.



Ref Paul Tierney was hounded over every decision, even when playing advantage, and when the official’s assistant caught Arsenal offside five times in the first half, the cries of injustice went up from the stands.

Arteta knew inwardly he had got it wrong though with his selection – starting a half fit Havertz in front of frustrated Viktor Gyokeres, an undiluted centre forward raring to go but with only 29 minutes of Premier League football under his belt this season so far.

The Swede was warming up on the touchline alongside midfielder Bruno Guimaraes when Leeds went ahead.

A charge down the left by Gudmundsson led to a low cross that Raya dived onto the turf and pushed clear but only to James Justin lurking unmarked on the right hand edge of the box.



He smashed the ball first time, taking aim for the roof of the net and the full force of the shot meant defender Gabriel’s gutsy attempt to head it back off the line only diverted it into the top corner.

Arteta was about to pull the trigger with three subs when Arsenal levelled to turn the momentum of the game their way and finally show their character as defending Premier League champions.

Madueke delivered a deep cross to the far post from his slot on the left, Ben White headed back across goal and trusty campaigner Riccardo Calafiori swept into the six-yard box to head home between two defenders.

Guimaraes and Gyokeres entered a pitch in full mood swing with Arsenal now on equal terms.

And with that the Brazilian rode the wave of positivity and got the second goal with 20 minutes to go.



Odegaard drove a ball into a channel in the Leeds area, Declan Rice produced a neat backheel into space and Guimaraes slotted the ball home.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

His celebratory run into the arms of the fans underlined the sense of relief that Arsenal had clawed themselves back into a match that looked like slipping away.

Sports.title: Tottenham team to fly to Marbella after Man Utd game as desperate Roberto de Zerbi makes rarely seen decision
Sports.content:
Next

ROBERTO DE ZERBI will fly his struggling Tottenham side out to Marbella after their trip to Manchester United to help his team bond.

Tottenham go into their clash at Old Trafford rock bottom of the Premier League after a winless start to the season.



Spurs have two draws and three defeats despite splashing out more than £300million on new signings.

De Zerbi’s men are also having trouble in the final third after netting just twice so far.



And the Italian has reportedly booked an unusual mid-season trip to Marbella in a bid to get his team clicking.

Most teams wait until December or January before jetting off on such a trip when winter kicks in.

But according to the BBC, De Zerbi is hoping the break will give his players a chance to gel.

And Spurs will have more time to prepare as they have nine days between the United clash and their next game against Coventry on October 19.

Players will also get a bit of sunshine, with temperatures of 25 degrees Celsius expected in Spain, compared to a forecast of drizzle in Enfield.

De Zerbi has a number of new faces who are still adapting to their surroundings.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

That includes new signings Jan-Paul van Hecke, Andy Robertson, Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Savio and Omar Marmoush.

This tactic is not unheard of from De Zerbi when the tough gets going for his teams.

In April 2025 he took his Marseille players for a break in Rome after a rough patch of form.

De Zerbi said he was not worried about Tottenham’s woes this season despite their bad start and insisted they have shown enough going forward to give him optimism.

He said: “It’s difficult. [Aston Villa defeat] was very, very tough, especially the first week. Yeah, but football is part of our real situation in this moment and we have to react, to work through this moment.



“I think we created chances enough to score many other goals in these seven games.

“I think even this improvement, I think we had the qualities to score more goals. Anyway, the most important thing is to bring the ball in the goal area.

“In the goal area we went many, many times. We are fourth in the table. So, it’s nothing, but I think we arrived there, but we are not good enough so far to score goals when we have a clear chance.”

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo accused of ‘stealing’ goal from Sadio Mane as he edges closer to 1,000 target despite Portugal fallout
Sports.content:

CRISTIANO RONALDO has been accused of “stealing” a goal from team-mate Sadio Mane as he closes in on an incredible 1,000 career goals.

The Portuguese superstar, 41, scored the 980th of his career during Al-Nassr’s 3-0 victory over Al-Diriyah in the Saudi Pro League.



But footage of the goal sparked cheeky accusations online that the five-time Ballon d’Or winner had pinched Mane’s moment.

Ronaldo was quickest to react after Kingsley Coman’s shot was parried by goalkeeper Waleed Abdullah in the 23rd minute.



The former Manchester United star made no mistake from close range before wheeling away to perform his trademark ‘Siuuu’ celebration.

The good news for Mane is that he appeared to be in an offside position, so even if he had tapped it in, it would have been ruled offside.

A football page on X, The Final Whistle, wrote: “Cristiano Ronaldo steals the shot from Sadio Mane and scores his 980th career goal! Al Nassr are leading against Al Diriyah.”

Fans replied to the post, with one saying: “Steals or scores? We see you Messi minion.”



Another added: “You gotta do what ya gotta do.”

A third wrote: “Not technically a steal if Mane was already offside.”

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Following the tap in – Ronaldo now needs just 20 more goals to reach the remarkable 1,000-goal milestone.

CR7’s latest goal came just days after his explosive fallout with Portugal manager Jorge Jesus during the international break.

The veteran was suspended after he stormed out of the national team camp when he was left on the bench during Portugal’s 2-1 Nations League victory over Norway.



He later accused Jesus of breaking promises over his playing time and admitted he could face punishment from the Portuguese Football Federation.

But Ronaldo has insisted he remains available to represent his country again as he continues his extraordinary pursuit of football’s 1,000-goal landmark.

Sports.title: Brutal Mikel Arteta decision in Leeds win sets clock ticking on Arsenal career
Sports.content:
Arsenal came from behind to beat Leeds United 2-1 and get back to winning ways at the Emirates.

James Justin deservedly put the visitors in front shortly after the break, but a Riccardo Calafiori header and a sensational Bruno Guimaraes strike earned the Gunners all three points to go level at the top of the Premier League.

The Gunners had three weeks to stew on the heavy defeat to Brighton before the international break, but hardly came flying out the traps against the determined and unbeaten visitors.

And with the Emirates crowd growing increasingly frustrated, Leeds had a golden chance to open the scoring. But after Anton Stach was picked out free at the back post, his effort was blocked by his own player Jayden Bogle.

‌



That was a theme for much of the first half, where despite dominating possession, Arsenal failed to land a glove on Daniel Farke’s charges.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

It was much of the same after the break, to such an extent that when James Justin’s opener came it was richly deserved.

‌



Arteta demanded a response from his players on the sidelines and got the perfect one after the hour mark when Riccardo Calafiori headed the Gunners level.

And with Arsenal back on the front foot, they got themselves in front with a simply sublime team goal. Bukayo Saka found Martin Odegaard, who in turn found Declan Rice. It was then Rice’s intricate flick that teed up Guimaraes to fire the Gunners ahead.

That goal appeared to break the Leeds resistance, with Arsenal able to hold on to join Manchester City on 15 points.

View 4 Images Arsenal have moved level with Man City at the top of the Premier League table

‌



IF NOT NOW, WHEN?

If Mikel Arteta was ever going to start Viktor Gyokeres, this felt like the time. During the recent international break, the Swede scored four in four matches, helping his nation to three victories and a draw.

Conversely, Kai Havertz managed 29 minutes for Germany, before suffering an injury which kept him on the sidelines for the rest of the break.

And Gyokeres also has good memories up against Leeds, after scoring three times against them last season. So it was all set up for Gyokeres to finally start in the Premier League and kick-start his second season in the top flight. Or so we thought.

View 4 Images Viktor Gyokeres was named among the Arsenal substitutes vs Leeds

‌



Instead, with Havertz deemed fit enough to start, Gyokeres had to be content with a spot on the bench yet again.

Sat on that bench he must have been looking at the pedestrian Arsenal attack in the first half and wondering just how far his stock had fallen to not get the nod.

It’s only a little over 12 months since Arteta handpicked Gyokeres as the final piece of the Gunners jigsaw. A year on and after a summer Arsenal publicly pursued his replacement, his future at the Emirates appears bleak.

Arteta finally turned to the striker after the hour mark, but it was hardly a vote of confidence for a player so desperately in need of some. And when he did finally come on, he failed to do much convincing and looked a different player to the one with such swagger that we see in a Sweden shirt.

‌



The Arsenal boss clearly doesn’t trust him to regularly spearhead the attack and unless there’s a major U-turn in the coming weeks, his days in North London look numbered.

RESULT OF CHAMPIONS

Make no bones about it, for 63 minutes of this one, Arsenal were bereft. The players were flat, the crowd were flat and for a while it had all the trademarks of a sleepy Saturday lunchtime performance.

Leeds were full of confidence and their lead was completely warranted when it came. But when Arsenal needed to punch back, they found their second wind.

To say the Man City saga has opened the door in the title race would be an understatement…it’s blown it off the hinges completely.

‌



That would have made a second successive defeat very difficult to take. Instead, Arsenal steadied themselves and earned the kind of result that could be very important in seven months’ time.

Their strength in depth is a sight to behold and they still look like they will be very difficult to stop on the pitch...if that is how the title is actually decided this season.

LOSING LEEDS STILL THE REAL DEAL?

This time last year, Farke was under huge pressure at Elland Road and looked to be nearing the exit door.

Leeds stuck with their man and how they have been rewarded. They headed to the capital unbeaten, but for an hour, this was a statement performance.

‌



View 4 Images Leeds were hugely impressive during the first hour against Arsenal

Yes, their unbeaten run is over. But it's difficult to imagine Farke being too downtrodden about what his side offered at the home of the champions.

There is quality throughout their team, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin one of the in-form strikers in the entire division as the focal point.

Leeds’ season won’t be defined by results against the likes of Arsenal on the road, but this was a display that bodes extremely well for the rest of their season.

‌

Sports.title: English football stadium that held 82,000 knocked down and rubble used to decorate London park
Sports.content:
English football stadium that held 82,000 knocked down and rubble used to decorate London park

One of England's most iconic grounds was reduced to rubble, which then helped lay the foundations for a little-known monument elsewhere in London

View 2 Images The old Wembley Stadium was demolished more than 20 years ago - but her remains were put to good use (Image: Mark Leech/Getty Images)

More than 20 years have passed since the old Wembley Stadium was knocked down to make room for a new home of English football. However, fans can still be close to the iconic ground, or at least parts of it, if they visit another London landmark.

‌



‌



The final matches were played at the old Wembley ground in 2000, some seven years before its replacement finally opened. The destroyed venue was used to host England internationals, FA Cup finals, play-off deciders, concerts and more for almost a century.

‌



That much is common knowledge to any football fan. What many might not know, though, is that the remains of the old Wembley were used to build a new site elsewhere in London.

‌



Rubble was taken from its original setting in north-west London to nearby Ealing. And there it was granted a second lease of life after being used to form four hilly mounds at Northala Fields.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Opened in 2008, one year after the new Wembley Stadium, the location is open to all members of the public. And it continues to serve the British people as a popular spot to exercise.

‌



Many locals may have even walked up the hills without even knowing they were traipsing over a piece of national history. Northala Fields also houses several fishing lakes, a cafe and a children's park to ensure those of all ages stay entertained.

The site is most typically known for the four-tiered, climbable fields dotted throughout. Each mound is made up of three distinct levels and can be summited to get a more expansive view of the surrounding areas.

View 2 Images The remains of the old Wembley Stadium were used to build three mounds at Northala Fields in Ealing (Image: Hollie Adams/Getty Images)

‌



The name of the park is purportedly inspired by the medieval spelling of Northolt, where the fields are based. This name ('Northall') was referenced in the Domesday Book in 1086 as 'Northala'.

It was more than eight centuries later that the original Wembley Stadium was eventually built in 1923. And it stood for 77 years before the decision was made to start afresh and move to England's current home, complete with its giant arch.

However, it may comfort some to know they can still, in a way, revisit that old ground today. And all that's required is a short trip down the A40 from its original site.

Sports.title: Ex-England manager Roy Hodgson back in work aged 79 just months after Bristol City exit
Sports.content:
Ex-England manager Roy Hodgson back in work aged 79 just months after Bristol City exit

Roy Hodgson has landed a new job at 79 years of age

View 2 Images Roy Hodgson is back to work (Image: Getty Images)

Roy Hodgson has clinched his first job since leaving Bristol City last season. The former England boss has enjoyed a storied 50-year managerial career across eight countries, with his last role at the Championship club.

‌



‌



The 79-year-old took over the Robins in March 2026, with the club sitting 16th in the table, but steered them to safety in the 2025/26 campaign, finishing in 12th. Hodgson left the side in May and has now secured his next role in football, having been appointed to UEFA's Technical Observer Group.

‌



The former Crystal Palace boss is joining former top-flight managers like Arne Slot, Erik ten Hag, Thomas Frank, Roberto Martinez and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer in the position.

‌



UEFA states the group will analyse the Champions League, Europa League and Conference League with "stats and video assistance, enabling them to deliver detailed reports on the latest developments in coaching, which are shared among the footballing community to give a dynamic account of the state of the game."

Regarding Hodgson's addition, the governing body wrote: "One of the most experienced Technical Observers, Hodgson has managed a total of 22 different teams in eight countries, including four national sides: Switzerland, United Arab Emirates, Finland and England. The well-travelled veteran, who speaks five languages, last season returned to Bristol City to help them avoid relegation."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Eight players set to miss Liverpool vs Man City clash as Erling Haaland update given READ MORE :

Hodgson stepped down from full-time management after his second spell in charge of Palace, but returned to the dugout on a short-term basis earlier this year. He admitted that while retirement was treating him well, the opportunity to prove whether he could still handle the pressure of management was too tempting.

He told BBC Radio Bristol: "I was relatively happily retired before this came along. It just probably showed there are opportunities sometimes that come your way that maybe seem a little bit left field and you wonder, 'Am I really capable of taking this on?' And I proved to myself I am. There's no doubt about that."

View 2 Images Roy Hodgson led Bristol City to safety last season (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

He questioned whether he'd ever want to take on another head coaching job, as he added: "Any fears I might have had that, 'Well, you're too old for this now, you can't get out on the field with the players, you can't do the coaching and manage the team in the way you always did.' No, that's not true, I can do.

"On the other hand, whether I want to put myself in this position again and offer myself up for that type of employment, that's another question altogether. Because I am the age I am and I've had the career I've had, which I'm very pleased with and very satisfied with, it's given me so much."

Sports.title: Declan Rice pinpoints exactly what sets Mikel Arteta apart from Premier League rivals
Sports.content:
Declan Rice pinpoints exactly what sets Mikel Arteta apart from Premier League rivals

Mikel Arteta has penned a new contract with Arsenal that is set to run until 2030 and one of his key stars has revealed just how he feels at the Spaniard staying with the club for his long time

View 2 Images Declan Rice is a huge fan of Mikel Arteta (Image: Getty Images)

Declan Rice believes Arsenal are "very lucky" to have tied boss Mikel Arteta down to a new deal. The Spanish coach penned a new contract earlier this week that sees him commit his future to the club until 2030.

‌



‌



Having been at the club since 2019 after replacing Unai Emery, that would take Arteta into a decade of service as manager following his prior stint as a player. And it’s fair to say that he has had a transformative impact on the club, having dragged the Gunners from mid-table mediocrity to Premier League champions.

‌



Arsenal also reached the Champions League final under Arteta's watch last term. One of the key pillars of his side has been midfielder Declan Rice.

‌



And the former West Ham star has waxed lyrical about Arteta following the news that he has officially signed a new deal. Speaking to ESPN Brazil, the midfielder said: "It's just tactically, training, managing, the detail he goes into, the things he sees that you would never see.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"He's constantly watching you when you don't think you're being watched. He's watching, constantly asking questions to try and catch you out, to see if you're listening. He's always keeping you on your toes, making sure that you're ready."

He added: "Every time we go into games, tactically we know what we're doing. Defensively, with the ball, how we're going to beat the opposition. It's just the fine details, the way he breaks everything down, which makes him the best for me.

"It's amazing that he [Arteta] signed a new contract and we get to have him as our manager for the next four years. So, we'll be very lucky."

‌



View 2 Images Mikel Arteta is now under contract with Arsenal until 2030 (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal are now in the unfamiliar position of defending their title, albeit Rice believes he and his teammates are relishing the opportunity.

He said: "It [winning the league] was an amazing achievement, but this year's a brand new season: New team, new opposition, new players. So it throws up a different challenge.

Article continues below

"So, yeah, OK, we are the champions, but we don't go on the pitch and think about last season. We're definitely playing with more confidence this season, you can feel that within the group, but it's about staying humble, and taking each game as it comes like we did last year and trying to win as many as possible."

Arsenal recommence their title defence on Saturday afternoon as they take on Leeds United at the Emirates Stadium.

Sports.title: Cole Palmer seals Chelsea future as club confirm huge update
Sports.content:
Cole Palmer seals Chelsea future as club confirm huge update

Cole Palmer has committed his long-term future to Chelsea after signing a new contract extension.

View Image Cole Palmer has signed a new contract extension at Chelsea

Cole Palmer has put pen to paper on a new deal with Chelsea with improved terms that will keep him at Stamford Bridge until the summer of 2034. The England international was already under contract until 2033 but has now extended his stay by a further 12 months.

‌



‌



The Blues have also offered Palmer improved terms, underlining his importance to the club and their plans for the future. Chelsea announced the news by sharing Palmer 'streaming' on Twitch.

‌



"Well, I just signed a new contract about 20 minutes ago, so I'm staying for eight more years," Palmer replied to a fan when asked how long he would be staying at the club.

‌



Premier League injury news: Club by Club updates and potential return dates READ MORE :

Chelsea's Cole Palmer banned from Twitch after EA FC 27 stream goes wrong READ MORE :

"So hopefully we can sing that song a little bit more that yous sing. Yeah, new contract. We've got a new contract announcement on stream.

"Eight more years, it's the song you all sing at Stamford Bridge for so long. I thought I'd share it with the chat, why not? That's me guys.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



"I'm really happy to sign a new contract and share with you guys and I look forward to eight more years. In a bit."

Speaking separately to Chelsea's official website, Palmer added: "Chelsea means a lot to me and I think the club is going in the right direction, so I'm delighted to sign and I’m obviously very happy.

"Speaking to the owners, to the sporting directors and obviously the manager, they gave me a lot of confidence so it was only right to sign. Speaking to players as well, everyone has the same ambitions.

‌



"I feel like we win major trophies here consistently and I want to be a part of that and play a big role in it too."

Chelsea then followed up the announcement with an official statement that read: "Chelsea Football Club is delighted to announce that Cole Palmer has signed a new contract until 2034. Since joining the Blues in August 2023, Palmer has established himself as one of the world’s finest attacking players.

"He has provided 91 goal contributions in 138 appearances, won the FIFA Club World Cup and UEFA Conference League, while claiming an array of individual awards. The 24-year-old has also made history on the international stage, becoming only the second England player to score in a European Championship final when he netted against Spain at Euro 2024.

‌



FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"And on the biggest stages, Palmer made his mark. He claimed two assists in our UEFA Conference League win over Real Betis, and later in the summer of 2025, scored twice and assisted Joao Pedro in our FIFA Club World Cup final win over Paris Saint-Germain. Last term, there were 14 further goal involvements, including a strike against Bayern Munich in the UEFA Champions League and yet another hat-trick, this time away to Wolves."

Palmer is the latest Chelsea star to commit his future to the club, joining Reece James, Moises Caicedo, Joao Pedro and Pedro Neto in signing new deals at Stamford Bridge.

Article continues below

Unfortunately, fans will have to wait a little longer to sing Palmer's chant, with the playmaker set to miss Chelsea's Premier League clash with Bournemouth this afternoon (Saturday) due to an ongoing groin injury.

Sports.title: Man City players 'ask about relegation clauses' as £400k bonuses risk being missed
Sports.content:
Man City players 'ask about relegation clauses' as £400k bonuses risk being missed

Manchester City will be forced to make massive changes if they are booted out of the Premier League

View 3 Images Manchester City players are said to be concerned about the ramifications of the guilty verdict (Image: Getty Images)

Worried Manchester City stars have reportedly queried if they can get out of their contracts if the club is kicked out of the Premier League. The eight-time Premier League champions are reeling after being found guilty of breaching 114 Premier League rules.

‌



‌



City, who maintain their innocence, have appealed against the verdict by an independent commission. If the commission's decision is upheld, potential punishments include being stripped of titles, a points deduction and expulsion from the Premier League.

‌



The latter would be a disastrous prospect for everyone associated with the club and would cast doubt on the future of their expensively assembled squad, as it would be unthinkable to see the likes of Erling Haaland playing in the EFL or National League.

‌



It could also see the club's top stars take a huge financial hit, as they are reportedly in line for bonuses of up to £400,000 for winning the Champions League.

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

The Times reports that once the verdict dropped, players were asking their agents about potential punishments, the consequences of not playing in UEFA's top club competition and whether there was any way to extract themselves from their contracts in the event of relegation.

‌



Vincent Kompany makes first statement on Man City guilty verdict as Enzo Maresca convinced READ MORE :

The report adds that there are no relegation clauses in players' contracts, meaning the club would have to dramatically cut costs and be forced into a fire sale of its leading talent.

Publicly, the players have flat-batted questions about the guilty verdict. Ahead of Sunday's trip to Liverpool, where City can expect a hostile reception from The Kop, manager Enzo Maresca insisted he had 100 per cent trust in the club and expects the appeal to be successful.

View 3 Images A cloud has been cast over City's success (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The Italian, who replaced Pep Guardiola in the summer, said: "The reason why I joined this club is because I completely trust, 100 per cent, the owner, the CEO, the sporting director, the whole organisation. I don't have any doubt about that.

"There is not another club in the world where I would like to be. I am very happy to be here, I am very proud, as I’ve said since day one.

"I would like to speak about this situation when we are going to win the appeal. I completely trust the club in this moment, in the future, always."

‌



View 3 Images Enzo Maresca has defended the club (Image: Manchester City FC via Getty Images)

Guardiola, who often struck a similarly defiant tone in relation to the charges, once said he would stay at the club and manage in League One if they were relegated. Asked if he would do the same, Maresca said: "I won the Championship with Leicester. So in case [of] League One, we are going to see, but we are thinking about something that we don’t know.

"What happens if we win the appeal? I don't know. We are predicting the future. I'm worried about tomorrow, in two days, three days. I don't know what is happening in the future.

Article continues below

"It is fair, from my point of view, from all of us, to respect the process. There is an appeal ongoing. We will see what happens."

Sports.title: Arsenal come from behind to beat stubborn Leeds
Sports.content:
Arsenal scored two goals in eight minutes to come from behind and get back to winning ways via a 2-1 comeback win over Daniel Farke's stubborn Leeds.

After their 3-0 loss to Brighton before the international break, a blip threatened to become a bigger issue as Leeds not only were the better team for the best part of an hour at the Emirates - but they took the lead through James Justin's strike 10 minutes after half-time.

It was the least Leeds deserved. David Raya made four saves to deny the Whites before the opener - and with Farke's side holding the joint-best defensive record coming into the game, Arsenal were in trouble.

But they were given a lifeline by Leeds goalkeeper James Trafford. The England international, given a chance by Thomas Tuchel during the latest England camp, failed to keep out Riccardo Calafiori's effort from inside the box seven minutes after Leeds' opener.

Image: Riccardo Calafiori wheels away after levelling for Arsenal

Mikel Arteta, perhaps unimpressed by his side's performance so far, was unmoved on the touchline - and backed up the leveller with a triple substitution he was planning to make anyway. One of those changes was Bruno Guimaraes, who completed the comeback five minutes later.

Arsenal wake up after Leeds goal Arsenal had five shots in the 15 minutes following Leeds’ opener, including their two goals to put them ahead. They’d only had five shots in the opening 55 minutes before Leeds scored.

Martin Odegaard's ball forward was brilliantly flicked by Declan Rice into the path of the Brazilian on the edge of the box and he crashed the ball into the bottom corner.

Eventually, it rounded off a good week for Arteta, who earlier signed a new deal until 2030.

He made the brave call to play Noni Madueke at left wing over Eberechi Eze to replace the injured Christos Tzolis - and he was Arsenal's best player and was crucial in Calafiori's equaliser. Then the Arsenal made the super sub change for Guimaraes.

Image: Arsenal's Bruno Guimaraes celebrates scoring their second goal

Arsenal move level on points with leaders Manchester City at the top of the Premier League, with Enzo Maresca's side facing Liverpool at Anfield on Super Sunday, live on Sky Sports. Leeds, meanwhile, are beaten for the first time in the Premier League this season.

More to follow...

8: CLOSE! Noah Okafor has an early sight of goal as a corner is cleared to his path but his effort is deflected just wide of the far post.

21: BIG CHANCE MISSED! Madueke does well down the left wing and hangs a cross for Havertz, whose header is straight at Trafford.

Image: Arsenal's Kai Havertz heads at goal

25: BLOCK! Anton Stach gets a free shot of goal unmarked at the far post but his effort inside the box is blocked by his own team-mate Bogle!

27: SAVE! A loose ball runs through to Jayden Bogle in the box but Raya comes out well to make the save.

34: CHANCE! Raya punches a Leeds free-kick clear and Ampadu's header nearly chips the Arsenal goalkeeper, who holds the ball on the line.

52: WIDE! Justin gets the ball on the edge of the Arsenal box and curls just wide of the far corner.

53: END TO END! Raya makes his fourth save of the game, tipping Ao Tanaka's long-range drive over the bar.

55: GOAL! Leeds make the pressure count as Gudmundsson's cross flies across goal and Justin crashes the ball into the net at the back post.

62: GOAL! Madueke's cross is put across the penalty area by Ben White, leaving Calafiori to tap home.

70: GOAL! Five minutes after coming on, Guimaraes slams Arsenal in front after being teed up by Rice's flick.

83: WHAT A CHANCE! Martin Odegaard has chance to seal the points from two yards out but Rice's cross comes off his boot and Trafford holds.

90+5: BIG MISS! Bukayo Saka breaks through on goal but puts a one-on-one wide.

Arteta: We got out of a bad mixture

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta:

"We knew it was going to be really tough, we are coming from three weeks without 16 players [because of internationals] after a heavy defeat [against Brighton] and we had all these things in the tummy.

"Today we had two objectives, one face the challenge because this is a team that hasn't lost in the Premier League and they are in a great position because they fully deserved it. And secondly because we had a point to prove something was touched in our identity against Brighton, especially in the manner that we reacted after being in a difficult situation and context.

"And today even though we started extremely well and being really dominant we didn't capitalise on the spaces, the situation, the overloads that we had to attack the goal and the box. So that left the game a little bit open and we knew that they don't need much to threaten you.

"Every time they are putting the ball in the box, they are incredibly dangerous and we got into a situation with losing 1-0, at home after a defeat, 12.30pm kick-off, it is a bad mixture. And we got out of that through pinching our desire to win, to have a reaction to show the personality and courage that we have in this team.

"And once the equaliser went in, the energy changed, the finishers came in and made a huge difference again to help us to win the game and that's what we are made of.

"And we know that it's going to be every single week the same, because every game that I have watched in those three weeks [during the international break], it's not going to be any different to that."

Sports.title: Bristol City extend Charlton's winless run to six games
Sports.content:
Bristol City goalkeeper Sam Tickle pulled off two big saves in the second half to extend Charlton's winless run in the Championship to six matches after a 1-1 draw at The Valley.

The Addicks are still unbeaten in SE7 this season but were left to rue not taking a couple of huge opportunities.

Charlton took the lead through Karlan Grant's second goal of the campaign in the eighth minute which was wiped out before the interval by Scott Twine.

Grant showed a deft touch to bring Tyreece Campbell's left-wing cross under control with his first touch before dispatching a left-footed finish past Tickle.

Referee Tom Reeves ruled that Arthur Okonkwo did not foul Yu Hirakawa as City's right winger looked to punish a weak header back by Josh Edwards. If it had been deemed a free-kick then the Wrexham loanee would have been at serious risk of a red card.

Charlton's high-tempo start faded quickly and there were warning signs of a City comeback.

Dom Ballard headed over a cross by Brian De Keersmaecker from 10 yards out before City restored parity in the 27th minute.

Conor Coventry produced a clear late tackle on Ballard inside the penalty area and Twine showed absolutely no nerves from the spot as he opted for placement - not power - to slot home his third goal of the season.

Twine went close to adding to his tally from a free-kick awarded after he was fouled by Oliver Skipp. His 30-yard effort forced Okonkwo to turn around his right post for a corner.

Twine drove wide in a packed penalty area at the start of the second half after Charlton struggled to clear a free-kick by Rio Cardines.

The Addicks switched from 4-2-3-1 to 5-3-2 soon after - introducing Kayne Ramsay and Ivan Mesik for Josh Edwards and Micah Mbick - and they finally enjoyed greater composure on the ball as they produced a spell of pressure around the hour mark.

Tickle produced a superb reaction save to parry from Campbell in the 77th minute, with the Jamaican international only able to send a second attempt over the crossbar. Tickle had spilled Miles Leaburn's low delivery from the right to present the initial chance to Charlton's top scorer but instantly redeemed himself.

Charlton had one final chance to go back ahead as the contest ticked over into added time.

Cameron Pring pulled Billy Koumetio over on the edge of the box but substitute Harvey Knibbs' full-blooded strike was tipped over by Tickle.

Sports.title: Alcaraz displays new look in win at Shanghai Masters
Sports.content:
Carlos Alcaraz's exceptional touch at the net, alongside a slick new look, was on full display during his opening victory at the Shanghai Masters on Saturday.

The world No 3, sporting a freshly trimmed moustache, delivered an aggressive performance to defeat Juan Manuel Cerundolo 6-3 6-3 and reach the third round of the ATP Masters 1000 event.

Alcaraz repeatedly surged forward with purpose during their 66-minute encounter, showcasing his deft touch to extend his winning streak to seven matches following his successful title defence in Tokyo.

"It's going to stay for the week," Alcaraz confirmed when asked about his moustache. "I always wanted to step on court at least once with a moustache.

"Before Tokyo with the team, we said, 'If I win the tournament, we all have to do the moustache and play Shanghai with it.' We're having fun with it. It came to stay."

Cerundolo, who stunned Jannik Sinner in five sets in the second round of Roland Garros this year, was seeking to become the first player to defeat both the Italian and Alcaraz in the same season since Andrey Rublev in 2024.

However, Alcaraz stuck to his attacking game plan, using Shanghai's quick court conditions to unsettle his opponent and press forward at every opportunity.

Medvedev advances at Shanghai in first match since China Open disqualification

Daniil Medvedev won his first match since being disqualified at the China Open for hitting a spectator in the eye with a ball.

Medvedev beat Jan-Lennard Struff 4-6 6-4 6-3 to reach the third round.

Medvedev, who now holds a 10-2 career edge over Struff, was disqualified from the China Open during his semi-final against Novak Djokovic.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Daniil Medvedev was defaulted against Novak Djokovic during the China Open after hitting a ball at a spectator.

Medvedev, who apologised after the incident, saying it was an accident, lost the $285,000 prize money he would have received for making the semi-finals in Beijing.

In other early second-round matches Saturday, fourth-seeded Felix Auger-Aliassime beat Camilo Ugo Carabelli 4-6 7-6 (7-1) 7-5.

Sports.title: Priske penalty earns Birmingham narrow win over WBA
Sports.content:
West Brom defender Nat Phillips was at fault for the second successive derby as Birmingham won 1-0 at The Hawthorns.

Phillips, whose back pass let in Fer Lopez in the 1-0 defeat to Wolves last time out, gave away a 41st-minute penalty scored by August Priske, who he fouled.

Albion lost their 10-match unbeaten home league run, the first since James Morrison took charge in February.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player August Prise calmly converted a penalty for Birmingham to take the lead against West Brom just before the break.

In a lively first 20 minutes, a mis-hit lobbed back pass by Phil Neumann caused panic for Birmingham.

Goalkeeper James Beadle dashed well outside his box to beat Aune Heggebo to the loose ball and clear.

At the other end, Albion goalkeeper Max O'Leary made a superb reflex save to deny Jay Stansfield's sliding shot from point-blank range.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max O'Leary added to his collection of fabulous saves as he thwarted Jay Stansfield from close range.

Albion broke at speed and Heggebo steered a shot against the foot of a post with Beadle beaten.

Jhon Solis got his footing wrong after Heggebo's poor clearing header from Alex Cochrane's cross, the Colombian midfielder shinning his effort from 12 yards.

Felix Horn Myhre should have put Albion ahead in the 28th minute, heading just over the crossbar with more than half of the goal to aim at.

Albion went close again when Callum Styles curled a low free-kick around the three-man wall and Beadle tipped the ball behind.

Blues took the lead from the spot after Phillips caught Priske in the air with a clumsy challenge from Neumann's deep cross.

Image: August Priske's penalty sealed a narrow Birmingham victory

Priske coolly side-footed the penalty high to O'Leary's left for his second Sky Bet Championship goal of the season.

Albion had O'Leary to thank for preventing a second goal with a superb reaction save to divert Neumann's fierce downward header over the bar just before half-time.

No fewer than four Albion players slid in to block Solis' shot from six yards after O'Leary got a hand to Cochrane's corner.

Blues substitute Patrick Roberts appealed for a penalty after falling following minimal contact from Chris Mepham, but the referee was unmoved.

Ousmane Diakite was not far away with a long-range angled drive as Albion tried to find an equaliser.

Cutting in from the left, centre-back Mepham was the unlikely figure dancing through Stansfield and Solis before forcing Beadle to smother.

Substitute Barney Stewart's glancing header was tipped over by the keeper from Jimmy-Jay Morgan's cross.

Stansfield curled straight at O'Leary after substitute Max Bird won the ball high up for Blues.

West Brom right-back Brayann Pereira sliced high and wide after a 40-yard run from inside his own half.

At the death, O'Leary's foot denied Birmingham substitute Demarai Gray at the near post.

Sports.title: Swansea fight back to beat Norwich and extend Championship lead
Sports.content:
Adam Idah made up for three near misses in the first half to head Championship leaders Swansea to a 2-1 home win over Norwich.

The Republic of Ireland striker came back to haunt his first club with a glancing header in the 59th minute to complete his side's comeback after falling behind to Jacob Wright's goal in the first half.

Swansea emerged from the international break with an injury to Canadian Stephen Eustaquio. He joined Josh Key on the injury list, while the Canaries were without top scorer Mohamed Toure.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Swansea draw level against Norwich after a fantastic team move is finished off by Moussa Yeo.

West Ham's draw the night before left the Swans sitting pretty at the top of the table as they sought to extend their unbeaten home run in the Championship to five. They looked a little rusty and Norwich harassed and hounded them on the ball to knock them out of shape.

It took 15 minutes before Moussa Yeo unleashed the first shot of the game from just outside the Norwich box but Vladan Kovacevic saved comfortably. Moments later Mathias Kvistgaarden had a chance at the other end after Pelle Mattsson put him in a good position to shoot.

Joseph Opoku gave top scorer Idah a great chance to add to his three goals already this season in the 22nd minute after winning the ball on halfway and driving to the Norwich box. Idah took a heavy touch from what looked to be a scoring pass and Kovacevic saved.

Norwich were quick on the counter-attack and a great cross from the left forced Stephen Welsh to head over from under the Swansea bar to concede a corner.

Image: Moussa Yeo (left) scored Swansea's first at the Swansea.com Stadium

The corner was cleared but Andre Brooks and Oscar Schwartau combined to rob Welsh of the ball and Schwartau passed across the box to enable Wright to score in the 28th minute.

Idah had two more chances to level matters before the break, but again Kovacevic was up to the mark to deny him.

It took the league leaders a mere four minutes after the restart to get back on level terms when Yeo made it three goals in as many games. Some neat interplay on the left touchline eventually freed Josh Tymon and his cross was missed at the near post by Idah before being converted at the back post by Yeo.

Swansea looked a different side in the second half and Goncalo Franco set up Idah for a shot that Kovacevic saved, then Ruairi McConville cleared off the line as Opoku fired the rebound goalwards.

The second goal came just before the hour as Idah headed home from an inch-perfect cross from Melker Widell. Moments later Idah limped off to be replaced by Zan Vipotnik.

Norwich had two good chances in the dying minutes but Lawrence Vigouroux saved Sam Field's shot and then saw Jovon Makama head over the bar from five yards out.
