Sports.title: Jack Catterall Demands His Turn Against Teofimo Lopez
Sports.content:
Jack Catterall insists his title fight with Teofimo Lopez must come next, while Teofimo’s manager Keith Connolly left the outcome open with a brief response on X: “Let’s see how it all plays out.”

The comments come as Teofimo seeks to overturn the WBA’s order to face Catterall and the October 22 negotiation deadline approaches. Catterall expects the organization to enforce the arrangement established before he fought Shakhram Giyasov.

“Was awarded a voluntary title shot coming off a loss. Im next,” Catterall wrote. “I’ve got no doubts the WBA will honour what they said and agreed before I boxed Giyasov. More waiting around but it is what it is.”

Connolly’s response stopped short of promising that Catterall would get the fight. It also offered no explanation of how Teofimo’s team expects the dispute to end, leaving Catterall waiting while the champion pursues an exception.

The WBA’s published ruling supports Catterall’s account of the arrangement. When Rolando Romero was elevated to super champion at welterweight, the organization allowed him one optional defense, with the Giyasov-Catterall winner due to face him afterward. Teofimo defeated Romero on August 22 and inherited that obligation.

Teofimo’s appeal seeks permission to pursue bigger fights. That may make commercial sense for his team, but Catterall completed the route the WBA established. Allowing another opponent would mean extending his wait after the optional defense had already been used.

Catterall’s reference to Teofimo receiving a title shot coming off a loss sharpens his complaint. Teofimo received an opportunity without having to rebuild first. Catterall now wants the opportunity attached to his own win over Giyasov.

The sides have until close of business, Eastern Time, on October 22 to reach an agreement. If negotiations fail or either side withdraws, the WBA Championship Committee may order a purse bid with its president’s approval. That is a possible next step, rather than an automatic event on deadline day.

Teofimo could relinquish the belt to pursue another opponent. Keeping it while avoiding Catterall, however, would require the WBA to change the conditions it had already attached to the title.

Sports.title: Osleys Iglesias Wants Canelo Or Mbilli Winner
Sports.content:
Osleys Iglesias wants a unification against the winner of Canelo Alvarez’s October 31 fight with Christian Mbilli. Getting that fight could prove harder than defending his IBF title. Canelo has bigger commercial options, while Mbilli could be drawn into a lucrative rematch if he wins.

“I hope the winner [of Canelo-Mbilli] faces me. I’d like my next fight to be a unification,” Iglesias said after stopping Oliver Zaren in Quebec on Thursday.

The seventh-round stoppage lifted Iglesias to 16-0 with 15 knockouts. Those numbers help explain the difficulty of finding a willing opponent. He brings a world title, southpaw skills and heavy power, but lacks the name recognition that would turn a Canelo fight into a major event.

Canelo would be risking more than another points defeat. Iglesias has the power to hurt him and force a punishing fight, with a stoppage a serious possibility. Another belt might not be enough compensation when better-known opponents could offer more money and a better chance of winning.

Hamzah Sheeraz and Chris Eubank Jr. would give Canelo fresh opponents with British interest behind them. Neither is a guaranteed victory, but his team could view both as less dangerous choices than Iglesias.

Canelo also has a remaining fight under his agreement with Turki Alalshikh’s boxing operation. What Alalshikh wants to fund will influence the selection, leaving Iglesias competing against names that could sell a bigger show.

Mbilli appears more likely to accept a unification, but beating Canelo could change his immediate plans. A rematch would be difficult to turn down financially, provided Canelo wanted another attempt. His defeats against Floyd Mayweather and Dmitry Bivol did not produce second meetings.

If Canelo moves on, Mbilli against Iglesias would offer plenty in the ring. Mbilli’s relentless pressure would test the Cuban, while also bringing him within range of dangerous southpaw counters.

That is Iglesias’ best opening. A Canelo victory could leave him making another defense while the Mexican pursues a more profitable opponent.

Sports.title: Amir Khan Rules Out December Manny Pacquiao Fight
Sports.content:
Amir Khan is interested in facing Manny Pacquiao, but says he would not be ready for December 11. His admission leaves the proposed comeback dependent on more than agreeing on a payday, with the former light welterweight champion approaching five years out of the ring.

“That’s a rumor,” Khan told Metro about appearing on the Tyson Fury–Anthony Joshua undercard. “Even if it was for that fight night, I wouldn’t be ready for it, and I don’t think Manny would be either. “We’ve both been traveling, and we’re obviously not back in camp. It’s only about nine weeks away. I don’t know where that came from.”

Khan says talks are taking place and that he is happy with the money and location discussed. That establishes interest, but no signed fight or date has been announced.

The preparation question is particularly significant for Khan. He has not fought since Kell Brook stopped him in February 2022, and his last victory over a leading opponent came against Chris Algieri in 2015.

A longer camp could help Khan recover his conditioning. Whether he can regain the timing and reactions needed against Pacquiao is harder to judge. His best boxing depended on fast combinations and getting out before opponents could answer. Returning after years away would test both parts of that approach.

Pacquiao has been inactive too, but his July 2025 draw with Mario Barrios provides more recent evidence that he can compete over 12 rounds. Khan would enter negotiations without a comparable performance to point to since his retirement.

That difference makes a return fight worth considering before Khan commits to Pacquiao. Sparring can help him prepare, but an actual bout would offer a clearer picture of what remains.

Khan has always wanted the matchup, and the proposed terms appear attractive. His decision to dismiss December is sensible. The next question is whether additional time produces a prepared fighter or simply delays a difficult comeback.

Adding Pacquiao against Khan, who hasn’t fought since Brook stopped him in 2022, would turn the Cardiff card into an expensive nostalgia show. Fury–Joshua is already years overdue, and the proposed Jai Opetaia–Deontay Wilder fight features a faded former champion who turns 41 before December 11. Another pairing built around aging stars would leave the event trading heavily on what these fighters used to be.

Sports.title: Joshua-Fury Needs Promotion as Dana White and Eddie Hearn Bicker
Sports.content:
Dana White now describes himself as one of the promoters of Anthony Joshua’s December 11 fight with Tyson Fury, saying that his team will produce the event that night.

White’s latest comments put him alongside Eddie Hearn and Frank Warren in his description of the operation, although his clearest commitment concerns production.

“I’m producing the fight. Me and my team will be producing the fight that night. And I guess we’ll call me one of the promoters of the event because you do have Frank Warren and Eddie Hearn that are both promoters too, promoting the event,” White told BBC 5 Live.

The heavyweight fight is scheduled for Cardiff’s Principality Stadium. White also credited Hearn with securing the UK location during his interview with Steve Bunce.

The wording deserves attention. “I guess we’ll call me” sounds like White describing how he sees his involvement rather than announcing a newly agreed contractual position. It leaves the formal promotional arrangements unresolved, but makes clear that he expects a substantial role when the fighters enter the ring.

White and Hearn’s continuing argument over their roles is becoming tiresome. Every interview spent discussing who gets to call himself a promoter is another opportunity lost to explain why Joshua-Fury is still worth watching in December.

The names are familiar, but that does not mean the fight sells itself. Many fans see Joshua and Fury as two former champions meeting years after the contest should have happened. The promotion needs to address that skepticism rather than assume their past achievements will be enough.

There is still a fight to sell: the rivalry, the contrasting styles and the consequences of defeat for both men. Fans want to know what Joshua and Fury have left and whether either can produce something better than their recent performances suggest.

White and Hearn arguing over credit gives those viewers little reason to get excited. They need to spend more time promoting the fighters and less time promoting their own involvement.

Sports.title: Floyd Schofield Camp Threatens Cancellation Over Bahdi Weight
Sports.content:
Floyd Schofield’s father is threatening to pull Saturday’s fight against Lucas Bahdi if the Canadian exceeds 146 pounds at the second-day weight check, according to Chris Mannix. Bahdi’s team disputes his account of the negotiations and insists its fighter will come in at 145 or below.

The disagreement emerged Friday night ahead of their vacant WBA lightweight title fight in Chicago. Mannix reports that Illinois requires fighters in championship bouts to come in within ten pounds of the contract weight at a second-day check. For a fight contracted at 135 pounds, that means a 145-pound limit.

Floyd Sr. claims Bahdi’s side tried to negotiate a 15-pound allowance, which would permit him to reach 150 pounds. He also alleges they offered an additional $250,000 for each extra pound Bahdi was allowed.

According to Floyd Sr., Schofield’s camp agreed to 146 pounds but would refuse to proceed if Bahdi came in any heavier.

A representative from Bahdi’s side called Schofield’s version “total bullshit” and told Mannix that Bahdi would come in at 145 pounds or less.

That leaves two different accounts of what happened behind the scenes. The alleged financial offer comes from Floyd Sr., and Bahdi’s representative denies his version. It cannot be treated as an accepted account of the negotiations.

There is also an unanswered question about the 146-pound allowance. That figure exceeds the Illinois limit Mannix describes by one pound. His report does not establish whether the commission approved an exception or whether Floyd Sr. was describing only an agreement between the camps.

For Schofield, the concern is how much weight Bahdi can regain before they enter the ring. His father has now attached a cancellation threat to that concern, putting additional pressure on Saturday’s check.

Bahdi’s side has given itself a clear number to meet. If he comes in at 145 pounds or below, he would satisfy both the reported state limit and Schofield Sr.’s stated demand. Anything above 146 would test whether Schofield’s camp follows through on its threat.

Sports.title: Foster Questions Shakur Stevenson’s Chances Against Devin Haney
Sports.content:
O’Shaquie Foster argues that Devin Haney presents a far trickier technical challenge for Shakur Stevenson than Teofimo Lopez ever did. In his view, Stevenson’s victory over Lopez fails to prove how he would manage Haney’s specific tools.

While Foster stopped short of outright picking Haney, his breakdown casts doubt on Stevenson’s ability to rely on his trademark patience. He sees a scenario where Stevenson must abandon his comfort zone to press the action against an opponent who scores effectively from range.

“I have yet to see Shakur deal with the reach and the long jab of an elite fighter, like an elite boxer that can think on the move like him, that can make adjustments,” Foster told Sean Zittel. “It’s going to be difficult.”

Foster based that comparison on a harsh critique of Teofimo. While acknowledging Lopez’s physical gifts, Foster slammed his ring generalship.

“He’s athletic. He uses that to his advantage, but his IQ is terrible,” Foster said.

That contrast forms the core of Foster’s argument. Wild bursts of athletic speed present entirely different problems than a disciplined jab fired from the outside by a composed boxer.

If Haney controls distance with that jab, Shakur risks falling behind on the scorecards while waiting for openings that never arrive. To win rounds, Stevenson would have to close the space, disrupt the timing, and initiate contact instead of waiting on mistakes.

Applying pressure brings real danger. Stevenson would need to slip through Haney’s reach without overextending or aimlessly following him across the canvas. Foster also noted that Haney might sit down on his punches if he respects Stevenson’s power less over time.

Foster also waved off old sparring clips as irrelevant ancient history.

Ultimately, Foster envisions a tactical duel where Stevenson must prove he can adapt to an opponent who matches his boxing brain from distance. For Foster, beating Lopez left those questions unanswered.

Sports.title: WBA World Title Bout Schofield vs Bahdi
Sports.content:
In the Golden Boy and Most Valuable Promotions (MVP) cross-promoted main event, a new champion will be crowned as Floyd Schofield will face Lucas Bahdi on Saturday night, October 10th, at the Wintrust Arena in Chicago, live on DAZN.

This matchup features two undefeated fighters who are both determined, hungry, and ready to take their careers to the next level. The winner of this highly anticipated lightweight fight will be awarded the vacant WBA world title.

Since signing with Golden Boy Promotions in August 2022, Floyd Schofield has made the transition from prospect to contender. In his most recent outing, a definitive statement was made as he stopped Tevin Farmer in the first round.

His October 10th opponent, Lucas Bahdi, didn’t have the luxury of being guided by a well-known promotional company. Bahdi was winning consistently, as he achieved most of his success under the radar.

Two years ago, Bahdi introduced himself to the mainstream when he knocked Ashton Sylve out cold in the sixth round. Now in a high-stakes matchup, Lucas “Prince” Bahdi (20-0, 15 KOs) is set to battle Floyd “Kid Austin” Schofield (19-0, 13 KOs).

Lucas Bahdi is a very patient fighter who is accurate, good at controlling range, has good timing, and has a powerful right hand. The fear for Bahdi is due to his economical punch output; he can get outworked and fall behind on the scorecards.

Floyd Schofield is athletic, has a solid jab, fast hands, throws a variety of combinations, and is a strong puncher. Schofield is a fast starter, but the question for Schofield is: can he sustain his energetic pace during the later rounds?

Now promoted by MVP, the Ontario, Canada native Lucas Bahdi knows a win on Saturday night will take his career to another level. Bahdi plans on representing and taking full advantage of the opportunity.

“I’m very proud to be Canadian. I wear that flag on my back when I enter the ring,” Bahdi said.”That was all part of the journey. Now here we are. We’re fighting for the world title and I’m ready.”

When the Austin, Texas product Floyd Schofield enters the ring on Saturday night, he will also be attempting to win his first world title. He appreciates the opportunity, and he appreciates the person that made it possible.

“This fight is for my pops. At the end of the day, he sacrificed his whole life for me just to be in this position. So I got a lot to prove Saturday,” Schofield said at the press conference.

On Saturday night, October 10th, the Schofield vs. Bahdi clash is guaranteed to be an action-packed event. Both men will enter the ring undefeated, but by the end of the night, somebody’s 0 has got to go.

Ghana News.title: Ghana’s BRICS move requires clear strategy to manage risks – Godfred Bokpin
Ghana News.content:
Economist Prof. Godfred Bokpin says Ghana must develop a clear strategy to manage the economic and diplomatic risks associated with its decision to formally apply to join BRICS.

Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa has announced that the government has decided to formally apply for membership of the bloc of emerging economies.

Mr Ablakwa said the move is intended to diversify Ghana’s international partnerships, expand economic opportunities and strengthen cooperation with countries in the Global South.

Reacting to the development on JoyNews’ Newsfile, Prof. Bokpin said the decision reflects the shifting balance of the global economy but requires careful management of Ghana’s relations with its traditional partners, particularly the United States.

“I will not disagree with government taking this move, but again, we have to have a strategy to engage and manage that risk very, very carefully,” he said.

He cautioned that Ghana’s closer engagement with BRICS could affect its relations with Western partners.

“Our traditional partners, the U.S. and the rest, they will not take it kindly,” he said, emphasising the need for a clear strategy to guide the government’s engagement with both sides.

His comments come amid concerns over potential trade implications following US President Donald Trump’s threat to impose 100 per cent tariffs on countries associated with BRICS.

Prof. Bokpin argued that Ghana should consider the bloc’s growing economic significance in determining its international partnerships.

He said BRICS member countries account for more than 40 per cent of global GDP, adding that projections suggest China could become the world’s largest economy by 2050.

He further cited projections that four of the world’s five largest economies could be BRICS members by 2075.

“The direction is quite clear,” he said, adding that Ghana must position itself to benefit from the changing global economic landscape while carefully managing the associated risks.

Prof. Bokpin stressed that the government’s decision should not be pursued on a situational basis but must be supported by a deliberate strategy that protects Ghana’s economic interests and maintains its existing international relationships.

Ghana News.title: Pay teachers realistic income – Duncan Amoah to gov’t
Ghana News.content:
The Executive Director of the Chamber of Petroleum Consumers (COPEC), Duncan Amoah, has called on the government to pay teachers realistic salaries and provide adequate funding for teaching and learning materials, arguing that investment in education must translate into improved outcomes for students and the wider economy.

He said addressing teachers’ concerns about their conditions of service requires sustained dialogue between the government and teacher unions to prevent recurring industrial action and ensure stability in the education sector.

Speaking on a current affairs programme on Saturday, October 10, Mr Amoah stressed that education spending must be matched by better remuneration for teachers and adequate resources to support effective teaching and learning.

“Let’s pay teachers realistic incomes or salaries. Let’s pay for educational material,” he said.

He questioned the value of substantial investment in education if graduates ultimately struggle to secure jobs that match their qualifications and training.

“So we spend so much on education and at the end of the day, the economy does not throw out the kind of jobs that the educated ones would now require,” he added.

His comments highlight concerns about the need to align public spending on education with improvements in teaching quality, learning outcomes and employment opportunities for graduates.

Dialogue needed to address teachers’ concerns

Mr Amoah said teachers had made their grievances known and urged the government to respond constructively to their demands.

“The teachers have made their case, strongly and forcefully and I think that the government has also listened,” he said.

He also welcomed reports that the strike had been called off, describing the development as a positive step towards resolving the dispute.

“I am hearing the strike has been called off. It is the right way to go,” he added.

However, he cautioned that ending the industrial action should create room for further engagement rather than bring discussions over teachers’ conditions of service to an end.

“I think that a lot more dialogue and a lot more jaw-jaw should happen,” Mr Amoah said.

He emphasised that sustained negotiations would be crucial to resolving outstanding concerns and preventing similar disputes from disrupting academic activities in the future.

The COPEC Executive Director further stressed that the success of negotiations would depend on the willingness of both the government and teacher unions to engage in good faith.

He said the government’s response to teachers’ demands would influence the level of confidence the unions placed in the negotiation process.

“But then again, the goodwill at the table also would tell the unions whether the government is responsive or not,” he said.

His remarks underscore the importance of moving beyond negotiations to concrete measures that address teachers’ concerns and improve conditions within the education sector.

Ghana News.title: Bechem to become chicken capital of Ghana – Mahama projects
Ghana News.content:
President John Dramani Mahama has projected that when the Poultry and Meat Processing Factory at Bechem in the Ahafo Region becomes operational, it will make the town the chicken capital of Ghana.

The President projected an inspection tour of ongoing construction work on the project, which is 50 percent complete.

The inspection forms part of day one of the President's two-day Resetting Ghana Tour of the Ahafo Region.

It would be called that the President officially cut the sod for a modern poultry, meat, and feed processing plant in Bechem on November 27, 2025, which is expected to be ready for commissioning by the end of the first quarter of 2027.

President Mahama advised the youth of Bechem to take advantage of the factory and enter into poultry farming, adding that there was a ready market for them.

He said as part of efforts to ensure a value chain in the poultry industry, they started with the Nkoko Nketenkete initiative before work began on the factory, so that there would be more poultry for processing.

He reiterated that upon completion, the factory would create jobs for more people.

Mr Eric Opoku, the Minister of Food and Agriculture, said following the launch of the Nkoko Nketenkete initiative under the Feed Ghana Programme, Ghana's domestic poultry production had increased from 4.6 per cent to 22 per cent as of May 2026.

Ghana News.title: Gov’t targets recruitment of 16,500 health professionals in 2026
Ghana News.content:
Government says it plans to recruit 16,500 health professionals in 2026, as it steps up efforts to address staffing gaps and improve healthcare delivery across the country.

Deputy Chief of Staff Nana Oye Bampoe Addo says financial clearance has been secured ahead of the recruitment exercise to ensure newly employed health workers do not have to work without pay.

Speaking at the Ghana Health and Labour Summit 2026 at the University of Ghana, Legon, she said the planned recruitment forms part of broader efforts to address the challenges facing Ghana’s health sector, including unemployment among trained professionals and the migration of skilled workers.

“Government plans to recruit 16,500 health professionals in 2026, and with financial clearance secured ahead of recruitment, so that no new recruit works without pay,” she said.

The announcement comes amid concerns about the country’s ability to retain skilled professionals, with some health facilities struggling with staffing shortages while trained workers remain unemployed.

Ms Bampoe Addo said improving recruitment alone would not resolve the talent-retention crisis, stressing the need to create working environments that encourage professionals to build their careers in Ghana.

Representing the Minister for Labour, Jobs and Employment, Chief Labour Officer Dauda Ibrahim Braimah said workers’ decisions to remain in the country are influenced by more than salary levels.

“Ultimately, retention depends on quality of life, including housing, security, transportation, and workplace culture,” he said.

He said the Labour Ministry was pursuing reforms to strengthen labour market governance, improve working conditions and expand access to decent employment opportunities.

The Ministry is also working with social partners to ensure labour laws and institutions respond to changing workplace realities, including technological developments and evolving employment expectations.

Mr Braimah called for collective action from government, employers, educational institutions, professional associations and workers to address the challenge.

He said employers must invest in their workforce, while educational institutions align training with labour market demands and workers commit to continuous professional development.

The Ghana Health and Labour Summit 2026 brought together policymakers, labour representatives, employers, researchers and professionals to discuss strategies for improving workplace wellness and addressing Ghana’s talent-retention challenges.

Ghana News.title: Two-week strike will not derail academic calendar – GNAT President
Ghana News.content:
The President of the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT), Prosper Tachie, says the two-week strike by teacher unions will not throw the academic calendar into disarray, insisting that lost contact hours can be recovered.

He said the focus should not be solely on the disruption to academic activities but also on the welfare of teachers and the need for government to honour its commitments to them.

Speaking on JoyNews' Newsfile, Mr Tachie said the concerns over the academic calendar should not overshadow the issues that led to the industrial action.

“It’s quite unfortunate the concentration is on the academic calendar, but not our welfare. If you take good care of the employees, the employees in turn will take good care of the clients,” he said.

His comments follow a question about whether teachers could have trusted the government’s promises earlier to avoid disrupting the academic calendar.

Mr Tachie maintained that the lost instructional time could be recovered when teachers return to the classroom.

“It’s not about the academic calendar. It’s about execution, and once we return back to the classroom, you ensure that we make up for the lost contact hours. And I don't think the two weeks will put the entire academic calendar into disarray. We can put in some mechanisms to mitigate the situation to ensure that things return to normalcy,” he said.

Teacher unions suspended their strike following engagements involving the Minister of Labour and the Council of State, after assurances and commitments were given towards addressing the concerns of the teacher unions.

Mr Tachie stressed that the debate surrounding the strike should also consider teachers’ welfare and the implementation of agreed conditions of service.

Ghana News.title: Headmaster detained after BBC investigation into alleged sexual abuse of students
Ghana News.content:
A former headmaster of an Islamic boarding school in Indonesia has been named as a suspect in a sexual abuse investigation and detained by police, following a BBC Eye report.

Ahmad Imanuddin Sumar, known to students as Abah, led the Abul Barokat boarding school on the island of Lombok.

Police reopened the case after the BBC World Service revealed accusations of sexual abuse against him, and documented how former students had gathered evidence in an effort to bring the allegations to the authorities.

The story sparked public outrage and led to 12 more former students giving testimony to police.

The student detectives

Central to the BBC Eye investigation were former students Ziadatur Rahmah, known as Zia, and Sukma Rohana Fajar.

They launched their own investigation after Zia told a former classmate, Yusron Azzahidi, that the headteacher had sexually assaulted her when she was 17. The pair had been star pupils at the school.

By the time Zia confided in Yusron, she was studying in Cairo, Egypt, while he was in Jakarta.

Yusron suggested they gather evidence to support Zia's allegation. Speaking to former classmates, they spoke to Sukma, who alleges that Abah attempted to rape her at the school.

Yusron compiled a seven-page document detailing the allegations, and they gave it to representatives of Nahdlatul Wathan Diniyah Islamiyah (NWDI), the organisation that ran the school.

Thinking the school would support them, the students say that instead, they were pressured to withdraw their accusations.

In a secretly recorded phone call, Abah pleaded with Yusron to protect him and his reputation.

"Cover the shame of your teacher. Everyone makes mistakes, my child," Abah said.

Abah also contacted Zia, who secretly recorded their conversation and shared it with the BBC.

In the recording, Abah is heard apologising, but pleads with her to remain silent.

Following the BBC investigation, Abah held a news conference where he denied all the allegations. He did not deny that the voice heard in the recorded calls was his, but said the recordings were not confessions.

Sukma told the BBC she had been forced to sign a document saying her allegations were lies. She later secretly recorded a conversation with Abah's wife, known to students as Umi. In the recording, Umi tells Sukma that the document was intended to protect "her good name".

The former students eventually resumed their efforts to seek justice, with support from lawyer Joko Jumadi, who has experience in similar cases.

More students come forward

The day after the BBC investigation was published, parents arrived at the school to collect their children, with some travelling from other islands.

One mother said she had begun crying when she heard the news, thinking about her daughter.

"I'm moving her right now," she said. "I absolutely want my child to leave this school."

Yusron said he and Zia, who recently got married, were overwhelmed by the response from former students.

"It was beyond what we expected," he said. "So many people contacted us - on Instagram, WhatsApp. They contacted me and Zia directly, and lots of them were saying, 'I'm a victim too'."

Police interviewed Zia and Sukma, along with the 12 other former students who came forward with allegations of abuse.

"They thought they were the only ones - and it's been really shocking for them to learn, like I did, that they weren't alone," Zia said.

Sukma said she felt relieved and grateful that the allegations are now being taken seriously.

"It's not about revenge. It's more the acknowledgement that what he did was wrong. I'm waiting for the day when he admits that himself," she told the BBC.

Abah has resigned from the school and has said he will respect the legal process.

The BBC contacted Abah and his wife during its original investigation, but they did not respond at the time.

NWDI denied trying to cover up the allegations and said it was investigating them internally. It said it had a duty to protect the organisation from being tarnished by the alleged actions of individuals.

In the wake of the BBC investigation, NWDI vowed to ensure such abuse never happened again and said it would safeguard the rights of students who came forward.

Ghana News.title: GNAT pushes for clear implementation procedures of teachers’ conditions of service
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT) is pushing for clear procedures to guide the implementation of teachers’ conditions of service, warning that agreements risk remaining unfulfilled for years without a defined process for accessing the benefits.

GNAT President Prosper Tachie said the union wants the Ministry of Education and the Ghana Education Service (GES) to finalise the procedures for implementing the provisions of the collective agreement before concluding outstanding negotiations.

Speaking on JoyNews' Newsfile, he said implementation had been a major challenge in previous agreements, with benefits often left hanging despite agreements being reached.

“One of the major challenges confronting us so far as our collective agreement is concerned is about implementation. We will agree to the substantive document, but when it comes to procedural matters, as to how to assess the benefits within the document, we leave it hanging over the years, and this time round we are not ready for such a commitment,” he said.

Mr Tachie said GNAT wanted the relevant authorities to specify how teachers would access the benefits provided under the agreement.

“We want the Ministry of Education, Ghana Education Service, to finalise the document specifying processes of assessing certain benefits within the document,” he added.

His comments follow the pre-tertiary teachers’ decision to suspend its nationwide strike after engagements involving the Labour Minister and the Council of State, alongside assurances from the government on outstanding demands.

The government has committed to paying promotion-related arrears to more than 51,000 teachers by October 16. Payments relating to the professional development allowance and digital support allowance are expected in November and December, respectively.

Mr Tachie said the union had also secured revised positions on some allowances following negotiations with the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission and the Ministry of Finance.

He stressed that the suspension of the strike was interim, with discussions on outstanding provisions of the collective agreement expected to continue.

Teachers are expected to return to the classrooms on Monday, October 12.

Ghana News.title: Recurrent strikes threaten quality of education and academic calendars – Prof Bokpin
Ghana News.content:
Economist and University of Ghana Business School Professor Gofred Bokpin has warned that recurrent labour strikes in Ghana’s education sector are undermining teaching time, academic calendars and the quality of graduates.

Speaking on JoyNews' Newsfile on Saturday, he said Ghana had experienced significant disruptions in the health and education sectors every two to three years over the past 15 to 20 years, describing the trend as a major concern for a country seeking sustained socio-economic development.

Prof. Bokpin said lost instructional time could not be recovered, even when negotiations eventually led to the resolution of disputes.

He argued that industrial harmony in education was essential to developing human capital, improving labour quality and supporting national development.

Prof. Bokpin said the situation was particularly worrying for senior high schools operating under the Free Senior High School policy, where the double-track system and infrastructure constraints had already affected the time students spent in school.

He warned that further disruptions could compromise the quality of education, adding that students were not receiving the level of tuition they needed while the state continued to provide for their upkeep.

He also questioned the effectiveness of online learning as a substitute for classroom teaching when students on double-track arrangements returned home.

The economist said universities were facing uncertainty over their academic calendars, noting that the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) had announced a postponement of its next academic year's reopening.

He said universities had worked to restore their academic calendars following the COVID-19 pandemic, but disruptions caused by industrial action were now creating further difficulties.

While acknowledging that teachers, lecturers and administrators had demands that needed to be addressed, Prof. Bokpin said the government must prioritise industrial stability in the education sector.

He argued that strikes often ended with negotiations and some concessions to workers, but the resulting loss of teaching time and productivity could not be reversed.

Prof. Bokpin also cautioned against pursuing fiscal discipline at the expense of social priorities, saying government spending decisions should reflect the country's development aspirations and the needs of its people.

He urged the government to manage labour relations more effectively to protect the academic calendar and ensure that students receive quality education.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
