His criticism has added a political dimension to the debate over the government’s response to rising petrol prices, with the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, subsequently accusing Atiku of making verbal attacks on Tinubu because of political defeat.



The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has defended the petrol price discount, maintaining that it is a commercial decision by NNPC Retail to temporarily surrender its profit margin rather than a return to the petroleum subsidy regime.



The price cushion initiative, which offers a N60-per-litre reduction by allowing NNPC Retail to forgo its retail profit margin, is intended to cushion households, commuters and commercial transport operators against rising petrol prices triggered by global oil market volatility amid tensions in the Middle East. However, the initiative has generated divergent reactions, with the government insisting that the measure is a commercial decision rather than a return to fuel subsidy, while industry operators have questioned its implementation framework and implications for competition.



Atiku, accused Tinubu of wrongly copying his petroleum pricing proposal after previously criticising the idea.

The former Vice President said: “Tinubu has had more than three years to improve our lives. What has he given us? A bag of food that costs more each time we go to the market. A journey to work that eats up our salaries. A business that cannot keep its lights on. A farm we may be too afraid to visit.



“This is the cruel record he wants Nigerians to applaud. I have heard the anger in your voices, and I share it. Across this country, people are ready to stand with us and demand better. I will stand with you until we make life affordable again.

“You have demanded painful sacrifices from the people while you, your family, and friends are junketing all over the place. You told Nigerians to be patient as the price of petrol has pushed up the price of almost everything else. But now that an election is approaching, you have suddenly discovered their pain.



“Nigerians did not need a press conference to tell them they were suffering. They have lived it for 1,229 days since you took office. They know who made their lives difficult, and they are ready to hold you to account and mark your script.



“Yesterday, your government announced a 30-day discount on petrol at NNPC stations, with priority for public transport operators. You also proposed a measure to contain petrol prices. When I proposed targeted support to ease fuel costs, you called me ignorant of economic policy. Your government said it could not be done. Now, in a desperate and clumsy retreat, you have shamelessly embraced the principle you mocked. You owe me an apology. But more importantly, you owe Nigerians an answer: what happens on day 31?

Speaking further, Atiku said: “My production subsidy proposal is a lasting, targeted plan. Yours is a temporary palliative dressed up as a solution. Nigerians can see the difference between a leader who has done the work and a government scrambling for an election-season headline.



“Your 30-day discount is a sugar rush masquerading as economic policy: a fleeting taste of relief at the pump, followed by the same brutal crash when the month ends. Families cannot plan their meals around a temporary discount. Transporters cannot set stable fares on it. Businesses cannot invest or plan for the future on it. Nigerians need lasting relief through a well-designed production subsidy that supports local refining and lowers fuel costs – not a N50 sweetener with an expiry date.

“But I am glad you have finally acknowledged the failure of your approach. It is a pity you still seem to have learned nothing from it. I offered a plan because Nigerians’ welfare matters more to me than who gets the credit. You chose to mock it, then copied it badly.



“You created the hardship and now want a medal for announcing fake relief. This is Deception 101 – or, better still, yahoo-yahoo subsidy. For three and a half years, your government has driven up the cost of living.

“Now you offer a N50 petrol discount for 30 days and expect applause for returning a fraction of what Nigerians have lost? How can you make daily life unbearable for years and expect one month of token relief to wipe the record clean?

“Nigerians are neither foolish nor forgetful. They have lived with the consequences of your decisions, and they will judge you by them. Can’t you smell the coffee I am brewing? Nigerians can smell it. They know the difference between a government with a plan and a government buying time.



“Do not hide behind the word “discount.” You say public transport operators come first. Will fares fall? Who will enforce that? What about the farmer moving produce, the trader restocking a shop, the manufacturer running a generator, and the family paying for food? They all pay for fuel, even when they never fill a tank.



‘What you have announced is not relief. It is a late confession of failure on the eve of a general election. Do you think that millions of Nigerians, whom you have condemned to poverty and hardship for three and a half years, will applaud you for failing so abysmally? You have miscalculated. Nigerians are fed up with you.”



Atiku said the economy “has collapsed under your watch,” adding that, “by offering a 30-day relief package, you admit you have no idea how to fix it. That is why you summoned your gang of tax collectors for help. It is a sad spectacle. You have run out of time. Nigerians need leadership with the political will, administrative experience, and sound economic judgment to make life affordable again.”



“You still reach for the same old excuse. You blamed past administrations for the hardship your decisions have inflicted today. You are the President. The petrol price is your problem. The collapsing purchasing power is your problem. The shops closing under the weight of fuel and power costs are your problem. Take responsibility for the country you govern.



“My alternative is clear. Support petroleum products actually refined in Nigeria and sold to Nigerians. Cap the support. Put it in the budget. Audit it independently. Exclude imports. Show the public what it costs and what they save. Give families relief they can count on and give domestic producers a reason to produce more. That is the lesson you missed.



“Fuel is only one part of the damage. We must make food affordable, restore reliable power, put people to work and let businesses grow. We must secure the roads and farms. We must remove the obstacles that hold back young Nigerians with the talent to compete anywhere in the world. A speech about growth means nothing to a family that cannot afford dinner.”

Oyedele: Discount a Commercial Decision by NNPC, Not Subsidy

Meanwhile, the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has defended the petrol price discount, insisting that it is a commercial decision by NNPC Retail to temporarily surrender its profit margin rather than a return to the petroleum subsidy regime.



In a statement issued by the Ministry of Finance yesterday, Oyedele explained that a retail margin discount occurs when a marketer voluntarily reduces or temporarily relinquishes its profit margin to lower the price paid by consumers.

The price cushion initiative offers a N60-per-litre reduction by allowing NNPC Retail to forgo its retail profit margin. It is intended to cushion households, commuters and commercial transport operators against rising petrol prices triggered by global oil market volatility amid tensions in the Middle East.

Oyedele said the cost of the discount was being borne by NNPC Retail and that no public funds had been committed to the initiative.



“Every marketer adds a margin to the price it pays for the fuel it sells. A margin discount means the retailer chooses to take a smaller margin, or no margin at all for a period, and passes the saving to the customer. The cost of the discount is borne by the retailer alone,” the minister said.

He maintained that the arrangement differed from a subsidy, under which the government pays part of the price consumers would otherwise bear using public revenue.



According to him, NNPC Retail continues to purchase petrol from Dangote Refinery and other suppliers at prevailing market prices on commercial terms before applying its retail margin to determine pump prices.

\Oyedele also argued that the reduction in earnings per litre could be offset by higher sales volumes as motorists patronised NNPC stations because of the lower prices.



Speaking further, Oyedele said: “We must not keep quiet and allow populism to move our country in the wrong direction. To answer your question, if Nigeria produces 1.8 million barrels of crude oil per day, that volume does not belong to the country alone. Under production-sharing contracts and joint ventures, the crude is shared among the parties involved, and the ratios vary. For illustration, let us assume a 45:55 ratio. A portion of the crude goes to the contractors, while another portion goes to the government.



“There is also the cost of production—the cost of extracting the crude oil from the ground. This is recovered through cost oil, which further reduces the volume available. Royalties must also be deducted before the parties can share the remaining profit oil. The point I am making is that, before the recent reforms, almost all the crude oil revenue available to Nigeria had been exhausted by the cost of the fuel subsidy.”



“Before President Tinubu introduced the reform in May 2023, the NNPC, which holds crude oil on behalf of the country, had less than 100,000 barrels of free crude left. When government revenues were exhausted, the government resorted to printing money, but that was still insufficient. We then began using future crude oil production to secure commitments and borrow money to subsidise current consumption.”



According to the minister, Nigeria was in an unsustainable situation as of May 2023, when the President introduced his subsidy removal reform.

Nigeria had less than 100,000 barrels of free crude available. What the government has achieved since then is the result of increased production, reduced oil theft and the renegotiation of some commitments that previously tied down crude oil. Many Nigerians will remember when Mr. Tony Elumelu, went on social media that the country was unable to account for much of the crude oil it produced because of theft. He later returned to say that the estimated level of theft had fallen to about five per cent. These developments reflect some of the efforts made by the current government.



“However, despite the increase in production and the reduction in oil theft, Nigeria still does not have up to 700,000 barrels of free crude oil available to service Dangote Refinery. Therefore, those suggesting that the government should simply offer crude oil at a discounted price based on the cost of production may not fully appreciate the technical and commercial realities involved.



“It is also important to understand that Nigerian crude is predominantly light and sweet. It may not be the most optimal feedstock for every refining requirement, and Dangote Refinery still needs to import some heavier crude grades. I do not want to go into the technicalities, but the reality is that Nigeria does not currently have up to 700,000 barrels of free crude oil available to supply any single buyer, including Dangote Refinery.



That is why the President introduced the naira-for-crude arrangement, which was intended to help provide greater stability for the refinery and the domestic market. The arrangement has helped, but the available volume is still insufficient to meet all the refinery’s requirements.



“As we ramp up production and free up more barrels from existing commitments, we should reach a point where Dangote Refinery can obtain the crude it requires and other refineries can also secure adequate supplies. Personally, I hope Nigeria will eventually reach a stage where all the crude oil it produces is refined domestically and only the surplus of refined petroleum products is exported.



“However, I cannot provide the exact volume of free crude currently available because I do not have that figure. What I can say is that it is below Dangote Refinery’s requirements. It is important to establish that fact: the refinery still imports crude oil, and Nigeria must continue to increase production and make more crude available to domestic refiners.”

Keyamo: Atiku’s Attacks on Tinubu Sign of Political Depression

In a direct response to Atiku’s criticism, the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, yesterday described the former vice-president’s recent verbal attacks on President Tinubu as symptoms of “agitated depression” fuelled by political defeat.



Keyamo who made this known in his verified X (Twitter) account, said Atiku was pained and that the pain stemmed from the fact that President Tinubu, has outsmarted him politically to become the President.

“The pain and bitterness stems from the fact that he, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu @officialABAT finally outsmarted him politically to get the most coveted position of President and he can’t mentally deal with this fact. What we are witnessing with all his recent tantrums against Mr. President, veiled as opposition heroics, is actually a higher form of depression in the field of mental health called agitateddepression.



“Recall that President Bola Tinubu was Governor of Lagos State at a time when he was Vice-President of Nigeria and was generally regarded as politically ahead of President Tinubu in the pecking order of those who aspired to be President. This is not a forum to restate the political journey these two eminent politicians embarked upon when both left their offices as Vice President and Governor in 2007, both in union sometimes and in disunion some other times, with both of their eyes fixed on the ultimate prize,” Keyamo said.



He said, however, through a combination of fate, luck, divine interventions and political dexterity, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu finally clinched the Presidency “At the first try as against his (Atiku’s) never-ending ambition since 1993. Here lies his pain, anger, despair and depression.”



“But let me remind Atiku Abubakar that, despite all the invectives he has poured on the President of late, power is given only by God Almighty, not by man. My most favourite Bible verse since I was 10 years old is actually Ecclesiastic 9:11 which states:

‘I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all,'” Keyamo said.

The Minister also added, “We should all pity Atiku Abubakar rather than goad him on. Those close to him should actually administer anti-depressants on him. Rather than win supporters, he will lose most intelligent ones by his recent posturing.

“Atiku Abubakar urgently needs mental health support at this critical time as he finally peters into political oblivion,” Keyamo added.

Marketers Warn Against Market Distortions

Despite the government’s explanation, the intervention has raised questions among industry operators about its implementation, the implications for competition and the ability of suppliers to recover their costs. Independent marketers are now faced with the challenge of competing with NNPC Retail during the 30-day discount period without eroding their margins or losing customers to cheaper outlets.

A petrol marketer, who pleaded to remain anonymous, said the price reduction had changed market dynamics and forced operators to reconsider their pricing strategies to retain customers.

“The price reduction has changed the dynamics of the market, and every marketer now has to review their pricing strategy to remain competitive. Customers will naturally gravitate towards outlets offering lower prices, so we are looking at ways to retain our customers through better service, efficient operations and competitive pricing. It is now a question of adapting quickly to the new market reality,” the marketer said.

For his part, former Chairman of the Major Energies Marketers Association of Nigeria (MEMAN), Tunji Oyebanji, warned that the N1,350-per-litre price benchmark could create confusion in a market where petrol prices are expected to reflect prevailing supply costs.

He questioned how suppliers would manage the difference between market prices and the proposed benchmark, particularly if they were required to absorb higher costs temporarily and recover them when market conditions improved.

“By the price benchmark, you have created all sorts of confusion. What will happen now is that everybody will gravitate around that point,” Oyebanji said.

He argued that the arrangement could place additional financial pressure on importers and refiners, especially where the cost of financing inventories remained high.

According to him, suppliers could be forced to borrow at elevated interest rates to sustain the arrangement, while uncertainty over when and how they would recover additional costs could undermine their operations.

Oyebanji also recalled the experience of the former petrol subsidy regime, when delayed reimbursements reportedly exposed marketers to financing costs and foreign-exchange losses.

He warned that widening price differences between Nigeria and neighbouring countries could create fresh incentives for the smuggling of petroleum products across the borders.

A senior official of the Depot and Petroleum Products Marketers Association of Nigeria (DAPPMAN), who spoke on condition of anonymity, said marketers were not consulted before the intervention was announced. The official declined to assess the merits of the policy, stating that the industry had not been adequately involved in its formulation.

Officials of the Major Oil Marketers Association of Nigeria (MOMAN) and Dangote Petroleum Refinery, who were contacted, declined to comment on the matter.

Agbakoba, Analysts, APC, ADC Differ

The debate over the petrol price discount has extended beyond the government and industry operators, with policy analysts, business groups and political parties offering differing views on whether the intervention can provide meaningful relief without creating fresh fiscal or market-related problems.

Notwithstanding Oyedele’s explanation, the Centre for Social Justice (CSJ) said the government’s proposed price modulation mechanism, intended to keep petrol prices at no more than N1,350 per litre, fell short of the relief Nigerians expected.

The organisation’s Lead Director, Eze Onyekpere, said Nigerians had been paying about N800 per litre before the outbreak of the America-Israel-Iran war and expected a more comprehensive plan to reduce prices towards N400 to N500 per litre over the medium term.

He proposed a domestic crude oil pricing differential that would allow local refineries to obtain crude at prices below international benchmarks, alongside measures to prevent the diversion and smuggling of refined products.

Onyekpere also called for the concession of the four NNPC refineries to technically and financially capable investors, as well as the recovery of funds allegedly lost through turnaround maintenance projects.

He argued that part of the savings arising from subsidy removal could be deployed to reduce the cost of petrol and ease the hardship facing households and businesses.

Professor Emeritus of Petroleum Economics, Wumi Iledare, said the discount could only be justified if it remained temporary, targeted and transparent.

“The decisive question is simple: who pays for the discount? If NNPC Ltd sells below economic cost and government later reimburses it — or an implicit public liability arises — the measure is subsidy-equivalent, whatever its name,” he said.

Iledare urged the government to disclose the discount per litre, eligible volumes, financing source, maximum fiscal exposure and exit plan.

He added that any intervention should be transparent, subject to fiscal limits, independently auditable and designed to preserve competitive neutrality in the downstream petroleum market.

Energy analyst Dan Kunle also criticised the policy as an ad hoc response to rising prices, arguing that it could distort the market without addressing the underlying factors driving petrol costs.

He proposed a more coordinated arrangement involving the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA), NNPC Retail, Dangote Refinery and qualified downstream operators, including MRS and AP, to improve domestic crude allocation and petrol pricing.

Kunle suggested allocating 250,000 barrels of crude oil per day to Dangote Refinery for domestic processing, with NNPC Retail purchasing the resulting petrol at N1,320 per litre and selling it at N1,350.

“Your local problem has local solution,” he said, urging the relevant parties to negotiate a workable framework and submit it to President Tinubu for approval.

The Director of the Abuja School of Social and Political Thought, Sam Amadi, described the N60-per-litre reduction as a face-saving measure that was politically motivated and economically insufficient to address the pressure on households.

Speaking on Arise News Channel, Amadi argued that the reduction would have little immediate effect on transport fares or the broader cost of living.

“First, I think it’s a face-saving strategy. Again, the government has been too late, too little,” he said.

He added that the intervention might have some political value but would not substantially ease the economic difficulties confronting Nigerians.

The debate has also assumed a political dimension, with the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) insisting that the petroleum subsidy regime would not return.

The APC National Secretary, Senator Surajudeen Ajibola Basiru, said the distinction between a retail discount and a fuel subsidy was clear, maintaining that the government would not return to the previous arrangement.

“The issue of fuel subsidy, just as the Minister of Petroleum said yesterday, is that we are not going back to subsidy. It is gone, and gone forever,” Basiru said.

He argued that the removal of the subsidy had freed the government from the financial pressures associated with borrowing to fund salaries, pensions and development projects.

The APC National Chairman, Nentawe Yilwatda Goshwe, also criticised opposition proposals to reduce petrol prices through crude oil pricing arrangements, arguing that local refineries could not depend entirely on government-supplied crude because part of Nigeria’s crude production belonged to joint-venture partners.

The ADC, however, described the proposed intervention as a loan to Nigerians, arguing that costs absorbed by suppliers today could eventually be passed on to consumers.

In a statement issued by its National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, the opposition party said the discount did not provide a lasting solution to the cost-of-living crisis.

“The principle is straightforward: what suppliers forgo today, Nigerians will pay later. The government wants to announce a discount, collect the applause and leave the Nigerian people to settle the bill,” the party said.

The ADC argued that a temporary reduction in petrol prices would not resolve the broader pressures on food prices, transport fares and household expenditure.

Separately, a Senior Political Assistant to the ADC presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, Demola Olarewaju, accused President Tinubu of adopting an idea previously advanced by Atiku on petrol pricing.

In a post on X, Olarewaju criticised the administration’s approach to the intervention and called for a full return to fuel subsidy, further intensifying the political debate surrounding petrol prices.

Amid the controversy, former President of the Nigerian Bar Association, Olisa Agbakoba, advocated a domestic crude oil price differential that he said could bring petrol prices down to N400 per litre.

Speaking at the annual conference of the Association of Energy Correspondents of Nigeria in Lagos, Agbakoba argued that Nigeria could consider a pricing arrangement that gives domestic refiners access to crude oil at a lower price than the international benchmark.

He said the approach could reduce the cost of locally refined petrol and provide more meaningful relief to consumers.

The immediate challenge for independent marketers, however, is how to compete with NNPC Retail during the 30-day discount period without eroding their margins or losing customers to cheaper outlets.

The Chief Executive Officer of the Centre for the Promotion of Private Enterprise (CPPE), Muda Yusuf, said the initiative would bring relief to some people.

Yusuf told THISDAY that the key distinction was that the intervention was limited in scope and possibly more targeted at vulnerable segments of society who would not mind long queues.

He said the fiscal burden of the discount would be much less than that of a blanket subsidy, under which about 50 million litres would have to be covered.

“A blanket subsidy is surely not sustainable. This intervention is also time bound. It also has a significant symbolic value,” Yusuf said.

He emphasised that “addressing the cost-of-living challenge is a shared responsibility among all tiers of government — federal, state and local governments” and suggested that “more investment in mass transit vehicles with subsidised transport fares is needed to complement this latest intervention.”

Similarly, the Chief Executive Officer of BIC Consultancy Service, Boniface Chizea, said it was not surprising that calls for a return to subsidy were gaining ground, considering the level of hardship in the country.

Chizea said: “After all, we must not stop reminding ourselves that the core essence of leadership is the welfare and well-being of a generality of the population.

“The pump price today at above N1,400 per litre is at the same time punitive, excruciating, even wicked, and most certainly not sustainable.

“Therefore, the various steps being taken are to temporarily ameliorate the hardship that has been visited on the population.

“It is often recommended as a matter of fact that it is better to subsidise production rather than consumption for more reasons than one.”

He said there were several reasons Nigeria should avoid returning to pump-price subsidies, describing such payments as a wasteful misallocation of scarce resources.

“If you also make pump price in Nigeria much lower than those in neighbouring countries, we weaponise irresistible and difficult to control products smuggling as economic agents take undue advantage.

“What we must bear in mind is that it is urgent for us as a country to think properly through how to cater for the welfare and well-being of the majority of our population living on the margin by making our budgeting pro-poor,” Chizea said.

The competing positions have left the 30-day petrol discount at the centre of an increasingly broad debate over fuel pricing, market competition and the government’s response to rising living costs. While the government maintains that NNPC Retail is temporarily sacrificing its margin rather than reinstating a subsidy, critics are questioning the sustainability of the relief and the implications for the wider downstream market. Atiku’s central question remains whether the intervention will be followed by a lasting policy framework or whether consumers and businesses will face renewed pressure when the discount expires.

World.title: Four more Cape Town beaches in line to earn Blue Flag status
World.content:
Big Bay beach has been named among four new Blue Flag pilot sites in Cape Town. Image: Pixabay

Four more Cape Town beaches are in line for international Blue Flag recognition, joining eight that have retained full status for the 2026/27 season.

Chapman’s Peak in Hout Bay, Big Bay, Strand and Strandfontein have been selected as pilot sites under the internationally recognised programme.

The announcement was made at the annual Blue Flag and Green Coast Awards ceremony in Hermanus this week.



Cape Town has participated in the programme for 25 years. This marks the fifth consecutive season in which eight of its beaches have secured full Blue Flag status.

Four new Blue Flag pilot sites named

The four pilot sites will undergo a feasibility assessment to determine whether they can meet the programme’s international criteria.

These include water quality, safety, accessibility, environmental management and public amenities.

The eight Cape Town beaches awarded full Blue Flag status for 2026/27 are:

Bikini Beach

Camps Bay Beach

Clifton 4th Beach

Fish Hoek Beach

Llandudno Beach

Melkbosstrand

Muizenberg Beach

Silwerstroomstrand

The programme operates in more than 50 countries. In South Africa, it is facilitated by the Wildlife and Environment Society of South Africa (WESSA), which has coordinated the initiative since 2001.

Blue Flag status provides an internationally recognised benchmark for beach management. It also offers reassurance to residents and visitors about water quality, safety and facilities.



“Eight full Blue Flags and four pilot sites are significant recognition of the year-round work that goes into maintaining our beaches and preparing them for residents and visitors,” said Francine Higham, Cape Town’s Mayco Member for Community Services and Health.

Amphibious wheelchairs to improve beach access

The City is also introducing new amphibious wheelchairs at several beaches this summer, including most of its Blue Flag beaches.

The wheelchairs will help beachgoers with mobility impairments access the ocean.

“As we head into summer, we are improving access through new amphibious wheelchairs at several beaches,” Higham added.

The City has deployed lifeguards at designated swimming beaches and has urged beachgoers to take precautions when enjoying the Cape coastline.

World.title: Zondo Commission: R17.2bn recovered, but where are the convictions?
World.content:
The Presidency has defended the nearly R1 billion spent on the Zondo Commission, revealing that government agencies have recovered R17.2 billion linked to state capture investigations. Image: Flickr

The Presidency has defended the nearly R1 billion spent on the Zondo Commission, revealing that government agencies have recovered R17.2 billion linked to state capture investigations.

Presidency director-general Phindile Baleni told Parliament on Friday, 9 October, that the recoveries far exceeded the cost of the four-year inquiry.

She presented the figures while briefing MPs on the Presidency’s annual report.



WHERE DID THE R17.2 BILLION COME FROM?

Baleni said the National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) accounted for approximately R8.2 billion in recoveries.

The South African Revenue Service (SARS) recovered another R5.4 billion, while the Special Investigating Unit (SIU) contributed R3.5 billion.

The amounts represent recoveries by government agencies linked to the commission’s work, rather than money recovered by the inquiry itself.

“This is one of those that we are absolutely proud of. The commission that has been set up has more than repaid the costs that were incurred,” Baleni said.

She told MPs that the inquiry had also contributed to institutional reforms.

The commission, chaired by former Chief Justice Raymond Zondo, investigated allegations of state capture, corruption and fraud involving government departments and state-owned entities between 2018 and 2022.



Its final report detailed widespread wrongdoing and recommended criminal investigations, prosecutions and changes to government institutions.

WHAT ABOUT STATE CAPTURE PROSECUTIONS?

Despite the financial recoveries, the pace of prosecutions remains under scrutiny.

In August, National Director of Public Prosecutions Andy Mothibi told Parliament that 99 people were facing prosecution in state capture matters, while investigators were still pursuing 56 cases.

Mothibi acknowledged that prosecutors needed to do more but said lengthy legal battles had delayed progress.

The Presidency previously reported that 80% of the 60 actions in its implementation plan were either complete, substantially complete or on track.

However, Baleni acknowledged another concern during Friday’s briefing.

The Investigating Directorate Against Corruption (IDAC), which forms part of government’s response to state capture, has itself faced scrutiny at the Madlanga Commission.

As previously reported by The South African, the commission heard allegations involving former IDAC head Andrea Johnson and the handling of investigations into senior police officials.

Baleni said government needed stronger safeguards to prevent institutions established to fight corruption from losing direction.

She also conceded that corruption levels in South Africa remained unacceptably high, despite the recoveries and reforms.

World.title: Durban protests: 19 arrested after homes torched, shops looted
World.content:
Protesters took to the streets of Durban amid violent unrest that saw police arrest 19 suspects following incidents of arson, looting and damage to property. Image: X

KwaZulu-Natal police have arrested 19 suspects following violent protests that left two houses burnt, vehicles torched and shops looted across Durban.

Officers arrested 15 people on Friday night, 9 October, after taking four others into custody on Thursday for attempted murder and discharging a firearm in public.

Police confirmed that the unrest spread through the city and surrounding suburbs, with two houses set alight in Umbilo and several businesses damaged.



MORE ARRESTS EXPECTED

Provincial police spokesperson Colonel Robert Netshiunda said most of those arrested were students.

The latest 15 suspects face charges of public violence and malicious damage to property, although investigators could add further charges.

#sapsKZN

[FIFTEEN SUSPECTS ARRESTED AND MORE EXPECTED FOR DURBAN PROTESTS]



Fifteen suspects were arrested on Friday night following violent protests which engulfed the city of Durban and surrounding suburbs. This brings the number of suspects arrested to 19, including the four… pic.twitter.com/6kzAAd8m8a — SA Police Service 🇿🇦 (@SAPoliceService) October 10, 2026

Crime Intelligence officers and detectives are tracking down those responsible for burning vehicles and buildings.

The suspects will appear in court soon.

As previously reported by The South African, Thursday’s unrest saw protesters torch 14 vehicles in Durban and another 10 in Soweto.



KwaZulu-Natal Police Commissioner Lieutenant-General Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi intervened as authorities stepped up their response.

The violence also prompted the United States to issue a security warning, urging Americans to avoid affected areas.

The protests followed controversy over asylum application procedures. The Department of Home Affairs withdrew its contentious asylum intake directive on Friday.

POLICE ISSUE STERN MTN8 WARNING

Meanwhile, police have dismissed social media rumours suggesting that Saturday’s MTN8 final between Orlando Pirates and Mamelodi Sundowns at Moses Mabhida Stadium could face disruptions.

Netshiunda confirmed that the match would proceed, with security measures in place to protect spectators, officials and players.

“All roads leading to the stadium are open and will remain open,” he said.

He also warned anyone planning to protest near the venue.

“Anybody who attempts to stage any kind of protest on the routes leading to the stadium, or anywhere in the vicinity of Moses Mabhida Stadium will be met with the strong arm of the law,” Netshiunda said.

World.title: The best Kruger National Park camps for wildlife sightings
World.content:
Where can you see cheetahs in Kruger National Park? Image: canva

Where you stay in the Kruger National Park can make a really big difference to the type of wildlife you see.

There are no guarantees on safari (wild animals have a habit of ignoring itineraries), but some camps are particularly well positioned for certain species and habitats.

Here’s where to head for the best viewings.



Which Kruger National Park camp should you choose?

If you want to see. . . Consider staying at. . . Why? Lions Satara Open grasslands support plenty of prey species and predators Leopards Lower Sabie / Skukuza Productive river areas and good game-viewing roads Elephants Letaba / Olifants Major rivers attract large numbers of elephants Rhinos Berg-en-Dal Strong rhino habitat in the southwestern park Buffalo Lower Sabie / Crocodile Bridge Water and productive grazing areas Hippos & crocodiles Lower Sabie / Olifants Both camps overlook major rivers Wild dogs Satara / Skukuza area Central and southern Kruger offer opportunities for sightings Birds Punda Maria / Letaba Northern habitats and river systems offer excellent birding Big Five Skukuza / Lower Sabie Excellent all-round southern Kruger habitat Quieter safari Punda Maria / Talamati Smaller or more remote camps with fewer visitors

Satara: one of the best for big cats

If you’re hoping to see lions, Satara is one of the Kruger camps worth putting near the top of your list.

The camp sits in central Kruger, surrounded by relatively open grassland and savanna. These areas support large numbers of herbivores such as zebra, wildebeest and impala, which means plenty of prey for predators.

Lions are particularly associated with the area, while cheetahs and leopards can also be encountered.

Best for: Lions, cheetahs and general game viewing.

Lower Sabie: an excellent all-rounder

Lower Sabie is one of the strongest choices if you want good all-round wildlife viewing.

The camp overlooks the Sabie River, which attracts animals to the water and acts as an important wildlife corridor.



Elephants, hippos, crocodiles, buffalo and antelope can all be seen around the river, while the surrounding roads offer opportunities for big-cat sightings.

Best for: Elephants, hippos, lions, leopards and general game viewing.

Skukuza: a good base for first-time visitors to Kruger National Park

As Kruger National Park’s largest rest camp, Skukuza is popular with first-time visitors.

Its position beside the Sabie River puts it close to some productive wildlife areas, while the extensive network of roads around the camp provides plenty of opportunities for self-drives.

The area can produce Big Five sightings, as well as elephants, hippos, crocodiles and a huge variety of birds.

Best for: Big Five and general wildlife viewing.

Letaba: elephant country

If elephants are at the top of your list, Letaba deserves serious consideration.

The camp sits alongside the Letaba River, an important water source for wildlife. The area is particularly well known for elephants, while buffalo, hippos, crocodiles and numerous antelope and bird species can also be found nearby.

Best for: Elephants and river wildlife.

Berg-en-Dal: a good choice for rhinos

In southwestern Kruger, Berg-en-Dal is particularly interesting for anyone hoping to see rhinos.

The surrounding granite hills and mixed vegetation provide suitable habitat for both black and white rhinos. Elephants, buffalo and other large mammals are also regularly encountered.

Best for: Rhino, elephants and buffalo.

Olifants: wildlife with a view

Olifants Rest Camp has one of the most spectacular settings in Kruger National Park, overlooking the Olifants River from high ground.

The river attracts elephants, hippos, crocodiles and buffalo, while the surrounding bush offers opportunities to see predators and other wildlife.

Even when the animals aren’t cooperating, the view is doing some heavy lifting.

Best for: Elephants, hippos, river wildlife and scenery.

Punda Maria: explore the quieter north

Punda Maria offers a very different experience from the busy southern camps.

The northern part of Kruger tends to be quieter and has different vegetation and wildlife habitats. Elephants, buffalo, giraffe, zebra and antelope can be seen, while the area is particularly attractive to birdwatchers. It’s also one of the cheaper options if you’re on a budget.

Best for: Birds, elephants and exploring northern Kruger.

Talamati: for a quieter safari

For visitors who prefer smaller camps and fewer people, Talamati is worth considering.

The camp overlooks a waterhole, giving visitors the chance to watch wildlife coming to drink. It doesn’t have the extensive facilities of Kruger’s major rest camps, but that’s part of its appeal.

Best for: Waterhole sightings and a quieter bush experience.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs injury update: Phili, Petersen, Da Silva, Mako
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs could have several players available when they face Stellenbosch FC in the Betway Premiership on Tuesday evening.

Amakhosi are looking to close the gap at the top of the table after dropping valuable points last month.

Fernando Da Cruz’s men find themselves seven points behind leaders Mamelodi Sundowns, although they have a game in hand.



Tuesday’s clash against Stellies at FNB Stadium will be an important test of their title ambitions. Anything less than three points could deal a significant blow to their hopes, with rivals Orlando Pirates also six points ahead of them.

Which Kaizer Chiefs players could be available?

A major boost for Chiefs could be the return of Langelihle Phili. The 21-year-old winger suffered an ankle injury during training and has missed two months of action.

Although he could be nearing full fitness, a return against his former club appears less likely.

Paseka Mako is another player who could be available for selection. The 32-year-old left-back has yet to feature in a match this season but has returned to training with the team.

Flavio Silva could also be in contention to lead the Kaizer Chiefs attack. The striker has missed the team’s recent matches but is reportedly fit and ready to return.

Silva was among Amakhosi’s standout signings last season, scoring nine goals, and his return would provide a welcome boost to the team’s attacking options.



Meanwhile, Brandon Petersen has recovered after missing the match against Golden Arrows before the FIFA international break.

The captain is expected to reclaim his place in goal, although Renaldo Leaner has given Da Cruz something to consider after keeping a clean sheet in Petersen’s absence.

Kaizer Chiefs will hope to have as many players as possible available as they prepare for a crucial encounter against Stellenbosch.

World.title: When is the cheapest time to visit Kruger National Park?
World.content:
The time of year you visit Kruger can make a difference to your budget. Image: wikimedia commons

A Kruger National Park holiday can get expensive, particularly during peak periods when demand for accommodation is high.

But travellers looking to save money can often get better value by choosing the right time of year.

So, when is the cheapest time to visit Kruger National Park?

The summer and shoulder-season months are generally the best bet for budget travellers.



Kruger’s rainy season runs from October to March, while the dry season lasts from April to September. SANParks notes that the dry winter months traditionally offer the best game viewing because vegetation becomes thinner and animals are more concentrated around available water.

That popularity can make the dry-season period more desirable for visitors.

The warmer, wetter months can therefore offer an opportunity for travellers who are more focused on lower prices and fewer crowds than on peak game-viewing conditions.



January to March can be good for bargain hunters

The first few months of the year are worth looking at if price is your priority.

SANParks has previously offered discounted accommodation during parts of January to March, and its 2026 pensioner concession, for example, included 21 January to 20 March at participating Kruger camps.

The exact discounts don’t apply to every visitor, however, so ordinary travellers should check the accommodation rate for their chosen dates rather than assuming a particular percentage reduction.



The weather is also hot and wet, with more vegetation making some animals harder to spot.

April and May offer a useful compromise

If you want better game viewing without necessarily travelling during the busiest winter period, April and May can be worth considering.

The rains begin to ease, the landscape remains relatively green, and temperatures become more comfortable. The park moves towards its dry season, when wildlife viewing traditionally improves.



June to August is one of the most popular periods for a Kruger National Park safari. The weather is generally dry and pleasant during the day, while sparse vegetation and limited water make wildlife easier to find.

The downside is that this is also a particularly attractive time to visit, so budget accommodation can be harder to secure.

If you’re travelling during these months, booking well in advance is important.



September and October can be another sweet spot for budget Kruger National Park visitors

Late winter and early spring can offer a useful balance between weather, wildlife and price. The park begins warming up, while the landscape is still relatively dry.

By October, however, the rainy season starts to return, with SANParks describing October to March as Kruger National Park’s rainy season.

But the cheapest dates aren’t necessarily determined by the weather alone.



Weekdays can be cheaper and easier to book than weekends, while school holidays and long weekends can increase demand.

SANParks’ senior-citizen concession dates also show how its discounted periods can change from year to year, with certain dates, camps and accommodation types specifically included or excluded.

So if you’re trying to save, compare several dates rather than simply choosing an entire month.



So, when should you book?

SANParks currently has bookings open into 2027, with booking periods changing periodically. The current booking period runs through 31 August 2027, with another booking window opening in October 2026 for stays through October 2027.

For popular camps, especially during school holidays and the dry season, booking early is the safest way to secure the accommodation you want.

World.title: Four killed in KwaMsane tavern
World.content:
ESHOWE – A police constable allegedly shot and killed three women and injured a man before turning the gun on himself at a tavern in KwaMsane, KwaZulu-Natal.

Police spokesperson Robert Netshiunda said police responded to reports of a shooting at a liquor establishment at Nkodibe area in KwaMsane, and when they arrived they found four bodies with gunshot wounds, and one victim with a gunshot wound who was taken to hospital.

“It was reported that the off-duty police constable also disarmed another man of his firearm during the incident. Both firearms were found at the scene. The cause of the shooting is unknown at this stage.”

In a separate incident, police in Eshowe are tracing a suspect who allegedly shot and killed three people at a grocery chain store in Eshowe on Saturday.

“Reports indicate that the suspect, who is former employee of the store, had gone to the store for his internal disciplinary hearing. The suspect allegedly produced a firearm and shot three people who were declared dead at the scene. A manhunt for the suspect is underway.”

World.title: SANDF arrives in Durban
World.content:
DURBAN - The army has been spotted in Durban, KwaZulu-Natal, amid tensions over asylum applications and illegal immigration.

Protests erupted after the Constitutional Court ruling that everyone must be given a fair chance to apply for asylum, regardless of documentation.

Violent unrest led to looting and the torching of vehicles.

Government has called for calm as tensions simmer.

World.title: Joburg Water warns of possible outages
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A power outage at the Zuikerbosch Water Treatment Plant has crippled pumping at the Palmiet Booster Station.

Johannesburg Water warns that parts of Sandton, Diepsloot, Rabie Ridge, and surrounding areas could face low water pressure or total outages.

The utility said it is monitoring the system and taking steps to stabilise supply.

Residents are urged to use water sparingly.

World.title: ‘Captured’ casts spotlight on prison life
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - Ex-Pollsmoor Correctional Centre inmates are using visual art to depict the realities of life behind bars.

This they say helps them deal with past trauma, their reintegration into society, and also to make a living.

Dubbed "Captured", the visual storytelling project, is set to eventually become a coffee table book.

Life behind bars is often reduced to statistics, without the human factor.

Enrico Samuels, an artist, served sixteen years behind bars for armed robbery said art connected him with people helping him to navigate life now as a free man.

"I want to become a successful artist, doctor is helping me to get there with the projects...lovely projects and I enjoy myself in the projects and from there I see a brighter future from doc's side, because she is taking me that way, so I can see the sun on the other side already,” said Samuels.

Michael Sauls said art serves as a conduit in helping them deal with their past and educate the public.

“People have no an idea of what prison is like, they think that everything is happy go-lucky or it's like a journey to another paradise, it's not worth it being there...you see it's easy to commit a crime, but it's not easy serving the time."

Dr Suzette Leal, the founder of Words Set Free, said the art tells the stories of the people behind it.

"If you say the work is beautiful, that's a complement to our artists and their ability, but the story is not beautiful. It's real and true and painful and traumatic. So, I think if anything I hope it discourages someone from getting involved in crime, but I think we don't reduce crime by making prison sentences longer or by making the conditions within them worse. We reduce crime by creating opportunities for people to create a livelihood outside of crime.”

Another artist, Kleinbooi Hendricks said: "I said to myself, although the parole board gave me a date to go out of prison, I'm not going. I will either complete my entire sentence but I'm not going out if I haven't worked on myself being a changed man or a different person. I did that because I said I'd either eat out of a dustbin outside, but I'm not going to commit crime again."

World.title: Change living conditions – Ndlozi
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Real change begins with communities taking responsibility for their own development.

Those are the views of Dr Mbuyiseni Ndlozi, Founder of the Batho Pele Convention.

The initiative calls on South Africans to take the lead in improving their own living conditions.

“We are here to say you are the solution you are looking for. We are here to say you are the saviour, the developer, the healer and the builder you are looking for. We are here to vote for you to do it on your own.

“We are here to say you are the saviours you are looking for. We are not a corporate think tank. Long have we interpreted our misery from broadcast to podcast, think shops to talk shops.

“The point is to change our living conditions, one pothole at a time, one classroom at a time and one production hub at a time,” Ndlozi said.

World.title: Repairs delay Joburg's pool reopenings
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Johannesburg's public pools are missing out on the summer rush.

And most are still closed despite the rising temperatures.

Community leader Dulton Adams said poor planning, lack of proper budgeting and no clear management plans, are leaving residents without these facilities.

The city has 57 public pools, but only 13 are open so far.

Ten more are expected to open on Monday.

"Every season there's just no budget.

There's just no management plan. There's no vision to make sure that the children come off the streets and you look at the pool. This is not the only pool.

"Remember spring day, pools must open first. Then the City Council asked for 1 October, pools would be open. That was missed and then now the 7th," Adams said.

World.title: ‘ANC could be the biggest loser’ - political strategist
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The ANC could emerge as the biggest loser in this year's municipal elections.

This is the view is political strategist Brutus Malada.

He said the party’s declining support could leave it with less influence across key metros and this could push it into a weakened position ahead of the 2029 elections.

“ANC will be the big loser in this. The trend is clear. It's clear that they are losing at a margin of 10 to 12 percent and that will actually mean the end of the ANC and it will become lame duck for this period in between the two elections.

“That it will sit, it will be a national government President Ramaphosa sitting in Tshwane. The Union Buildings which is led by another party and in Cape Town which is the legislative arm of the state which is led by the DA.

“So here is a political party that is running the country as the head of the State but it has no control of the economy hub, it has no control of administrative hub, it has no control of legislative hub,” Malada said.

World.title: Murdered teen twins buried in Mamelodi
World.content:
Mamelodi – The family and friends of the slain 14-year-old twins have gathered in Mamelodi West to bid farewell to the boys.

Bonolo and Botlhale Makena were found dead in their home a week ago. They had multiple stab wounds.

The boys' mother made the gruesome discovery at home, when she returned from work.

As police investigate, residents are demanding that this case does not become another unresolved killing.

Neighobour Padi Matlala said the Mamelodi West community is demanding justice.

“The community has been here before. The community is saying, ‘please justice system, don't take us there.’ We were there in 1982. Two members of the community were brutally murdered. 44 years later, nobody has been held responsible.

“The community is saying justice system never, never again should you go through this. The pressure that you put on the government throughout the week, the outrage you showed must bear fruit. Somebody or some people must be held responsible for this. We are better than this,” Matlala said.

World.title: Ebola: Why Ministry has suspended hotel meetings, conferences
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Ministry officials brief the country on the first imported case of Ebola at Afya House on Tuesday, October 6, 2026. [Jonah Onyango, Standard]

The Ministry of Health has suspended hotel-based meetings, conferences and seminars for its staff following Kenya’s confirmation of its first Ebola case.

In a circular seen by The Standard, the ministry said the move was intended to prioritise emergency preparedness, contact tracing and response measures to prevent further spread of the disease.

“All meetings, seminars and conferences scheduled to be held in hotels are suspended with immediate effect from Wednesday, October 7, 2026, until further notice. Any exception shall require prior approval,” Health Principal Secretary Mary Muthoni said.

The directive applies only to Ministry of Health staff and does not amount to a blanket suspension of government meetings and seminars held in hotels.

“For avoidance of doubt, this measure does not constitute a blanket suspension of government meetings or seminars held in hotels,” the ministry said in a notice to newsrooms.

Kenya confirmed its first imported case of Ebola on October 6, involving a citizen who travelled by road from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) to Uganda before flying to Nairobi.

The patient presented symptoms consistent with Ebola, including fever, chills, extreme fatigue, muscle pain and bleeding under the skin.

After testing positive for the Bundibugyo virus, the patient was treated at Nairobi Hospital but died on Monday evening. He was buried on Tuesday in accordance with public health guidelines.

As of Saturday, October 10, at least 60 contacts had been traced, while 10 people had been placed in quarantine.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale has assured the public that Kenya has not experienced an Ebola outbreak, adding that the country remains open to travel, tourism and trade.

World.title: Kalonzo to Ruto: You have no numbers
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka speaks during launch of economic empowerment equipment distribution at Kenyatta Stadium in Machakos town on October 9, 2026. [John Muia, Standard]

The united opposition will deal President William Ruto a humiliating defeat in next year’s general election, Wiper Party leader Kalonzo Musyoka has predicted.

Speaking Friday in his Ukambani backyard during an empowerment equipment handover ceremony hosted by Governor Wavinya Ndeti at the Kenyatta Stadium in Machakos, Kalonzo declared the opposition will defeat Ruto at the ballot ‘no matter what magic he (Ruto) deploys.

“Ruto has been cornered. We have heard him suggesting that they will import foreigners from neighboring countries to vote for him but even so, he will not secure the numbers. We in the united opposition have committed to produce a single candidate that will face Ruto at the ballot,” Kalonzo said.

Recognizing the need to consolidate his lower Eastern vote bloc, Kalonzo rallied the Akamba community to come out in huge numbers to register as voters in the upcoming voter listing initiative by the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC).

“It is the time to redeem this country. The IEBC will as from next month undertake the final leg of voter registration and I urge all eligible voters to apply for national identity cards and register as voters,” he said, vowing he will defeat Ruto in Luo Nyanza.

Kalonzo called out Ruto over what he termed as the president’s habit of making empty promises to Kenyans. “The other day I heard Ruto promising thousands of dams across the country. He should come for benchmarking in Machakos. Retired President Mwai Kibaki and I secured African Development Bank (ADB) funding for the construction of Yatta Dam and now he has ten months left in office. When will he build?” he posed.

Former Attorney General Justin Muturi, who flanked Kalonzo, declared time was fast running out for the opposition to identify and name its presidential flag bearer for the next year’s general election.

The DP party leader, who has gone public declaring his choice of Kalonzo as the presidential ticket bearer for the opposition expressed his frustrations for the opposition’s dillydallying in naming its flag bearer.

“We (the opposition) are tired of singing one song for years that we will produce and name one person to face Ruto. When you see us here another day, do not entertain such kind of talk. Demand that it is Kalonzo for State House,” said Muturi.

During the ceremony, Governor Wavinya Ndeti unveiled assorted empowerment equipment targeting about 6000 beneficiaries across the county.

Addressing residents during the forum, Wavinya jeered at UDA-allied politicians who have been dishing out cash handouts to residents, terming it untenable.

“It is time to demonstrate to those who are approaching our people with cheap hand-outs that when the people of Machakos are given the tools to work, they produce real wealth. My commitment is that I will continue allocating resources to asset-based empowerment until every household in Machakos enjoys economic dignity,” Wavinya said.

World.title: Revealed: 84 Kenyans killed, 52 missing in Russia-Ukraine war
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi. [File,Standard]

The government has records of 354 Kenyans linked to the Russia-Ukraine war, including 84 classified as killed or missing in action and five being held as prisoners of war in Ukraine.

Prime Cabinet Secretary and Foreign and Diaspora Affairs Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi gave the updated figures in a response to Parliament on the recruitment of Kenyans into the Russian military and the detention of Kenyans in Ukraine on Thursday, October 8.

The records show that 77 Kenyans remain on the front lines, 38 are in camps, 52 have an unknown or unclassified location and 34 are hospitalised.

Another 62 Kenyans have been repatriated, while one is in detention and another has completed a military contract.

The government said Russia has stopped the enlistment of additional Kenyans after Kenya secured the country’s placement on Russia’s ‘Stop List’ during Mudavadi’s visit to Moscow in March.

“The Embassy of Kenya in Moscow has since confirmed that no additional Kenyan nationals have been enlisted in the Special Military Operation following the implementation of the Stop List,” Mudavadi said.

Russian authorities have told Kenya that requests to terminate military contracts will be considered on a case-by-case basis by individual military unit commanders.

Mudavadi said Kenya continues to engage Russian authorities and affected families over the burial, cremation or repatriation of remains after Russia said its Defence Ministry could not meet the cost of repatriating the remains of deceased Kenyans.

Five Kenyans held in Ukraine

Five Kenyan nationals are currently being held as prisoners of war in Ukraine, according to information sent to Kenya by the Ukrainian Embassy in Vienna on September 3.

The government identified them as Evans Kibet, detained since May 2025; Willi Muniu Macharia, detained since November 2025; Haron Kibet Pachenge, detained since March 2026; Joseph, detained since April 2026; and Francis Ndarua Ndungu.

Kenya’s Honorary Consul in Ukraine visited the Zakhid 1 prisoner-of-war camp and reported that the detainees were being held in humane conditions, had access to medical services and were being treated under rules governing prisoners of war.

The government also said Ukraine was holding the remains of four other Kenyans.

They are Simon Gitau, Clinton Nyapara Mogesa, Dennis Bagaka Obwori and Eric Mwangi Nyambura.

Kenya is seeking the release and repatriation of the affected Kenyans through diplomatic channels, including engagement with Ukraine and the International Committee of the Red Cross.

The government wants Kenyans held as prisoners of war to be considered as possible victims of international human trafficking.

Mudavadi said many of the affected Kenyans reported that recruiters lured them with promises of employment before they ended up in military service.

The government says the circumstances surrounding their recruitment could fit the definition of trafficking under Article 3(a) of the Protocol to Prevent, Suppress and Punish Trafficking in Persons, also known as the Palermo Protocol.

It wants the issue considered during negotiations over their repatriation so the Kenyans can access assistance available to trafficking victims.

President William Ruto has also raised the matter directly with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy during a telephone conversation, according to the government.

Kenya has further received approval from Kyiv for its ambassador to Ukraine, with the government saying this will improve its ability to respond to cases involving Kenyans in the country.

The State Department for Diaspora Affairs said families should report cases to the government as soon as communication with relatives in Russia is disrupted.

Once a family reports a case, the department collects identification details, travel information and next-of-kin contacts before referring the case to the Kenyan Embassy in Moscow for verification.

The government has also facilitated the return of 62 Kenyans who had been involved in Russia’s military operations.

It has provided affected families with updates from diplomatic missions, information on compensation processes, psychosocial support and guidance on the repatriation or burial of remains.

The government said it is also expanding measures to prevent deceptive recruitment by providing pre-departure information, urging Kenyans to verify recruitment agencies and employment offers and strengthening emergency assistance through Kenyan diplomatic missions.

The scale of the recruitment first emerged publicly in February when Parliament was told that more than 1,000 Kenyans had been recruited to fight for Russia.

The National Intelligence Service report presented to lawmakers said recruiters targeted former security personnel and civilians with promises of lucrative employment, salaries and bonuses.

The figures at the time included 89 Kenyans on the frontline, 39 hospitalised, 28 missing in action, 35 in camps or bases, 30 repatriated, one detained and one who had completed a contract.

The government then stepped up diplomatic efforts. In March, Kenya announced an agreement with Russia to stop further enlistment of Kenyans into its military operations and to facilitate consular support and voluntary disengagement for Kenyans already serving.

The issue remains unresolved for many families. More than 30 families affected by the recruitment were reported this week to be seeking a meeting with President Ruto before Kenya's delegation travels to Moscow for the Russia-Africa Summit, demanding answers on missing relatives, repatriation of survivors and the return of remains.

World.title: Wajir patient isolated over suspected viral haemorrhagic fever
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The patient, a resident of Habaswein in Wajir South Sub-County, is currently admitted at Albadar Nursing Home. [File, Standard]

A 20-year-old man in Habaswein, Wajir County, has been isolated after presenting with symptoms consistent with a suspected viral haemorrhagic fever, following recent travel from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

The patient, a resident of Habaswein in Wajir South Sub-County, is currently admitted at Albadar Nursing Home, where he is being treated after developing fever, headache and cough. He was also found to have severe anaemia, with a haemoglobin level of 4g/dL.

According to a disease surveillance report filed at Habaswein Police Station, the patient told health officials that he had recently travelled to the DRC, where he worked as a “tan boy” on a cargo truck or trailer.

He reportedly developed fever and headache while still in the DRC on September 2, 2026, before traveling by trailer to Uganda, where he stayed for about five days and sought medical attention.

The report states that he was treated with antibiotics in Uganda before travelling by trailer to Malaba. From Malaba, he travelled by motorcycle to a relative's residence, where he stayed for approximately five days.

He later travelled by trailer to Nairobi and proceeded by bus to Isiolo, where he stayed for about 10 days before travelling to Habaswein by Probox vehicle. He arrived in the town around September 20.

Upon arrival, the patient sought treatment at Hilac Medical Clinic, where he was managed for pneumonia and septicaemia for about three days.

However, his condition did not improve and he was subsequently transferred to Albadar Nursing Home, where he remains admitted.

The report adds that the patient is receiving intravenous Augmentin and paracetamol and has been transfused with two units of whole blood.

“Despite the above interventions, the patient remains clinically unwell and sick-looking,” the report states.

Authorities have since placed the patient in isolation as investigations continue to establish the cause of his illness.

“Sample collection has been completed, and the specimen will be shipped to National Public Health Laboratories tonight,” the report states.

World.title: Complainant letters cannot be used to initiate judge's removal, court rules
World.content:
Chief Justice Martha Koome. [File]

A letter addressed to the Chief Justice seeking administrative intervention cannot form the basis for removing a judge, the Employment and Labour Relations Court (ELRC) has ruled.

Delivering a unanimous judgment in a case filed by Environment and Land Court Judge Anthony Ombwayo, a three-judge ELRC bench comprising Justices Jemimah Keli, Onesmus Makau, and Dr. Jacob Gikeri ruled that a letter written to the Chief Justice cannot simply be forwarded to the Judicial Service Commission (JSC) and treated as a petition for removal.

World.title: How KNEC plans to stop cheating in 2026 exams
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The Kenya National Examinations Council (KNEC) Chief Executive Officer Dr David Njengere. [File]

The Kenya National Examinations Council (KNEC) will use smart padlocks to secure all examination storage containers as more than 3.6 million candidates sit the 2026 national examinations and assessments.

KNEC Chief Executive Officer Dr David Njengere said the council would monitor the containers from its headquarters to prevent anyone from accessing examination papers before the scheduled times.

“Last year KNEC piloted the use of smart padlocks in 250 containers. This year all containers will be secured using the smart padlocks which will be monitored from the KNEC headquarters,” said Dr Njengere.

Under the system, officials will open containers at designated times. Officials will access Kenya Primary School Education Assessment (KPSEA) and Kenya Junior School Education Assessment (KJSEA) papers at 6 a.m., while centre managers will collect Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education (KCSE) papers at 7 a.m. and 12:30 p.m.

However, Dr Njengere identified mobile phones as the biggest challenge in preventing examination malpractice.

“Mobile phones remain our biggest challenge in administration of KCSE examination,” observed Dr Njengere.

He warned that the council would not allow candidates or examination officials to have mobile phones at examination centres during examination sessions.

“Any contravention of this rule will constitute a malpractice as per the KNEC Act and the Rules and Regulations,” noted Dr Njengere.

The council will deploy 342,005 contracted professionals to administer and manage the examinations and assessments. They include centre managers, supervisors, invigilators, security officers and drivers.

For KCSE, KNEC will deploy 10,765 centre managers, 12,274 supervisors, 57,432 invigilators and 21,388 security officers. Each examination centre will have at least two police officers.

Centre managers will collect KCSE papers twice a day, and KNEC will place morning and afternoon papers in marked cartons to reduce mix-ups and unauthorised access.

KNEC has personalised question papers with candidates’ details, and examiners will receive anonymised scripts with those details removed.

The 2026 examination and assessment season will involve 3,634,846 candidates, a 6.13 per cent increase from the 3,424,836 registered in 2025.

KCSE rehearsals will take place on Friday, October 16. Examinations for papers with low candidature will run from Monday, October 19 to Friday, October 30, while papers with large candidature will run from Monday, November 2 to Friday, November 20.

KPSEA and KJSEA assessments will run from Monday, October 26 to Friday, October 30.

KNEC Chairperson Prof. Julius Nyabundi said the council was preparing for possible disruption from El Nino rains.

“As we start off the 2026 field administration season, one of the risks we contend with are the attempts to cheat in assessments and examination,” said Prof. Nyabundi.

He urged candidates, parents and examination officials to protect the integrity of the examinations, warning that malpractice could undermine public confidence in the education system.

“Cheating in examinations undermines public confidence in the credibility, fairness and quality of the entire education system,” noted Prof. Nyabundi.

KNEC will operate a 24-hour call centre with toll-free numbers for candidates, officials and members of the public to report incidents and seek assistance during the examination period.

The 2026 cycle will continue the implementation of Competency-Based Education assessments, including School-Based Assessments in primary, junior and senior school.

Grade 10 learners are undertaking their first School-Based Assessment, which will contribute 15 marks towards the Kenya Certificate of Basic Education.

World.title: Mbadi hits out at Sifuna, says opposition lacks economic agenda
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

National Treasury CS John Mbadi after opening new classrooms and administration blocks constructed by the M-Pesa Foundation at Ligongo Primary School in Suba South Constituency. [James Omoro, Standard]

The National Treasury CS John Mbadi has hit out at Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna, saying that criticising President William Ruto should not be an agenda for a presidential candidate.

Speaking when he opened new classrooms and administration blocks constructed by M-Pesa Foundation at Ligongo Primary School in Suba South Constituency, Mbadi said lack of economic agenda makes the opposition unsuitable to lead the country.

“I have heard of opposition leaders who want the presidency, but they do not have an agenda for the economic transformation of this country,” he said.

The CS claimed that none of the opposition leaders is suitable for the presidency.

“These opposition leaders cannot make any economic change in this country. They should not be elected,” he said.

He told Nyanza residents to shun the new wave of opposition led by Sifuna.

Mbadi claimed that opposition leaders lack political direction.

He said Sifuna had taken too long to unveil a political party that he will use to run for the presidency.

“Do not join the opposition bandwagon. We are just a few months away from the General Election, but Sifuna still doesn’t know a political party he will use to run for the presidency. They are still leaving in confusion,” Mbadi said.

He said Sifuna has not demonstrated how to improve this country’s economy.

“Former President Uhuru Kenyatta left the economy of this country in tatters. We have tried to improve it but we are not yet where we want it to be,” Mbadi said.

He urged Nyanza residents to support Ruto.

The CS said Ruto’s government had improved mega infrastructural projects across the country as part of economic transformation.

He cited the 74 km Mbita- Sindo- Sori road, Lake Victoria ring road and other infrastructure projects as some of the reasons residents should support Ruto.

“I urge you to support Ruto so that we can continue acquiring more development projects in this region,” Mbadi said.

World.title: Kericho Annex Prison under scrutiny over death of remand prisoner
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Brenda Chemutai, 19, who allegedly committed suicide inside the Kericho Annex Prison where she was awaiting trial for an offence of being in possession of bhang that was seized in a vehicle allegedly belonging to a senior police officer. [Courtesy]

Questions are mounting over security and accountability at Kericho Annex Prison following the death of a 19-year-old remand prisoner in a suspected case of suicide.

Her family is demanding answers about how she obtained a bedsheet and why they were not notified until nearly 10 hours after the incident.

Brenda Chemutai was reportedly found hanging from a double-decker bed at around 9 am when her fellow cellmates were having breakfast on Friday.

The cell had eight inmates, who had gone for breakfast, according to a police report.

However, her relatives state they were not informed until about 7 pm, after her body had already been taken from the prison and transferred to the Kericho County Hospital Mortuary.

The delay has raised serious concerns for the family, which calls for authorities to clarify what happened between the time Chemutai was discovered and when her next of kin were contacted.

Kericho East Directorate of Criminal Investigation (DCI) officer, Kennedy Apindi, said police have launched investigations following reports from prison officials that the incident was a suicide.

He mentioned that preliminary information indicated Chemutai allegedly used a bedsheet.

The family, however, insists that investigators determine when she was found, who discovered her, when the incident was reported to police, who authorised her body’s removal, and why her relatives were not notified immediately.

“We had spoken with Brenda. She was expected to be released around December, and by January we would all have been together at home,” said her sister, Phyllis Cherotich.

Cherotich added that the family had seen no signs indicating Chemutai intended to take her own life.

"Her death has shocked us deeply. She never mentioned any plans of this nature. We want to understand how this was possible given the level of security at the facility," she said.

The circumstances surrounding the alleged use of a bedsheet have also raised questions for the family.

Her uncle, Michael Rono, questioned how such an item came into Chemutai's possession while she was in a remand facility.

"I am deeply surprised. When one enters the prison, one is carefully searched. Where did the bedsheet come from? We ask the government to ensure justice is done," Rono said.

Chemutai had been in remand since 2024, with her relatives saying she was arrested while still a minor and had spent nearly two years awaiting the conclusion of her case.

She was being tried for the offence of possession of bhang in a vehicle allegedly belonging to a senior police officer.

Her death has consequently brought renewed scrutiny to not only what happened inside the prison but also the circumstances that led to her prolonged detention.

Youth activists from the Voice of Youth Organisation, led by Kelvin Kipchichir, have joined the family in demanding investigations into both the death and the case that resulted in Chemutai's detention.

Kipchichir claimed Chemutai was arrested alongside other suspects in a vehicle allegedly linked to an Officer Commanding Station serving in Kakamega.

According to the activists, police recovered 32 rolls of bhang from the vehicle, while some of the suspects allegedly fled, leaving Chemutai behind.

The claims have not been independently established.

Kipchichir questioned why Chemutai remained in custody for such a prolonged period and called for scrutiny of the circumstances surrounding the vehicle and its alleged connection to the police officer.

“We are concerned that an OCS in the National Police Service could allow a vehicle to be used by an individual with a known criminal record,” he said.

He called on the Ministry of Interior to establish who owned or controlled the vehicle and under what circumstances it was allegedly being used.

The activists said the vehicle was still at Kericho Police Station.

For the family, the tragedy has been compounded by personal loss. Chemutai's father died while she was in remand, while she leaves behind a young child.

Relatives said detectives had informed them that the person alleged to own the bhang had since been arrested and was being held in Kisumu.

But the immediate question for Chemutai's family is what happened during her final hours.

They want a clear account of the period between the reported discovery of her body at about 9 am and the notification of the family nearly 10 hours later.
