World.title: Government cars go electric as Hichilema restores fuel duty and targets ERB pricing
World.content:
All government institutions will from now on buy only electric vehicles, President Hakainde Hichilema has announced. He said the change is needed because conflicts abroad have made global fuel supply unstable. Opening the First Session of the 14th National Assembly in Lusaka on Friday, he also confirmed that excise duty on fuel has been restored this month. He said the Energy Regulation Board’s monthly pricing mechanism will be reviewed, adding: “Personally, I don’t like it.”

“This is a fundamental change so that we can reduce the demand side for fuel,” the President told MPs. “Unless it is not practicable, you will have to drive an electric vehicle in Government and public institutions.”

Government will invest in charging infrastructure across the country in partnership with the private sector. Mr Hichilema urged businesses, cooperating partners and citizens to join the move to what he called cleaner, more affordable and self-reliant transport.

Why the tax break ended

The announcement came with a frank account of the past year at the pump. Global conflicts, the President said, feed directly into the price of fuel in Zambia. “As we have often said, instability anywhere is instability everywhere,” he told the House.

To shield motorists, Government had taken what he called unprecedented steps, including temporarily removing taxes on fuel. Those measures assumed that the global market would settle quickly. It did not.

Government has since reviewed its position on fuel tax waivers to protect its spending commitments. The President named four programmes: free education, the Constituency Development Fund, the School Feeding Programme and the Social Cash Transfer. “As a result of this review, excise duty has been restored on fuel this month,” he said.

He promised further measures to keep fuel prices competitive and supply secure.

The pricing formula under review

The ERB’s monthly fuel price review will be looked at again. It is one of the most closely watched announcements in the country, and the President made his own view clear.

“I must say, personally, I don’t like it,” Mr Hichilema said. He added that the issue needs to be addressed “so that we can bring a little bit more stability and a predictable pricing environment in the economy.”

His written address framed the review as part of a wider aim: a secure, predictable and efficient petroleum supply system.

Four pipelines and more depots

On supply, the President said Government will “aggressively” pursue four pipeline projects:

the Angola–Zambia pipeline

the Namibia–Zambia refined-petroleum and natural-gas pipelines

the Tanzania–Zambia multiproduct pipeline

the Zimbabwe–Zambia pipeline

The aim is to end the country’s reliance on a single supply route. He said the projects would also create jobs, business opportunities and Treasury revenue.

Existing fuel depots in Chipata, Lusaka, Mansa, Mpika, Mongu, Ndola and Solwezi will be put to full use, and new depots will be built in other provinces to increase storage capacity. Government will also strengthen management of the TAZAMA open-access system so that it stays competitive and helps bring down the cost of petroleum products.

The Ministry of Energy has been told to implement the fuel-blending strategy “without delay”. The President said blending will cut the fuel import bill and support the local ethanol industry. Public-private partnerships and joint ventures will be used to speed up all of these projects.

Power for the new fleet

Electric vehicles need electricity, and the President restated his target of 10,000 megawatts of generating capacity. During the first term, he said, Government expanded thermal and solar generation, and the take-up of solar by households and institutions has added to supply.

He said the State cannot close the gap alone. Private and citizen-led investment in generation will be encouraged. The national transmission network will be upgraded, and connecting the grid to regional power pools is now “critical”, with a call for more private participation in transmission and distribution.

One large project is already lined up on the Copperbelt. Mpongwe District is to host a US$519 million solar plant with a capacity of 500 megawatts, to be built by EnerSynk Solar Energy Limited in the Kashitu area under Chieftainess Malembeka.

The plant will cover 615 hectares and be built in three phases over 18 months. District Commissioner Mwambashi Mwitwa said it is expected to create more than 1,000 direct jobs.

“This project will bring massive investment, create jobs for our people and boost our local economy,” Mr Mwitwa said.

The plant will feed into the national grid through the Kabwe–Kitwe 330-kilovolt line and is designed to run for 25 years, reducing reliance on hydropower in dry years. It received approvals from the ERB and the Attorney-General in July. EnerSynk and ZESCO signed a 25-year power purchase agreement on 15 September.

What happens next

The address did not set a date for the ERB review or a timetable for the electric-vehicle rule. It also did not say what happens to vehicles already in the government fleet.

Those details are expected to come through the Ministry of Energy and the 2027 Budget. The President asked the House to support that Budget, saying it will set out how Government intends to finance its development plans.

World.title: Nigeria: American Lobbying Firms Disagree Over $57m U.S. Lawsuit Against Tinubu
World.content:
DCI Group has rejected allegations in a $57 million US lawsuit against President Bola Tinubu and others, while Femi Fani-Kayode's office says he has not been formally served.

American lobbying firm DCI Group has rejected allegations made by Washington-based lobbyist Karl Von Batten in a $57 million lawsuit against President Bola Tinubu, the Federal Government of Nigeria, former aviation minister Femi Fani-Kayode and the firm.

DCI has been hired by the Nigerian government for lobbying activities in the United States, while Mr Von Batten is doing the same work for former Vice President Atiku Abubakar.

Mr Fani-Kayode's office also told PREMIUM TIMES that he had not been formally served with the court papers and maintained his earlier denial of the allegations.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The case, filed at the United States District Court for the District of Columbia on 28 September, concerns allegations of defamation and a conspiracy to kidnap and physically harm Mr Von Batten. The claims are disputed and have not been established by a court.

DCI, Fani-Kayode respond

In an email to PREMIUM TIMES on Wednesday, Craig Stevens of DCI Group dismissed the allegations.

"Mr. Von Batten's allegations are so far past unfounded that they reach the point of the absurd," Mr Stevens said.

He said DCI's work for the Nigerian government focused on strengthening relations between Nigeria and US policymakers and referred the newspaper to the firm's disclosures under the Foreign Agents Registration Act.

Mr Stevens did not address the specific allegations individually.

Mr Fani-Kayode's office, responding separately, answered "No" when asked whether the former minister had been formally served. It also confirmed that he stood by his earlier denial of the allegations.

Mr Fani-Kayode had previously indicated that he would pursue a $100 million counterclaim against Mr Von Batten.

Asked whether the counterclaim had been filed or lawyers instructed to commence proceedings, his office replied: "All in good time."

The response did not confirm any filing.

What the lawsuit alleges

The US federal court docket identifies the case as Von Batten v. Tinubu et al., No. 1:26-cv-03374, before Judge Randolph D. Moss.

The defendants include President Tinubu, the Federal Government of Nigeria, Mr Fani-Kayode, DCI Group AZ, LLC, and 10 unidentified persons.

In a public announcement, Von Batten-Montague-York said it was seeking $36 million jointly from President Tinubu and the Nigerian government, $3 million from Mr Fani-Kayode and $18 million from DCI.

The firm alleged that the defendants were involved in efforts to defame, kidnap or physically harm Mr Von Batten over his advocacy concerning US government records relating to President Tinubu.

Close 

The publicly accessible docket records the filing and issuance of summonses, although this does not establish that the defendants have been formally served.

PREMIUM TIMES has requested the complete file-stamped complaint and exhibits to examine the allegations and the damages sought.

Presidency, others yet to respond

PREMIUM TIMES contacted the Presidency through Bayo Onanuga, Special Adviser to President Tinubu on Information and Strategy, seeking its response to the allegations, confirmation of any formal service and its position on the court's jurisdiction.

The enquiries were sent by email and WhatsApp, followed by telephone contact and reminders.

The newspaper also contacted Mr Atiku's ADC campaign to establish whether the former vice president or his representatives knew about the lawsuit before it was filed and whether they endorsed its allegations.

The campaign was further asked about the status of Mr Atiku's $1.2 million lobbying agreement with Mr Von Batten's firm, payments made and their source.

Mr Von Batten was separately contacted for the full complaint, supporting documents and his response to the denials by DCI and Mr Fani-Kayode. PREMIUM TIMES also sought clarification on the alleged threats, the damages claimed and whether the incidents had been reported to US law-enforcement authorities.

During a telephone call to his firm's office on Thursday, an answering-service representative took the reporter's contact details and said the enquiry would be forwarded.

By the time this report was filed, the Presidency, the ADC campaign and Mr Von Batten had not provided substantive responses.

World.title: Kenya: U.S. Report Flags Kenya's Failure to Act On Officials Linked to Human Trafficking
World.content:
Nairobi — Kenya has failed to report meaningful enforcement action against public officials and recruitment agencies allegedly linked to human trafficking, with a new United States report warning that official complicity continues to undermine the country's efforts to prosecute the crime.

The 2026 Trafficking in Persons Report said Kenyan authorities investigated three Ministry of Labour officials suspected of accepting bribes to facilitate potential trafficking involving migrant workers travelling to the Middle East, but highlighted broader concerns over alleged collusion between public officials and recruitment networks.

The report also found that the government had not reported action against recruitment agencies allegedly owned by government employees and suspected of facilitating trafficking, with authorities frequently pursuing lesser offences such as failure to register recruitment companies.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"Corruption and official complicity in trafficking crimes remained significant concerns, inhibiting law enforcement action during the year," the report stated.

The findings raise questions about accountability within institutions responsible for regulating overseas recruitment and protecting Kenyans seeking employment abroad.

Media reports cited in the assessment indicated that more than 10 per cent of Kenyan government officials held ownership interests in private employment agencies, including firms recruiting migrant workers for jobs overseas, creating potential conflicts of interest.

Observers also alleged that criminal syndicates colluded with law enforcement and immigration departments at border checkpoints and airports to transport trafficking victims into and within Kenya.

The report further cited allegations that some Kenyan embassy officials in Saudi Arabia demanded sex or cash payments from women seeking government assistance to escape abusive employers and return home.

The allegations come against the backdrop of declining anti-trafficking prosecutions and convictions.

Kenya convicted six traffickers in 2025, down from 21 in 2024, while prosecutions fell from 44 cases to 14.

The government investigated 43 trafficking cases during the year, compared with 42 in 2024.

The report also detailed allegations involving the fraudulent recruitment of more than 1,000 Kenyan men to fight for the Russian military in the war against Ukraine, with officials reporting that Kenyan and Russian officials had colluded with illicit recruiters to facilitate the recruitment.

Despite the concerns, Kenya remained on Tier 2 in the US assessment, which recognises significant efforts to combat trafficking while finding that the government has not fully met the minimum standards for eliminating the crime.

Close 

The report credited Kenya with identifying more victims, repatriating citizens exploited in overseas online scam operations, and securing its first civil judgment against a fraudulent recruiter.

However, it said persistent concerns over official complicity continued to hamper law enforcement and victim identification, while protection services for adult survivors remained limited.

World.title: South Africa: Navi Pillay's Nobel Win Draws Attention To Her Work Defending Media Freedom And Beyond
World.content:
Navi Pillay speaking at the South African National EditorsÂ Forum (SANEF) Nat Nakasa Award for Courageous Journalism in 2022.

Recognised by the Norwegian Nobel Committee for her efforts to promote peace and international law, Navi Pillay is being celebrated by African media, legal and civil society voices for a career advancing justice, accountability and human rights — including the right to report freely and safely.

Navanethem 'Navi' Pillay’s Nobel Peace Prize, announced on Friday, 9 October, is drawing attention to her support for media freedom and a career spanning some of the most consequential developments in international human rights law.

The South African jurist has backed initiatives to strengthen legal protections for free expression and promote a free and pluralistic information space.



Pillay is the fifth South African to receive the Nobel Peace Prize, following Albert Luthuli, Desmond Tutu, Nelson Mandela and F. W. de Klerk.

Announcing the Nobel, Norwegian Nobel Committee chair Jørgen Watne Frydnes linked Pillay’s early legal work under apartheid to her later role in international justice, from defending Nelson Mandela and others who opposed apartheid to serving as a judge in major international cases.

The committee said she had helped strengthen the international legal order and institutions responsible for holding perpetrators of serious crimes accountable. It also highlighted the uneven application of international law and the ability of powerful states and leaders to evade responsibility.

“Whenever might overtakes right, it undermines stability, trust and peaceful co-existence," the committee said.

Pillay’s win is particularly being celebrated by the media fraternity in Africa, most of whom are citing her efforts in defending media freedom.

Reacting to the announcement, Moky Makura, executive director of Africa No Filter said Pillay “embodies African agency”.

“For decades, she has worked tirelessly to create the change she wants to see in the world. This Nobel Prize shines a well-deserved spotlight on her extraordinary contribution. It is a reminder that African progress is not always about what is happening, but also about what the world is failing to see,” Makura said.

Churchill Otieno, president of The African Editors Forum (TAEF), also said Pillay’s record held particular significance for journalists because of its emphasis on accountability and the right to report freely.

“From her struggle against apartheid to her work in international human rights and law, she has shown that peace cannot endure without accountability,” Otieno said.

“For us journalists and media workers, her record also speaks directly to the right to report freely and safely. As UN High Commissioner, she called for journalists to be protected from political interference and physical threats. Her recognition affirms that defending human dignity, press freedom and the rule of law takes courage, especially when powerful interests resist scrutiny.”

In February 2025, Pillay delivered the keynote address at the launch of South Africa’s Free Expression Legal Network in Johannesburg. Developed by the South African National Editors’ Forum (SANEF), the Press Council, the Campaign for Free Expression and other organisations and legal experts, the network connects journalists and others facing legal threats over their expression with support, including legal representation.

Information and digital rights activist Izak Minnaar notes that Pillay had actively supported the network and advanced media freedom initiatives internationally.

“As the only South African on the global Information and Democracy Commission, she has been spearheading initiatives to support media freedom in South Africa and beyond,” Minnaar explained.

Anton Harber, director of the Henry Nxumalo Foundation, said Pillay had been particularly consistent in defending independent journalism.

“Navi Pillay has stood firm on many human rights issues, but has had particularly clear, strong and consistent views in defence of media freedom and the importance of independent journalism.”

“Whenever called upon to defend the media, she has been quick to stand up and be counted, even when it was not an easy thing to do. Her prize will be celebrated by journalists,” Harber added.

At the network’s launch, Pillay stressed the value of collective action. “If you clap with a single hand, nobody yells for you. But if a lot of people form a network clap, they will be heard,” she said, according to SANEF.

In its statement congratulating her, SANEF recalled Pillay’s call for governments to promote a free press that can “combat disinformation, build public trust and advance the promotion and protection of human rights.”

She also emphasised the need to protect those who help journalists expose wrongdoing. “I would say that such action must also protect media sources and whistle-blowers,” she said, according to SANEF.

Pillay served on the International Commission on Information and Democracy, convened by Reporters Without Borders in 2018. The 25-member commission developed principles for protecting freedom of expression and democratic debate in the global information space. Its declaration described information and communication as a common good and called for freedom, pluralism and reliable information.

President Cyril Ramaphosa said the award recognised Pillay’s contributions to peace and human dignity in South Africa and internationally.

“She has served humanity with principle and the belief that the world can and should be a better place,” Ramaphosa said.

Mameltwe Sebei, president of the General Industries Workers Union of South Africa (Giwusa) and an attorney at Lawyers for Human Rights, described the Nobel as recognition of Pillay’s legal career serving oppressed and marginalised people.

Her work defending anti-apartheid activists and involvement in international cases concerning atrocities, including the Rwanda genocide and the occupied Palestinian territory, made the award a source of pride for South Africans, he said.

“Most importantly, this should affirm our commitment to the principles of justice that underpin the work of any lawyer who stands on the side of the oppressed,” Sebei said. “She represents that type of jurist, that type of lawyer, and this Nobel Peace Prize is a well-deserved recognition of that.”

South Africa’s parliamentary Portfolio Committee on International Relations and Cooperation also described the award as a source of national pride, citing Pillay’s contribution to international justice and accountability for war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide.

Na’eem Jeenah, Senior Researcher at Mapungubwe Institute for Strategic Reflection (MISTRA) and political analyst said the award carries significance beyond South Africa.

“This then is an honour not only for South Africa but for the whole of Africa, a continent that is battling with its own conflicts and violations of international law,” Jeenah said.

While he believes the Nobel Prize would not change conditions for Palestinians nor stop the violence in Gaza, it “adds to the body of moral and legal evidence against Israel, including several UN reports (including on genocide), and the ICJ genocide case”.

Born on 23 September 1941 in Clairwood, Durban, to a family of Indian Tamil descent, Pillay grew up under apartheid. She graduated from the University of Natal with a bachelor’s degree in 1963 and an LLB in 1965.

In 1967, she became the first Black woman to open her own law practice in Natal, now KwaZulu-Natal. She represented political detainees and exposed abuses including torture and solitary confinement. In 1973, she successfully challenged restrictions preventing political prisoners from accessing legal counsel, according to South African History Online.

After earning postgraduate law degrees at Harvard University, she became the first Black woman appointed to South Africa’s High Court in Natal in 1995. She also participated in the Women’s National Coalition during the country’s constitutional transition and co-founded Equality Now, an organisation campaigning for the rights of women and girls.

In 1995, Pillay joined the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, established to prosecute those responsible for the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi. She became its president in 1999, serving until 2003.

A landmark case during her time on the tribunal was the trial of Jean-Paul Akayesu, a former local official convicted of genocide and crimes against humanity. The tribunal’s 1998 judgment established that rape and other forms of sexual violence could constitute acts of genocide when committed with the intent to destroy a protected group, in whole or in part.

Pillay later served in the International Criminal Court’s Appeals Division from 2003 to 2008. She became United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights in 2008, serving until 2014, a period that included the Arab Spring uprisings and the Syrian civil war.

Close 

Her later work included international proceedings and investigations into alleged serious crimes. In December 2019, she was appointed an ad hoc judge at the International Court of Justice in the case brought by The Gambia against Myanmar over alleged genocide against the Rohingya minority. The court confirmed its jurisdiction and ruled the application admissible.

From 2021 to 2025, Pillay chaired the United Nations Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and Israel.

In September 2025, the commission concluded that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza. Israel rejected the conclusion. The finding was made by a UN commission of inquiry, not a final judgment by an international court.

The commission’s work highlighted a central challenge for international law: translating findings of serious violations into consequences for those responsible, particularly when powerful states are involved.

The Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) said the award underscored the importance of international law at a time when its institutions face growing pressure.

“Throughout her long career, Navi Pillay has set a high moral example, speaking out and standing up for justice, accountability and the rule of law,” said SIPRI director Karim Haggag.

Haggag said the award also recognised the institutions Pillay had served, warning that powerful states were increasingly resorting to power politics and transactionalism while international law and its institutions faced attack.

South African investigative organisation Open Secrets also welcomed the award, saying it affirmed the importance of international law and its promise of holding human rights abusers to account.

Pillay was a panellist at the first People’s Tribunal on Economic Crime in the arms trade, convened by Open Secrets and civil society partners in 2018. The tribunal sought accountability for arms companies and politicians in the aftermath of apartheid and State Capture.

The announcement also prompted a lighter moment. Reacting to the news in Nuremberg, Pillay joked with supporters, “If you clap a little bit louder, I may share this prize with Trump,” according to an amateur social media clip.

World.title: Nigeria: Customs Uncovers ₦3.67bn Drug Haul in Imported Cars, Spare Parts
World.content:
The importation of illicit drugs concealed in used vehicles and automobile spare parts has come under scrutiny following the interception of two 40-foot containers containing suspected narcotics worth an estimated â¦3.67 billion at Tin Can Island Port, Lagos.

The seizure was made by the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Tin Can Island Port Command, in collaboration with the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA).

The seized substances included Delta-8 cannabis-infused cookies and gummies, which were allegedly hidden among imported used vehicles and automobile spare parts to evade detection.

The command's Public Relations Officer, Oscar Ivara, disclosed the interceptions in a statement issued on Friday, attributing the operation to the vigilance of Customs officers and cooperation with the NDLEA.



According to Ivara, the first consignment, concealed in a 40-foot container with identification number MSDU655132/0, was intercepted on September 2, 2026.

"Following a thorough 100 per cent joint physical examination conducted by both agencies, it was found to contain a total of 890 packs of Delta-8 cannabis-infused cookies and gummies, with a combined weight of 598.08 kilograms, alongside two used vehicles, namely a 2008 Mercedes-Benz and a 2012 Nissan Infiniti," Ivara said.

He said another 40-foot container, with identification number SKU625643/6, was intercepted on September 16, 2026.

A physical examination revealed "1,207 packages of Cannabis Indica weighing 603.75 kilograms, with an estimated street value of N3.62bn," he said.

"Following a thorough 100 per cent joint physical examination conducted by both agencies, it was found to contain a total of 890 packs of Delta-8 cannabis-infused cookies and gummies, with a combined weight of 598.08 kilograms, alongside two used vehicles, namely a 2008 Mercedes-Benz and a 2012 Nissan Infiniti," Ivara said.

He said another 40-foot container, with identification number SKU625643/6, was intercepted on September 16, 2026.

A physical examination revealed "1,207 packages of Cannabis Indica weighing 603.75 kilograms, with an estimated street value of N3.62bn," he said.

The second container also contained two used Toyota Sienna vehicles, two used Toyota Corolla vehicles and used engine spare parts.

According to Ivara, the combined seizures from the two containers weighed 1,201.83 kilogrammes, with an estimated street value of â¦3.67bn.

Close 

He said concealing the substances among vehicles and automobile spare parts highlighted smugglers' attempts to exploit containerised cargo to move prohibited items into the country.

Ivara added that the seizures demonstrated the agencies' resolve to prevent the smuggling of illicit substances through Nigeria's seaports and protect the health, safety and security of citizens.

He said the seized substances would be formally handed over to the NDLEA for further investigation and other necessary actions within its statutory mandate.

"This partnership between the NCS and the NDLEA remains critical to identifying, intercepting and dismantling the activities of individuals and networks involved in drug trafficking," Ivara said.

He commended officers of both agencies for their vigilance and professionalism, adding that their collaboration was essential to tackling smuggling and other transnational crimes.

"Let me use this opportunity to send a clear and unequivocal message to smugglers and all individuals engaged in the illegal importation of prohibited substances: desist from these criminal activities immediately," Ivara warned.

He said the Tin Can Island Port Command would continue to strengthen surveillance, intelligence gathering, cargo examination and enforcement operations in collaboration with relevant security and regulatory agencies.

Ivara also urged importers, licensed customs agents, freight forwarders and other stakeholders to comply with applicable laws, regulations and import procedures.

"Legitimate trade must not be used as a cover for criminal activities," he added.

World.title: Nigeria: Police Chief Speaks On Alleged Ransom Payment for Freed 20 NYSC Members
World.content:
The police reaction followed widespread claims of ransom payments by some parents of the 20 prospective NYSC members who were released on Wednesday, exactly one week after they were abducted on 1 October.

The Commissioner of Police in Imo State, Audu Bosso, says he was not aware of any ransom payment for the 20 prospective members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) who were freed.

Mr Bosso spoke on Thursday afternoon during an interview on Channels TV, which was monitored by PREMIUM TIMES.



The commissioner's reaction followed widespread claims of ransom payments by some parents of the 20 prospective NYSC members who were released on Wednesday, exactly one week after they were abducted on 1 October.

The NYSC members were travelling from Ibadan, Oyo State, to orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states when they were abducted at about 6:30 a.m. on 1 October along the Owerri-Onitsha Road by Umunoha in Imo State.

Not aware of ransom

Speaking during the interview, Mr Bosso insisted that the abductors freed the victims following intense pressure from joint security operatives.

"To my knowledge, no," he responded when asked if any ransom was paid to secure the victims' release.

The police commissioner continued: "I am not aware whether a ransom was paid or not. We did what we were supposed to do as professionals, and that was how we got them."

Meanwhile, in separate interviews with News Central TV, some parents of the abducted NYSC members claimed that they paid between N5 and N6 million to the abductors to secure the victims' release.

Alirat Wahab, mother of one of the victims, told the TV station that her family paid N6 million ransom to the abductors who asked them to convert it to dollars.

Suspects arrested?

Speaking at the TV show, Mr Bosso admitted that none of the abductors had been arrested at the moment, but claimed operations were still ongoing to track down the attackers.

"As we speak, we still have ongoing coordinated operations - combing the bushes to make sure that the perpetrators are arrested," he said.

Avoiding recurrence

Mr Bosso said, to avoid recurrence of the kidnapping attack, the Inspector-General of Police, Tunji Duso, had deployed more tactical teams to the area.

Close 

"As we speak, mobile men are on the ground, and the intelligence response team is equally on the ground. We have fortified the axis where the attack happened and the entire state," he said.

World.title: South Africa: High Court Orders ANC to Reinstate Andile Lungisa After Unlawful Removal
World.content:
With elections less than a month away, the high court has ruled that the ANC's removal of Andile Lungisa from its Nelson Mandela Bay candidate list is unlawful, ordering the party to reinstate his name and pay his legal costs.

The ANC has been left with egg on its face after the high court ruled that its decision to remove mayoral hopeful Andile Lungisa from its candidate list for Nelson Mandela Bay was unlawful and unconstitutional, finding that the party had failed to justify his removal shortly before the candidate-nomination deadline.

In a judgment handed down on Friday, 9 October, Judge Nelisa Mali ordered the ANC to reinstate Lungisa on its internal proportional representation candidate list and directed the party to submit his name to the Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) if the law permits it to supplement its list.

Lungisa had accused party Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula of removing his name after the ANC's candidate-selection process had advanced to its final stages. However, the court did not find Mbalula personally liable.



"The decision to unilaterally remove the applicant's name from the second respondent's proportional representation list was accordingly unlawful and unconstitutional," Mali ruled.

The judgment comes as the ANC gears up for the 4 November local government elections, while also fighting the exclusion of 181 of its candidates in six municipalities by the IEC. The party has taken the matter to the Constitutional Court, which is expected...

World.title: Ethiopia: Ethiopia to Observe Seventh National Cybersecurity Month
World.content:
Addis Ababa — Ethiopia is set to observe its seventh National Cybersecurity Month from October 11 to November 9, 2026.

Announced by the Information Network Security Administration (INSA), the month-long initiative aims to raise public awareness of cyber threats and promote the safer use of digital technologies.

The observance will be held under the theme "An Active Citizen for a Secure Country," INSA officials announced during a press briefing.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

During the briefing, INSA Director-General Tigist Hamid noted that the rapid expansion of technology has been accompanied by a surge in cyberattacks targeting individuals, public and private institutions, and critical national infrastructure.

She underscored the urgent need to build widespread cybersecurity awareness, enabling citizens and organizations to better understand threats and implement robust protective measures.

A primary focus of this year's campaign will be online child protection, with targeted efforts to educate families and youth on the risks associated with internet use.

Planned activities include youth-oriented competitions and discussion forums exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence and cybersecurity.

Reaffirming INSA's commitment to safeguarding the nation's digital space, Tigist called for a collective, nationwide effort to strengthen cybersecurity resilience.

She also urged both public and private sector organizations to mark the month by organizing employee awareness programs, emphasizing that cybersecurity is a shared responsibility.

INSA confirmed that all preparations for the successful rollout of the campaign are complete.

Globally, the cybersecurity awareness observance is being marked for the 23rd time, and for the seventh consecutive year in Ethiopia.

World.title: Liberia: Charged in U.S.$30,500 Land Deal, Eric Wowoh Denies Fraud and Challenges Police Allegations
World.content:
MONROVIA — Eric W. Wowoh, the Liberian businessman charged in connection with a disputed US$30,500 property transaction involving a Liberian-American couple, has broken his silence, strongly denying allegations of fraud and unlawful land conveyance while challenging the financial claims and property ownership documents at the center of the criminal case.

Wowoh, who is associated with Change Agent Network, maintained that he neither misappropriated funds nor unlawfully sold property belonging to Rebekah Acquah and her husband, John Acquah, both residents of Rhode Island, United States.

In a formal response to the allegations, Wowoh disputed the police account of the transaction, insisting that the matter should be determined through documentary evidence and the judicial process rather than public accusations.

"I deny the allegations that I misappropriated money or sold property belonging to the Acquahs. These claims must be evaluated against the evidence presented in court, where I intend to respond fully," Wowoh stated.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

His response follows criminal charges brought against him by the Liberia National Police (LNP) for theft of property, receiving money under false pretenses and criminal conveyance of land in connection with a disputed property in the Rock Church Community, Duazon, Margibi County.

According to a police charge sheet dated Oct. 6, 2026, Wowoh allegedly entered into an agreement in December 2024 to sell the couple two lots of land valued at US$5,500 and an unfinished residential structure valued at US$25,000, bringing the total transaction to US$30,500.

Investigators alleged that Wowoh received payments from the couple, provided property documents and subsequently retrieved those documents before selling the same property to another buyer.

However, Wowoh rejected the suggestion that the transaction amounted to criminal conduct, maintaining that the full purchase price was never paid and that no deed transferring ownership to the Acquahs was executed by him.

While acknowledging that the agreed purchase price was US$30,500, he disputed claims that he received US$18,741 toward the transaction, arguing that the reported figure requires documentary verification.

According to Wowoh, he has not been presented with a complete accounting establishing the dates, amounts, recipients and purposes of the payments allegedly made by the couple.

He maintained that money paid directly toward the property should be distinguished from payments made to organizations or for separate projects, warning against combining unrelated financial transactions to establish the amount allegedly owed.

Wowoh called for a comprehensive reconciliation of all payments before any conclusion is reached regarding the financial dispute.

The police charge sheet itself contains differing figures concerning the transaction. While the complaint indicates that the Acquahs paid US$18,741, investigators reported that Wowoh acknowledged receiving US$9,200 from Rebekah Acquah as part payment.

The discrepancy remains a central issue in the competing accounts of the transaction.

Addressing allegations that he unlawfully conveyed the property to another buyer, Wowoh acknowledged that discussions concerning a possible new sale agreement had taken place but maintained that no new agreement was finalized with the Acquahs.

He said he subsequently informed the couple that he would no longer proceed with the transaction before selling the property to another purchaser.

According to him, he never signed a deed transferring ownership of the disputed property to the Acquahs, a position that directly challenges the allegations contained in the police investigation.

Wowoh also disputed claims surrounding the handling of the property documents.

He maintained that the warranty deed initially provided to the couple was neither signed nor dated by him and therefore questioned whether it could establish a completed transfer of ownership.

He further disclosed that Rebekah Acquah had informed him that the original property documents were missing in the United States, although he acknowledged that he did not personally witness their disappearance.

According to Wowoh, he subsequently used available copies of the documents and his identification to obtain replacement property records based on the information available to him.

He maintained that he had not received the original documents and was prepared to submit relevant records to clarify the circumstances surrounding their replacement.

"I am prepared to provide the records in my possession, including receipts, bank or transfer records, written communications, property documents, and other relevant materials that can help clarify the transactions and the circumstances surrounding this dispute," he said.

The businessman also confirmed that he and his legal representative appeared at the Monrovia City Court at 9 a.m., as directed, to address the allegations.

He claimed that the Acquahs' legal representatives were not present when he appeared, based on his observation at the time, but declined to speculate about their absence.

Wowoh emphasized that the court remains responsible for determining the next steps in the proceedings.

Despite disputing the allegations, he expressed willingness to address any verified financial obligations arising from the transaction.

He said he was prepared to provide records of payments received and discuss the return of amounts established to have been paid specifically toward the property.

However, he insisted that any repayment must be based on a proper reconciliation of the transactions rather than disputed or unverified figures.

The controversy has attracted attention following the police decision to charge Wowoh under Chapter 15, Subchapter A, Sections 15.5 and 15.23 of Liberia's Revised Penal Code.

The Acquahs, through their legal representative, Atty. Stephen B. Lavelah of Kailando and Associate Law Firm, reported the matter to the police Crime Services Department on Sept. 11, 2026.

Police subsequently arrested Wowoh on Sept. 16 at LNP headquarters in Monrovia before completing their investigation and filing the charges.

Investigators maintain that the evidence gathered supports allegations that Wowoh received money for the property and subsequently conveyed it to another buyer.

Close 

Wowoh, however, insists that the police allegations do not accurately reflect the circumstances surrounding the transaction and that the evidence must be subjected to judicial scrutiny.

He also appealed to journalists and media institutions to exercise caution in reporting the case, emphasizing the importance of distinguishing allegations from established facts.

According to him, statements attributed to third parties, disputed financial records and claims concerning ownership should not be presented as conclusive evidence before the court makes its determination.

Wowoh further maintained that he intends to protect his personal reputation and that of Change Agent Network, stressing that the organization should not be implicated in allegations arising from the disputed transaction without evidence establishing its involvement.

The available police account does not establish that Change Agent Network participated in the property transaction or the alleged offenses.

While the police have maintained that their investigation supports criminal charges, Wowoh's response introduces competing claims concerning the amount paid, the status of the property documents and whether ownership was ever legally transferred to the Acquahs.

Those issues are expected to form part of the evidence examined during judicial proceedings.

It remains unclear whether the parties have reached any agreement concerning repayment or whether the disputed property has been subjected to additional legal action.

Wowoh maintains that he will cooperate with the judicial process and present available documents to support his defense.

World.title: What WWE's Money in the Bank card says about the company's development of future superstars
World.content:
The Money in the Bank card is filled with major matches and WWE superstars, both who are rising through the roster and those who are already established. Looking deeper, there’s one thing that stands out among the more than two dozen wrestlers who will be involved in the matches – the NXT brand.

NXT is billed as WWE’s developmental brand. It’s a way for those who either don’t know the art of professional wrestling to get hands-on training or those who don’t know the television side of the business to ingratiate themselves before, hopefully, moving to the Raw or SmackDown brands.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Nearly everyone on the card has been in NXT before heading up to the main roster. The outliers include Roman Reigns, who got his start in Florida Championship Wrestling, which came before NXT was founded, and CM Punk, who made his mark outside the WWE before making his way to WWE’s Ohio Valley Wrestling. Penta never competed in NXT either. He became a legend in Mexico before receiving substantial face time on American programming.

Everyone else got their feet wet in NXT, whose show takes place at the WWE Performance Center. The Money in the Bank card underscores how far WWE has come in creating the superstars of tomorrow in NXT.

"The Performance Center is a very special place," women’s U.S. champion Jacy Jayne told OutKick Dropkick. "I feel like they, well, not I feel, I know they have the best coaches in the world. There's a coach that can help you with literally everything. There's someone for everybody. There's a lot of cooks in the kitchen, sometimes you gravitate more towards one or the other, but you definitely learn your craft, you learn how to talk, you learn how to be confident, you learn cameras, you learn everything.

"So, they set you up for success. And I know it might not come as quick as some people want it to, and they get tired of being in the same routine, but it definitely pays off if you listen to what they have to say and you apply it."

Hundreds of thousands tune into NXT on Tuesday nights and monitor the WWE Universe on social media on the daily.

With the number of superstars who have come out of NXT and who have transcended sports entertainment, it’s worth wondering whether there was a "secret sauce" to the training that goes on behind the scenes in the Performance Center.

Jayne agreed to a point.

"There's so many people with experience that work there that you might not really know about, like people that used to be on NXT, people that were wrestlers or behind the scenes people," she said. "There's so much happening at the Performance Center every day. There's so many different classes that you can take, extra work, like ring work. It's a machine, really, and they're just pumping out superstars by the day."

Jayne will be among the women contending in the Money in the Bank ladder match along with Lola Vice, Tiffany Stratton, Sol Ruca, Lash Legend and Roxanne Perez.

Joe Hendry, a former NXT champion who joined WWE from Total Nonstop Action Wrestling (TNA), isn’t involved in the Money in the Bank. He just put out an album titled "Beyond Belief."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

However, in an interview with OutKick Dropkick, he applauded those working in NXT for helping him get ready for the next level.

"NXT was a fantastic resource for me. It allowed me to come into the company and to learn how WWE works very quickly. I'm proud to say that I was NXT champion. That was something I was able to achieve. I worked very hard for it," he said. "When I came to WWE it was not mandatory for me to be there on a day-to-day basis. I could have just showed up for the shows, but I said, nope, I'm going to be there every day for classes. I'm going to take part in their gym sessions and the nutrition stuff. I'm going to be there for all the classes and I'm going to do all of the smaller live events as well.

"I took part in everything and I think that was a really important part of my career, and I think it was a huge part of my development personally. I think that’s a testament to the fact that I was able to win the NXT Championship and also, as you say, seeing the amount of superstars that are being called up from NXT to the main roster right now, that is a testament to the system."

Saturday’s Money in the Bank puts forth the notion that if you give your all and you put all of your energy and effort into the craft that is professional wrestling, you could possibly achieve the most wildest dreams.

World.title: Rare coin bearing face of king with infamous nickname unearthed after 1,000 years
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Archaeologists in Scotland recently uncovered an Anglo-Saxon coin dating back 1,000 years — minted under a king known as "the Unready."

The coin was unearthed during an excavation in Nesting, a coastal community in Scotland's eastern Shetland Islands, according to Jam Press.

Pictures show a thick, greenish-brown patina covering its surface, though some of the original markings remain visible.

TEEN STUMBLES ON MYSTERIOUS COIN FROM LEGENDARY CITY, PUZZLING ARCHAEOLOGISTS OVER ITS JOURNEY

The excavation was originally conducted to investigate prehistoric structures threatened by coastal erosion, according to Archaeology Shetland.

The archaeological investigation included an examination of nearby Iron Age structures.

The artifact was minted between 991 and 997 A.D., Jam Press noted.

The coin's face depicts King Ethelred the Unready, who ruled England from 978 to 1013 A.D.

DISCOVERY BENEATH SOCCER FIELD REVEALS MASSIVE MEDIEVAL CONVENT LOST FOR CENTURIES

Ethelred, best known for his failed attempts to fend off Viking invasions, was eventually driven from the throne by Danish king Swein Forkbeard.

He regained power in 1014 and ruled until his death in 1016 — making him the longest-reigning Anglo-Saxon monarch.

Elinor Graham, an archaeologist from the University of Aberdeen, was on vacation in Shetland when she participated in the excavation, according to Jam Press.

MAN SEARCHING WITH METAL DETECTOR UNEARTHS MASSIVE VIKING AGE FORTUNE, SHATTERING RECORDS

"This is exactly how I wanted to spend my holiday," Graham said.

She added, "The writing on the coin is still so sharp, and we knew immediately that it was extremely rare, actually unique, in this context."

"We knew immediately that it was extremely rare, actually unique, in this context."

The discovery could offer clues about ancient trade routes between Viking-controlled Shetland and Anglo-Saxon England, though researchers have not ruled out the possibility that the coin was taken during a Norse raid.

World.title: Key American industry seeing blue-collar jobs boom as Trump's re-shoring policies pay off
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

FIRST ON FOX: Critical blue collar manufacturing jobs in the U.S. are making inroads after years of Biden-era offshoring hollowed out the workforce, according to a new economic report.

A Council of Economic Advisors (CEA) report says 72,000 manufacturing jobs have been added in 2026 alone, many of them due to a rise in the manufacturing of durable goods like metal and transportation equipment. The advisors say this is a reverse of a Biden-era trend that saw 200,000 manufacturing jobs disappear in the last two years of the former president's administration.

Not only is the current administration's focus on re-shoring jobs contributing to the uptick, but so are his tariff policies, according to the CEA, a White House agency responsible for providing President Donald Trump with economic analysis.

AMERICA’S NEW BLUE-COLLAR JOB BOOM IS ONE NOBODY SAW COMING — AND IT’S JUST GETTING STARTED

In particular, Trump's landmark One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBB) has laid the groundwork for American companies to expand in the United States, instead of shipping jobs overseas, according to the report. The bill's provisions include allowing manufacturers an immediate 100% tax deduction on expenses related to new factory building, and purchasing machinery and equipment.

The report highlights success stories from corporations that are reinvesting in Americans and expanding their businesses.

LARGEST-EVER US STEEL PLANT IS COMING TO A KEY RED STATE AS TRUMP UNVEILS $15B INVESTMENT

For example, the 100% expensing provision in the OBBB has helped Jergens, a manufacturing company based in Ohio, expand to Illinois.

"Since the passage of the bill [OBBB], our employees are voluntarily working additional hours," the company's CEO, Jack Schron, said. "They are keeping more of what they earn, putting more money back into the American economy and Jergens has a ready workforce. It is a win-win-win: a win for the employee, for Jergens and for the United States economy."

BESSENT CREDITS TRUMP IMMIGRATION POLICIES WITH HELPING RETURN JOBS TO AMERICANS AS WAGE GAINS RESUME

Schron added that 83% of his workers are picking up overtime after the OBBB provision established no taxes for overtime work.

In another example touted in the CEA report, a company in North Carolina, Ketchie Inc., has expanded its workforce by 25% after taking advantage of the 100% expensing provision to purchase new machinery. The report says the company waited to buy the equipment until the OBBB passed.

As for wages, manufacturing workers are seeing benefits, too, with their pay increasing by 7.9% since January 2025.

"Adjusted for inflation, this means that blue-collar manufacturing workers are earning nearly $2,500 more per year, on average, since President Trump took office," the report says.

It also touts figures from the construction industry, including 100,000 construction jobs added since Trump took office.

Semiconductor chip manufacturing, an industry in which the United States typically competes with China, is on the rise in the United States too.

Micron is building memory chip plants in Idaho, Virginia and New York, which the report says is a $250 billion investment in the United States. Apple is investing $600 billion in American semiconductor production, too.

The report also says that major pharmaceutical companies like GSK and Gilead are investing billions of dollars in the United States, along with automakers like Stellantis.

PESSIMISTS SAY THE ECONOMY IS WEAK. THE GOOD NEWS IS, THEY ARE WRONG

All told, the reshoring and tariff policies have resulted in $11 trillion in investments in the United States during Trump's second term in office, according to the report.

Meanwhile, the economy is on everyone's mind with only a few weeks left until the midterm elections. Inflation, particularly high gas and grocery prices, continue to impact Americans before they head to the polls.

According to a Fox News Poll, the cost of everyday items is a hardship for voters: 61% say gas prices are a major problem, up from 48% two years ago, while 52% say the same for healthcare costs, up from 44%. Majorities also view housing costs (54%, down from 60%) and grocery prices (62%, down from 66%) as major problems.

Nearly two-thirds of Americans say the economy is worse under the Trump administration than before.

World.title: High school football referee suspended for grabbing a player and acting like a buffoon
World.content:
Here we are — Week 8 of the high school football season in the books. Hard to believe, right?

One day you wake up and you're getting ready for Kickoff Classics in August, and then you blink and the playoffs are a month away.

Time flies when you're having fun!

FLORIDA HIGH SCHOOL FOOTBALL GAME ERUPTS INTO VIOLENT BRAWL INVOLVING PLAYERS, COACHES AFTER FINAL WHISTLE

Or, in one referee's case ... when you're putting your hands on a player and then getting suspended by the district for acting like a complete buffoon for no reason whatsoever!

Either-or.

I've taken it upon myself here at OutKick to highlight at least one high school football play/ player/ story each and every Saturday during the season. These guys are all about to be millionaires with the silly NIL rules, so we might as well get ahead of the curve and start identifying them early.

BEHEMOTH HIGH SCHOOL FOOTBALL STAR SLAMS DEFENDER TO THE GROUND LIKE A RAGDOLL AFTER INTERCEPTION

So far this season, we've seen (arguably) the country's top running back do incredible things in Tennessee on multiple different occasions, a wild Hail Mary in Florida, an entire California team get suspended because the mascot shot the bird to some fans, and a giant running back in Kentucky.

What a run we've been on, and I can assure you, it won't end today ... unfortunately.

Take a look:

The school district didn't take long to suspend this ref

Goodness gracious. I've covered a lot of high school football over the years. It's all I did from about 2015-2021. I can safely say that I have never, in my life, seen that.

The player in the video is Joelle Rover — a receiver for the Glendale Falcons, in Springfield, Missouri. To me, he looks like he did nothing wrong. At all. A nice catch-and-score for 43 yards, and a celebration with his teammates.

Obviously, you can't hear what he said, but boots on the ground don't mention anything about a verbal interaction with the ref. Everyone is as confused as we are, including Glendale coach Frank Tristan.

"I think it really tarnished the whole game with that," he told the Springfield News-Leader.

Ya think?!

The Missouri State High School Activities Association suspended the referee less than 24 hours later, which should also tell you something. They didn't wait long to investigate or ask questions.

It's pretty clear what transpired from the video, and they didn't need much else.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

In fact, this play was so blatant, and looked so bad, it caught the attention of former Heisman winner, Robert Griffin III on X.

"This referee done lost his DAMN MIND PUTTING HIS HANDS ON A HIGH SCHOOL FOOTBALL PLAYER FOR NO REASON," he posted Friday evening.

Now, the question is ... why? Why did this ref get so angry at this kid for scoring a touchdown and celebrating? I have no clue. It's a harmless touchdown celebration.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"He doesn't need to be touching my player, you talk to me, that's ridiculous," Tristan can be seen yelling from the sidelines after the play. "You need to grow up."

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Wild scene. Again, I've never seen anything like it. High school football never disappoints, folks. It's undefeated. Every week, it gives us content — both good and bad.

On that note, let's end the day by highlighting Joelle Rover. The 6-3 senior finished last year with 11 touchdown passes and 1,017 yards, and currently has offers from Princeton, Western Illinois and Lindenwood, according to 247Sports.



He's also a nightmare to try and take down.

Good luck, fellas!

In case you haven't noticed, American amateur golf has a full integrity issue

Case in point, watch what happens when Paige Spiranac, the world's No. 1 ranked golf influencer, as named by OutKick, and her playing partner face what looks like a knock-in and move on putt. Paige, who used to play in professional tournaments, pushes the putt only to be one-upped by her partner who pulls her putt to the left.

Are they just doing this for YouTube so men will keep watching? Could be. Here's the problem: We have an integrity issue in this country when it comes to golfers claiming to be better than they are. Golfers are calling four-footers gimme range.

WYNDHAM CLARK ADDRESSES CHEATING ALLEGATIONS AFTER BEING ACCUSED OF IMPROVING LIE DURING BMW CHAMPIONSHIP WIN

Ten handicap players make 65% of 3 to 6 foot putts, according to MyGolfSpy data. In case you can't visualize a 3-foot putt, we're talking the length of a guitar, or a youth baseball bat.

CAITLIN CLARK CRUSHES A DRIVE AS SHE WORKS TO DIAL IN HER GOLF GAME WITH LEXIE HULL, SAINTS FAN FIGHT & DONUTS

Did you hear about the Tony Romo incident where he signed a scorecard where he might've been shaving strokes? It's unclear if it was intentional or not. That's why I wrote "might've."

America, we have to do better and it starts today at the courses across this country. I want to start hearing about your full integrity experiences. World.title: Socialists set sights on the ground floor of government as GOP warns of bigger plan unfolding
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

FIRST ON FOX — Dozens of individuals backed by the Democratic Socialists of America are set to appear on ballots as candidates for state legislature seats on Election Day, something Republicans say could set in motion a trend that transforms the Democratic Party.

At least 65 DSA-aligned candidates have advanced to contest state legislative seats in November’s general election. The Republican State Leadership Committee — the official GOP body responsible for ensuring state-level conservative victories — claimed that these races could very well determine the future of the Democratic Party, according to a memo obtained exclusively by Fox News Digital.

"The statehouse trend is also relevant because several prominent DSA-aligned Congressional candidates in 2026 have emerged from state and local political organizing," the memo reads. "These victories demonstrate one potential progression: movement organizations can help develop candidates locally and at the state level, provide them with political experience and organizational networks, and eventually support campaigns for Congress."

SOCIALISTS CHEER ‘SHOCKWAVE’ PRIMARY NIGHT AS DSA-BACKED CANDIDATES WIN, ADVANCE ACROSS THE MAP

"The scale of that presence matters not only because DSA-aligned candidates could influence the direction of their state legislatures if elected, but because state legislative offices can provide a platform, governing experience, donor networks and organizational infrastructure for future campaigns for higher office," it continues.

The RSLC's methodology included candidates who are DSA members, DSA endorsees or self-identified members of the organization.

DSA-affiliated candidates identified by the RSLC take positions on a number of issues that crucial swing voters and independents may find extreme, including defunding or abolishing police departments, left-wing economic policies and demanding race-based reparations.

Opposition to traditional policing has emerged as a prominent issue among some of the DSA-aligned state legislative candidates identified by Republicans.

"As a State Senator I will continue to do everything I can to end policing and incarceration in New York State," Democratic State Sen. Jabari Brisport’s campaign website reads. Brisport also supports decriminalizing prostitution, arguing that removing criminal penalties for sex workers while maintaining protections against trafficking and exploitation would help keep communities safe.

TALARICO PUT ON DEFENSE AFTER 2020 COMMENTS ABOUT DEFUNDING POLICE RESURFACE: 'WE MUST REPLACE'

Over in Wisconsin, Democratic State Rep. Ryan Clancy has stood by his statement that police work has "no dignity or value."

"It means that American policing has always been bad and it always will be," Clancy told a local outlet in 2023, alleging that American police forces have their roots in slave patrols. "It’s not like we can get back to this to the early days… American policing… [is] epically racist and classist because that’s a dead end. That is the point of American policing."

Clancy told Fox News Digital that his comments concerned officers who abused their authority over sex workers, although his original remarks and subsequent 2023 interview criticized policing more broadly as an institution he argued was inherently racist and could not be reformed.

He concurred with the RSLC's assertion that DSA-aligned candidates are shaping the future of the Democratic Party.

State Rep. Eleanor Chávez, running with the DSA’s backing in New Mexico, meanwhile has called Immigration and Customs Enforcement "fascist" and compared its agents to the KKK. Republicans in New Mexico have condemned such rhetoric, arguing that it could spur people to commit violence against law enforcement officers.

Despite its propensity to draw attention to its stances on social issues, the DSA bills itself as an economically motivated organization.

NEWSOM ADMITS DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST IDEAS ‘MAINSTREAM’ IN DEMOCRAT PARTY: ‘PRETTY ALIGNED’

To this end, some of its members running for state legislatures have called for reforms some have described as radical.

New York Democratic Assemblywoman Sarahana Shrestha, who is running for re-election with the backing of the DSA, has pushed legislation that would allow the government to acquire the privately held Central Hudson Gas & Electric Corp., potentially through eminent domain if a negotiated purchase cannot be reached.Dylan Wegela, a DSA-backed state house candidate in Michigan, has similarly pushed for state acquisitions of utility companies.

Shrestha agrees with the RSLC's assessment that DSA-aligned state lawmakers could influence the Democratic Party’s trajectory.

"The things DSA-aligned state lawmakers are fighting for are things that are extremely popular with voters, and have been for a long time," she told Fox News Digital. "A majority of our constituents believe the energy sector should not be for profit, healthcare should be single-payer and universal, the government should play a positive role in building necessary infrastructure such as permanently affordable housing and public transit, and so on."

The DSA-affiliated lawmaker also defended her plan to take over the Central Hudson Gas & Electric Corp., citing a feasibility study commissioned by supporters of the bill that found it would lower costs for consumers.

Sometimes, the stances of DSA clash with Democratic policy priorities.

Gabriel Acevero, a DSA-backed lawmaker in Maryland, for instance, opposed a marijuana legalization measure he argued did not go far enough to address racial inequities, declaring that "cannabis legalization without reparations for communities harmed by the intentional drug war is not progressive policy." Scores of DSA-affiliated candidates running in states such as New York, Minnesota and Massachusetts have thrown their support behind reparations for racial minorities.

SOCIALISTS ARE HELPING GOP CAMPAIGNS HEADING INTO NOVEMBER

Republicans have a vested interest in tying the mainstream Democratic Party to the DSA. A Fox News poll from September found that 55% of registered voters had an unfavorable opinion of the DSA.

While some in the Democratic Party argue that Republican attempts to tie the Democratic Party to socialism are bad-faith campaign tricks, party leadership has recently made significant concessions to its left-wing flank.

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer backed Abdul El-Sayed's more moderate opponent in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary, but a super PAC aligned with Schumer has since committed millions of dollars to supporting El-Sayed's general-election campaign. El-Sayed is a progressive backed by prominent figures on the party's left, but who has said he is not a socialist.

Due to the disorganized nature of the DSA and the varying degrees of affiliation held by candidates, estimates of the number of socialist candidates running for state legislature vary across sources. The Brookings Institution, for instance, found at least 76 had advanced to the general election, while the RSLC’s analysis identified a minimum of 65 running in a total of 24 states.

Though the DSA's gains have received significant attention, a Brookings Institution analysis found that candidates backed by the organization represent only a tiny fraction of the nation's state legislative seats, raising questions about how far the socialist movement's growing influence extends.

"The RSLC has consistently said that socialism starts in the states and that is where we need to stop it," the RSLC’s memo reads. "The DSA’s growing presence in statehouse races could have dangerous impacts for state policy in the short-term, and it reflects a clearly orchestrated long-term effort to build political power from the state-level up."

World.title: 5 marriage mistakes couples make without realizing it — and how to avoid them
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

The secret to a happier, longer-lasting marriage may involve much more than chemistry and compatibility.

Recent research published in the journal Family Process found that improvements in communication and emotional safety were linked to greater relationship satisfaction.

Maintaining that connection takes effort, particularly as couples settle into routines and begin to feel as though they already know everything about each other, according to Tammy Nelson, Ph.D., a board-certified sexologist, sex therapist and integrative relationship therapist in Los Angeles.

‘FOOD DIVORCE’ TREND AMONG COUPLES COULD DRIVE THEM APART, EXPERTS WARN

"Compatibility can feel different to different people at different times," she told Fox News Digital. "The relationship will go through developmental stages just like you do."

From losing curiosity to avoiding difficult conversations, Nelson shared five common mistakes that can weaken a couple’s connection — and ways to avoid them.

No. 1: Assuming you know everything about your partner

Losing curiosity about a partner can chip away at attraction over time, according to Nelson.

"That’s how we fall in love, when someone's curious about us," she said. "When they come along and say, 'I'm so interested in you. I'm curious about you.'"

WHY COUPLES SHOULD FLIRT WITH EACH OTHER EVERY DAY — PLUS THE ‘RED FLAG’ TO AVOID

"We're attracted to something in the space in between us — not so much when it's sitting next to us on the couch every night, and so we tend to lose that curiosity."

While someone may feel they know everything about their partner — "what they like to eat, what they'd like to watch on TV, what they might like in bed" — those preferences can evolve over time, Nelson said.

"Don't put your partner in a box," Nelson said, urging couples to stay curious and ask questions. "Who are they becoming? What are they thinking? What do they desire? What's their vision for the future?"

POLITICAL FIGHTS CAN RIP COUPLES APART — THERAPIST SHARES 3 WAYS TO SAVE A RELATIONSHIP

The therapist suggested that losing curiosity about a partner can sometimes make attention from someone outside the relationship particularly appealing.

"That's why we have affairs, right? Somebody comes along and they're fascinated by us," she said. "We love that. And it's why we pay a therapist, so someone will ask questions about us."

No. 2: Avoiding difficult conversations

Avoiding difficult conversations — and failing to pay attention to what goes unsaid — can create problems in a relationship, Nelson cautioned.

"Pay attention to what you're not talking about and why," she advised.

When it comes to relationship problems, couples who avoid conflict may be more vulnerable than those who openly disagree.

"It's not the people who fight and communicate all the time — it's the people who aren't fighting, aren't arguing, aren't communicating," the expert said.

COMMON MARRIAGE HABIT COULD QUIETLY KILL YOUR SEX LIFE, EXPERT WARNS

Nelson encouraged couples to notice which topics make them pull back or shut down during conflict — such as money or sex — and instead make an effort to lean into those difficult discussions.

"You're probably avoiding it because you don't want to get into a conflict, which is totally legitimate, but maybe pay attention to those spaces where there could be more room for communicating," she advised.

No. 3: Focusing on what’s wrong with your sex life

When couples talk about sex, focusing on complaints rather than what is working can make intimacy more difficult, according to Nelson.

"The key here is not to talk about what's not working or what your partner's not doing, or why you’re not doing it more often," she said.

The "magic formula," Nelson said, is for partners to share what they like and what is working.

"The key to the universe is, you get more of what you would appreciate," she said. "If you point out how your partner is not acting the way you want, then you're in conflict, you're defensive, you feel bad about yourself. That's not going to help, it’s not very sexy."

"Expand on what’s already working."

Instead, she recommends focusing on the positive by telling a partner what they've liked about their sex life, whether it is something happening now or a meaningful experience from years ago.

"Whether you’re a new couple or you've been together forever, start with something you appreciate, and then something that you would like more of," she suggested. "Expand on what’s already working."

No. 4: Getting stuck in ‘maintenance mode’

Another potential mistake is allowing the everyday responsibilities of life to crowd out opportunities for growth and excitement.

Nelson encouraged couples to consider whether their relationship is primarily in "maintenance mode" or "expansion mode."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Maintenance mode involves managing the everyday responsibilities of a shared life, which Nelson said is essential.

"You know, we need to pay the bills. We need to make sure the air conditioner is working," she said. "We need maintenance in a relationship, just like you need maintenance at a job or just in life, but you also need expansion."

CLICK HERE TO 

Expansion mode, meanwhile, involves trying new things together and finding ways to keep the relationship exciting.

If there’s too much maintenance and not enough expansion, one or both partners could get bored and feel stuck, Nelson cautioned.

"On the other hand, if there’s too much expansion, you're going to feel like you’re always doing something new and there's no rest and maybe not enough connection," she said.

"All relationships need freedom and connection."

No. 5: Keeping feelings of connection to yourself

Couples may also miss opportunities for connection when they feel affection toward their partner but don't express it, according to Nelson.

She encouraged couples to notice the positive emotions and physical sensations they experience when thinking about their partner — and to share those feelings with each other.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"Where in your heart or in your body are you feeling the most 'juice,' the most 'aliveness,' when you think about your partner?" she asked.

Some people are more aware of these physical sensations than others, Nelson acknowledged.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"But if you can put your hand on your heart or on your stomach or your shoulders and say, ‘you know, when I think about you, I get this warm feeling in my heart’ — that's all you have to share with your partner. And sometimes that means everything to them."

Ultimately, Nelson emphasized that avoiding these common pitfalls comes down to ongoing attention, curiosity and a willingness to keep discovering new things about each other.
