World.title: 'Ragebait' is the 2026 German Youth Word of the Year
World.content:
Already named the 2025 Oxford Word of the Year, "rage bait" has also been widely adopted in German slang.

The 2026 Youth Word of the Year, "Ragebait," was announced on Saturday at the Frankfurt Book Fair by publisher PONS Langenscheidt.

The "Jugendwort des Jahres," or German Youth Word of the Year, is an annual campaign that documents the popularity of new slang expressions.

"Ragebait" (in English: rage bait) refers to social media content that is deliberately designed to make people angry, frustrated or morally outraged.

It aims to drive engagement, since the algorithms of platforms like Instagram, TikTok and X reward high-energy interaction. A post that generates a heated debate through angry comments, or that is widely shared due to the emotional reaction it provokes, counts as high engagement, which leads the platforms to push the content to more feeds.

Shortlist also included 'Peak' and 'Crashout'

"Ragebait" was on a shortlist of three words for the 2026 Youth Word of the Year, alongside "Peak" and "Crashout."

All three terms are borrowed from English, demonstrating once again the language's significant influence on German youth culture.

Around one million young people, aged 11 to 20, have voted since August 28 for their favorite term.

"Ragebait" obtained 36.5% of the votes, followed by 33.8% for "Peak" and 29.7% for "Crashout."

"The close result shows that all three terms have a firm place in the vocabulary of generations Z and Alpha," said Artur Raiser, marketing manager at PONS Langenscheidt, in a press statement. "'Ragebait' held a slight lead from the start," but only by a narrow margin throughout the voting period, he added. "It remained an exciting race for us at the publishing house, too, until the very last moment."

Peak crash out

"Crashout" (used by young Germans as "crashout gehen," or "going crash out") originally comes from the English "to crash out," which traditionally means to fall asleep very quickly due to exhaustion.

But in newer internet slang, popularized on gaming and social media platforms, "crashing out" means having an intense emotional breakdown, losing control of one's temper or reacting with sudden, uncontrolled anger or stress. It is often used with a touch of humor, to emphasize that the reaction might be somewhat exaggerated.

As for the other shortlisted word, "Peak," it refers to something that is the absolute best. In German youth slang, it functions like an adjective: "That was peak football" or "that is peak comedy."

PONS Langenscheidt, a publishing company that specializes in language reference works, has been selecting the German Youth Word of the Year since 2008 — originally via a jury, and since 2020 through an online vote. Offensive, racist or discriminatory terms are not permitted. The multi-stage public nomination and voting process for next year's word will start in the summer of 2027.

"Das crazy" was selected last year, while "Aura" was the Youth Word of the Year 2024.

This article was originally written in German.

World.title: Germany sticks to Russia sanctions after Trump diesel deal
World.content:
10/10/2026 October 10, 2026 Germany 'committed' to further Russia sanctions

Germany has not purchased Russian oil since 2023 [FILE May 2024] Image: Alexander Ryumin/TASS/dpa/picture alliance

Germany on Saturday said it would continue pursuing sanctions against Russia over the war in Ukraine, coming a day after US President Donald Trump announced a temporary US sanctions reprieve on Russian diesel.

"The federal ⁠government ⁠has taken note of the US decision relating to Russian diesel deliveries," government spokesperson Stefan Kornelius said in a statement.

"The federal government ​remains committed to the decisions on ​sanctions against ‌Russia and is working with its European partners on further sanctions," the statement added.

Germany's "support for Ukraine in its struggle to defend itself remains unfailing ... Diplomatic efforts for a peaceful solution continue," he added.

After Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Moscow has been subject to round after round of sanctions packages led by the US and EU.

Russian crude and other oil products have been subject to EU sanctions since 2023, and Germany has not imported any oil or oil products from Russia since then.

A spokesperson for Economic Affairs Minister Katherina Reiche said Saturday that "Germany stands fully behind the sanctions packages."

"Our supply is diversified in this area; we are independent of Russian oil," the spokesperson said.

Germany remains Ukraine's largest financial backer in Europe. During a visit to Kyiv last weekend, Chancellor Friedrich Merz reiterated Germany's unwavering support for Ukraine.

In what amounts to a major reversal in US policy, Trump on Friday said he would temporarily lift US sanctions to allow Russia to "immediately" supply over 300,000 tons of diesel fuel to US and global markets.

The move comes as diesel prices reach record levels after the war in Iran launched by the US and Israel sent diesel prices skyrocketing around the world. In the US, the high prices are putting political pressure on Trump's Republicans ahead of the midterm elections in November.

However, despite Trump's claims on social media, it remains unclear how much Russian fuel will reach global markets amid domestic fuel shortages as Ukraine continues to target refineries.

World.title: Operations Plan Germany: How the Bundeswehr trains for NATO collective defense
World.content:
How prepared is Germany for national defense? The answer lies in the Operations Plan Germany. Military exercises such as "Red Storm Charlie" are designed to put these preparations to the test in realistic scenarios.

In a residential district of Hamburg at midnight, the streets are quiet and deserted. Suddenly, the silence is shattered: Several helicopters circle the night sky, and flashing blue lights illuminate the darkness. A long convoy of vehicles moves through the streets. Soldiers stand atop armored Bundeswehr vehicles, their machine guns at the ready. For local residents, it is an unusual, perhaps even unsettling sight in an otherwise peaceful port city.

"Red Storm Charlie" is the name of the exercise that will bring parts of Hamburg, northern Germany's largest city, to a standstill for three days. The Bundeswehr, police, and civilian organizations are jointly testing how well prepared they are to respond in a crisis.

The scenario centers on a deteriorating security situation on NATO's eastern flank. NATO troops, represented in the exercise by Bundeswehr soldiers, arrive at the port of Hamburg, Germany's largest seaport, before moving eastwards through the Hanseatic city.

Acts of sabotage and demonstrations, also included in the scenario, hamper their advance. With around 1,700 participants, including 500 soldiers, the exercise held in late September 2026, was the largest of its kind to date.

"Red Storm Charlie" forms part of a classified strategy known as the "Operationsplan Deutschland " (Operations Plan Germany). Through this document, the Bundeswehr is preparing for the possibility of a Russian attack on NATO territory. The Operations Plan Germany is an integral element of NATO's broader defense planning and is closely aligned with the Alliance's overall defense framework.

NATO members in Kyiv: 'We stand unwavering with Ukraine' To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

In the event of war or a major crisis, not only the city of Hamburg but Germany as a whole would assume a pivotal role as a logistics hub for hundreds of thousands of NATO soldiers, weapons, and pieces of heavy equipment. "This is a highly detailed and strictly classified plan that specifies exactly where NATO allies would arrive in Germany, including which ports they would use and which routes would be required for their transit across the country," security expert Aylin Matlé of the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) told DW.

Germany as a transit country for NATO troops

The Baltic states are widely regarded as the region where NATO considers a Russian attack most likely. In such a scenario, the alliance would concentrate large troop contingents from its 32 member states there. To reach the region, soldiers from southern and western Europe would need to pass through Germany. "In concrete terms, this means that around 800,000 soldiers and 200,000 vehicles would have to move through our country within six months. Those are the calculations," says Marcel Bohnert, a Bundeswehr officer who contributed to the first version of the Operations Plan.

Speaking to DW in a personal capacity rather than as a representative of the Bundeswehr, Bohnert explained: "We must ensure that soldiers can use our roads and ports safely. That is why we take care of all their needs: We arrange accommodation, provide food, ensure their security, and guide them through our transport network."

The plan also covers transport in the opposite direction, from east to west, including the evacuation of wounded soldiers and civilians fleeing the conflict. Its development was commissioned by Bundeswehr Inspector General Carsten Breuer in the wake of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. As Germany's highest-ranking military officer, Breuer is far from alone in his concern that Russia could target additional countries. Germany is already confronting a wide range of Russian hostile activities, from cyberattacks to acts of sabotage directed against the Bundeswehr.

German spy chief warns of rising Russia threat To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Defense Minister Pistorius: 'Moscow is testing our response'

A new dimension of the threat emerged with the attempted attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport in early August. An explosive-laden drone was deployed there and failed to detonate only through luck. The German government holds Russia responsible. "The threat is becoming more tangible. It is serious, acute, and increasingly visible. This is exactly what the Russian president wants. Moscow is testing our response," Defense Minister Boris Pistorius of the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD) told the Bundestag on September 23.

The Bundeswehr is also addressing this threat through the Operations Plan Germany, which is continuously being refined and updated. Lessons learned from exercises such as "Red Storm Charlie" are incorporated into the plan. According to Bohnert, the plan also serves as a deterrent: "We hope to discourage Russia from further aggression by demonstrating our strength through the rapid build-up of military capabilities and the highly organized, swift deployment of forces to the borders."

Roads and bridges need upgrading

How well prepared is Germany for its role as a military logistics hub? Matlé identifies one major vulnerability in the country's ageing and, in some cases, deteriorating infrastructure. Germany, she argues, must address the maintenance and repair of the bridges, roads, and transport routes required for troop movements "far more quickly and comprehensively." "Some of this infrastructure dates back to the Cold War and was not designed to accommodate heavy loads or military equipment."

A further challenge lies in striking the right balance between confidentiality and public involvement. To guard against acts of sabotage, sensitive details such as the precise transit routes for NATO troops must not fall into Russian hands. At the same time, the plan can only succeed through close cooperation between the Bundeswehr and civilian society, including local and regional authorities, the police, and relief organizations. "Parts of the plan must be publicly accessible because we need support from society, as well as from ministries and governments, to make it work," said Bohnert.

Could the AfD pass on sensitive information?

The debate over the confidentiality of the more than 1,000-page document recently resurfaced after the far-right Alternative for Germany(AfD) emerged as the strongest party in recent elections in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt.

Security experts expressed concern that the party, which is classified in part as right-wing extremist and is regarded as Russia-friendly, could pass information from the plan to Moscow if it were to assume the office of state premier. The Defense Ministry rejected these concerns, noting that no federal state is given access to the complete document. Instead, the sensitive sections of the Operations Plan are shared only in excerpts and strictly on a need-to-know basis.

According to observers, however, the growing number of hybrid threats is underscoring the need for secrecy. During the "Red Storm Charlie" exercise in Hamburg, accredited journalists were not informed of routes or locations until the very last moment because of concerns over potential disruptions and acts of sabotage.

This article was originally written in German.

World.title: US midterms: Women candidates could make history
World.content:
The US is holding Congress and state governors elections. At all levels of US politics, women are underrepresented — but they may win some historic victories in the midterms on November 3.

Around 51% of the population of the United States is female, but that is not reflected in the make-up of the US Congress, where only 28.4% of the members are women . Nevertheless, with 152 women in total sitting in the House of Representatives and Senate, the number is higher than it has ever been in the history of the United States. The number of female governors of the 50 US states is also currently higher than ever before: Some 14 of them — 28% — are women.

There are a number of reasons why there are still comparatively few female representatives in the US Congress. "Some of them are structural: There are rules and processes in place in our political system that make it harder for any newcomers to break in," says Kelly Dittmar, director of research at the Center for American Women and Politics (CAWP) at Rutgers University. "Historically, women were newcomers."

Seats in the Senate only come up for election every six years. Members of the House of Representatives serve two-year terms, but there is no limit to the number of times they can stand for reelection, so in theory they can stay in office for decades.

Also, as Dittmar points out, election campaigns in the US are very expensive. Women have historically been less able to access networks of rich donors — who, like many party leaders, are still most likely to be men. Leading male politicians are also more likely to recruit men to stand as new candidates. Finally, cultural biases also play a role: "Stereotypes and expectations about what women can and should do."

The elections on November 3 will decide whether more or fewer women will sit in the US Congress over the next two years. All 435 seats in the House of Representatives and 35 of the 100 seats in the Senate are up for election in the midterms. And in 36 states, the citizens will also decide who will move in to the governor's villa.

Amy Klobuchar is already a leading Democrat in the Senate Image: Nathan Posner/Anadolu/picture alliance

House of Representatives: Female Democrats outnumber female Republicans three to one

125 of the 435 representatives in the House are women. As in the Senate, and also with the gubernatorial posts, they are not evenly distributed between the two parties: There are more women among the Democrats than among the Republicans. At present, there are 95 women sitting as representatives for the Democrats, and 30 for the Republicans.

"There is a far less robust support infrastructure for women within the Republican Party," says Dittmar. She comments that organizations that specifically recruit, train, and fund women candidates are almost all either on the Democrat side, or non-partisan. Besides, she adds, "A lot of the [Republican] party leaders don't see an electoral incentive or pressure" to recruit more women. Diversity is more important to Democrat voters, who place greater value on seeing women among their elected representatives.

The Republicans currently have a majority in the House of Representatives, which means that they also get to appoint the Speaker or majority leader. At the moment, the position is held by Mike Johnson. Only one woman has held this powerful post to date: Nancy Pelosi, who was the Democrats' Speaker from 2007 to 2011, and again from 2019 to 2023.

Peggy Flanagan wants to become the first Native American woman to join the US Senate Image: Stephen Maturen/Getty Images/AFP

US Senate: Even higher bar for women

Women currently constitute 27% of the US Senate – 16 Democrats and 11 Republicans. Each of the 50 states is represented by two senators. The term of office is longer in this chamber of the US Congress, and the majority of the officials here represent many more voters than the representatives in the lower house.

According to Dittmar, it's even harder for women to win a seat in the Senate. "With the Senate, it's an opportunity and timing issue," she says. Each seat comes up for election every six years. There are 100 in total, and every two years only a third of them are available. Little opportunity, then, for women who have not previously sat in the Senate to advance. A state-wide senatorial election campaign is also more expensive than the equivalent campaign for a seat in the House of Representatives — and studies indicate that female candidates are generally less wealthy than their male counterparts.

For one senatorial candidate, the November midterms could prove historic. If the Democrat Peggy Flanagan wins in Minnesota, she will be the first Native American woman to sit in the US Senate. Flanagan is Ojibwe, otherwise known as Chippewa, an indigenous people from the Great Lakes region spanning the US and Canada.

Flanagan currently holds the post of lieutenant governor of Minnesota. Polls suggest that her chances are good. She has a slight lead over her rival, the Republican Michele Tafoya, previously a sports reporter and advisor to conservative politicians.

Keisha Lance Bottoms is vying to become the first ever female black governor Image: Elijah Nouvelage/Getty Images/AFP

First black woman state governor?

Ten of the current 14 female governors are Democrats, while four are Republicans. Six of the 14 are standing again, including Sarah Huckabee Sanders, the governor of Arkansas, who was President Trump's press secretary during his first term in office.

For the first time in US history, it is possible that a Black woman may be elected state governor. In Minnesota, the Democrat Tim Walz — Kamala Harris's vice-presidential candidate in the 2024 election — is not standing for reelection. The main rivals for his seat are the Democrat Amy Klobuchar and the (Black) Republican Lisa DeMuth. Meanwhile, the Black Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms is running for governor of the state of Georgia.

Kelly Dittmar doesn't think DeMuth will win in Minnesota — the state is regarded as solidly Democrat. And Klobuchar is well known among the people there; she has represented Minnesota in the US Senate since 2007.

But in Georgia, according to Dittmar, it's a different story: "That race is considered a toss-up, 50-50." Dittmar believes that Bottoms "absolutely has a chance to be the first Black woman governor." Former President Barack Obama is her most prominent supporter, while President Trump has declared his support for the Republican candidate, Rick Jackson.

This article has been translated from German.

World.title: Taiwan to boost military spending to 'deter war' with China
World.content:
President Lai Ching-te ⁠said in a National Day speech that his country is boosting defense spending to 'deter war' with China. It comes after US President Donald Trump asked Taiwan to pay for US protection.

Taiwan plans to boost defense spending to deter war, President Lai Ching-te said on Saturday, as China steps up military pressure to assert its claim over the self-governed island.

Lai's government has allocated a record NT$1.1 trillion ($34.5 billion) for defense spending in 2027, equivalent to more than 3% of GDP.

Taiwan's 23 million people face the threat of a Chinese attack. Beijing claims the island as part of its territory and has not ruled out using force to bring it under its control.

"Our aim in increasing investment in national defence is not to provoke, but to deter war," President Lai Ching-te said in a speech marking Taiwan's National Day.

Successive governments have increased military spending as Taiwan strengthens its defenses against a potential Chinese invasion and seeks to demonstrate to the United States its commitment to defending itself.

Lai says China must respect Taiwanese people's right to exist

"We do not seek hegemony, nor do we seek to dominate others," Lai said in his annual address outside the Presidential Office in Taipei, attended by thousands of people, including foreign diplomats.

He warned that peace could not be taken for granted, accusing China of using military and grey-zone activities to change the status quo across the Taiwan Strait.

Lai welcomed talks between the United States and China but stressed that Beijing must respect "the right of the people of Taiwan to exist."

Officials in Washington and Taipei have repeatedly said US policy on Taiwan remains unchanged under President Donald Trump, although some of his remarks have raised concerns in Taipei.

US arms deal in focus as Taiwan awaits Trump's approval

Trump raised concerns in May when he suggested that US arms sales to Taiwan could be used as a bargaining chip in negotiations with Chinese President Xi Jinping, following their meeting in Beijing.

Taiwan is awaiting Trump's approval of $14 billion in weapons sales, including the US-made Patriot air defense system.

At a high-profile summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington in September, trade and artificial intelligence dominated the agenda. One of the most contentious issues, Taiwan, was discussed only behind closed doors.

Ahead of Lai's speech, Taiwanese fighter jets and two Chinook helicopters carrying giant Taiwan flags flew over the capital.

Facing China's much larger military, which continues to expand its arsenal with advanced weapons, including stealth fighter jets, aircraft carriers and a vast array of missiles, Taiwan is increasing defence spending and modernising its armed forces.

Lai said Taiwan's resolve was about more than its survival in the face of "authoritarian expansion" in his National Day speech Image: Chiang Ying-ying/AP Photo/picture alliance

Washington remains Taipei's most important security backer

China's Taiwan Affairs Office did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Lai's speech. Beijing has never renounced the use of force to bring Taiwan under its control, calls Lai a "separatist" and has rejected his offers of talks.

Democratically governed Taiwan faces growing military and political pressure from China, which claims the island as its territory despite strong objections from the government in Taipei.

The United States welcomed Lai's commitment to maintaining peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait. A senior US administration official said that, referring to China, "a routine speech is no justification for aggressive or coercive actions."

The United States switched official diplomatic relations from Taipei to Beijing nearly 50 years ago, but Washington is Taipei's most important security backer.

Saturday's celebrations marked the 115th anniversary of the 1911 revolution that toppled China's Qing dynasty and paved the way for the founding of the Republic of China.

The dispute between China and Taiwan dates back to the Chinese civil war, when nationalist leader Chiang Kai-shek fled to the island in 1949 after his forces were defeated by Mao Zedong's communists.

Edited by: Roshni Majumdar

World.title: Is China seeking to restrict Taiwan's cultural presence?
World.content:
From coffee competitions to literature awards, Beijing appears to be working to limit Taiwan's international cultural and political impact.

When Taiwaneseauthor Yang Shuang-zi's "Taiwan Travelogue" won the 2026 International Booker Prize, it marked a historic breakthrough on the global stage. But behind the triumph lay a sharp geopolitical reality.

On stage, Lin King, who translated the book into English, gave voice to the anxiety looming over Taiwan, where she spent a large part of her childhood.

"In 2022, when Russia invaded Ukraine, I made the explicit decision that rather than translating Sinophone works indiscriminately, I would only translate writing from Taiwan for the foreseeable future," she said in her acceptance speech. "I will continue to do so until the day comes that my homeland's sovereignty is no longer a provocation or a punchline — until no English speaker feels comfortable saying to me, 'I really should come visit you in Taiwan while it still exists.'"

Literature and politics

"Taiwan Travelogue" follows a young Japanese writer visiting Japanese-colonized Taiwan in May 1938 on an official government-sponsored lecture tour. As she and her Taiwanese interpreter explore local street food together, a subtle intimacy unfolds between them. The narrative centers Taiwan's history rather than Beijing's preferred "Greater China" framework.

"Literature and politics are directly connected," Yang told DW. "Politics determines the allocation of resources, and the allocation of resources determines which works get pulled out, held up high and defined as 'good literature.' The idea that politics can just be kept out of it doesn't exist."

A few days after the 2026 International Booker Prize was announced, China's Taiwan Affairs Office reacted by saying: "Writers from both sides of the Taiwan Strait should firmly uphold a national standpoint, respect historical facts, and squarely face the immense suffering inflicted upon the Chinese people ... by Japan's war of aggression and fascism."

"From China's perspective, they do not want to see Taiwan's voice gain prominence." Yang said.

Her book demonstrates that Taiwanese culture is shaped by multiple historical strands — including indigenous, Japanese colonial and local Han influences, rather than being merely a "branch of Chinese culture."

During Yang's German book tour this October, an event at the Literaturhaus in Munich sparked controversy when the writer's interpreter significantly shortened certain statements concerning Taiwan, China, history, and politics. The interpreter later admitted that there had been oversights and shortcomings in the translation but denied deliberately deleting content due to their political stance or the situation in Taiwan.

Taiwan and China

Beijing claims Taiwan as a Chinese province and has long threatened to use force to bring the island under its control. Taiwan's democratically elected president has rejected Beijing's assertion that its laws apply to Taiwan.

Since 1949, Taiwan has functioned with de facto independence, maintaining its own government, military, and legal systems while facing ongoing military pressure from Beijing.

Taiwan's democratically elected president, Lai Ching-te, rejects China's assertion that its laws apply to Taiwan Image: Taiwan Presidential Office/AP Photo/Picture alliance

China's international overreach?

China's monitoring of Taiwanese international engagement reaches far further than words over a literature prize.

"The target of suppression and harassment primarily include outspoken individuals, exiled activists, diaspora community organizers, alongside their family members and close affiliates back home," said Dr. Yan-ho Lai, senior fellow of Georgetown Center for Asian Law. "From the PRC's (People's Republic of China) eyes, these groups are a threat to regime security, as they are able to amplify the dissenting voices and alternative stories of China to the West."

In April this year, Taiwanese barista Lin Shao-hsing, also known as Bala, won the 2026 World Latte Art Championship in the United States. Soon after, all mention of Taiwan as it related to Bala's win was removed from the official World Coffee Championships website.

It now says that Bala was representing "the competition body of Chinese Taipei," a term often used in international contests, such as the Olympics, to refer to Taiwan, but almost never used in Taiwan itself.

According to a 2026 poll by National Chengchi University's Election Study Center, the vast majority of people in Taiwan identify as "Taiwanese," while only 2.5% identify as Chinese.

In 2024, China allegedly planned to stage a "car collision" during Taiwanese Vice President Hsiao Bi-khim's visit to the Czech capital Prague. Czech intelligence officials told local media that the incident had been part of a much larger and escalatory plan by Chinese diplomats and intelligence officers working out of the Chinese embassy in Prague.

In early October this year, the FBI said authorities arrested a woman in California for allegedly spying on the son of Taiwan's president.

According to the US Department of Justice, the woman had traveled to Seattle in 2025 under instructions from Beijing to monitor the Taiwanese president's son and his family, capturing photos, video footage, and license plate information.

During a press conference on October 6, China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said it "consistently opposes the hype surrounding so-called 'Chinese spies' and the smearing and vilification of China."

"It reflects the ambiguity and limitation of international law, that the PRC using soft power to restrict the visibility of Taiwan may not directly fall into international law arena, as Taiwan is not recognized by international bodies as a sovereign state party." said Dr. Lai.

Edited by: Kate Martyr

World.title: How the Houthi-Saudi conflict is affecting countries on Africa's Red Sea coast — and beyond
World.content:
The Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which Yemeni government forces are trying to take back from the Houthis, is located not far from Djibouti and other African states.

In September, one of the major conflicts in the Middle East came within sight of Africa, as Iran-backed Houthi rebels captured Yemen's Perim Island.

The island forms the narrowest point of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which connects the southern entrance of the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden. It is roughly 20 kilometers (12 miles) from Djibouti and 20-minutes by air from Ethiopia.

In early October, Yemen's armed forces and their Saudi allies launched a counteroffensive. The Iran-backed Houthis have been firing on merchant ships since the start of the Gaza war in 2023.

Economic consequences are coupled with higher number of refugees

African economies are already suffering from crisis in the Strait of Hormuz, which is making fuel and fertilizer scarce and more expensive.

If the Bab el-Mandeb Strait also becomes impassable, the situation could deteriorate further. Shipping companies would have to make detours via the Suez Canal, which is controlled by Egypt, or the southern tip of Africa, as some already do. The additional costs would be passed on to consumers.

Bab el-Mandeb trade disruption: What it means for Djibouti To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The human cost of the escalation in Yemen hit Djibouti almost immediately. According to the UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR), at least 3,700 refugees have crossed from Yemen into Djibouti since September. Most of those who made it to the country's northern Obock region are women and children.

The UNHCR is preparing to assist another 10,000 people who have not yet crossed into Djibouti. But Obock, which is on the border with Eritrea, is extremely dry and this is causing other issues.

"We don't have much water here. There's no groundwater at all," Alessandra Roccasalvo, the UN Development Program (UNDP) representative for Djibouti, told DW. "Everything has to be desalinated."

Thousands flee to Djibouti from Yemen's war To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Djibouti is a strategic military hub

Despite its small size, Djibouti — a Muslim-majority country at the Horn of Africa with a population of just over a million — is a major player in the region. Its position at the entrance to the Red Sea makes it an attractive commercial and military shipping hub.

The United States, China, France, Italy, and Japan all operate military bases in Djibouti. The German Bundeswehr was also present until 2021, as part of a naval mission to combat maritime piracy.

The country's civilian ports serve as transshipment, or intermediate hubs for global shipping cargo, goods and containers. So far, the Houthi advance has not led to empty docks in Djibouti.

But there are still potential consequences, said Roccasalvo: "Basically, there's an economic upswing here — which means, as in any country experiencing an upswing, building materials are needed: cement, raw materials, and other things."

Less of that money is now coming in because ships have to pay nearly twice as much for insurance and reinsurance as they used to. "Many ships no longer want to pass through the Suez Canal. Many no longer want to pass through the Red Sea."

Knock-on effects for landlocked neighboring Ethiopia

Ethiopia — the world's most populous landlocked country — handles about 95% of its imports and exports through Djibouti's ports. Price hikes resulting from higher shipping insurance premiums to cover for potential war-related loss are affecting the country greatly.

Shortly after the Houthis seized Perim, Ethiopia's economy faced another, even more immediate threat: On September 23, fighting broke out in the country's northern Tigray region.

Since then, the Ethiopian National Defense Forces (ENDF) have reportedly made gains against the Tigray-led rebel coalition that aims to overthrow the national government. The rebels briefly advanced toward the main corridor used for transporting goods between Djibouti's ports and the Ethiopian hinterland.

Why northern Ethiopia is seeing growing violence once again To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

According to certain experts, the ENDF's advances have since reduced the threat of yet another trade blockade — but as long as the conflict remains unresolved, the situation could potentially deteriorate again.

For months now, Ethiopia has suffered more than almost any other African country from the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and has already had to ration fuel at times. In the long term, the country aims to reduce its dependence on imports, for example by powering vehicles with domestically generated electricity instead of imported gasoline.

In early 2024, Ethiopia became the first country in the world to impose a ban on the import of internal combustion engine vehicles Image: Shewangizaw Wegayehu/DW

Can the conflict in Ethiopia affect Bab el-Mandeb access?

Ethiopia and its northern neighbor, Eritrea, have severed diplomatic ties; other regional powers such as Sudan, Egypt, and Somalia may find themselves siding with Eritrea rather than with Ethiopia.

Eritrea sees itself as facing a threat that Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has reiterated on several occasions: With Ethiopia deprived of access to the sea since Eritrea's independence, Abiy has often alluded to rectifying this perceived injustice — either through a political agreement, as was once sought with Somalia's breakaway region of Somaliland, or by force.

The port of Assab is located on the edge of Eritrea's panhandle — and is often described as the most likely target should Abiy choose the path of aggression. If the fighting within Ethiopia further escalates into a full-blown regional war, this could also lead to additional restrictions on safe passage through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and the surrounding waters.

Experts have also raised concerns about the Shiite Houthis increasingly collaborating with the Sunni terrorist group Al-Shabab, which is based in Somalia. Although their ideologies are fundamentally different, they are particularly united by their hostility toward Israel and the US.

Inside Somalia's arms smuggling network To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

What tools are at the disposal of African countries to help remedy the situation?

The three African non-permanent members of the UN Security Council — the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Liberia, and Somalia — held an emergency meeting in mid-September, jointly calling for free shipping lanes and endorsing the demand that the crisis in Yemen be resolved under the auspices of the UN.

Liberia's UN Ambassador Lews Garseedah Brown formulated joint principles with his counterparts from Somalia and the Congo: the African nations are hoping for a UN-led diplomatic solution for Yemen Image: Bianca Otero/ZUMA/picture alliance

The situation at Bab el-Mandeb and in northern Ethiopia once again demands flexibility from Africa. In fact, some African economies could also benefit from relocation activities: Ports inKenya and Tanzania, for example, are becoming increasingly attractive for transshipment.

And while many countries are suffering from high oil prices, Nigeria's Dangote Group has announced an initial public offering and a new refinery in Kenya.

This article was originally published in German. It has been updated.

Edited by: Benita van Eyssen

World.title: Indian authorities crack down on 'Cockroach' protest in central Delhi. Follow live.
World.content:
Videos released by opposition leaders show that several senior figures were detained in New Delhi on Saturday.

They include Arvind Kejriwal, leader of the Aam Aadmi Party and former chief minister of Delhi.

"It's official... we are living under an absolute dictatorship," Kejriwal wrote on X.

Mamata Banerjee, who lost power as West Bengal's chief minister earlier this year, was also detained.

Pinarayi Vijayan, a communist leader who headed the southern state of Kerala until May, was among those detained.

Rahul Gandhi, leader of India's opposition Congress party, called the crackdown an act of "cowardice" and described Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah, right-wing, Hindu nationalist RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat, Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and National Security Adviser Ajit Doval as "the villains of this story" who were "slowly finding the space closing around them. We are closing that space."

Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Rahul Gandhi's sister and a Congress MP, wrote in a social media post: "India is not a democracy anymore. It is a dictatorship being run by Mr. Narendra Modi and Mr. Amit Shah."

Opposition parties and critics have warned that the electoral-roll revision exercise could strip millions of people of their voting rights and give an advantage to Prime Minister Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

The Election Commission of India has rejected allegations of wrongdoing, saying the "special intensive revision" aims to remove duplicate and ineligible voters.

The protests echo the CJP's mass mobilization in July, which forced the then education minister to resign over an examination scandal.

This time, demonstrators are demanding the resignation of election chief Gyanesh Kumar.

World.title: Sánchez se centra en vivienda y ataca al PP por dudar del voto por correo: “Estos son los de cuantos menos voten, mejor”
World.content:
Pedro Sánchez ha arrancado en el auditorio Los del Río de Dos Hermanas (Sevilla) su primer mitin de la larga campaña electoral ante unas 5.000 personas, según el PSOE. Los socialistas han dejado definitivamente atrás las invocaciones a la llegada de la derecha y la extrema derecha. Ya gobiernan juntas en cuatro comunidades. Ya están ahí, así que hay poca novedad. A lo que sí ha apelado el presidente del Gobierno y candidato a la reelección es a Maricarmen Abascal, la mujer de 87 años que falleció el pasado miércoles días después de haber sido desalojada de la que había sido su casa durante 70 años.

“La causa social lleva el nombre de una mujer de 87 años y honraremos ese ejemplo de vida cuando afirmó: ‘Lo que yo he sufrido, que no lo sufra nadie más”, ha dicho Sánchez, que se ha mostrado convencido de que el desbordamiento de la sociedad es lo que procurará “una mayoría progresista”. Y se ha comprometido a reforzar los decretos ley de la vivienda tras las elecciones, dando por hecho que ganará.

01:30 Sánchez, sobre los que ponen en duda el voto por correo: “Ahora son los de ‘cuantos menos voten, mejor” El presidente del Gobierno y secretario general del PSOE, Pedro Sánchez, en Dos Hermanas (Sevilla), durante el primer mitin de precampaña electoral. Foto: PACO PUENTES

Sánchez se ha referido al “bulo” de que el voto por correo en España no es seguro. “¿No os parece un poco raro?”, se ha preguntado el líder socialista, quien cree que tras esa duda lo que el PP manifiesta es “miedo porque van a perder”. En un intento de ser pedagógico, Sánchez ha afirmado que el voto por correo lo utilizan los trabajadores que están de guardia en domingo o los que “viven fuera” o “las personas desvalidas” que ni pueden desplazarse por sí solas. “Estos de ‘los que puedan hacer que hagan’ [una frase de José María Aznar] son los de ‘cuantos menos voten, mejor”.

En su opinión, el PP y Vox llevan ocho años lanzando “mensajes de miedo” y están siempre con la “fábula de Pedro y el lobo. El lobo son ellos; yo, en todo caso, un perro que no tiene amo”.

Una simpatizante de Pedro Sánchez sostiene un cartel con su imagen, este sábado en Dos Hermanas (Sevilla). PACO PUENTES

Antes del mitin, el PSOE ha publicado en redes un vídeo de campaña donde se recogen todos los insultos dirigidos al presidente del Gobierno y candidato socialista a la reelección. Feijóo, Abascal, Tellado, Milei, Trump, Díaz Ayuso, entre otros, aparecen profiriendo graves acusaciones contra el líder socialista. Un cartel con las palabras “Pedro Sánchez, hijo de puta” cierra la primera parte del vídeo. ¿Por qué nos insultan?”, se preguntan. “Nos insultan porque somos el Gobierno de la gente que pone en su sitio a los de arriba”, responden. El PSOE ya convirtió en suya la expresión “PerroSánchez” a su favor, y ahora pretende hacer lo mismo con los insultos, en un video que evoca el difundido por los socialistas en la campaña de 1996, en el que se veía la imagen de un amenazante perro dóberman con el que el PSOE quería alertar de lo que ocurriría si el PP de José María Aznar llegaba a La Moncloa, como finalmente ocurrió. Sánchez ha justificado en algunas ocasiones determinadas decisiones de las que renegaba en el pasado apelando a que había que hacer “de la necesidad virtud”. Más o menos es lo que pretende hacer ahora. El lema electoral en estos primeros días es “La fuerza de la gente”.

Sánchez ha apelado al triunfo de la política frente a la “mala educación” y ha asegurado que estas elecciones son de “susto o muerte”, porque si el PP sigue en la oposición, seguirá con los insultos y, si gobierna, “recortan”. Tanto el candidato como la secretaria general del PSOE andaluz y vicesecretaria federal, María Jesús Montero, han hecho repaso de la gestión del Gobierno (subida de las pensiones, SMI, reforma laboral, crecimiento económico) y han advertido de la propuesta de Vox de implantar un sistema mixto de pensiones.

Menos de 24 horas después de anunciar el pasado lunes la disolución de las Cortes y la convocatoria de las elecciones para el 29 de noviembre, la secretaría federal de Organización comunicó al PSOE andaluz que Sánchez abriría la campaña en Dos Hermanas por deseo expreso del presidente del Gobierno. Después de perder el poder en todas las capitales de provincia andaluzas, esta ciudad es la más grande que gobiernan los socialistas en Andalucía. Sánchez arrancó aquí en 2017 su carrera interna para recuperar la secretaría general del PSOE, tras su dramática salida en 2016. En Dos Hermanas inició la campaña de 2019 y de nuevo eligió esta ciudad en la de 2023. “El presidente tiene un especial vínculo emocional con Dos Hermanas”, comentó días atrás la secretaria general del PSOE de Andalucía, María Jesús Montero.

Pedro Sánchez, junto a María Jesús Montero y Francisco Rodríguez. PACO PUENTES

La elección de esta ciudad de 146.522 habitantes para arrancar la campaña tiene mucho de simbología porque pretende invocar a las remontadas de Sánchez en momentos difíciles. Y es una manera de lanzar el mensaje de que el PSOE andaluz, en sus horas más bajas, aún tiene músculo para llenar los recintos. El sitio escogido es el auditorio Los del Río, con capacidad para 3.386 personas sentadas, aunque dispone de una gran extensión de césped y puede llegar a albergar hasta 4.526 personas, según recoge la web de la Junta. “Es una ciudad talismán y queremos llevar al presidente en volandas”, afirma el secretario adjunto de Organización del PSOE andaluz, Alejandro Moyano. Para llenar el auditorio, han tocado el cornetín en las ocho provincias andaluzas, con la contratación de un centenar de autobuses. Pese al esfuerzo, este acto palidece con los que antaño se celebraron en el velódromo nazareno, donde el PSOE llegó a reunir a 20.000 personas para escuchar a Felipe González, Alfonso Guerra o José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero, todos hoy fuera de juego por distintos motivos.

El PSOE andaluz afronta otro reto seis meses después de las autonómicas de mayo ―donde obtuvo el peor resultado de su historia en unas autonómicas). Lleva perdidas las cinco últimas elecciones —andaluzas de 2022; municipales de 2023; generales de 2023; europeas de 2024 y andaluzas de 2026— y está por ver si conseguirá quebrar esa curva descendente. En 2023, los resultados en Andalucía y Cataluña fueron claves para apuntalar a Pedro Sánchez. Aportaron 21 y 19 escaños, respectivamente. En esta ocasión, Andalucía elige 60 diputados, uno menos por la pérdida de población en Cádiz que gana Madrid. El pasado mayo, el PP aventajó al PSOE en Andalucía en 19 puntos, lo mismo que hace cuatro años en autonómicas. Pero en las generales ese margen se estrecha mucho. Ocurrió en 2023, cuando los socialistas lograron recortar, movilizaron más de medio millón de votos y se quedaron a tres puntos. Ese es el objetivo también ahora.

World.title: Carrie White no se quema en el infierno
World.content:
Carrie White no se quema en el infierno, pese a la pintada frente a su casa que aparecía en las últimas páginas de la novela de Stephen King y en el inolvidable final con susto que remataba la no menos célebre adaptación cinematográfica de Brian de Palma de 1976. No, la atormentada adolescente de 16 años con poderes telequinésicos Carietta White que devastó la población de Chamberlain, Maine, causando según las últimas estimaciones (de la novela) 440 muertos confirmados y 18 desaparecidos (77 de las víctimas estudiantes del Instituto Ewen), sigue entre nosotros, y muy activa. Ahora, una nueva edición en catalán de la obra de King (Carrie, traducción de Míriam Cano, Males Herbes, 2026), se suma al homenaje que le rinde al personaje el festival de cine de Sitges, que le dedica su cartel al cumplirse 50 años de la película, y al estreno esta misma semana en Amazon Prime Video de la serie de ocho episodios que vuelve a adaptar el libro (hubo otros dos remakes cinematográficos en 2002 y 2013, aparte de una secuela). El papel de Carrie, que hizo inolvidablemente Sissy Spaceck, lo interpreta en la serie Summer H. Howell, a la que acredita en el terror su relación con el infame muñeco Chucky.

Es difícil dar la medida hoy de lo que significó Carrie cuando la leímos por primera vez y éramos absolutamente vírgenes -como la propia Carietta- de los horrores que nos desvelaría en los años siguientes Stephen King. Corría 1976 (la edición que cayó en nuestras manos era la primera en castellano de Pomaire, de ese año; la primera en catalán es de 1988, en Laertes, en 2000 la publicó La Magrana), y fue un shock. La mezcla del relato con supuestas noticias sobre el caso y otros textos ficticios que contextualizaban la historia de Carrie (entrevistas de testigos, informes psiquiátricos, fragmentos de un libro acerca del suceso, las memorias de la amiga, Susan Snell, frases apuntadas en una libreta por la propia protagonista) conferían un tono de crónica real a la novela. La devoramos: era una nueva forma de narrar el terror como algo que emergía en lo cotidiano, aquí al lado. Algunos pasamos directamente de los clásicos del género (Bram Stoker, Mary Shelley, Poe, Lovecraft) a Carrie.

Muy poco después llegarían Salem’s Lot (La hora del vampiro en la edición de Pomaire) y El resplandor (seguramente las dos mejores novelas de King), Christine, La zona muerta, Ojos de fuego (en la que volvía al tema de los superpoderes psíquicos, en este caso los de una niña, Charlie, perseguida por una agencia gubernamental para realizar experimentos)… Pero Carrie ha permanecido como la gran novela iniciática de muchos fans de Stephen King. Ayudó la película, claro: con sus momentos culminantes del bombardeo de la pobre Sissy con compresas y tampones en la ducha del instituto durante su primera, desconocida, regla; el baño de sangre de cerdo en la fiesta de graduación con la Spacek literalmente teñida de rojo y de un espanto que deriva a una explosión de ira y violencia (por ahí andaba acarreando cubos John Travolta como el malote del instituto Billy Nolan), y la citada escena final, de la que nos sorprende hoy tanto la mano ensangrentada que sale del suelo como el peinado de Amy Irving (la amiga superviviente Sue) solo comparable al de Jenifer Beals en Flashdance.

Volver a leer Carrie en la nueva edición catalana despierta oleadas de melancolía, pero también produce la sorpresa de que resulta una novela muy fresca y que engancha, aunque lo sepas todo de ella (así que podemos imaginar lo que producirá en los nuevos lectores). El King de sus primeras obras era estupendo, no en balde nos conquistó a tantos (y el mercado). Carrie, que empezó como relato corto, no le resultó fácil de escribir (tenía 24 años, dos hijos pequeños, vivían en una autocaravana y le rechazaban todas las historias). De hecho, la tiró a la papelera tras el primer esbozo y fue solo gracias a la mano de su esposa Tabitha que la recuperó y la continuó hasta convertirla en su primer éxito. En la apasionante Monstruos en el archivo, de Caroline Bicks (Lunwerg, 2026), la autora explica los cambios que introdujo en Carrie hasta llegar a la versión definitiva. De entrada transcurría en Massachussets, y había muchos elementos sobrenaturales (a Carrie le salían cuernos y se convertía en un ser físicamente monstruoso). Bicks observa muy perspicazmente la influencia de las desgraciadas chicas jóvenes de Shakespeare (Ofelia, Julieta) en Carrie así como la imaginería sangrienta de Macbeth.

Summer H. Howell, en una imagen de 'Carrie'. Amazon Prime Video

Volver a los vestuarios de chicas del instituto después del entreno de voleibol, con la pobre Carrie (mucho más fea que en la peli y con ojos y cabellos castaños) duchándose “com una granota entre cignes”, y empezando a sangrar creyendo que se muere mientras las otras se ríen de ella (“tapa-t’ho! tapa-t’ho!, tapa t’ho!”) es revivir la experiencia Stephen King original. El escritor, que se basó en dos jovencitas inadaptadas de su propio instituto, situó su novela algo en el futuro, en 1979. Con todo se adelantó a la oleada de matanzas en los institutos de EE UU que se desató a partir de la del de Columbine en 1999. Porque Carrie tiene todos los ingredientes, y esto es escalofriante, de esos sucesos, empezando por la adolescente inadaptada que explota en una orgía de violencia salvaje. Es un gran debate moderno sobre Carrie si estamos ante una víctima o una perpetradora -incluso un monstruo- producto de una educación represiva (su madre, fanática ultra religiosa). De hecho, la novela es uno de los libros más prohibidos en las escuelas estadounidenses, no vaya a cundir el ejemplo. King también se adelantó al concepto de acoso escolar y bullying, del que Carietta es asimismo un ejemplo de manual.

Estamos en fin frente a un feliz, si puede decirse así, reencuentro con Carrie y una oportunidad de oro para repasar la carrera de un gran escritor popular y para revisar, bañados en sangre, uno de los mitos fundacionales del horror moderno, nada menos.

World.title: La Federación portuguesa de fútbol abre un expediente disciplinario a Cristiano Ronaldo y le impone una “suspensión preventiva”
World.content:
El futbolista abandonó de forma abrupta la selección el pasado 30 de septiembre por desavenencias con el seleccionador Jorge Jesus, tras no haber sido alineado en el partido contra Noruega en Oslo

La Federación Portuguesa de Fútbol (FPF) ha abierto un expediente disciplinario contra Cristiano Ronaldo tras su repentina salida de la selección de Portugal debido a desacuerdos con el seleccionador, Jorge Jesus, según anunció este sábado.

En un comunicado, el Comité Disciplinario de la Federación Portuguesa de Fútbol (FPF) afirma que Cristiano se encuentra bajo “suspensión preventiva” y que “se ha otorgado carácter urgente al proceso”. Según la nota, el caso está ahora en manos de la Comisión de Instrucción Disciplinaria de la Federación portuguesa.

Cristiano Ronaldo abandonó de forma abrupta la selección el pasado 30 de septiembre por desavenencias con Jorge Jesus, tras no haber sido alineado en el partido contra Noruega en Oslo el pasado 27 de septiembre (1-2). Según una nota del exmadridista, el motivo del desentendimiento fue Jesus haberlo hecho calentar durante media hora y luego no sacarlo al campo. También en ese comunicado, Cristiano afirmó que aceptaba una sanción por su decisión y dejó la puerta abierta a un regreso a la selección de Portugal tras ese posible castigo.

“El 9 de octubre de 2026, la Sección No Profesional inició un procedimiento disciplinario contra Cristiano Ronaldo dos Santos Aveiro con el objetivo de determinar la posible relevancia disciplinaria de los hechos denunciados el 7 de octubre de 2026. Sin perjuicio de la suspensión preventiva automática a la que estaba sujeto hasta la fecha de inicio del procedimiento, se determinó una suspensión preventiva no automática del jugador y se le otorgó carácter de urgencia. El expediente fue remitido el 10 de octubre de 2026 al Comité de Instrucción Disciplinaria de la FPF (Federación Portuguesa de Fútbol), y se excluyó su publicación hasta la finalización de la investigación”, dice el comunicado.

World.title: Las cajas de ahorro islámicas están de moda en Turquía
World.content:
Sus sucursales se han multiplicado en los últimos años, especialmente en las capitales de provincia del interior de Turquía, donde ocupan los puestos de honor de las principales avenidas. Sus lustrosos y modernos escaparates prometen hacer realidad los sueños de sus clientes: adquirir una casa, un automóvil o una tienda “sin necesidad de créditos” o “sin pagar intereses”. Son las Empresas de Financiación mediante Ahorro (TFS, en turco), una suerte de cajas de ahorro islámicas basadas en los principios de las finanzas islámicas, como el rechazo a los intereses —aunque esto, como mucho en las finanzas islámicas, tiene truco— y la mutualización del riesgo: un grupo de ahorradores aporta cuotas mensuales a un fondo común y, por turnos o por sorteo, cada miembro recibe el capital solicitado para adquirir la propiedad elegida.

Algunas, como Eminevim o Fuzul, se han convertido en grandes grupos empresariales. Comenzaron su existencia como sociedades de ahorro colectivo creadas durante los años noventa por empresarios del entorno del islamismo político deseosos de financiarse fuera de unos bancos controlados por la —entonces dominante— élite laica del país. Otras quebraron o fueron liquidadas, pues operaban en un vacío legal. Su historia cambió en 2021, cuando el Gobierno del conservador Recep Tayyip Erdogan endureció los requisitos de solvencia, profesionalizándolas y poniéndolas bajo el control de la Agencia de Regulación y Supervisión Bancaria. Pero sobre todo, su verdadera explosión se ha dado desde que, en 2023, Mehmet Simsek fue nombrado ministro de Finanzas con el mandato de reducir una tasa de inflación que había llegado a superar el 100% interanual. Aplicó el manual más ortodoxo e instó al Banco Central a elevar el precio del dinero, lo que ha supuesto que los bancos restrinjan los créditos y eleven los intereses de sus préstamos hipotecarios por encima del 40% anual (la inflación sigue sin bajar del 30%). “Debido a las medidas de macroprudencia financiera, se ha hecho muy difícil acceder a créditos bancarios. Aunque, al inicio, las TFS se dirigían a personas de bajos ingresos, ahora les interesan a trabajadores de cuello blanco e incluso a gente de ingresos altos que no puede acceder a créditos bancarios”, explica Ahmet Büyükduman, analista financiero.

Una comisión fija por adelantado

Frente a los elevados intereses que demandan los bancos —y que implican que se termine pagando casi cuatro veces el capital inicial en préstamos a diez años—, las TFS cobran una comisión fija por adelantado, equivalente a entre el 7% y el 10% del capital solicitado. La pega es que solo se puede acceder a la casa, el automóvil o el negocio que se va a adquirir cuando se ha aportado al fondo el 45% de su valor, lo cual puede ocurrir pronto —si se adelanta parte del capital o se eligen cuotas de pago mensuales elevadas— o tardar varios años. La TFS, luego, hipoteca el bien hasta que el cliente ha terminado de pagar los plazos, pero entretanto puede hacer uso de él. Otro de los problemas es la protección de los ahorros contra la inflación galopante, ya que la cantidad solicitada por un cliente al inicio del programa puede haberse convertido en insignificante cuando llega a ejecutarla. Así que las TFS han tenido que establecer programas de inversión de estos ahorros en oro, bonos del Estado acordes con las finanzas islámicas (sukuk) o fondos.

De los apenas 370.000 usuarios que las TFS tenían hace tres años en Turquía se ha pasado a más de 1,5 millones en la actualidad, y su tamaño en activos se ha multiplicado por diez hasta superar los 9.000 millones de euros. Aun así, apenas suponen una fracción de la banca tradicional, y es que muchos turcos mantienen cierta suspicacia: por el carácter islámico de este sistema y porque algunos lo acusan de ser un esquema piramidal, debido a la necesidad de que lleguen nuevos ahorradores para mantenerse. Pero Büyükduman atribuye estas críticas a falta de información: “También los bancos pueden quebrar si los depositantes se retiran”. Para este experto, lo más importante es que estas entidades “promueven el ahorro antes de ofrecer un préstamo” y permiten a personas que trabajan en sectores informales acceder a financiación.

World.title: ¿Qué aspirador comprar? Estos son los mejores modelos según el tipo de limpieza que busques
World.content:
Después de probar decenas de opciones, hemos reunido nuestros favoritos para ayudarte a encontrar el que mejor encaja con tu casa

Aspirar es una de esas tareas domésticas que hacemos casi por inercia, pero basta con fijarse un poco para darse cuenta de que no todos buscamos lo mismo a la hora de elegir un aspirador. El objetivo general no es otro que mantener la casa limpia a diario, pero puede que, además, tengamos mascotas y queramos acabar con los pelos del sofá o quizá busquemos una opción específica para limpiar el colchón. También hay modelos que incorporan vapor, otros que prescinden del cable y algunos que están especialmente pensados para determinados tipos de suelo.

Con tantas opciones sobre la mesa, elegir puede ser más complicado de lo que parece. El tipo de superficie, el uso que vayamos a darle, el espacio disponible o, incluso, la frecuencia con la que limpiemos son algunos de los aspectos que pueden hacer que un dispositivo resulte más adecuado que otro. En EL PAÍS Escaparate sabemos de lo que hablamos pues hemos probado decenas de modelos y, de hecho, ya valoramos los mejores aspiradores según su uso para comprobar cómo se comportaban en cada situación. Ahora hemos querido ir un paso más allá y hemos reunido en esta guía los que mejor resultado nos han dado en nuestras comparativas, para que encontrar el más adecuado sea un poco más sencillo.

Aspiradores escoba sin cable

Los aspiradores escoba sin cable destacan por su comodidad y versatilidad, ya que permiten limpiar distintas superficies sin depender de un enchufe y, además, muchos pueden convertirse también en modelos de mano. Tras probar varios modelos, el que más nos convenció fue el Dreame Z40 Station por su potencia, su base de autovaciado y la variedad de accesorios. Como actualmente no está disponible, el Dreame Z30 es una alternativa de la misma familia que mantiene buena parte de sus prestaciones, aunque prescinde de la mencionada base.

Aspirador escoba sin cable Dreame Z30. CORTESÍA DE AMAZON

Aspiradores con vapor

Los aspiradores con vapor combinan la recogida de suciedad con la limpieza mediante este sistema, por lo que permiten realizar ambas tareas en un mismo paso y conseguir así un acabado más preciso. En nuestra comparativa, el Polti Vaporetto fue elegido como el mejor por ofrecer un excelente equilibrio entre potencia, ligereza y maniobrabilidad. Durante la prueba destacó por su buen rendimiento con diferentes tipos de suciedad, además de por su comodidad de manejo gracias a sus 2,4 kilos de peso. Por último, cabe destacar que puede utilizarse como aspirador escoba y de mano, lo que amplía sus posibilidades de uso.

Aspirador con vapor Polti Vaporetto. CORTESÍA DE AMAZON

Aspiradores para mascotas

Los aspiradores para mascotas están especialmente pensados para recoger el pelo y la suciedad que perros y gatos dejan por casa, aunque cada formato responde a una necesidad diferente. Tras realizar varias pruebas, el Polti Rollysteam WD40C fue el mejor valorado por su versatilidad; además de aspirar y fregar, utiliza vapor para desinfectar y cuenta con filtro HEPA, autolimpieza y secado automático del rodillo.

Aspirador para mascotas Polti Rollysteam WD40C. CORTESÍA DE AMAZON

Aspiradores Dyson

No estaría completa esta guía sin hacer una mención especial a Dyson, una de las marcas más reconocidas dentro del mundo de los aspiradores gracias, en gran medida, a una gama que abarca diferentes formatos. Tras valorar varios de ellos, el Gen5detect fue nuestro favorito y, sin ninguna duda, también el aspirador escoba que mejor limpia de Dyson. Lo que más nos gustó fue su nuevo botón de encendido, que evita tener que mantenerlo pulsado durante la limpieza, y el cepillo Fluffy Optic, cuya luz verde ilumina el suelo y permite ver hasta las partículas de polvo más finas.

Aspirador escoba Dyson Gen5detect. CORTESÍA DE AMAZON

Aspiradores de mano

Los aspiradores de mano son una opción práctica para recoger rápidamente migas, polvo o pelos en superficies pequeñas y lugares de difícil acceso, tanto en casa como en el coche. El 2 en 1 sin cable de Black & Decker fue nuestro favorito por su diseño ergonómico y versatilidad, ya que permite aspirar tanto sólidos como líquidos y cuenta con una boquilla ancha para los residuos de mayor tamaño. Además, su depósito se puede enjuagar y su tamaño compacto facilita tenerlo siempre a mano.

Aspirador de mano 2 en 1 sin cable de Black & Decker. CORTESÍA DE AMAZON

Aspiradores para colchones

Los aspiradores para colchones están diseñados para eliminar polvo, pelos, ácaros y otras partículas que se acumulan en las superficies textiles. De todos los que probamos, el Jigoo J300 fue el modelo mejor valorado por su capacidad para realizar una limpieza profunda y por incorporar un sensor inteligente que muestra en pantalla el nivel de suciedad detectado. También nos gustó su potencia de 500 W y el sistema que combina aspiración, rodillo, luz ultravioleta, ultrasonidos y aire caliente.

Aspirador para colchón Jigoo J300. CORTESÍA DE AMAZON

Aspiradores sin bolsa

Los aspiradores sin bolsa prescinden, como su propio nombre indica, de las bolsas desechables y, en su lugar, acumulan la suciedad en un depósito que se vacía cuando es necesario. De todos, el Dyson Cinetic Big Ball Multi Floor 2 fue el que más nos gustó por su excelente calidad de fabricación, su poder de succión y un diseño especialmente manejable gracias a la manguera articulada de 360 grados. Además, gracias a su tecnología Cinetic puedes olvidarte de lavar o sustituir los filtros, lo que reduce considerablemente su mantenimiento.

Aspirador sin bolsa Dyson Cinetic Big Ball Multi Floor 2. CORTESÍA DE AMAZON

Aspiradores para suelos de madera

Los aspiradores para suelos de madera están diseñados para limpiar este tipo de superficies sin renunciar a una buena capacidad de succión. El Rowenta Silence Force Cyclonic fue nuestro favorito por su calidad y diseño, su amplio depósito de 2,5 litros y su rendimiento. Además, nos resultó muy manejable durante la limpieza.

Aspirador para suelos de madera Rowenta Silence Force Cyclonic. CORTESÍA DE AMAZON

Preguntas frecuentes sobre aspiradores

¿Cuál es el mejor aspirador para el hogar?

Depende del tipo de limpieza que realices y de las superficies de tu casa. Para una limpieza general, los aspiradores escoba sin cable son especialmente cómodos, mientras que los robots permiten mantener el suelo limpio de forma más autónoma.

¿Qué potencia tiene que tener un aspirador para que sea bueno?

No hay una cifra de vatios que determine por sí sola que un aspirador sea mejor. Conviene fijarse también en la potencia de succión, el diseño del cepillo, la capacidad del depósito y la eficiencia con la que recoge la suciedad.

¿Cada cuánto hay que limpiar el filtro de un aspirador?

Depende del modelo y de la frecuencia de uso, pero conviene revisarlo periódicamente y limpiarlo cuando acumule suciedad. Un filtro obstruido puede reducir el rendimiento del aspirador y aumentar su consumo.

[Recuerda que si eres usuario de Amazon Prime, todas las compras tienen gastos de envío gratuitos. Amazon ofrece un período de prueba gratuito y sin compromiso durante 30 días.]

*Todos los precios de compra incluidos en este artículo están actualizados a 10 de octubre de 2026.

World.title: Trump administration sanctions International Criminal Court
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

The United States has announced sweeping sanctions against the International Criminal Court (ICC), escalating Trump’s war on the international tribunal.

“We will ban transactions with this rogue court, cutting off their resources and crippling its ability to operate,” US secretary of state Marco Rubio said in an announcement.

The Trump administration has previously pledged to dismantle the court “brick by brick” and has sanctioned 13 current and former staff members, but this is the first time it has levied sanctions against the institution itself.

Ahead of the announcement, prime minister Rob Jetten said the Netherlands will protect the ICC “stone by stone”.

Foreign minister Tom Berendsen said the country would stand behind the court. “The announced sanctions against the International Criminal Court are an undesirable new escalation,” Berendsen said in a statement. “I deeply regret this new step.”

The sanctions will cut the court off from any US company or organisation, including providers of financial and technology services.

The announcement came hours after South African jurist Navi Pillay, who has served as a judge at both the ICC and the International Court of Justice in The Hague, was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.

Trump has long coveted the prize, telling reporters earlier this week that he deserved the award for what he said was ending eight wars.

World.title: Russia wants NL to hand over ICC judges
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Russia has asked the Netherlands to hand over nine International Criminal Court (ICC) officials who were convicted in absentia last year.

The prosecutor’s office in Moscow requested the extradition of the court’s president, Tomoko Akane, and other staff members for their involvement in the arrest warrant of Russian president Vladimir Putin.

The ICC issued the warrant for Putin’s alleged involvement in “the war crime of unlawful deportation of children” from occupied Ukraine.

The ICC has also issued an arrest warrant against Maria Alekseyevna Lvova-Belova, Russia’s commissioner for children’s rights.

In December, a court in Moscow convicted Akane and others in absentia, sentencing them to prison terms ranging from 3.5 to 15 years.

Japan, Akane’s home country, said the request was regrettable. “Measures targeting individuals connected to the ICC are unjust and unacceptable,” Masanao Ozaki, the country’s deputy chief cabinet secretary, said.

The United States has also sanctioned 13 staff members, including Akane, over the investigation into alleged Israeli war crimes in Gaza.

World.title: Unions call regional transport strike, threaten weekly walkout
World.content:
Regional bus services across the Netherlands will be heavily disrupted on Wednesday, after the FNV and CNV unions called a nationwide 24-hour strike in a dispute over a new pay and conditions deal.

If Wednesday’s strike does not shift the employers, the unions say they will hold an action day every week, and will only announce the dates shortly beforehand. Earlier this month they said they were considering weekly strikes in the run-up to Christmas.

Some 13,000 workers, mainly bus drivers, are covered by the public transport collective agreement, which expired on July 1. Staff at Arriva, EBS, Qbuzz, Keolis, Transdev and RET’s regional services are involved. City transport in Amsterdam, Rotterdam and The Hague is not affected.

Talks broke down after eight rounds of negotiations. This week an ultimatum to the employers’ organisation VWOV expired without a response.

“Employers are holding on to drastic cuts in working conditions,” FNV negotiator Marijn van der Gaag said in a statement. “In doing so, they are forcing their staff to take action.”

The unions say employers want to reduce sick pay, add more unpaid breaks to shifts and give staff less say over their rosters. Rosters are currently fixed about eight days in advance, and employers want to cut that to four days or less, Van der Gaag said.

The FNV wants a 6% pay rise. The CNV is calling for 9.5% over two years, as well as better arrangements for older workers and faster access to permanent contracts.

“We will not let employers sabotage the action by drawing up emergency rosters at the last minute,” CNV negotiator Niels Rook said, explaining why dates will not be announced in advance.

World.title: Former ICC judge Navi Pillay awarded Nobel Peace Prize
World.content:
South African jurist Navi Pillay, who has served as a judge at both the International Criminal Court and the International Court of Justice in The Hague, was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize on Friday for her efforts to promote peace and international law.

Most recently, the 85-year-old chaired the UN commission that concluded Israel had committed genocide.

Announcing the prize in Oslo, Jørgen Watne Frydnes, chair of the Norwegian Nobel Committee, said it was going to someone who “held states and national leaders accountable and brought hope to victims of violence and conflict”.

Reacting to the news in Nuremberg, Pillay said “if you clap a little bit more, I may share this prize with Trump.”

The award comes as the system of international justice is under attack. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has threatened to dismantle the International Criminal Court “brick by brick, if necessary”, and the US has sanctioned several of its staff.

Pillay played a significant role in the anti-apartheid movement in her homeland as a defence lawyer for Nelson Mandela and other activists. She went on to serve as a judge on the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, spending the last four of her eight years there as its president.

She was one of the ICC’s first judges, sitting in the appeals chamber from 2003 until 2008, when she stepped down to become UN High Commissioner for Human Rights.

In 2019, she was appointed as an ad hoc judge at the International Court of Justice by the Gambia, which had filed genocide proceedings against Myanmar over its treatment of the Rohingya minority.

Last year, as chair of the Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, she said Israel had committed genocide in Gaza.

In a post on social media, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen congratulated Pillay. “Few have devoted their lives to justice, peace and human dignity like she did,” she said.

The prize is administered by the Nobel Foundation and comes with 12 million Swedish kronor (around €1.07 million).

World.title: Museums, festivals and clubs in Groningen ban smart glasses

In a joint statement on Friday some 30 cultural organisations in Groningen announced they were banning the use of smart glasses from their buildings and events.

The devices, the most popular version is sold by Meta, look like normal glasses but allow users to film and take photos covertly.

“This technology compromises the privacy and safety of visitors, staff, and artists, and undermines trust in an open, respectful environment,” the statement says.

Backers including the Groninger Archieven, the Groninger Museum, Noorderlicht, Stichting Kunst & Cultuur and the Grand Theatre Groningen.

Last week, eyewear chain Hans Anders announced it would stop selling Meta camera glasses following demands from privacy advocates concerned about the so-called “pervert glasses”.

Dutch privacy watchdog AP has warned that sharing images made with camera glasses violates GDPR laws unless permission is given by everyone in the images.

The consumer watchdog Consumentenbond has also issued a warning about the glasses, noting that it was possible to manipulate or cover the indicator light to make it even harder to tell images were being captured.

MPs have called for a full ban on the glasses but the cabinet is opposed to a blanket measure and wants to see other restrictions put into place.

Utrecht music venue Tivoli Vredenburg banned smart glasses at its events in 2025 and has since refused entry to one man who would not take them off.

World.title: NL’s only legal medicinal cannabis grower goes bust
World.content:
Patients who use medicinal cannabis face having to switch to imported products after the only licensed grower in the Netherlands was declared bankrupt on Thursday.

A court in Groningen declared Veendam-based Bedrocan bankrupt two weeks after the company had applied for protection from its creditors. The firm, whose main growing site is in Emmeloord, employs around 70 people.

Bedrocan ran into trouble after the health ministry ended its contract at the start of this year. All medicinal cannabis sold in Dutch pharmacies is bought and distributed by the state-run Bureau for Medicinal Cannabis (BMC).

The ministry ended the deal in anticipation of a change in the law that will let growers sell directly to pharmacies. But health minister Sophie Hermans (VVD) told MPs in July that the change is not expected to take effect until July 1, 2028.

That left Bedrocan unable to supply the BMC and not allowed to sell to pharmacies itself, the Volkskrant reported. The state was by far its largest customer.

Limited stockpile

The BMC built up a stockpile of Bedrocan cannabis before the contract ended, but the minister said it was limited and had a finite shelf life. The BMC will switch to imported cannabis during 2027, with products matching current THC and CBD levels as closely as possible.

Around 7,000 people in the Netherlands are prescribed medicinal cannabis, according to the Volkskrant. They include people with multiple sclerosis (MS), severe pain, certain forms of epilepsy, and patients in palliative care.

Patients fear a different variety will not work as well for them. Cannabis contains many compounds that together determine its effect, and the mix depends on the plant and how it is grown.

The MS association has written to Hermans warning that some long-term patients depend on a specific variety.

Bedrocan also supplied patients in other European countries through the BMC. The BMC is due to stop exporting at the end of 2026. In September, Bedrocan told foreign pharmacies and wholesalers to order from it directly.

World.title: MPs vote to fly rainbow flag at parliament for first time
World.content:
The rainbow flag will fly at the Dutch parliament building on Sunday, Coming Out Day, after MPs overturned a decision by managers of parliament to drop the plan.

MPs backed the move by 90 votes to 36 in a vote late on Thursday night, public broadcaster NOS reported.

Parliament’s presidium, which runs its day-to-day affairs, initially agreed to the plan but changed its mind after Christian parties were told about the plan, RTL Nieuws reported on Thursday.

The orthodox Protestant SGP led the objections. “The rainbow flag is not a national flag but a flag of interest groups, which has grown into a symbol of activism,” SGP MP Diederik van Dijk told NOS.

Roll-call vote

Kati Piri, MP for opposition party Pro, then tabled a motion saying parliament should “stand up for the rights of the global LGBTI movement” and ensure “an inclusive working environment” for its staff.

Van Dijk responded by demanding a roll-call vote, in which each MP votes individually rather than by party. That meant MPs who had already gone home on Thursday had to return to The Hague.

Most MPs from D66, the VVD, CDA, PRO, PvdD, SP, ChristenUnie, 50PLUS and Volt voted in favour. The anti-immigration PVV, far-right Forum for Democracy (FVD), Denk and the SGP voted against, while MPs from JA21 and the Markuszower group were absent.

Purple Friday

The vote came on the eve of Purple Friday (Paarse Vrijdag), when schools mark LGBTI acceptance. This year it is being held in October for the first time, having been moved from December at the request of schools.

A record 3,130 schools have signed up, including 2,130 primary schools, compared with 2,890 last year, LGBTI rights organisation COC told news agency ANP.

The COC linked the rise to a survey published last month that found acceptance of homosexuality has slumped among teenagers. Only 22% of secondary school boys and 51% of girls now have a positive view, down from 40% and 78% in 2021.

World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work!
