Evening: Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi sharpen attack

NEW DELHI: Delhi witnessed an extraordinary security clampdown on October 10 as police moved to prevent the Cockroach Janta Partyâs (CJP) proposed protest against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar. What began with barricades, transport restrictions and preventive detentions escalated into a day of mass arrests, street demonstrations, reported clashes and a fierce political confrontation over the right to protest.By late afternoon, Delhi Police detained more than 3,000 people across the national capital. Those detained included CJP leaders, YouTuber Dhruv Rathee, Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal, former Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee, student activists, lawyers and other opposition leaders. Two police personnel were reported injured in incidents involving stone-pelting.As the detentions mounted, opposition leaders accused the government of suppressing dissent. BJP defended the police action and the SIR process, accusing the protesters of attempting to create unrest.Here is how the day unfolded for protesters, from the security measures before sunrise to the political confrontation that followed.Delhi Police denied permission for the proposed protest at Jantar Mantar, citing procedural lapses and law-and-order concerns. Authorities planned to deploy around 35,000 police and paramilitary personnel, with barricades, checkpoints, metro restrictions and mobile internet curbs in parts of central Delhi. Services to and from New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin stations were expected to be particularly affected.Police personnel wearing body cameras and drones were deployed for surveillance.Police also detained 30â40 people with criminal records as a preventive measure. At least 600 people had been detained across Delhi by 9am.CJP leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained inside an aircraft shortly after it landed in Delhi from Mumbai. CJP called the action pre-planned and demanded their immediate release.YouTuber Dhruv Rathee was also detained from his Gurugram residence. CJP accused the government of targeting young people who questioned its actions.CJP legal affairs head Ratna Singh and content creator Kavya Karnatac were also reported detained. CJP later alleged that Ratna Singh was being held inside a car surrounded by around 35 police personnel and the deputy commissioner of police. Police also placed several Congress workers and members of other political parties under house arrest ahead of the demonstration.Meanwhile, BJP president Nitin Nabin accused Rahul Gandhi and CJP associates of attempting to destabilise the country for political gains, alleging that their actions were driven by foreign forces.More than 400 SFI members, other student activists and lawyers marching from the Supreme Court towards Jantar Mantar were detained. SFI and Left party workers staged protests at INA and near the BJP headquarters as the protest crackdown continued.Former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan was also reported detained.Student leader Neha Bora, CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya, and activist Prashant Bhushan and Yogendra Yadav were among those detained near INA market while heading towards the protest. Bora had led a march from Jor Bagh towards Dilli Haat-INA.CJP named Ajinkya Shinde to lead the protest in a pre-recorded video. Following the announcement, Ajinkya urged protesters to turn any location where police stopped them into their âJantar Mantarâ.Congress MP Shashi Tharoor described the situation as an âundeclared Emer-GenZâ. He criticised the heavy security deployment, train cancellations, metro closures and restrictions on movement.Former Delhi CM Arvind Kejriwal, former Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee were detained while heading to join the protest. Mamata said they had been taken around in a prisoner van for two hours. She announced a sit-in at Dwarka North police station and said she would join the INDIA march on Monday.Congress leaders Mallikarjun Kharge and Priyanka Gandhi criticised the crackdown ahead of the planned protest. Kharge accused the Modi government of suppressing dissent, saying it had turned the âmother of democracyâ into a "muzzled democracyâ. Meanwhile, Priyanka alleged that the government had curtailed constitutional rights.Police officials reported stones being pelted at a bus carrying detained protesters in Jhandewalan. Two police personnel, including a Pink Force member, were reported injured. Another officer was injured in alleged stone-pelting near Baba Kharak Singh Marg in Connaught Place, where police said a scuffle broke out as they tried to disperse protesters.By late afternoon, the reported detention count had risen from at least 600 in the morning to around 1,000 by afternoon.BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra accused Rahul Gandhi of attempting to drag the President into a street protest. The party defended the police action, describing it as a victory for democracy over âmob ruleâ. Nabin had earlier accused the protesters of trying to destabilise the country.Chief Justice of India Surya Kant communicated to authorities that lawyers detained while peacefully protesting outside the Supreme Court should be released. The intervention followed an urgent letter from the Supreme Court Bar Association, which said several advocates had been taken to the Yamuna Sports Complex.CPM general secretary MA Baby filed a petition in the Supreme Court challenging restrictions imposed ahead of the protest, including curbs on metro services and mobile internet connectivity. TMC spokesperson Saket Gokhale also wrote to the Delhi high courtâs acting chief justice, seeking suo motu intervention over the transport restrictions.Rahul Gandhi targeted PM Modi, Amit Shah, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat, CEC Gyanesh Kumar and national security adviser Ajit Doval. He accused them of attacking the Constitution and vowed to continue the fight to defend democratic rights. Mamata Banerjee said she would remain in Delhi and join the INDIA march on Monday, in protest against the treatment of young people and other protesters.Meanwhile, an open letter signed by 124 former IAS and IFS officers strongly defended the Election Commission and the SIR process, adding to the debate over the electoral-roll revision.

World.title: ‘Loud slogans, selective action’: BJP chief Nabin questions Rahul’s silence on allegations against Congress MP after JNU dismissal
World.content:
NEW DELHI: BJP president

on Saturday questioned Congress leader

's silence over sexual harassment allegations against Congress MP and professor Angomcha Bimol Akoijam.

Accusing the Lok Sabha leader of the opposition of resorting to âloud slogans and selective actionâ, Nabin asked whether Rahul Gandhi would remove Akoijam from the Congress or reserve his moral outrage for âpolitical convenienceâ.

In a post on X, Nabin said, âThe mask is off the self-proclaimed champions of women's rights and the 'Smash the Patriarchy' brigade.â

His remarks came a day after Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) dismissed Akoijam with immediate effect following an inquiry that found him guilty of the allegations. Akoijam was a professor at the Centre for the Study of Social Systems under JNU's School of Social Sciences.

âLoud slogans, selective action. Will Rahul Gandhi demand accountability from his own MP and sack him, or is his moral outrage reserved only for political convenience?â the BJP chief added.

According to reports, at least 11 female students filed sexual harassment complaints against Akoijam in May. The complainants alleged that he invited students to his campus residence under the pretext of meetings or gatherings and attempted to sexually harass them. Some students also accused him of making âobscene and inappropriateâ remarks in class.

Reacting to JNU's decision, Akoijam alleged that he was being subjected to a âwitch-huntâ.

âI have not received the internal committee recommendations and even the official dismissal order yet. I have nothing to hide. This is nothing but a witch hunt,â he told reporters following his dismissal.

World.title: The period cycle: What happens in your body beyond the five days of bleeding
World.content:
âChill! Itâs just periods. Youâll feel better in a couple of days.â

But do women really get better in three to five days or are they caught in a recurring loop of exhaustion, mood swings and hormonal shifts that returns month after month from their first period till end.

From hormonal fluctuations and ovulation to fatigue, bloating and premenstrual symptoms, the menstrual cycle is a month-long process that extends far beyond the days of bleeding. Yet, what happens inside the body between periods remains poorly understood by many women.

For some, menstruation brings severe cramps, exhaustion and an overwhelming need to be left alone. Others struggle with bloating, back pain, irritability or difficulty concentrating at work.

And for many, the days leading up to a period can be just as challenging as the bleeding itself.

âI feel like somebody is constantly stabbing me with a sword, not even a knife, in my stomach,â says Sasha Singh, describing her experience of menstruation.

âEmotionally, I am so annoyed that eye rolls become the only friend that day. The Luteal phase is the worst for me, an indication of days ahead,â she adds.

For Shivanghii, the physical discomfort comes with an emotional toll.





âI feel like I need to punch whoever is talking to me and cry all the time. Physically its like my insides are getting drained and sawed repeatedly. I feel the first day and the day before that are the most painful.â

Their experiences highlight how differently women can experience the menstrual cycle, both physically and emotionally. They also raise a larger question: What happens inside the body when there is no bleeding?

The menstrual cycle is not confined to the three to seven days of menstrual bleeding.

It is a continuous process involving hormonal fluctuations and changes in the ovaries and uterus, as the body prepares for a possible pregnancy.

These changes can influence much more than the uterine lining. They may affect energy levels, sleep, appetite, skin, digestion and mood throughout the month.

While some women notice distinct changes from one phase to another, others experience few symptoms beyond their period.

What your body goes through during the entire cycle.

What is menstruation?

Menstruation is the shedding of the uterine lining through the vagina when pregnancy has not occurred. The bleeding contains blood and tissue from the lining of the uterus, also called the endometrium.

Periods generally last between three and seven days, although the duration and amount of bleeding vary. Menstruation usually begins during puberty, most commonly between the ages of 11 and 14, though it can start earlier or later.

It continues through the reproductive years until menopause, which typically occurs between the ages of 45 and 55.

The menstrual cycle, however, covers the entire interval from the first day of one period to the first day of the next.

A cycle is often described as lasting 28 days, but this is only an average. Many adults have cycles that fall within a range of approximately 21 to 35 days, and cycle length can vary with age and individual circumstances.

The cycle is regulated by hormones that coordinate activity between the brain, the ovaries and the uterus. Its four commonly described phases are menstruation, the follicular phase, ovulation and the luteal phase.

Importantly, these phases are not four completely separate stages. The follicular phase begins on the first day of menstruation and continues until ovulation, meaning the first two phases overlap.

The four phases: What happens inside the body?

Menstruation

The menstrual cycle begins on the first day of menstrual bleeding. When pregnancy has not occurred, the levels of hormones that support the uterine lining fall, prompting the lining to shed.

The uterus contracts to help expel this tissue, which can cause cramps in the lower abdomen and sometimes pain in the lower back. Some women also experience bloating, headaches, fatigue, breast discomfort or changes in mood.

For Priyanka, the first two days can be particularly difficult. âDuring my period, I usually feel physically tired, bloated and uncomfortable, with severe cramps and lower back pain. Emotionally, I tend to feel more irritable, sensitive and overwhelmed than usual. The most challenging phase for me is the few days leading up to my period the Luteal phase, when PMS symptoms like mood swings, fatigue and bloating are at their peak.

The first two days of my period can also be difficult,â she added.

Sneha, who works in the news field, says the physical discomfort can make demanding workdays more difficult.

âThe first three days are the most challenging for me. I, Sneha, usually feel drained due to severe stomach aches, which makes working in the news field even more physically and mentally exhausting.â

Hormone levels, particularly those of oestrogen and progesterone, are relatively low at the beginning of the cycle.

But this does not mean that the body's reproductive processes have stopped. As menstruation begins, hormones are already signalling the ovaries to start developing follicles for the next stage.

For most women, some discomfort during menstruation can be managed with appropriate measures. However, severe pain that interferes with daily activities should not automatically be dismissed as a normal part of having periods.

The follicular phase

This phase starts on the first day of menstruation and continues until ovulation.

During this time, the pituitary gland releases follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), which stimulates the development of follicles in the ovaries. Each follicle contains an immature egg, and usually one becomes dominant and continues to mature.

As the follicle develops, it produces increasing amounts of oestrogen.

This hormone helps rebuild and thicken the uterine lining after menstruation.

The changes are taking place even after the bleeding stops, although they may not produce obvious symptoms.

Some women report feeling more energetic or focused during the days after their period. Others do not notice any clear difference. These experiences can vary from one person to another and even from one cycle to the next.

Vijaya notices significant changes in her energy and concentration around her cycle.

âOh yes!! It changes drastically. Energy drops, concentration is hindered. Sleep becomes overpowering, as if body is on energy saver mode.â

However, it is important not to assume that every change in energy or mood is caused by menstrual hormones. Sleep, stress, nutrition, underlying health conditions and other factors can also influence how someone feels.

The follicular phase illustrates why the menstrual cycle is more than a monthly episode of bleeding.

While the body prepares an egg for possible release, the uterine lining is also being rebuilt.

Ovulation

As the dominant follicle matures, rising oestrogen levels help trigger a surge in luteinising hormone (LH). This surge causes ovulation, when the ovary releases a mature egg.

Ovulation is often described as occurring around day 14 of a 28-day cycle, but its timing varies. It does not necessarily happen on the same day for everyone, or even in every cycle for the same person.

After its release, the egg enters the fallopian tube, where it may be fertilised by sperm. The egg usually remains capable of fertilisation for approximately 12 to 24 hours. However, pregnancy can occur from sex in the days leading up to ovulation because sperm can survive in the reproductive tract for several days.

Some women notice changes around ovulation. Cervical mucus may become clearer, wetter and more slippery, while some experience mild pain on one side of the lower abdomen.

Others may notice no obvious physical changes.

There is also considerable variation in whether women report changes in mood, energy or sexual desire around this time. These experiences should not be treated as universal signs of ovulation.

Understanding ovulation is important not only for those trying to conceive but also for anyone seeking to understand the timing of their cycle. Calendar estimates and period-tracking apps can help identify patterns, but they cannot always predict the exact day of ovulation.

The changes are taking place even after the bleeding stops.

The luteal phase

After ovulation, the follicle that released the egg transforms into a structure called the corpus luteum. It produces progesterone, along with some oestrogen, to help maintain the uterine lining in preparation for a possible pregnancy.

If pregnancy does not occur, the corpus luteum breaks down. Progesterone and oestrogen levels fall, triggering changes that eventually lead to the shedding of the uterine lining and the start of the next period.

For some women, this phase brings premenstrual symptoms, commonly known as PMS. These may include bloating, breast tenderness, headaches, fatigue, irritability, changes in appetite and difficulty sleeping.

Priyanka says the days before menstruation can be particularly challenging, with mood swings, fatigue and bloating. Natasha also describes the luteal phase as a warning of the discomfort to come.

Shivanghii says the emotional changes can be difficult to explain.

âGetting irritated all the time and crying for no reason. It feels like everyone is being rude to me and they all hate me. No particular change in sleep.â

Sneha, meanwhile, says irritability is the main change she notices: âMood: Yes, but not with other things. I get irritated easily during my period.â

Premenstrual symptoms vary considerably. Some women experience mild changes that do not disrupt their routines, while others experience symptoms that affect work, relationships, studies and everyday activities.

In more severe cases, symptoms may be associated with premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD), a condition that can cause significant emotional and physical distress.

Women experiencing severe or persistent symptoms should discuss them with a healthcare professional rather than assuming they must simply endure them.

The effects of the menstrual cycle can extend beyond reproductive organs.

Why do hormones affect mood, energy, sleep & appetite

The effects of the menstrual cycle can extend beyond reproductive organs. Changes in oestrogen and progesterone may influence several bodily functions, although the extent of these effects differs between individuals.

According to Dr Asha Susawat, senior obstetrician and gynaecologist at Cocoon Hospital, Jaipur, hormonal fluctuations can influence how women feel throughout the cycle.

âWhile the hormonal fluctuations will be much more impactful than just your bleeding pattern, their importance will vary from woman to woman. For some, high levels of oestrogen before ovulation make them feel more energetic. Others will not perceive any significant differences.

Following the occurrence of ovulation, the progesterone hormone increases the temperature levels in the body and may affect the sleep pattern.

As the woman starts to bleed, some may feel sleepy, irritable, nervous, food craving, among other symptoms such as breakout, bloating, constipation, or diarrhoea. Nevertheless, not all the factors are felt by everyone and need more diagnoses.â

These accounts demonstrate the importance of recognising individual patterns.

Dr Rhythm Bhalla, senior consultant in obstetrics and gynaecology at Cocoon Hospital, Chandigarh, similarly notes that symptoms can begin before the next period arrives.

âThe physical effects of menstrual cycle on women may start long before the upcoming period. Variations in levels of oestrogen and progesterone affect moods, sleep, eating and energy levels. However, there is no standard experience in this regard since some women feel better before ovulation whereas some start experiencing fatigue, poor sleep, cravings and irritability prior to the onset of the period. Women may start experiencing acne and bloating, while digestive problems may turn into constipation or diarrhoea before the period starts.

There may be minor symptoms but serious problems should not be overlooked.â

More than mood swings: The body's changing rhythms

Some women experience irritability, anxiety, sadness or emotional sensitivity in the days before their period. Others notice little change, or find that their mood varies for reasons unrelated to their cycle.

Priyanka says she becomes more irritable and anxious before menstruation and sometimes struggles to concentrate. Shivanghii describes feeling upset and easily irritated, while Vijaya reports a noticeable decline in concentration and energy.

These accounts demonstrate the importance of recognising individual patterns. Hormonal fluctuations may contribute to mood changes, but they should not become a blanket explanation for every emotional response a woman experiences.

Sashaâs experience highlights another problem with how menstruation is discussed. Her first lessons about periods came in school, but the experience left her with questions about how much girls were actually being taught.

âI got my orientation to montly bleeding from school. It was a workshop conducted by Whisper for 7th class girls (boys were told it is a free PT period) when they poured blue ink on a sanitary pad in the name of 'sexual education',â she recalls.

Years later, she encountered a different kind of misconception at work. âWhen I worked in an all-boys work desk, I was often asked if I was on periods if I was not in a cheerful mood. Bad mood can be a product of multiple things, not just periods.â

Some women notice acne or changes in skin oiliness around their period. Others experience food cravings, bloating, constipation or diarrhoea.

These symptoms may be associated with hormonal fluctuations, but their causes can be complex. Persistent acne, unexplained hair loss, increased facial hair or substantial changes in weight should not automatically be attributed to the menstrual cycle.

Sneha lists several changes she has noticed, âface pimple,facial hair, bloating, hair fallâ

The same applies to digestive symptoms. Occasional bloating or changes in bowel habits may occur around menstruation, but persistent or severe abdominal pain, ongoing digestive problems or symptoms that disrupt daily life warrant medical attention.

Stress, thyroid disorders & PCOS: What else affects the cycle

The menstrual cycle is regulated by a complex interaction between the brain, the ovaries and the uterus. Several factors can interfere with this process, affecting ovulation, the timing of periods and the amount of bleeding.

Dr Susawat explains that stress can affect the hormones involved in ovulation, potentially delaying periods or causing them to be missed. Thyroid disorders can influence cycle length and bleeding patterns, while PCOS may interfere with regular ovulation and lead to irregular or absent periods.

Age is another factor. Cycles may be irregular during the years after menstruation first begins and may change again during perimenopause, the transition towards menopause. Hormonal contraception can also alter bleeding patterns, depending on the method used.

Dr Bhalla said that the cycle depends on several systems working together. âPeriods are the result of interaction between the brain, the ovaries and the uterus; there are many things that might interfere in this interaction.

Stress, combined with big changes in weight or poor eating habits, may lead to ovulation delay,â Bhalla said.

âThyroid issues may cause changes in bleeding amount and frequency. In PCOS, ovulation may be less frequent and make periods irregular. The menstrual problems can occur during the period of adolescence before the beginning of menopause. As hormonal contraceptives have an impact on the level of reproductive hormones and uterine lining in some form, so the bleeding can be less, spotting or absence of periods can occur,â she added.

This means that a change in the menstrual cycle does not necessarily indicate a serious health problem, but persistent changes should not be ignored.

A healthcare professional may consider factors such as stress, medication, pregnancy, thyroid function and PCOS when assessing irregular periods.

The information gap: What women know about their cycles

Despite menstruation being a regular part of life for millions of women, understanding of the complete menstrual cycle remains uneven.

Many learn about bleeding at school or at home but receive little information about ovulation, hormonal changes or the symptoms that may occur between periods.

When asked whether they knew hormonal changes continue throughout the month, even when they are not bleeding, the responses reflected different levels of awareness.

Vijaya said, âYes. The whole cycle is in process and goes beyond just shedding blood. There is constant hormonal fluctuations which ultimately affects the energy and motivation throughout the lifetime.â

Prisha Patnaik responded, âYes, I think 4 phases?â

Priyanka said, âYes, I know that the changing cycle can affect my mood, energy, sleep, appetite and concentration, even when we're not on our period.â

Shivanghii said, âI have a broad idea, like the luteal, follicular phases and all. Not really informed about the details.â

Their responses illustrate a distinction between knowing that the cycle involves hormonal changes and understanding how those changes occur across its different phases.

For many, school provides only the basics. Some learn more from their mothers, friends or online resources, while others have to seek information independently.

Vijaya said, âI didn't learn about periods at home, it was only until I got them did I have the conversation. In school it was only what textbook had to offer, they didn't even teach about pads etc.â

Priyanka said, âI learnt the basics at school, but very little about hormonal changes and their impact on our bodies.

One common misconception I've encountered is that periods are just about bleeding, when they actually affect our physical and emotional well-being throughout the month.â

Sneha said, âI donât have much to say about how periods were discussed at school. I got most of my information at home and from Google, which I explored out of curiosity.â

Shivanghii said, âI had my mother take me to a gynecologist to give me the talk, like covering all the aspects.

School never, unfortunately, even slightly brushed against the topic.â

These experiences underline the need for menstrual-health education that goes beyond explaining what bleeding is.

Girls and boys need age-appropriate information about the menstrual cycle, reproductive health, common symptoms and when medical care may be necessary.

Menstruation is something to hide rather than a normal biological process.

Menstruation, stigma and restrictions

In many parts of India, menstruation remains a subject surrounded by stigma and silence.

Some women continue to face restrictions on entering kitchens, touching utensils, participating in religious activities or discussing periods openly.

Pari (name changed), from Assam, describes the restrictions followed in her household.

"On the three days of my period, I sit and sleep on the floor. I eat on a separate plate as I am not allowed to enter the kitchen or touch any utensil or other furniture. I do not touch any male member be it my father, brother or husband.

These customs have been followed for a very long time in my household and me, my mother and sister have applied the same in our lives."

Her account reflects how cultural practices can shape women's experiences of menstruation beyond the physical symptoms themselves.

Yash Sonkar points to the gaps in menstrual-health education, saying, âMenstruation isnât even properly explained in our school curriculumâ¦ teachers skip the chapters at times.â

For Trisha, the problem goes beyond inadequate education to the stigma surrounding menstruation. One of the most persistent misconceptions she has encountered, she says, is that periods make women âimpureâ.

Shivanghiiâs experience reflects how deeply such beliefs can become embedded in everyday life. âAs for misconceptions, it's hard to think of one that I might not have been forced on. Days on which I can cut my nails, touching the pickle, touching gods or even mentioning it in front of a male entity,â she says, recalling the restrictions associated with menstruation.

These beliefs can persist through seemingly ordinary practices, from discouraging women from entering places of worship to treating menstruation as something that must be kept out of sight.

Even the habit of wrapping sanitary napkins discreetly or avoiding conversations about periods can reinforce the idea that menstruation is something to hide rather than a normal biological process.

When should you consult a gynaecologist?

Although changes in mood, energy and physical comfort may occur throughout the menstrual cycle, not every symptom should be attributed to hormones.

According to Dr Susawat, excessive bleeding between periods, bleeding after sexual intercourse, persistent pelvic pain or pain during intercourse should be evaluated. Unusual vaginal discharge accompanied by an odour, irritation or fever also warrants medical attention.

She adds that women should seek an assessment if their menstrual pattern changes significantly or if they miss periods for three months.

If pregnancy is possible, a missed period may be a reason to take a pregnancy test.

Dr Bhalla similarly advises that frequent bleeding between cycles, bleeding after intercourse, persistent pelvic pain and unusual discharge accompanied by itching, a bad odour or fever should not be ignored.

She says, âThis can be explained through the normal process of a woman. Abnormal bleeding that occurs frequently in between cycles, or bleeding following sexual intercourse, or constant pain in the pelvis area or during sexual intercourse should be dealt with appropriately.

Unusual vaginal discharge accompanied by signs such as itching, bad odor and fever should be attended to. Irregular periods which result in absence of menstruation for over three months should also be considered and an examination carried out.

This should be done as early as possible if pregnancy is one of the probable causes. Severe pelvic pain in addition to bleeding, missing periods and fainting should be handled as a matter of urgency.

Excessive vaginal bleeding accompanied by weakness, dizziness and difficulty breathing should also be handled urgently.â

Other warning signs include bleeding that lasts longer than seven days, very heavy bleeding, severe or worsening menstrual pain and symptoms that interfere with work, studies or daily activities.

Heavy bleeding can lead to iron deficiency anaemia, particularly when it occurs repeatedly.

Severe menstrual pain may also be associated with conditions such as endometriosis or adenomyosis, while irregular cycles may warrant assessment for PCOS, thyroid disorders or other underlying causes.

Severe pelvic pain accompanied by a missed period, bleeding or faintness requires urgent medical assessment, particularly when pregnancy is possible.

The key is to recognise the difference between a symptom that occurs occasionally and one that is persistent, severe or unusual for the individual.

The World Health Organisation (WHO) recognises menstrual health as more than a matter of managing bleeding. It includes access to accurate information, affordable menstrual products, safe sanitation facilities, appropriate healthcare and the ability to participate in everyday life without stigma.

The WHO has also highlighted the limited availability of high-quality scientific research on menstruation.

Better research and education can help improve care, support health policies and challenge myths surrounding the menstrual cycle.

The organisation estimates that around 500 million people who menstruate worldwide lack access to the full range of menstrual-health materials, facilities and services. It has also cited emerging national data indicating that around 39% of schools provide menstrual-health education.

These gaps matter because a lack of information can prevent women from recognising symptoms that require medical attention. It can also make it harder for them to discuss menstrual difficulties without embarrassment or fear of being dismissed.

Beyond the five days

For many women, menstruation is the most visible part of a process that continues throughout the month. While the uterus sheds its lining, the ovaries begin developing follicles.

As oestrogen rises, the uterine lining rebuilds.

Ovulation follows, and progesterone helps prepare the uterus for a possible pregnancy. If pregnancy does not occur, hormone levels fall and the cycle begins again.

The physical and emotional effects of these changes are not identical for everyone. Some women experience significant discomfort before and during menstruation, while others notice little variation.

Understanding the menstrual cycle means recognising that periods are not simply five days of bleeding. They are one stage in a continuous process shaped by hormones, health, age and individual circumstances.

Better menstrual-health education can help women understand their bodies, challenge stigma and recognise when symptoms deserve medical attention.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

It can also encourage families, schools and workplaces to treat menstruation as a normal health issue rather than a subject of embarrassment.

The more women understand what happens between periods, the better equipped they are to recognise their own patterns, ask informed questions and seek medical care when something feels wrong.

Greater awareness among men is equally important. When partners understand the physical and emotional changes women may experience throughout the cycle, they can offer greater empathy, support and understanding instead of dismissing symptoms or attributing every change in mood to menstruation.

World.title: Evening news wrap: Delhi in grips of anti-CEC stir; oppn leaders & protesters detained, BJP targets Congress
World.content:
Former Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee and Pinarayi Vijayan, opposition leader were detained by the Delhi Police during the ongoing CEC protest.

India warned Pakistan against using nuclear weapons as a means of political coercion, asserting that New Delhi would not yield to nuclear blackmail.

The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders failed to reach Jantar Mantar for their planned protest, as key members were detained by police before reaching the venue.

The Bharatiya Janata Party called Rahul Gandhi a ânalayak netaâ over his remarks following a meeting between an INDIA bloc delegation and President Droupadi Murmu.

BJP MP Sambit Patra on Saturday dismissed the Cockroach Janta Partyâs (CJP) proposed protest at Delhiâs Jantar Mantar as a âflop showâ.

Here are the top stories of the day:

SIR protest: Former CMs among opposition leaders detained from Delhi

Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee and Kerala leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Pinarayi Vijayan were detained by Delhi Police on Saturday during demonstrations against chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Mamata Banerjee was detained from South Avenue along with Trinamool Congress leaders Derek OâBrien, Dola Sen and other party members. Several CPM leaders were also taken into custody during the protest.

Former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal was detained as well.

Following the detentions, CPM leaders took to social media to condemn the police action. Party leaders in Kerala also criticised the move and called for protests in response.

India warns Pakistan at UN against nuclear threat

India on Friday issued a stern warning to Pakistan against using the threat of nuclear weapons to exert political pressure, asserting that New Delhi would not give in to nuclear blackmail. It also cautioned that any terrorist attack against the country would be met with an appropriate response.

Exercising its Right of Reply at the United Nations general assemblyâs first committee, which focuses on disarmament and international security, India stressed that nuclear weapons should not be viewed as âroutine instruments of statecraftâ.





Anmol Sher Singh Bedi, senior adviser (disarmament) at Indiaâs permanent mission to the conference on disarmament in Geneva, delivered the response after Pakistan raised the issue of Jammu and Kashmir.

Rejecting Islamabadâs claims over the region, Bedi reiterated Indiaâs position, stating, âJammu and Kashmir is an integral and inalienable part of India.â

Whatâs happening at Jantar Mantar? CJPâs âcockroachesâ grounded before anti-SIR showdown

The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders were unable to reach Delhiâs Jantar Mantar as planned after key members of the outfit were detained before arriving at the protest venue, throwing its âJantar Mantar 2.0â plans into disarray.

The extensive security measures across the national capital, which reportedly resulted in more than 1,500 detentions, further affected the anticipated turnout at the demonstration against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained by Delhi Police upon their arrival at Indira Gandhi International Airport from Mumbai.

'Nalayak neta': BJP accuses Rahul of dragging President into 'street fights', creating 'anarchy'

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Saturday called Rahul Gandhi a ânalayak netaâ over his remarks after a delegation of the INDIA bloc met President Droupadi Murmu. The party accused the leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha of misrepresenting the interaction and dragging the countryâs highest constitutional office into the political controversy surrounding allegations of âvote choriâ.

Addressing a press conference, BJP national spokesperson Sambit Patra challenged Rahul Gandhiâs assertion that the president had not rejected the oppositionâs allegations of electoral irregularities.

Patra argued that receiving a memorandum did not imply that the president agreed with the claims made in it.

âYesterday, you saw that some political leaders had gone to Rashtrapati Bhavan. Rahul Gandhiâs statement after coming out of the Rashtrapati Bhavan was equal to that of an incompetent leader, âNalayak netaâ,â Patra said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

'Anarchists have failed, planned to hold Delhi hostage': BJP slams Jantar Mantar stir

BJP MP Sambit Patra on Saturday dismissed the Cockroach Janata Partyâs (CJP) proposed protest at Delhiâs Jantar Mantar as a âflop showâ, claiming that the âanarchistsâ who sought to hold the national capital âhostageâ had failed in their attempt.

âJantar Mantarâs story is not Indiaâs story. What is happening at Jantar Mantar, what you can see on TV and a few social media handles, is not Indiaâs story. India is calm and going ahead under good governance,â Patra said. The BJP MP alleged that certain âanarchist forcesâ had been spreading unrest in a corner of Delhi over the past few days. He claimed that their efforts had failed, describing the proposed protest as a âflop showâ that had âcompletely collapsedâ.

âThere was an attempt to hold India, the national capital, captive; that there be arson here, that there be violence here. But today, âloktantraâ has triumphed over bheedtantra,â Patra said.

World.title: Stones hurled at bus carrying detained protesters in Delhi’s Jhandewalan, cops injured
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Stones were pelted at a bus carrying detained protesters in Delhiâs Jhandewalan area on Saturday as police continued detaining people attempting to reach Jantar Mantar for the Cockroach Janta Partyâs (CJP) proposed protest against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.

Stone-pelting was also reported in other parts of the national capital, including Connaught Place and Imtiaz Ali Marg, where police personnel were injured, officials said.

According to news agency IANS, the Jhandewalan incident occurred when police personnel were transporting detained individuals in a bus through the area. Officials said some protesters allegedly attempted to escape custody and damage the vehicle.

Police subsequently detained them again and moved them to a designated location.

Security was strengthened around Jhandewalan Metro Station, with heavy police deployment and traffic restrictions in place. The operation also led to traffic diversions in and around the area.

In a separate incident near Imtiaz Ali Marg, close to Akashwani Bhawan, around 25 to 30 protesters allegedly jumped barricades and pelted security personnel with stones after attempting to reach the protest site, officials said.





Two police personnel were injured in the incident, they added.

Stone-pelting was also reported near Baba Kharak Singh Marg in Connaught Place as police attempted to disperse protesters and take them into preventive custody.

Recounting the confrontation, Head Constable Nagendra told ANI, âWe were removing the protesters. During that process, we faced a scuffle, and my nameplate got broken... It happened near the Arya School lane, close to Baba Kharak Singh Marg.

There were several protesters. They were detained... There was stone-pelting; a stone even hit my shoe.â

Police Inspector Vivek Kumar said a group advanced towards a small police contingent before reinforcements arrived.

âIt must have been about two hours ago. There was a large crowd on Baba Kharak Singh Marg; there were many miscreants. While chasing them, I ended up in a side lane with four other men. We were left alone near the Race Course.

Seeing that we were few in number, they started advancing towards us. Some of them threw stones,â he said.

âFortunately, we escaped; just as they were closing in on us, our staff arrived from behind. We were saved... There must have been 60â70 people. No one was injured... No, none [protesters] were caught,â Kumar added.

Police detained more than 1,000 protesters across Delhi, with some reports putting the figure at over 1,500, as authorities enforced restrictions and prevented demonstrators from reaching Jantar Mantar.

The protest was scheduled to begin at 10.30 am, but permission had not been granted, officials said.

CJP leaders Abhijit Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were also detained at Delhi airport upon arriving in the capital. Dipke, who travelled from Mumbai, posted an Instagram video alleging that police detained him and his associates as they disembarked from their flight.

World.title: ‘Their core characteristic is cowardice’: Rahul Gandhi targets PM Modi, RSS; backs youth protesting against CEC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress leader

on Saturday backed youth protesters demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

The Lok Sabha leader of the opposition said he had been fighting Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), the ideological mentor of the ruling BJP, for âover a decade nowâ and knew them âinside out, like the back of my hand."

âThe core characteristic of these people is cowardice. Narendra Modi, (Union home minister) Amit Shah, Gyanesh Kumar and (National Security Advisor) Ajit Doval are slowly finding the space closing around them.

We are closing that space,â Rahul Gandhi said in a video message on X.

âMr Modi, do whatever you want. Call out all the police. Arrest all the leaders. Arrest all the young people. Arrest us all,â he added.

He further claimed to have âall the information we need,â an apparent reference to proof of what he describes as âvote choriâ (vote theft) by the BJP in collusion with the Election Commission.

âWe are going to defend our Constitution. We are going to protect the voice of the Indian people.





And we are going to ensure that what was done to India over the last 10-15 years will never, ever be done again,â the Raebareli MP further stated.

âYouth of India, I am proud of you. Keep protesting. We are standing with you. We are going to ensure that this regime and the people who have attacked our Constitution are defeated,â Rahul Gandhi asserted.

His remarks came amid a protest led by the youth pressure group Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) against CEC Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar in Delhi on Saturday.

Delhi Police detained more than 3,000 protesters attempting to reach the site. Over 600 people with criminal records were also detained as a preventive measure. According to police, permission for the protest had not been granted, and prohibitory orders were in force in the New Delhi area.

World.title: KTR demands probe into radial roads tenders
World.content:
HYDERABAD

Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) working president K.T. Rama Rao has accused the Congress Government of serious irregularities in the ₹3,296-crore Radial Road-2 tender process.

In an open letter addressed to Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy, Mr. Rao raised questions over the allocation of contracts, the disqualification of bidders who reportedly quoted lower prices and the award of packages at prices allegedly higher than the estimates. He demanded that the government disclose all tender documents and explain the decisions taken in the selection of contractors.

Alleging favouritism in tender allocation, the BRS leader said the project involves the construction of an 81.15-km greenfield expressway from the Outer Ring Road at Budvel to NH-167N near Kodangal. Further, he alleged that technical grounds were used to exclude certain companies and the contracts were awarded to preferred firms. He said the bid submission deadline was September 30, 2026, and allocation process was reportedly completed by October 8.

Questioning how 13 bids for a project of such a magnitude could be evaluated and processed within approximately five working days, he alleged that the contracts were awarded to those firms that quoted more than the estimated value. The BRS leader said Package-I was awarded to NCC Limited for ₹1,286.03 crore, reportedly 3.95% above the estimated cost. Package-II was awarded to BVSR and Package-III to GKC.

Stating that different eligibility decisions were raising questions, Mr. Rao pointed to reported inconsistencies in the technical evaluation of bidders. He stated that GKC was reportedly disqualified in Package-I but qualified in Package-III, while BVSR was reportedly qualified in Packages I and II but disqualified in Package-III.

He demanded a probe into the ₹600 crore loss allegation, referring to submissions made on behalf of Sushi Infra and Mining Limited in a court proceedings. He also raised concerns over the Radial Road-1 tender, stating that the estimated project cost of about ₹591 crore and an alleged final allocation around 15% above the estimate.

World.title: Two people drown, two go missing at Pakala Beach in Andhra Pradesh
World.content:
A jolly trip of a group of around 70 persons turned tragic as two of them drowned and another two went missing at Pakala Beach of Prakasam district on Saturday.

“Around 70 persons from Srirangapuram village in Kanigiri mandal came to the beach in three batches in three private vehicles around 2 p.m on Saturday. All of them are masons working in Hyderabad,” Ongole Sub-Divisional Police Officer (SDPO) R. Srinivasa Rao told to he Hindu.

They came to their native village for Vinayaka Chavithi celebrations and stayed back to celebrate Kolupulu (Poleramma Jathara) two days ago. They were supposed to go back to work in a few days, he informed.

They came to Pakala Beach for a short trip. While taking a bath, seven of them went deep into the water and were swept away by the strong waves. The other members of the group alerted the police.

The Singarayakonda police rushed to the spot and launched a rescue operation with the help of expert swimmers. Three people were rescued. One of them is stable, while another one was admitted to RIMS Hospital and another to Aster Ramesh Hospital in Ongole.

The two deceased have been identified as Paladugu Teja (20) and Battula Mahesh Babu (22), while the missing are Devala Vishnu (17) and Devala Narayana (32). Search efforts were on by using drones and boats till the last report came in.

Prakasam District Collector P. Rajababu and SP V. Harshavardhan Raju inspected the beach. The Collector said that the rescued were receiving advanced medical treatment.

He assured that the district administration would extend all support to the affected families. The Collector urged the beachgoers to exercise caution and adhere to the safety guidelines.

World.title: Kidwai’s home-based palliative care reaches over 3,000 patients and caregivers
World.content:
For patients with advanced cancer and other life-limiting illnesses, palliative care often needs to extend beyond hospital wards to their homes, where families grapple with pain, emotional distress, and the demands of long-term caregiving.

At the State-run Kidwai Memorial Institute of Oncology (KMIO), the Department of Palliative Medicine has made home-based care a key part of its services, reporting more than 750 home-care visits, over 12,000 km travelled and more than 3,000 beneficiaries, including patients and caregivers.

These services were highlighted while observing World Hospice and Palliative Care Day on October 10, which this year carried the theme ‘Pain management: An essential part of palliative care’.

“With the help of volunteers and NGOs, we also extend financial support for children’s education. We provide waterbed and airbed, ration kits, and nebuliser machines for use at home. It is not just about treating the patient,” M.K. Yadhuraj Gowda, Head of the Department of Palliative Medicine at KMIO, told The Hindu.

The home-care service is intended for patients who find it difficult to travel to the hospital because of advanced illness, reduced mobility, or other challenges. Multidisciplinary teams provide medical assessment, symptom management, nursing care, and support in familiar surroundings, helping reduce the burden of repeated hospital visits.

The department’s approach also recognises that serious illness affects entire families. Caregivers may need help managing the practical demands of looking after a patient, as well as support in coping with emotional and financial pressures, Dr. Gowda said.

Beyond death

Palliative care also includes bereavement support for families after the death of a loved one. KMIO’s department provides guidance to help family members cope with grief, manage emotional distress and access support during the grieving process.

The service reflects the broader role of palliative care, which addresses not only physical pain and other symptoms but also the psychological, emotional, social and spiritual needs of patients and their families. Volunteer services add another layer of support for families navigating serious illness and loss.

Pain relief and care for children

Institute director R. Krishnappa said the department provides inpatient palliative care for patients who require specialised management of pain and other distressing symptoms, with capacity for more than 30 patients. Its services include medication and interventional procedures such as nerve blocks and neurolysis for selected patients with severe cancer-related pain that remains inadequately controlled with conventional treatment.

It also provides paediatric palliative care, with age-appropriate pain and symptom management, emotional support and guidance for families caring for children with cancer and other serious illnesses, he said.

Music and sound therapy sessions are conducted for inpatients on Wednesdays, while yoga therapy sessions are held on Thursdays to promote relaxation and emotional well-being alongside medical treatment.

Teleconsultations extend specialist support

The department has relaunched its ‘Call for Care - Neravina Kare’ service to connect patients living outside Bengaluru and in distant locations with specialist palliative care. Through telephone and video consultations, a team comprising a palliative care physician, nurse and clinical psycho-oncologist offers guidance on symptom management and emotional support. Patients and caregivers can contact the service on 9008441708.

World.title: Counter Congress’ campaign against SIR, Telangana BJP chief tells party cadre
World.content:
BJP Telangana president N. Ramchander Rao has called upon party leaders and cadres to counter what he termed a misinformation campaign by the Congress against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, and explain to people the importance of maintaining clean voters’ lists.

Addressing a meeting of conveners of the party’s various cells, senior leaders, State spokespersons and media panelists at the BJP’s State office, Mr. Rao alleged that the Congress was creating a false narrative over the SIR process to mislead people.

He accused Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy of targeting constitutional institutions out of fear of electoral defeats.

Referring to the Congress delegation’s recent meeting with the President, Mr. Rao said Mr. Gandhi had stated that the President had sought evidence for the allegations made by the party. However, the Congress had failed to produce supporting evidence, he alleged. He also criticised the Congress for claiming that the President had acknowledged vote theft, describing it as an attempt to spread misinformation.

Explaining the SIR process, the BJP leader said the second phase of the exercise was a lengthy process lasting four to five months, involving verification at multiple levels.

Booth-level officers (BLOs) would visit households to verify voter details and check the status of deceased persons and those who had migrated before preparing the draft electoral rolls, he said. There was also a prescribed procedure for restoring names if objections were raised after their deletion.

Alleging that the Congress had failed to substantiate its claims of mass deletions, Mr. Rao challenged the party to identify voters whose names had been removed unlawfully. He said the BJP cadre should take the issue to the grassroots and highlight how a transparent and accurate electoral roll would strengthen democracy.

World.title: VMC sets up special drainage system for Saras Aajeevika Mela to ensure cleanliness at Punnami Ghat
World.content:
The Vijayawada Municipal Corporation (VMC) has arranged a special drainage system at Punnami Ghat, where the Saras Aajeevika Mela is going to be held from October 13, to ensure the smooth disposal of wastewater and prevent it from stagnating.

Municipal Commissioner Dhyanachandra H.M. said the measures are being taken in consideration of the large influx of vendors from across the country who are expected to set up their stalls here. The VMC Commissioner also directed authorities to provide underground drainage facilities wherever necessary and to ensure that cleanliness is maintained throughout the event. President Droupadi Murmu is also expected to attend the mela.

Earlier in the day, Minister of State for Rural Development and Communications and Guntur MP Pemmasani Chandrasekhar and Vijayawada MP Kesineni Sivanath (Chinni) inspected arrangements for the event at Punnami Ghat.

Later, speaking to the media, Mr. Sivanath said the event was held in Guntur last year and it was a great success. Efforts are being made to organise the event in Vijayawada along similar lines, he said, adding that the primary objective was to promote products made by women and create opportunities for them to access national markets, thereby strengthening their economic independence.

Mr. Sivanath urged women from self-help groups (SHGs) to participate in large numbers and utilise the opportunity. He said the mela would provide a valuable marketing platform for handicrafts, traditional products and other household items made by women.

Vijayawada Police Commissioner S.V. Rajasekhar Babu, Mr. Dhyanachandra and other district and corporation officials took part in the programme.

World.title: Maintenance of Coimbatore’s Smart City lakefronts comes under scrutiny
World.content:
The upkeep of seven waterbodies developed under the Smart Cities Mission in Coimbatore has come under scrutiny, with several facilities falling into disrepair despite the civic body outsourcing their operation and maintenance to a private contractor in 2024.

The waterbodies — Ukkadam Periyakulam, Selva Chinthamani lake, Kurichi Lake, Valankulam, Krishnampathy, Selvampathy and Kumarasamy Tank — were developed at a cost of about ₹350 crore, with the works completed in 2023. The facilities included walking tracks, seating areas, play equipment, gym equipment and toilets.

However, damaged walking paths and seating, broken or rusted play and gym equipment, and poor sanitation have raised concerns over their upkeep. At Ukkadam Periyakulam, waste dumped along the banks, including water hyacinths removed from the lake, has caused a foul smell. The toilets at both Valankulam and Ukkadam Periyakulam are also reportedly inaccessible and poorly maintained.

At Kurichi lake, activists have flagged littering and the presence of liquor bottles, cigarette butts and sachets of banned tobacco products on the premises. Despite fencing around the lake, unauthorised entry at night remains a concern.

A senior Corporation official said the contractor had cited problems with the existing equipment and toilet fittings, stating that they needed to be replaced by the Corporation to ensure proper maintenance. A review meeting involving the contractor and the Corporation Commissioner is scheduled for next week to discuss the issues in detail.

Meanwhile, the Commissioner Katta Ravi Teja inspected Kurichi lake on Friday (October 9, 2026) and instructed officials to clean the lake bund, plant saplings and ensure that the premises are maintained properly.

World.title: ED moves Telangana High Court seeking speedy trial in money laundering cases against YSRCP chief Jagan Mohan Reddy
World.content:
The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has approached the Telangana High Court seeking directions for the speedy, day-to-day trial of money laundering cases against YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) president and former Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Y. S. Jagan Mohan Reddy and others, citing prolonged delays in proceedings that have remained pending for nearly a decade.

The agency filed a writ petition on September 23, 2026, seeking directions to expedite the trial and ensure the personal appearance of all accused in the prosecution complaints filed under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002.

In a press release issued on Saturday (October 10, 2026), the ED said it had filed nine prosecution complaints against Jagan Mohan Reddy and others before the Special Court for CBI cases in Nampally, Hyderabad, between 2016 and 2021.

Although cognisance has been taken in all nine complaints, the cases remain at a preliminary stage, with discharge petitions awaiting hearings.

The agency pointed out that despite several years having elapsed since cognisance was taken, there had been no significant progress in the proceedings. It said the pendency of discharge petitions had delayed further progress in the prosecution complaints.

The ED’s investigation stems from FIRs registered by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) following directions issued by the erstwhile Andhra Pradesh High Court in 2011.

The CBI cases concern allegations that Jagan Mohan Reddy and others conspired to extend government favours to large corporations and individuals in exchange for investments in companies owned by him and his family members.

According to the ED, its investigation revealed that several companies and individuals made substantial investments through share subscriptions at exorbitant premiums in firms associated with the YSRCP president and his family.

The investors named by the agency include Aurobindo Pharma Ltd., Hetero Drugs Ltd., Indu Projects Ltd., Indu Techzone Pvt. Ltd., Lepakshi Knowledge Hub Pvt. Ltd., VANPIC Projects Pvt. Ltd., VANPIC Ports Pvt. Ltd., Nimmagadda Prasad, Ramky Pharma City (India) Ltd. and India Cements Ltd.

The investments were allegedly made in companies including Bharati Cement Corporation Pvt. Ltd., Jagati Publications Ltd. and Janani Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd., as part of a quid pro quo arrangement for favours extended by the then Andhra Pradesh government during the tenure of Jagan Mohan Reddy’s father, the late Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy.

ED cites Supreme Court observations

In its petition, the ED referred to observations made by the Supreme Court in a criminal appeal involving Jagan Mohan Reddy and the CBI in 2013, emphasising the seriousness of economic offences.

The agency cited the apex court’s observations that economic offences involving deep-rooted conspiracies and substantial losses of public funds required a different approach, considering their potential impact on the country’s economy and financial health.

Invoking the right to a speedy trial under Article 21 of the Constitution, the ED requested the High Court to direct the criminal justice system to ensure that the proceedings were conducted with reasonable expedition.

The agency also sought directions for day-to-day hearings of the prosecution complaints and the pending discharge petitions to prevent further delays. The ED maintained that the cases had remained pending for nearly 10 years and that the chronology of proceedings demonstrated the absence of reasonable expedition in prosecuting the matter. Further investigation is underway, the agency added.

World.title: Two arrested for robbing elderly woman on pretext of SIR in Udupi
World.content:
The Udupi Town police arrested two persons on Saturday for allegedly robbing an elderly woman of her gold chain by posing as personnel involved in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.

The police identified the accused as Vadiraj Ganiga, 44, of Puttur village in Udupi taluk and Sachin, 30, of Pudu village in Kaup taluk.

According to the complaint filed with the Udupi Town police by Shrikant Karanth, two men visited the house where his mother, Shanta Karanth, stayed alone, at 3.30 p.m. on Wednesday Claiming to be personnel involved in SIR, they handed over forms related to the exercise. When Ms. Shanta went inside the house to speak with her son, the accused entered and pushed her down. They snatched her gold chain, worth ₹4 lakh rupees, and fled from the scene.

A police team led by Udupi Town PSI Bharatesh Kankanawadi examined surrounding CCTV footage and gathered other evidence to zero in on Ganiga and Sachin, arresting them on Saturday. Authorities recovered the gold chain, an Ola electric scooter, and two mobile phones from the accused. They were produced before a jurisdictional magistrate court, which remanded them to 14 days of judicial custody.

In a press release, the police said that Ganiga lived near Ms. Karanth’s house and knew she lived alone, having previously taken a loan from her and several others. The second accused had also borrowed money from multiple individuals. The police said that the pair committed the robbery to clear their debts and lead a lavish lifestyle.

World.title: PM Shehbaz meets President Zardari as Centre mulls imposition of emergency in KP
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday met with President Asif Ali Zardari, with the country’s overall security and political situation coming under discussion as the federal government mulls imposing an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

A statement issued by the President House said the premier was accompanied by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Attorney General Mansoor Usman Awan and Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar.

It said that PPP’s Sherry Rehman and Syed Naveed Qamar were also present.

“It was agreed during the meeting to convene separate sessions of the National Assembly and the Senate on Tuesday (Oct 13),” the statement said.

The development comes as the PML-N-led federal government and the KP government led by the PTI — which is in opposition in the Centre — have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy. This was also one of the main reasons behind the breakdown of their Oct 3 talks.

The PTI has said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre has denied . It also calls for reviewing the counterterrorism policy, while the latter criticises the KP government’s efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objects to its stance on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban.

In recent days, federal ministers have assailed the PTI for staging a protest long march , which it has been warned against, at a time when KP faces security challenges. They have also linked differences over the counterterrorism policy with the possibility of an emergency or governor’s rule in KP.

Earlier on Saturday, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar assailed the KP government over a “lack of governance” in the province, alleging that the provincial administration was given Rs700 billion under the National Finance Commission for development projects.

“You did not upgrade the Counter Terrorism Department, did not establish forensic labs, did not install safe city cameras, which should be installed in the merged districts and all the entry-exit points of KP’s districts,” he alleged.

The information minister claimed that the PTI was instead spending this money on organising protests.

Minister says things headed toward ‘last option’

Speaking to Geo News on Saturday, Minister of State for Interior Affairs Tallal Chaudhry said that consultations were ongoing when asked about the imposition of an emergency in KP.

“This is something that requires comprehensive consultations,” he said. “This is not something we are in favour of as we are a democratic government, and this is a last resort.”

Chaudhry added that multiple options were being examined at different levels but questioned what other avenues were available, with the PTI failing to fulfil the federal government’s requests to cooperate in the fight against terrorism, and inciting people and speaking against national policy during the ongoing long march.

“Again, I say consultations are ongoing, and this is a last resort. The options before this, such as talks and backdoor discussions … we tried everything. We will try to make sure we think through this last step if there is no other option, but it looks like things are headed towards the last option,” he stressed.

The state minister added that ties with the PTI remained in place, as they are the opposition in parliament and currently govern KP.

“I previously said that during the second round of talks, the interior minister met the prime minister and told him that the KP government is ready to cooperate in fighting terrorism,” Chaudhry recounted.

“The prime minister told him to give KP whatever they need to fight terrorism on a political level, but they had to gather with us to fight terrorism and stand with our security forces.”

Chaudhry added that the federal government gave the PTI relevance and space, even at the expense of the ruling PML-N’s political goals, and that the government was not focused on politics but on the state and maintaining peace.

“We are ready to give everything and we have no ego. Whether we are in the government or opposition, our ego is Pakistan and it is not bigger than Pakistan,” he emphasised.

“We hoped that we could do this together and on a single platform, but how many martyrs are the prime minister and chief of army staff going to carry on their shoulders? These people [the PTI] are not ready to carry the burden with us or stand with us, so what other option is left?”

PM speaks to Fazl on reducing tensions between Centre, KP govt

Separately, Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam—Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman was set to meet PM Shehbaz in Islamabad after the two discussed reducing tensions between the Centre and the KP government during a phone call.

According to a statement from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), PM Shehbaz congratulated the JUI-F leader on performing Umrah and extended an invitation for talks at the Prime Minister House.

A later statement by the JUI-F confirmed that Fazl had departed for PM House for talks on the “country’s political situation”.

JUI-F spokesperson Aslam Ghauri, in the statement, said Fazl also took the “PTI leadership into confidence” before heading for the meeting with the prime minister.

The phone call follows recent contacts between Fazl, known for his engagement with politicians from across the board, and the opposition.

On Tuesday, TTAP leaders called on Fazl at his residence, following which the veteran politician advised the federal government not to obstruct the PTI long march heading towards Islamabad, as protests were a democratic right enjoyed by all political parties.

The next day, PM’s Adviser on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry and National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq met the JUI-F chief.

On Thursday, PTI MNA Junaid Akbar confirmed that Fazl had offered to play a role in ending the deadlock between the government and opposition, adding that the PTI’s “doors are open” to it.

Speaking on Geo News, Akbar had said no framework had been put forward by Fazl regarding his role in the negotiations, although he noted that the JUI-F chief had been in touch with PTI leadership while he was away for Umrah.

The same day, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif also hinted at efforts to restart negotiations between the Centre and the opposition, saying, “I wish a positive result comes out of the efforts of those involved in the talks. But, I have little hope.”

Speaking to Dawn, JUI-F spokesman Aslam Ghauri said his party chief was playing the role of a “facilitator, not a mediator”.

He distinguished the two roles by saying that a mediator would have the authority from opposition parties to make their own decision in light of their demands.

“It is our (JUI-F’s) priority to bring both sides on table for resumption of talks,” he added, pointing out that they had urged the government to call a multi-party conference in Parliament House, where political and security issues should be discussed.

The JUI-F leader said sitting at the table would benefit both sides, though the resumption of dialogue would mostly benefit the PTI because the KP government is “virtually being run by someone else and not by Chief Minister Sohail Afridi”.

World.title: Govt assails PTI over 'lack of governance' in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
World.content:
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar on Saturday assailed the PTI-led Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government over a “lack of governance” in the province.

Addressing a press conference in Islamabad, he alleged that the provincial government was given Rs700 billion under the National Finance Commission for development projects.

“You did not upgrade the Counter Terrorism Department (CTD), did not establish forensic labs, did not install safe city cameras, which should be installed in the merged districts and all the entry-exit points of KP’s districts,” he alleged.

On the other hand, the information minister claimed that the PTI was spending this money on organising protests.

“You don’t even give half an hour to discuss terrorism in the province, but you organise six-hour meetings to spread turmoil and vandalism,” he criticised.

Tarar further said that the PTI had “trapped” millions of people in the province to get its leader, former prime minister Imran Khan, released from jail.

“You trapped them in poverty, in disease by not providing the adequate health facilities, in ignorance by not providing educational opportunities, and in non-development by not improving infrastructure,” he said.

Tarar also alleged that the KP government had held the people of the province “captive to terrorists”.

“From the very first day, this is my opinion that they [PTI] are the B-team of the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan,” Tarar said.

The information minister said that the PTI facilitated terrorists in settling in the country.

“For how long will it go on? That the security forces will clear the area of terrorists and establish peace, but you will bring the terrorists back?” he asked.

During his address, Tarar said that the PTI government in KP had dragged the province into the “stone age” during the last 13 and a half years.

Citing various federal government projects, Tarar maintained that there was no comparison of the hours spent working by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi to address governance issues and take relief and reform measures.

He said that the chief ministers of all the provinces were working hard, questioning how many hours Afridi spent on governance.

“Tell us if you have ever given a big hospital, a university, a highway to your people, an information technology project to the youth of KP or given them laptops or gadgets,” he said.

“How long can such a system, where there is chaos and extremist politics, continue?” he asked.

He claimed that the KP government wanted to hand over the province to terrorists as it prioritised “personal interests over the national interests”.

“This province needs peace, not politics,” Tarar stated.

Asked about imposing an emergency or governor’s rule in KP, Tarar said that responding to this question would be premature.

“Everyone is asking how long KP and its people will remain at the mercy of its government,” he said.

“In my opinion, the conditions in KP have never been worse. They could not be worse than this. What’s worse than terrorists roaming in the streets? You have designated no-go areas in most of your districts because you collect ransom in collusion with terrorists,” he claimed.

He said that the people of KP go to Punjab or other provinces for medical treatment.

“Will there ever come a time when people from across Pakistan go to KP for treatment?” he asked. The information minister asserted that the PTI would not be allowed to destroy the province.

Addressing the same press conference, Coordinator to the Prime Minister on Information for KP Affairs Ikhtiar Wali Khan also questioned the lack of development in the province.

“Universities are shutting down because there are no vice chancellors there. Eighteen out of 34 universities in KP are on the verge of bankruptcy,” he said.

Wali said that people complained about the lack of good roads in Karachi. “But when people of KP go to Karachi, they say that Karachi’s roads are much better than KP.”

Calling on the people and journalists in KP, Wali urged them to talk about the “ground realities”, claiming that the people were crying over the existing health facilities in the province.

He referred to the KP police as the shuhada force, alleging that the provincial government had left them unarmed. He alleged that the PTI government had seized the money allocated to fund the CTD to combat terrorism.

Wali also accused KP ministers of corruption and bad governance in the province.

“The people of KP need peace, health facilities and a political culture based on tolerance, acceptance and respect,” he said.

The PML-N-led federal government and the KP government led by PTI — which is in opposition in the Centre — have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy. This was also a key reason behind the breakdown of the Oct 3 talks between them.

The PTI has said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre has denied. It also calls for reviewing the counterterrorism policy, while the latter criticises the KP government’s efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objects to its stance on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban.

Kundi, Muqam discuss KP’s security and political situation

In Peshawar, Minister for Kashmir Affairs and Gilgit Baltistan Amir Muqam met KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi at Governor House, where they discussed the overall law and order situation in the province.

According to a joint statement issued after the meeting, the two leaders also discussed the PTI’s long march and exchanged views on issues of mutual interest, particularly the political environment in the province.

Kundi and Muqam thanked the people of KP, saying they had rejected the politics of unrest and confrontation.

They reiterated that the federal government would continue taking all possible measures to restore lasting peace, strengthen security and accelerate public welfare and development in the province.

The two leaders also observed that the people of KP had grown frustrated with terrorism and what they described as political elements promoting instability, reaffirming the federal government’s commitment to ensuring peace and stability in the province.

In a post on X, Kundi said, “Our people have paid an unbearable price in the war against terrorism. They cannot be held hostage to the politics of anarchy and agitation.”

He affirmed that the federal government “will continue to take all possible measures to strengthen security, protect our people and support the province’s development”.

“The future of KP cannot be sacrificed at the altar of political ambition,” the governor declared.

“This province does not need any more political stunts that undermine security and endanger lives. I commend the people of KP for standing with peace,” he wrote.

In recent days, federal ministers have assailed the PTI for staging a protest long march, which it has been warned against, at a time when KP faces security challenges. They have also linked differences over the counterterrorism policy with the possibility of an emergency or governor’s rule in KP.

On Friday, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said the government had finished deliberating on the imposition of an emergency and warned that it would avail the option if the KP government did not cooperate on counterterrorism.

Gohar meets CM Afridi

On the other hand, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan said on X that he met CM Afridi in Peshawar to discuss the country’s political situation, the party’s long march and “other important matters”.

PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, MNA Junaid Akbar, Parliamentary Leader Shahid Kattak and KP Information Minister Shafi Jani were also present during the meeting.
