At the OSCE Human Dimension Conference in Warsaw, a representative of Switzerland, the organisation’s chair for 2026, said that the Chairpersonship was concerned about remarks made by the authorities in Georgia regarding the participation of Georgian civil society representatives in the conference, as well as information received from human rights defenders.

The Swiss representative’s statement followed comments by Georgian Parliament Speaker Shalva Papuashvili about NGO representatives attending the conference in Warsaw. On 7 October, Papuashvili said he did not understand how they had paid for the trip or who was funding them:

“How do they pay for these trips, and who funds them? These organisations are not registered in the transparency register. If they do not disclose [the source of their income] to the state, it means they are funded by ‘black money’. This is further evidence that organisations in Georgia receive ‘black money’, including from various European institutions,” the speaker said.

What did the Swiss representative say?

“Providing a platform where civil society representatives can participate and engage with OSCE participating States and executive structures is one of the OSCE’s core values. They must be able to do so without facing any negative consequences.

This is essential for the OSCE’s mechanisms to function. We are concerned about comments made in connection with the participation of Georgian civil society representatives in this conference, as well as reports received from various human rights defenders attending the OSCE Human Dimension Conference in Warsaw. We reiterate the importance of ensuring safe participation in OSCE events, without any reprisals.”

Incident at the conference

The conference in Warsaw is attended by Baia Pataraia, head of the Georgian NGO Sapari, and Tamar Oniani, head of the Georgian Young Lawyers’ Association.

On 5 October, during a speech by a representative of the Georgian delegation, Pataraia held up a banner reading: “Free all Georgian political prisoners.”

Pataraia says her protest was peaceful and silent, and that she had arranged it in advance in accordance with OSCE rules.

“Wherever I find myself alongside the [Georgian] government, I will remind them that prisons are full of political prisoners and that the Georgian people will never accept this,” she says.

Pataraia adds that Germany, Slovenia and other countries have urged Georgia to implement the recommendations of the Moscow Mechanism and stop persecuting media representatives, politicians and civil society members.

In this context, she also criticised the Georgian authorities’ bid to make Georgia the OSCE chair in 2027.

“They want benefits, money, prestige and power from everyone, but they themselves fulfil none of their obligations,” Pataraia said indignantly.

The ruling Georgian Dream party is seeking to secure the OSCE chairpersonship for 2027. Georgian Foreign Minister Maka Bochorishvili says the country has already submitted its application to the OSCE and hopes to win the support of participating States. However, according to the publication Rapporteur, EU member states do not support Georgia’s bid.



OSCE conference in Warsaw

World.title: Abkhazia plans pension reform, new law to take work history into account
World.content:
The government of Abkhazia has drafted a pension reform bill aimed at streamlining pension legislation, taking employment history into account when calculating pension payments and introducing specific support measures for socially vulnerable groups.

The draft pension law was prepared by the Ministry of Social Welfare and Demographic Policy. According to Minister Kama Adzynba, the bill aims to streamline regulations governing employment-related, insurance-based and funded pensions, as well as payments for special services to the country.

One of the key principles of the proposed reform is to take individuals’ employment history into account when determining pension payments. Currently, pensions in Abkhazia stand at 6,000 roubles [approximately $70], a standard amount paid to everyone, regardless of whether they have worked for many years or have never been formally employed.

Pensioners who hold dual Abkhaz-Russian citizenship and also receive a Russian pension have their Abkhaz pension reduced to a largely symbolic 500 roubles [around $6].

The new system is intended to address this “injustice”. It also provides for survivor’s pensions and other social benefits, which are expected to exceed the basic social pension.

The bill also introduces special pensions for distinguished service to the country. Recipients of state orders and veterans of the 1992-93 Georgian-Abkhaz war are among those proposed for inclusion in this category.

The draft law will be submitted to parliament for consideration.

World.title: Azerbaijan’s $90bn reserves draw criticism from former opposition leader
World.content:
Azerbaijan’s foreign currency reserves

Ilgar Mammadov, former chairman of Azerbaijan’s Republican Alternative (ReAl) party, has criticised the country’s accumulation of $90bn in foreign currency reserves. In a Facebook post, he argued that there was little reason to take pride in such substantial reserves when some elderly citizens were forced to survive on modest social benefits.

Mammadov proposed using part of the reserves to improve living standards while expanding economic freedoms.

“There are no reasonable grounds for a country like Azerbaijan to hold $90bn in foreign currency reserves,” the politician wrote.

What makes up Azerbaijan’s $90bn in foreign currency reserves?

Azerbaijan’s strategic foreign currency reserves comprise the Central Bank’s foreign exchange reserves and the assets of the State Oil Fund (SOFAZ). According to figures published by the State Statistical Committee, their combined value stood at $90.77bn as of 1 September 2026. This represents the total value of funds held in various financial assets.

The two institutions’ reserves serve different purposes. The Central Bank’s reserves are used to maintain stability in the foreign exchange market and mitigate risks associated with external payments.

The State Oil Fund accumulates revenues from oil and gas production, invests them, makes transfers to the state budget and builds up savings for future generations. Its assets are invested in bonds, equities, gold and property.

The authorities regard the substantial reserves as an indicator of the country’s financial resilience. Speaking at the Azerbaijan International Investment Forum in September, President Ilham Aliyev stressed that the reserves were approximately 20 times greater than the country’s external public debt.

According to Aliyev, this demonstrates the strength of Azerbaijan’s financial system and the stability of its national currency.

‘These $90bn have become a symbol of shame and disgrace’

Mammadov also approaches the issue from the perspective of public welfare. He argues that elderly citizens have contributed to the creation of national wealth not only through formal employment but also through domestic and agricultural work.

“Only the government of the New Azerbaijan Party (YAP) can proudly boast of having $90bn in foreign currency reserves in a country where 180,000 elderly citizens receive no retirement pension and are forced to make do with an old-age allowance of $130. This is simply shameful.

“People over the age of 65 have contributed to society throughout their lives through their labour and their role as consumers in the economy, helping to create the conditions for accumulating $90bn in foreign currency reserves.

“Whether it was a housewife who spent years supporting her husband as he worked as a labourer or engineer, or a man who worked in the fields for a pittance, supplying city residents with fresh fruit and vegetables, they all contributed to building up these reserves.

“This is a hardworking generation that the YAP authorities have left with virtually no means of subsistence in old age, while continuing to boast about the country’s foreign currency reserves.”

Mammadov argues that taking pride in growing reserves while this generation faces financial hardship is also morally unacceptable.

“Viewed from this perspective, even the question of economic efficiency becomes secondary. These $90bn have become a symbol of shame and disgrace.”

Assets held abroad and dependence on oil

Mammadov also argues that holding substantial foreign currency reserves abroad carries political risks. He cites Iraq and Libya as examples, pointing to the depletion of their financial resources during wars and the freezing of their assets. He links these events to the interests of external powers and suggests that Azerbaijan could face similar risks.

“By maintaining foreign currency reserves on this scale, Azerbaijan is merely provoking major players in the current world order, who are accustomed to playing by their own rules. It is like putting on our most expensive jacket, stuffing its pockets with bundles of cash and going for a walk at night down the most crime-ridden street in the city.

“There are plenty of historical examples. In 1980, Iraq’s foreign currency reserves stood at 36bn–40bn. In today’s money, that is just over $90bn. And what happened? A war with Iran was soon orchestrated, partly for the sake of that money, though not exclusively. As a result, all the money was spent on purchasing weapons from abroad, and the reserves were exhausted. Who benefited? The arms dealers.

“In 2011, Libya’s foreign currency reserves had barely reached $150bn when the country was plunged into turmoil. Some of the money was spent on arming the sides in the civil war, while around a third of the assets were frozen in foreign financial institutions (and someone is still profiting from them). The rest has never been traced.

“In today’s world, where the law of the jungle prevails, there is no point in keeping such substantial foreign currency reserves abroad. One day, a provocation could be staged against us too, and the money could be seized,” he wrote.

Mammadov also sees a potential collapse in financial markets as a serious threat. He believes securities are significantly overvalued and that a sharp fall in their prices could result in substantial losses for Azerbaijan.

Another of his arguments concerns the economy’s dependence on oil. Recalling the currency devaluations of 2015, he notes that the country’s foreign currency reserves failed to prevent the sharp depreciation of the manat.

“The reason reserves are rapidly depleted during a crisis and cannot serve as a financial safety net lies in the unhealthy state of our economy and its dependence on oil.”

According to Mammadov, if oil prices remain low for a prolonged period, substantial foreign currency reserves alone cannot guarantee economic security.

What does Mammadov propose?

Mammadov is not calling for Azerbaijan to spend all its foreign currency reserves. He believes some funds should be retained to deal with economic crises and natural disasters, although he does not specify how much should be set aside.

“There is an urgent need to improve people’s living standards, particularly those of the elderly. At the same time, economic freedoms must be expanded without delay so that citizens can realise their creative and entrepreneurial potential and generate new wealth,” the politician wrote.

Mammadov sees the rule of law as a fundamental prerequisite for these reforms. He concluded his post by urging voters to support the Republican Alternative (ReAl) party.

World.title: Pashinyan on extradition of Azerbaijani soldier, meeting Aliyev and Medvedev’s statement
World.content:
Pashinyan on Azerbaijani serviceman’s extradition and other issues

The extradition of Azerbaijani serviceman Nasimi Musayev is not under discussion, and Baku has not made such a request. Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan told journalists this during his traditional hour-long briefing.

“What extradition are you talking about? There is no such issue, and we are not discussing it. Azerbaijan has made no request,” he said.

At the same time, he stressed that Armenia would have returned Musayev on the same day if he had not committed a crime.

Pashinyan described the Azerbaijani serviceman, who illegally crossed into Armenia and shot a resident of the village of Shaki, as having committed an “ordinary crime”. The prime minister drew parallels with other forms of cross-border crime:

“We also have other cases of cross-border crime. Drugs are constantly exported to Armenia and transported through Armenia in transit. There is no need to turn this into an apocalypse.”

The prime minister does not believe the incident in Shaki could threaten the peace process between Armenia and Azerbaijan.

He considers the peace that Armenia and Azerbaijan have established an achievement that requires protection. He warns that they could destroy it in a day, while reaching the current state of relations could take another 30 years. For this reason, he does not consider it appropriate to make statements that could threaten the peace process.

On 1 October 2026, Nasimi Musayev illegally entered the village of Shaki in Armenia’s Syunik Province. Local residents found him inside a house, where he opened fire with an assault rifle and wounded a 39-year-old woman. Her three children witnessed the incident. Her two sons also suffered injuries, while her daughter has yet to recover psychologically.

Musayev fled after the shooting, but authorities detained him shortly afterwards in another house. The Armenian Prosecutor’s Office brought criminal charges under five articles of the Criminal Code. The charges include illegally crossing the border, causing serious bodily harm to a local resident and violating the inviolability of a home. A court ordered his detention for two months.

During the briefing, the prime minister also addressed Dmitry Medvedev’s controversial statement about turning Armenia into a “new Ukraine”, a possible meeting with Aliyev at the CIS summit and the issue of missing persons.

“No official meetings are planned”: on contacts with Putin and Aliyev

On 8-9 October, Pashinyan will attend the CIS summit in Turkmenistan. Asked about possible meetings with the presidents of Russia and Azerbaijan, he recalled that his latest meetings with Putin and Aliyev took place in Bishkek last month. He also spoke to the Russian president by phone the day before.

“The format is such that contacts with the president of Russia and the president of Azerbaijan will certainly take place. We will be in the same place today and tomorrow. No official meeting is planned. If it turns out that such a meeting is necessary, it may take place,” he said.

“Armenia has already faced such a threat”: response to Medvedev

People in Armenia continue to discuss Russian Security Council Deputy Chairman Dmitry Medvedev’s statement. He said that Armenia’s leadership had decided to change the country’s course and that this would not lead to anything good.

“The worst thing that could happen to Armenia is for it to turn into a new Ukraine,” Medvedev said.

Journalists asked Pashinyan whether Armenia could face such a threat. He replied:

“Armenia has already faced a similar danger and situation. In September 2022, [during the Azerbaijani armed forces’ invasion of Armenia’s sovereign territory], the CSTO failed to fulfil its obligations.”

The Collective Security Treaty Organisation is a military alliance led by Russia. Armenia is a member of the CSTO. Under the organisation’s charter, its allies had to provide military assistance to a member state, but that did not happen.

The Armenian prime minister could not explain why Medvedev was making such statements and threats:

“Following the same logic, someone else could say: ‘We do not want Armenia to turn into a “new Russia”, given that explosions can be heard in various parts of Russia.’ This is an unfortunate genre.”

He assured that Armenia would not turn into anything else and would instead become an even more independent state.

“Some circles in Azerbaijan use this issue for political purposes”: on missing persons

Azerbaijan periodically demands that Armenia provide information about the fate of missing Azerbaijanis and the locations of their graves. President Ilham Aliyev repeated the demand at an international conference on missing persons in Baku.

According to Armenia’s prime minister, both sides should make joint efforts to establish the fate of missing people:

“We have stated that we are ready to cooperate. The problem is that some circles in Azerbaijan use this issue for political purposes, including to generate hostile rhetoric and pursue other aims.”

According to figures Pashinyan presented, the whereabouts of around 1,000 people who went missing during wars since the 1990s remain unknown in Armenia.

He says the wording itself — “their whereabouts are unknown” — shows how little information the authorities have about these people:

“Some circles in Azerbaijan sometimes try to create the impression that we know where these people are and refuse to share the information. But that is not the case.”

Pashinyan believes the two sides should resolve the issue through cooperation and close this chapter. He said that in Bishkek, he and the Azerbaijani president also discussed stepping up joint efforts by the relevant commissions of the two countries.

Pashinyan on Azerbaijani serviceman’s extradition and other issues

World.title: ‘Light rosè’, or why claim that Abkhazia has no good wine is outdated. VIDEO
World.content:
Wine in Abkhazia

For a long time, Abkhazia was known mainly for its basic range of wines. The region’s unpredictable climate, with annual rainfall of up to 2,000 mm, was seen as a challenge, as was the popularity of mass-produced semi-sweet wines.

However, modern winemaking practices have challenged this perception. Today, Abkhaz wine producers are shifting their focus towards premium wines.

The Association of Winemakers is actively reviving local indigenous grape varieties. It says fermentation control and modern scientific methods now make it possible to produce delicate, dry and fresh rosé wines.

World.title: European Parliament resolution on banning opposition parties in Georgia: what it says
World.content:
On 8 October, the European Parliament adopted its latest — and seventh — critical resolution on Georgia. This time, it focuses on the ruling Georgian Dream party’s attempts to ban five opposition parties and political groups.

In the resolution, the European Parliament strongly condemns the attempts to outlaw these opposition parties and calls for the immediate withdrawal of the constitutional lawsuit against them.

The draft resolution also once again calls for the release of political prisoners and sanctions against those responsible for Georgia’s democratic backsliding. It specifically names Georgian Dream founder and honorary chairman Bidzina Ivanishvili, party secretary-general Kakha Kaladze, Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze and Parliament Speaker Shalva Papuashvili.

The document says that the actions of Georgian Dream have caused the situation in Georgia to deteriorate further. Democracy and media freedom have declined, while human rights and the rule of law face growing violations. The document says this increasingly conflicts with Georgia’s international obligations and responsibilities, including the Copenhagen criteria.

The draft resolution also notes that two German foundations — the Konrad Adenauer Foundation and the Friedrich Naumann Foundation — had to close their offices in Tbilisi after the authorities rejected their funding applications under the grants law.

The draft resolution also again refers to the persecution of journalists in Georgia who covered the authorities’ repression of the opposition and civil society.

According to the draft resolution, the European Parliament:

Strongly condemns the attempt to outlaw Georgia’s opposition parties and calls for the immediate withdrawal of the constitutional lawsuit against them. It stresses that a functioning political opposition is an indispensable pillar of democracy and that using judicial mechanisms to eliminate legitimate political opposition is incompatible with democracy. It notes that banning the only opposition party represented in the Georgian parliament undermines the government’s previous narrative that it targeted only parties “under boycott”;

Timeline of European Parliament resolutions on Georgia

Since October 2024, the European Parliament has adopted six critical resolutions concerning the Georgian government. In these documents, MEPs have criticised Georgian Dream’s policies on democracy, the rule of law, human rights and the country’s European integration.

BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 10. Deputy Minister of Economy and Commerce of Kyrgyzstan Mederbek Tumanov met with Head of the Islamic Development Bank’s (IsDB) Regional Hub in Almaty Hammad Zafar Hundal and bank representatives on October 8, 2026, at the ministry to discuss the preparation of new initiatives.

This was reported by the press service of the Ministry of Economy and Commerce of the Kyrgyz Republic.

"On October 8, 2026, a meeting was held at the Ministry of Economy and Commerce of the Kyrgyz Republic between Deputy Minister of Economy and Commerce of the Kyrgyz Republic Mederbek Tumanov, Head of the Islamic Development Bank’s (IsDB) Regional Hub in Almaty Hammad Zafar Hundal and representatives of the bank," the statement said.

During the meeting, Mederbek Tumanov outlined key areas for further cooperation, including the implementation of ongoing projects, the preparation of new initiatives and the expansion of engagement in areas that are priorities for the Kyrgyz Republic.

The deputy minister noted that the Islamic Development Bank is an important and reliable partner for Kyrgyzstan.

"Long-standing cooperation covers a wide range of issues related to the country’s socio-economic development. With the support of the IsDB, a number of significant projects aimed at developing infrastructure and supporting economic growth are being implemented and prepared," the ministry’s press service noted.

Mederbek Tumanov emphasized the importance of regular direct dialogue between the ministry and the bank’s leadership.

The sides noted that this format of engagement makes it possible to address emerging issues promptly, find joint solutions and identify new opportunities for cooperation.

Mederbek Tumanov also congratulated Hammad Zafar Hundal on his appointment as regional director of the Islamic Development Bank and expressed confidence that his professional experience would contribute to further strengthening cooperation between Kyrgyzstan and the bank.

World.title: Kyrgyzstan and Mongolia discuss expanding trade and economic ties
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 10. Deputy Minister of Economy and Commerce of the Kyrgyz Republic Sultan Akhmatov met with Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Mongolia to the Kyrgyz Republic Demchig Tegshjargal on October 9, 2026, to discuss bilateral trade and economic cooperation.

This was reported by the press service of the Ministry of Economy and Commerce of the Kyrgyz Republic.

"During the meeting, the sides discussed current issues of bilateral trade and economic cooperation, prospects for increasing mutual trade, developing industrial cooperation and implementing joint projects," the statement said.

Particular attention was paid to strengthening ties between the business communities of the two countries, organizing business forums and exhibitions, as well as identifying new mechanisms for cooperation.

Following the meeting, the sides expressed interest in further expanding Kyrgyz-Mongolian trade and economic cooperation and continuing joint efforts to implement the agreements reached.

Meanwhile, Kyrgyzstan continues to develop economic ties with countries across Asia, seeking opportunities to expand trade, attract investment and strengthen business cooperation. Contacts between government representatives provide a platform for discussing trade barriers, identifying areas of mutual interest and exploring opportunities for joint initiatives.

Cooperation with Mongolia could involve exchanges of experience in sectors where both countries see potential for development, as well as stronger links between companies and business associations. Business forums, exhibitions and direct contacts between entrepreneurs can help identify potential partners and support the development of commercial relations.

Industrial cooperation and joint projects may provide additional opportunities to diversify bilateral economic ties. Further progress will depend on the priorities identified by both sides, the involvement of businesses and the practical implementation of agreements reached during bilateral discussions.

World.title: International conference participants end visit to Azerbaijan's Karabakh (PHOTO)
World.content:
LACHIN, Azerbaijan, October 10. The visit to Azerbaijan’s Karabakh by participants of the 4th International Conference held within the framework of the Baku Dialogue on Missing Persons has concluded, Trend's Karabakh bureau reports.

The delegation visited the Khojaly, Fuzuli, Aghdam, and Lachin districts, as well as Shusha city, during the trip, which took place on October 9–10.

The guests also visited the Khojaly Genocide Memorial Complex and explored the sights of Shusha.

On the final day, the delegation visited Zabukh village in the Lachin district. Masim Mammadov, the Special Representative of the President of Azerbaijan in the Lachin district, provided the guests with detailed information about the work being carried out in the village and the current situation.

Then, the conference participants visited the boulevard established along the banks of the Hakari river. After viewing the city from an observation point in Lachin, the guests also visited Heydar Aliyev Street, where they were briefed on Lachin city.

The delegation included ambassadors and military attachés accredited in Azerbaijan, representatives of non-governmental organizations, as well as former heads of state and government.

The 4th international conference, organized by the State Commission on Prisoners of War, Hostages, and Missing Persons, was dedicated to "Strengthening Trust and Developing Effective Mechanisms in Addressing the Issue of Missing Persons".

World.title: Russian attacks kill at least 12 in Ukraine after Trump-Putin diesel deal
World.content:
Russian strikes have killed at least 12 people in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says.

The deadly strikes came a day after US President Donald Trump announced a deal to buy Russian diesel, which Kyiv warned would help bankroll Moscow's war in Ukraine.

Three children were among those killed when Russian aerial bombs hit residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia, Mr Zelenskyy said on Saturday.

At least 14 people were wounded in the attack in the early hours of Saturday.

"Today, Russia expressed its thanks for the lifting of sanctions on diesel exports by dropping five glide bombs on residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia," Mr Zelenskyy wrote on X.

The Russian air strike happened in the early hours of the morning on Saturday. (Reuters: Stringer)

He said the attacks show Moscow understands "any easing of pressure to mean they can keep fighting, to mean they can keep dropping bombs on cities," adding that "different signals are needed".

Four civilians were killed and five others were wounded as a result of Ukrainian attacks on the Russian-controlled Luhansk region in eastern Ukraine in the past 24 hours, the region's Russian-installed governor Leonid Pasechnik said on Saturday.

There was no immediate comment from Kyiv about those attacks.

Trump's Russian diesel deal

The latest attacks came a day after United States President Donald Trump said he had struck a deal to obtain diesel from Russia.

The deal is a stunning reversal of years of US pressure on Moscow over its war with Ukraine, and an attempt to address high fuel prices ahead of the US midterm elections.

At least seven people were killed in the strikes in Zaporizhzhia. (AP Photo: Kateryna Klochko)

Mr Trump said on social media on Friday that he struck the deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin in a phone call in which he had been expected to discuss a suspected case of plague in Russia.

Instead, Mr Trump announced that Russia will immediately supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel, followed by an additional 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons "immediately thereafter."

Russia will deliver an additional 3 million tons "within a short period of time" after that, he wrote.

Mr Trump's shocking announcement was in stark contrast to a sweeping Russia sanctions law he signed last month that aimed at clamping down on the oil and gas revenues that fuel Russia's war against Ukraine.

Following Mr Trump's announcement, Germany said on Saturday it would maintain sanctions against Russia over its war on Ukraine.

The Kremlin said Mr Trump conveyed his ideas about how to de-escalate the war in Ukraine to Mr Putin during their phone call on Friday.

Mr Putin received the proposals "with understanding", Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Saturday according to the state TASS and RIA Novosti news agencies.

He didn't elaborate on what the proposals were or the Russian president's response.

Mr Trump has long sought to broker an end to the more than four-and-a-half year conflict, but talks between Russia and Ukraine remain largely deadlocked.

Trump deal a 'weak decision', Zelenskyy says

In a lengthy post online reacting to the deal, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia would repay it "with further terror and perfidy."

'Poster child' for Putin's propaganda machine Russia is not just abducting Ukrainian kids, it is embarking on a campaign of mass indoctrination, as Denys Kostev experienced firsthand.

He cast it as an investment in the war, allowing it to be prolonged.

"It plays into Russia's hands — allowing it to kill more, wage war for longer, have even less respect for America, and inflict even greater losses and damage on the world," he said.

According to a statement released by the Ukrainian Embassy in Washington, Mr Zelenskyy called it "a weak decision, unfortunately, a weak decision by strong partners".

Mr Trump announced the deal as his envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner were meeting with Ukrainian officials in Miami to discuss a proposal to end the war.

"I believe our team is simply being used as a smoke screen, and that is certainly not fair. It is certainly not how partners should treat each other," Mr Zelenskyy said.

Ukraine is struggling to counter escalating Russian bombardments that have killed more than 55 people over the past four days, including in a bus stop attack that killed 33 people on Thursday.

AP/Reuters/AFP

World.title: Woman found dead in Carlton apartment identified as 21yo Jayda Allen Bonner
World.content:
The family of a young woman found dead in a Melbourne apartment block overnight has told the ABC they had serious concerns about her safety and had recently sought help from police.

Twenty-one-year-old Jayda Allen Bonner was described by her aunt as a "gentle soul" with a "heart of gold."

"[She] would do anything to help anybody," Kellie Carter-Bell said on Saturday.

She said Jayda was a Yagera woman with family in Queensland.

Homicide detectives are investigating after police were called to an apartment in the inner-city suburb of Carlton in the early hours of Saturday.

Authorities said they were called to the apartment on Cardigan Street just before 2am and when they arrived, found the body of a woman.

Jayda Allen Bonner's family says they had recently raised concerns with police about her safety. (Supplied)

While investigations are underway and no charges have been laid, Ms Carter-Bell said the family had been so concerned about Jayda's welfare that they had recently sought help from police.

"The really horrible, horrible thing is that the system's so broken that about six weeks ago, we begged for their help," she said.

"We begged for their help, and because we were ringing them and not Jayda, their attitude was, 'Well, what do you want us to do?'"

Victoria Police did not respond to the family's claim, with a spokesperson telling the ABC it could not comment while an investigation was underway.

Man arrested, then released

Police said a 60-year-old man was arrested and interviewed nearby after a crime scene was established in Carlton, but has since been released.

Forensic detectives were seen removing evidence from the complex on Saturday.

Ms Carter-Bell said she wanted the community to see Ms Allen Bonner's picture so they could understand her story.

"We are absolutely devastated," she said.

"We need people to know that the system is so broken," she said.

World.title: Opal Tower declared defect-free eight years after evacuations
World.content:
A ribbon-cutting ceremony has taken place at the once-plagued Opal Tower in Sydney's west to mark the building officially being declared defect-free.

The celebration brings an end to a saga, spanning close to eight years, that involved a class action, two legal cases, ongoing rectification work and relocations after cracks appeared on level 10 of the complex on Christmas Eve in 2018.

Fearing a collapse, thousands of people were forced to evacuate with the emergency response also shutting down the nearby train station and surrounding roads at Sydney Olympic Park.

Opal Tower was officially declared defect-free on Saturday. (ABC News)

At the time, police said the tower had moved "1 to 2 millimetres".

Days later, more cracks were discovered on other levels of the 36-storey high-rise.

Opal Tower Owners Corporation chairman Shady Eskander has been at the forefront of the fight to get the complex made up of 392 units repaired, and secure compensation for those affected.

"The story is about defects, but really it's about devastation to people's lives when something goes wrong in your home, it completely up-ends you," he said.

"It's fantastic to announce that Opal Tower is defect-free."

Shady Eskander says the impact of the defects has been devastating for residents. (ABC News: Liam Patrick)

Mr Eskander told the ABC that a lot of work had taken place and millions of dollars had been spent to be able to declare "this building is the safest and best residential building in Australia".

"Everything that was done was done with the consultants, with the builder, with all of those involved in the design and construction of Opal Tower.

"We came alongside each other in a very collaborative manner."

Developer Ecove, backed by Japanese firm Kajina Corporation, engineers WSP, and builder Icon have been the other parties involved in the process.

20-year structural warranty

An engineer's report commissioned by the NSW government concluded in 2019 that the cracks had been caused by a combination of "design and construction matters, in particular changes made after the original design".

In what Mr Eskander described as an Australian-first, the high-rise is now protected by a 20-year structural warranty.

A report concluded the defects were caused by a combination of "design and construction matters". (Supplied)

All owners have been fairly compensated, and all legal matters have been resolved.

"This is the greatest property comeback story in Australian history," Mr Eskander said in a statement.

Nutan Borkar was out of her unit for 11 months after the incident, and was glad there was finally "light at the end of the tunnel after a big struggle".

"It's great because a lot of time has been invested in getting the building back to the way it should've been," she said.

"I love being here. I wouldn't think of being anywhere else but here now. It's home."

Nutan Borkar says she "wouldn't think of being anywhere else". (ABC News: Liam Patrick)

Building standards were lifted across the state, with the Coalition government at the time introducing the role of building commissioner and a suite of other reforms.

"The lesson that can be learnt from Opal Tower … is that quality needs to be there so that defects aren't," Mr Eskander said.

"And we need to ensure that defects don't occur in the towers that are being constructed over Sydney because builders and contractors will spend more on fixing the defect than building it right the first time."

World.title: Zach Bates qualifies on pole for Bathurst 1000
World.content:
Supercars rookie Zach Bates — not qualifying king Brodie Kostecki — will start the Bathurst 1000 in pole position.

Kostecki was on track to become the first driver to snare four straight pole positions after laying a mighty lap of two minutes and 4.4912 seconds as the fifth driver in Saturday's top-10 shootout.

Proven race winners Will Brown, David Reynolds and Anton De Pasquale tried, but failed to beat Kostecki's time.

But provisional pole-sitter Bates refused to waver, proving his mettle as the last driver with a searing lap around the famous Mount Panorama track.

Bates denied Kostecki with a scorching lap of Mt Panorama. (Getty Images: Robert Cianflone )

A day after becoming the fastest Gen3 racer, the 22-year-old clocked 2:04.2062 to deny Kostecki by 0.285 seconds.

Bates had earlier become the first to go below the 2:04 benchmark in the Gen3 era after taking provisional pole with a time of 2:03.9376.

In just his second pursuit of the holy grail of Australian motorsport, Bates is the third rookie to claim pole position after Klaus Ludwig (1987) and Marcos Ambrose (2001).

The Canberra local is the son of former rally and Supercars driver Rick Bates, and the nephew of four-time Australian Rally champion Neal Bates.

His surprise success comes after his mother Alison Drower died from cancer weeks before his Bathurst 1000 debut last year, in which he finished 10th as part of the Triple Eight Race Engineering wildcard with the great Craig Lowndes.

Team 18 driver De Pasquale will start in the second row with fourth-fastest Cooper Murray, while series leader Matt Payne was 10th.

But Grove Racing star Payne will be far from disheartened, given he had started from 18th en route to last year's epic wet-weather triumph with former co-driver Garth Tander.

Reynolds will start on the grid in eighth after a family of ducks threatened to derail his bid for a second Bathurst 1000 title.

Tickford co-driver Mark Winterbottom was forced to a sudden halt when ducks were spotted crossing the track at Conrod Straight during practice on Friday.

Brock inspires Bathurst 20 years on Just as he does every year, Craig Lowndes is drawing on memories of Australian motorsport legend Peter Brock to fuel yet another attempt at the Bathurst 1000.

Winterbottom's sudden braking caught out Reynolds' co-driver James Courtney, who locked up and slammed into the rear of the Tickford Ford Mustang.

But both cars were able to return to complete the 60-minute practice session before the shootout.

Defending Supercars champion Chaz Mostert was among the big names to miss out on the top-10 shootout and will start from 16th for the best qualifying result in the Toyota Supra.

Payne's teammate Kai Allen fell agonisingly short in 11th, while title contender Broc Feeney was 12th ahead of Cam Waters in 13th.

Kostecki's rookie teammate Rylan Gray will start from the back row with Ryan Wood after the duo crashed out in separate incidents in Friday's first practice session.

ABC Sport will have a live blog of the Bathurst 1000 from lights out to the chequered flag on Sunday, October 11.

World.title: Police investigating unexplained infant death at Adelaide motel
World.content:
South Australian Police have attended the Tollgate Motel in Glen Osmond on Saturday morning to investigate a reported infant death.

ABC News understands police and ambulances were called to the Tollgate Motel, adjacent to the South Eastern Freeway, five kilometres south-east of the Adelaide CBD, from 9am.

Some witnesses estimated around 20 officers were present.

Police vehicles attended the scene throughout the morning. (Supplied)

"There were at least four or five police cars here," a nearby resident told the ABC.

"It's a bit concerning that we've got police cars down the end of our quiet cul-de-sac."

Police left the scene by mid-afternoon, after establishing a cordon.

Police have cordoned off a room at the Tollgate Motel. (ABC News: Briana Fiore)

The cause of the child's death is currently undetermined.

Police have confirmed that an investigation is ongoing with the assistance of crime scene investigators and Eastern District Detectives, and a report will be prepared for the coroner.

World.title: Light strikes again, ending play early after Renshaw's career-best knock
World.content:
Matt Renshaw has notched his career-high Test score to lead Australia into a healthy spot on day two of the first Test against South Africa in Durban.

Renshaw's 190 eclipsed his previous best from way back in January 2017 and carried the team from 6-124 to 390 all out by the time he nicked off two balls after tea.

Renshaw was supported in an 86-run partnership with Pat Cummins (43 off 98) that was eclipsed by a marathon 134-run stand with Nathan Lyon (27 off 92), which stands as Australia's second-best stand for the ninth wicket in Test history.

Australia's bowlers wasted no time making an impact in their primary role as Josh Hazlewood removed South Africa opener Ryan Rickelton for a duck with the ninth ball of the innings.

Aiden Markram played some glorious drives to be unbeaten on 15 alongside David Bedingham, who was 12 not out at stumps.

Look back at all the action in our live blog below, and check out all the stats in our ScoreCentre.

World.title: Two 'very lucky' men survive light aircraft crash in field
World.content:
A light aircraft plunged into a field north of Perth on Saturday, with the two men on board surviving the crash with non-life-threatening injuries.

Police said the pilot of the single-engine aircraft crashed near the Greenside private airfield, off Brand Highway in Muchea, north-east of Perth, this morning.

Emergency services responded to the incident, during which the aircraft sustained "significant damage", police said.

A man in his 60s and another man in his 30s were treated at the scene.

The two men on board survived the crash with non-life-threatening injuries. (ABC News: Mya Kordic)

Department of Fire and Emergency Services (DFES) district officer Gareth Deeg attended the scene and said one occupant extracted himself from the aircraft, while the other person was assisted out.

"Without knowing the investigation and seeing the speed and the reasons behind it, any aircraft that comes on an abnormal landing is obviously critical," he said.

" The two gentleman are very lucky today to be able to walk away and be safe. "

'Complex' crash site

The men were transported to Royal Perth Hospital at priority one, and St John Ambulance said they are believed to have non-life-threatening injuries.

Mr Deeg said several people at the airfield at the time of the crash quickly came to the aid of the two men.

He described the crash scene as "complex".

"It's complex for a number of natures: the location, the information that's provided, the fuel, the aircraft, what it's made out of," he said.

The Greenside Recreational Flyers Club, one of the state's largest, operates at the airfield, according to its website.

The aircraft crashed around 250 metres from the airfield's runway. Its fuselage, wings and tail were badly damaged.

Police said their inquiries are ongoing.

World.title: St Kilda end the drought to send Dal Santo out a winner
World.content:
St Kilda gave departing AFLW coach Nick Dal Santo the perfect send-off with a drought-breaking two-point home win over Collingwood.

With the bottom-of-the-table Saints holding a 0-8 record, Dal Santo announced on Friday he was standing down and took charge of the team for the final time in Saturday's game at Moorabbin Oval.

After scoring just one point last week and tallying five behinds in the first half on Saturday, the Saints kicked five second-half goals on their way to a 5.9 (39 ) to 5.7 (37) win.

Jesse Tawhiao-Wardlaw kicked two goals and Tyanna Smith bagged 25 touches and 12 clearances for the Saints, who ended an 11-match losing streak stretching back almost a full year.

Collingwood (1-8) kicked the only two goals of the first half, the first to captain Ruby Schleicher, who later came off the ground with an injury to her right shoulder.

The other major went to Sabrina Frederick in her 100th AFLW game, as Collingwood stretched a two-point lead after a goalless first quarter to 12 at half-time.

The victory was St Kilda's first of the AFLW season. (Getty Images: Daniel Pockett)

With the wind at their backs, the Saints rallied In the third quarter, kicking three straight goals and four for the term to lead by 10 points at the last change.

Ashley Centra, who gathered 25 touches for the Pies, kicked a goal in the final 30 seconds to cut the gap to two points, but the Saints held on.

"I understand this is my last game, but that was a really good game by the girls. I thought we fought really hard," Dal Santo told Fox and Kayo.

"I'm really proud of this group. It's been a delight and I'm really grateful for being a part of their journeys.

"I've loved it. Five years and the time is right," added Dal Santo, who finished with a 23-39 win-loss record.

AAP

World.title: Australia vs South Africa LIVE: South Africa one down at stumps after Renshaw shines with 190
World.content:
Matt Renshaw’s coming-of-age moment in Test cricket has taken Australia from a position of peril to one of command in the series opener against South Africa.

Almost a decade after his last hundred as baby-faced 20-year-old, Renshaw enjoyed the finest day of his career as his 190 led Australia to 390 on day two in Durban.

Josh Hazlewood then had Ryan Rickleton caught edging a drive to third slip for a duck, before South Africa were 1-27 when bad light stopped play.

Australia’s Matt Renshaw celebrates on day two. AP Photo/Themba Hadebe

Andrew McDonald had spoken in the lead up this Kingsmead Test about the importance of lower-order runs and being willing to get into grind, and Australia delivered on both on Saturday.

After Australia slumped to 6-124 midway through the first day of the series, Renshaw and Pat Cummins (43) combined for an 84-run seventh-wicket stand.

Renshaw and Nathan Lyon (27) then added 134 together, marking Australia’s largest ninth-wicket partnership since 1894.

All the while Renshaw managed the innings magnificently, knocking back singles and keeping the strike with South Africa were guilty of letting the game drift.

Renshaw’s last Test century came with in his fourth Test in January 2017, before finding himself dropped from the side 10 months after that score of 184.

Some 3567 days on from that hundred, Renshaw is now a 30-year-old who looks a far more complete cricketer after earning his third recall as an opener in August.

Australia’s Matt Renshaw plays a shot on day two. AP Photo/Themba Hadebe

So good was Renshaw’s innings, Australia may have another selection headache after Nic Maddinson came into the side and opened in this Test with a 33-ball duck.

If Renshaw is this settled in the middle order, can they afford to move the Queenslander back to open once Cameron Green or Josh Inglis comes back in?

Australia’s selectors had copped heavy criticism on Friday when they brought Nic Maddinson in to open, and he made a 33-ball duck.

But at least the decision to move Renshaw to No.5 paid off, after the Queenslander gave a glimpse of what was possible in the middle in the ODI series.

He was busy against the spin on Friday, and hit most of his early boundaries against the quicks behind square in the first half of his innings.

After bringing up his half-century in the first over on Saturday, Renshaw got through a tough period with the second new ball just after Cummins fell.

But as the morning went on Renshaw became more comfortable, cover-driving and cutting Anrich Nortje for two boundaries in one over.

He then hit his 204th ball from Marco Jansen to the long-on boundary to bring up his century, prompting a long embrace with Lyon and meaningful celebration.

After lunch he started reverse-sweeping the spinners to the boundary and even uppercut Nortje for a six.

Another big hook shot bounced onto the hill at Kingsmead, while the left-hander routinely hit through gaps on the legside.

He eventually edged spinner Simon Harmer to slip two balls after tea, but by that point his 397-ball stay had ensured Australia were well on top.

At the other end, Cummins, Mitchell Starc (5) Lyon and Hazlewood saw out 226 balls between them and lasted a combined 388 minutes alongside Renshaw.

Even after he was out, Renshaw and Hazlewood (5no) added another 26 for the last wicket.

The other concern for the Proteas was the lack of purchase they got out of their spin, after going with two tweakers.

While Harmer (1-68) and Keshav Maharaj (0-75) are there for when the pitch dries later in the game, the fact they did little damage was notable.

That meant Nortje (2-88) was forced to bowl 28 overs in his first first-class game in three-and-a-half years, while Wiaan Mudler (4-68) bowled 27 and Jansen 31 for his 3-68.



AAP

World.title: Australia Cup final as it happened: South Melbourne claims Australia Cup on record-breaking night
World.content:
South Melbourne have become the first non A-League team to win the Australia Cup after beating Melbourne Victory on penalties in an emotion-charged blockbuster final.

In one of the greatest nights in Australian domestic soccer history, former NSL powerhouses South first took Victory to extra time then fought back from 1-0 down to level it at 1-1 at the death before winning 4-3 on penalties in front of a pumping sellout crowd of 29,911 fans at AAMI Park.

South Melbourne, who have long craved an A-League licence, only strengthened their bid for that with a win that capped off an extraordinary evening.

South Melbourne Hellas is in delirium. Getty Images

Denis Genreau scored an athletic, improvised half-volley in the 95th minute to put Victory in front, before Max Mikkola forced home an equaliser in the 117th minute to send the game to penalties and the crowd into ecstasy.

In the penalty shootout, South goalkeeper Javier Lopez was the hero, denying former South captain Harrison Sawyer, before Victory skipper Jason Davidson hit his must-score penalty over the bar.

In becoming the first NPL team to win the Australia Cup, Sinisa Cohadzic’s South succeed where Heidelberg last year and Sydney United 58 in 2022 could not.

With the win, South also technically claim a berth in next season’s Asian Champions League 2 competition.

The defeat also extends Victory’s silverware drought, with the club’s most recent trophy the 2021 Australia Cup.

4. Jeremy Williams 7.5/10 The Wallabies’ best tight-five forward. Williams won two lineouts (11th and 19th minute) and won a penalty in the 22nd minute when he got on the ball. He was guilty of giving away one penalty in the 32nd minute, but that was a rare mistake. Jeremy Williams after the All Blacks scored – again. Getty Images 5. Lukhan Salakaia-Loto 6.5/10 The tight-head lock stood up physically over 80 minutes and won a lineout in the 60th minute. It wasn’t in the tight that the Wallabies lost.



6. Rob Valetini 6/10 Made an important linebreak early in the second half and combined well with his loose-forward teammate Fraser McReight. But Valetini, unfortunately, was penalised a minute later when he and Angus Bell were pinged for obstruction at the attacking lineout. It was a match-defining moment – and the big miss for the Wallabies. 7. Fraser McReight 7/10 Excellent on both sides of the ball. McReight got on the ball successfully twice, but his efforts weren’t rewarded because Andrew Brace was playing advantage on both occasions in the first half. McReight’s running game was on show, too. 8. Harry Wilson (c) 8.5/10



The Wallabies’ best player. Wilson led from the front and got through a truckload of work. Wilson scored a try and was just shy of making 30 tackles. It was a captain’s knock and one of his best performances. Harry Wilson dives under the posts to score for the Wallabies. Getty Images 9. Ryan Lonergan 6/10 Missed a crucial penalty in the 25th minute, which showcased the halfback’s nerves. The miss just added to the anxiety for the Wallabies and the All Blacks scored soon after to extend their lead out to 10 points. Otherwise, Lonergan’s pass was strong, but he wasn’t allowed to play with the same tempo and poise he had over past two months against sides missing plenty of top-line talent. 10. Ben Donaldson 6.5/10



Despite the loss, Donaldson should take some confidence out of his performance. The Wallabies certainly didn’t lose because of him. In fact, he was among the Wallabies’ stronger performers. He set up two tries, including a special one on the stroke of half-time, and he later won the Wallabies a five-metre lineout after putting the ball behind in the 45th minute and forcing Beauden Barrett to run it into touch. But he also kicked once out on the full and was beaten in his overall head-to-head with Damian McKenzie. The Wallabies celebrate after Harry Wilson’s try before half-time. Getty Images 11. Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii 5/10 A quieter performance than hoped. Suaalii was beaten in the air by Jordie Barrett in the 12th min, which proved a big moment as the All Blacks hit back seconds later. Later, Suaalii was pinged for a no-arms tackle. 12. Len Ikitau 4/10



Rushed back from injury, Ikitau struggled early before being forced off after 30 minutes following a failed head injury assessment. He dropped a ball on the All Blacks’ line and was beaten in defence by a hot-stepping Damian McKenzie ahead of the All Blacks’ first try. He was also beaten on a couple of other occasions, but that had less to do with him and more the stress the entire side were under in the opening half-hour. Len Ikitau was forced off after 30 minutes against the All Blacks. Getty Images 13. Isaac Henry 5.5/10 Didn’t do a lot wrong and defended well, but Henry was barely sighted and well beaten by his opposite Quinn Tuapea. 14. Max Jorgensen 6.5/10



There was quality, but just not enough of it. His timing and ball to Tom Wright for the opening try was superb. Unfortunately, the Wallabies’ outside backs just couldn’t get their hands on the ball. Jorgensen did find some space from the kickoff in the second half, but that was about it. Tom Wright dives over for the opening try. Getty Images 15. Tom Wright 6.5/10 Scored the Wallabies’ first try after pinning the ear back and bursting onto a ball from Max Jorgensen. Tried hard and looked threatening at stages, but like his teammates in the back three just simply couldn’t get involved enough. Replacements



16. Josh Nasser 4/10 The replacement hooker had his first throw pinched on his own line. Nor could the hooker influence the game on either side of the ball. Is it time to see Billy Pollard return? 17. Aidan Ross 4.5/10 Replaced Angus Bell with 25 minutes left, but was barely sighted. 18. Massimo De Lutiis 4.5/10



Spent his half-hour tackling. That’s it. Codie Taylor celebrates a try for the All Blacks. AP 19. Lachie Shaw 4.5/10 Came on for the last 21 minutes, but had little impact. 20. Nick Champion de Crespigny N/A



Replaced Valetini in the final 10 minutes, but barely sighted. 21. Tate McDermott 5/10 One clumsy moment alongside Wilson. McDermott’s running game wasn’t seen with the Wallabies on the back foot. 22. Declan Meredith 4/10 Replaced Donaldson in the 68th minute. Unfortunately, his final pass hit the turf and Will Jordan got on the end of it and scored. Time and chances are running out for the Brumbies playmaker.



23. Harry Potter 5/10 Replaced Ikitau and jumped on the wing after 30 minutes, Potter couldn’t get into the game and was largely a sitting duck under a couple of kicks. Overall, the Wallabies’ bench had very little impact. News, results and expert analysis from the weekend of sport sent every Friday.

World.title: Shame young hoons not to drive recklessly
World.content:
NationalNSWLetters Shame young hoons not to drive recklessly October 10, 2026 — 9:00pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

The shocking events in Newcastle last Saturday (“Newcastle’s shouts of joy turn to tears as fans grapple with crash”, October 4) should prompt the NSW government to revisit the highly effective “Pinkie” campaign from the early 2000s. The advertising targeted young male drivers, aged 17 to 25, but instead of using traditional, graphic scare tactics, the ad relied on social shame and peer judgment to challenge reckless driving. The tagline “Speeding. No one thinks big of you”, combined with a well-known gesture indicating a small penis, struck a chord with those young males which other approaches failed to do. Perhaps this could help compensate for the lack of a fully developed prefrontal cortex.

Tim Parker, Balmain Paramedics prepare to transport a patient by helicopter after 10 people who had gathered to farewell the Newcastle Knights team bus were injured by a car. Sitthixay Ditthavong What happened in Newcastle last weekend is obviously devastating for Novocastrians and devastating for the fans, players and people like me keen to seek out something that was joyful, community centred and just celebrated a cornerstone of what it is to be Australian – sport. Is this an opportunity for the government to start thinking about compulsory community service for our young? I’m pretty sure it’s not only me who is exhausted, shattered and shocked that with every passing day/week we see or hear about our young (men in particular) shooting, murdering, beating up or raping someone; running them over with a hotted-up e-bike, hooning in cars or filming someone doing same and hoisting it online. Two years of part-time compulsory community service would instil routine, discipline, help to develop skills and give young blokes an opportunity to participate in our society in positive ways, build character and resilience and make them realise that being a citizen is an actual thing and that everyone benefits when we all pull together. Can someone please look into this?

Dorin Suciu, Eleebana Breed, don’t buy, players How right is Brad Fittler that premiership titles and the like are not bought (“Kerry Packer offered me some advice, but I wasn’t buying his logic”, October 4). Rugby Australia has tried that approach, “buying” certain players, and it has not been successful. A team is individuals playing for each other and not always about the money. A team is not individuals playing for themselves and about the money.

Jenny Greenwood, Hunters Hill



Same old Hanson mantra One Nation is not saying anything new, in fact, it’s been the same old mantra for decades (“One Nation’s silence speaks loud and clear”, October 4). So why has it become such a threat to the major parties? People are hurting at the moment and, at times like this, they blame the government. Normally, the opposition is the party that people will turn to but the Coalition under the leadership of Angus Taylor has become a disaster and thus people are now looking to Pauline Hanson and One Nation. Since its birth, One Nation has been a disorganised rabble, its tactics mirroring Donald Trump through populist appeal, blaming foreigners and attacking the press. Just as the world is waiting for the midterm elections in the US, many Australians will nervously await the success of One Nation at next month’s Victorian election.

Peter Miniutti, Ashbury Article leaves us in the clouds Parnell Palme McGuinness (“Australia has to be smart about AI”, October 4) provides readers with yet another challenge to understand her position. As our resident expert on business behaviour and everything else, she rails against leaders in the AI industry in the US becoming very concerned about their industry inventing agents that can breach databases around the world. The delayed revelations of data break-ins reinforces their concerns, and ours. Their joint call for over-arching regulation can hardly be considered “a conspiracy against their competitors”. To rely on Georg Zoeller as an “international AI expert” when he is a merely a co-founder of a boutique non-profit training centre for AI leadership (C4AIL) in Singapore, is drawing on a very minor player in the complex AI universe. The article fails to explain how data centres “would keep us safe” – surely a catch-cry of floundering politicians – nor how AI regulation “would keep us weak and backward”. This article leaves us no further advanced in our understanding of the complexities of dealing with AI.

Bill Johnstone, Blackheath Flagging fervour



The mention of the Australian flag (Letters, October 4), reignites the pride factor we should all have in our flag, even if a new flag eventually adorns our poles. New Zealand tried to change its flag by referendum, aimed at removing the Union Jack, and it was soundly defeated. The Union Jack remains on its flag. Back in the 1980s, my son belonged to the Scout movement, becoming a Queen’s Scout and eventually a Leader. All scouts are taught flag protocols, especially that the national flag must never touch the ground. Then a newly elected politician presented a new flag to my son’s group and almost allowed the flag to touch the ground when handing it over, missing by millimetres. The whole troop erupted as one with “Woes”. After the ceremony, the new MP was privately educated by the Scout Leader.

David Sayers, Gwandalan On a high note Kate Ceberano may have said “No” to a Strictly Ballroom part but has since excited us all with her undeniable energy and fabulously strong voice for decades (“Ceberano winds back clock for encore 40 years in the making”, October 4). Her live gigs are always exciting, but the sultry Ceberano jazz plays in the comfort and background of my home and car hold long moments of intimacy for ever. I hold Kate Ceberano close, and she wouldn’t even know my gratefulness.

Janice Creenaune, Austinmer To submit a letter to The Sun-Herald, email letters@smh.com.au. Click here for tips on how to submit letters.

World.title: Australia vs South Africa LIVE: South Africa one down at stumps after Renshaw shines with 190
World.content:
Matt Renshaw’s coming-of-age moment in Test cricket has taken Australia from a position of peril to one of command in the series opener against South Africa.

Almost a decade after his last hundred as baby-faced 20-year-old, Renshaw enjoyed the finest day of his career as his 190 led Australia to 390 on day two in Durban.

Josh Hazlewood then had Ryan Rickleton caught edging a drive to third slip for a duck, before South Africa were 1-27 when bad light stopped play.

Australia’s Matt Renshaw celebrates on day two. AP Photo/Themba Hadebe

Andrew McDonald had spoken in the lead up this Kingsmead Test about the importance of lower-order runs and being willing to get into grind, and Australia delivered on both on Saturday.

After Australia slumped to 6-124 midway through the first day of the series, Renshaw and Pat Cummins (43) combined for an 84-run seventh-wicket stand.

Renshaw and Nathan Lyon (27) then added 134 together, marking Australia’s largest ninth-wicket partnership since 1894.

All the while Renshaw managed the innings magnificently, knocking back singles and keeping the strike with South Africa were guilty of letting the game drift.

Renshaw’s last Test century came with in his fourth Test in January 2017, before finding himself dropped from the side 10 months after that score of 184.

Some 3567 days on from that hundred, Renshaw is now a 30-year-old who looks a far more complete cricketer after earning his third recall as an opener in August.

Australia’s Matt Renshaw plays a shot on day two. AP Photo/Themba Hadebe

So good was Renshaw’s innings, Australia may have another selection headache after Nic Maddinson came into the side and opened in this Test with a 33-ball duck.

If Renshaw is this settled in the middle order, can they afford to move the Queenslander back to open once Cameron Green or Josh Inglis comes back in?

Australia’s selectors had copped heavy criticism on Friday when they brought Nic Maddinson in to open, and he made a 33-ball duck.

But at least the decision to move Renshaw to No.5 paid off, after the Queenslander gave a glimpse of what was possible in the middle in the ODI series.

He was busy against the spin on Friday, and hit most of his early boundaries against the quicks behind square in the first half of his innings.

After bringing up his half-century in the first over on Saturday, Renshaw got through a tough period with the second new ball just after Cummins fell.

But as the morning went on Renshaw became more comfortable, cover-driving and cutting Anrich Nortje for two boundaries in one over.

He then hit his 204th ball from Marco Jansen to the long-on boundary to bring up his century, prompting a long embrace with Lyon and meaningful celebration.

After lunch he started reverse-sweeping the spinners to the boundary and even uppercut Nortje for a six.

Another big hook shot bounced onto the hill at Kingsmead, while the left-hander routinely hit through gaps on the legside.

He eventually edged spinner Simon Harmer to slip two balls after tea, but by that point his 397-ball stay had ensured Australia were well on top.

At the other end, Cummins, Mitchell Starc (5) Lyon and Hazlewood saw out 226 balls between them and lasted a combined 388 minutes alongside Renshaw.

Even after he was out, Renshaw and Hazlewood (5no) added another 26 for the last wicket.

The other concern for the Proteas was the lack of purchase they got out of their spin, after going with two tweakers.

While Harmer (1-68) and Keshav Maharaj (0-75) are there for when the pitch dries later in the game, the fact they did little damage was notable.

That meant Nortje (2-88) was forced to bowl 28 overs in his first first-class game in three-and-a-half years, while Wiaan Mudler (4-68) bowled 27 and Jansen 31 for his 3-68.

World.title: Australia Cup final as it happened: South Melbourne claims Australia Cup on record-breaking night
World.content:
South Melbourne have become the first non A-League team to win the Australia Cup after beating Melbourne Victory on penalties in an emotion-charged blockbuster final.

In one of the greatest nights in Australian domestic soccer history, former NSL powerhouses South first took Victory to extra time then fought back from 1-0 down to level it at 1-1 at the death before winning 4-3 on penalties in front of a pumping sellout crowd of 29,911 fans at AAMI Park.

South Melbourne, who have long craved an A-League licence, only strengthened their bid for that with a win that capped off an extraordinary evening.

South Melbourne Hellas is in delirium. Getty Images

Denis Genreau scored an athletic, improvised half-volley in the 95th minute to put Victory in front, before Max Mikkola forced home an equaliser in the 117th minute to send the game to penalties and the crowd into ecstasy.

In the penalty shootout, South goalkeeper Javier Lopez was the hero, denying former South captain Harrison Sawyer, before Victory skipper Jason Davidson hit his must-score penalty over the bar.

In becoming the first NPL team to win the Australia Cup, Sinisa Cohadzic’s South succeed where Heidelberg last year and Sydney United 58 in 2022 could not.

With the win, South also technically claim a berth in next season’s Asian Champions League 2 competition.

The defeat also extends Victory’s silverware drought, with the club’s most recent trophy the 2021 Australia Cup.
